BESPOKE SAINTS ENGLISH
THE NEW TESTAMENT
Complete provisional reading draft · 12 November 2026

All 27 books; 260 chapters; 7,943 stored units. Inherited drafts plus seven proposed changes. Full Greek review, independent review, human read-aloud and editorial acceptance remain unfinished. See manifest.json and focused-reviews.json.


MATTHEW

Matthew 1
Matthew 1:1  A book of the origin of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham.
Matthew 1:2  Abraham begot Isaac; and Isaac begot Jacob; and Jacob begot Judah and his brothers;
Matthew 1:3  Judah begot Perez and Zerah by Tamar; Perez begot Hezron; Hezron begot Ram;
Matthew 1:4  Ram begot Amminadab; Amminadab begot Nahshon; Nahshon begot Salmon;
Matthew 1:5  Salmon begot Boaz by Rahab; Boaz begot Obed by Ruth; Obed begot Jesse;
Matthew 1:6  Jesse begot David the king. David begot Solomon by the wife of Uriah;
Matthew 1:7  Solomon begot Rehoboam; Rehoboam begot Abijah; Abijah begot Asaph;
Matthew 1:8  Asaph begot Jehoshaphat; Jehoshaphat begot Joram; Joram begot Uzziah;
Matthew 1:9  Uzziah begot Jotham; Jotham begot Ahaz; Ahaz begot Hezekiah;
Matthew 1:10  Hezekiah begot Manasseh; Manasseh begot Amos; Amos begot Josiah;
Matthew 1:11  Josiah begot Jechoniah and his brothers at the deportation to Babylon.
Matthew 1:12  After the deportation to Babylon, Jechoniah begot Shealtiel; Shealtiel begot Zerubbabel;
Matthew 1:13  Zerubbabel begot Abiud; Abiud begot Eliakim; Eliakim begot Azor;
Matthew 1:14  Azor begot Zadok; Zadok begot Achim; Achim begot Eliud;
Matthew 1:15  Eliud begot Eleazar; Eleazar begot Matthan; Matthan begot Jacob;
Matthew 1:16  and Jacob begot Joseph, the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.
Matthew 1:17  So all the generations from Abraham to David were fourteen generations, from David to the deportation to Babylon fourteen generations, and from the deportation to Babylon to the Christ fourteen generations.
Matthew 1:18  The origin of Jesus Christ was like this. When His mother Mary was betrothed to Joseph, before they came together she was found to be with child from the Holy Spirit.
Matthew 1:19  Joseph her husband, being righteous and unwilling to expose her to public disgrace, decided to divorce her quietly.
Matthew 1:20  As he considered these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph, son of David, do not fear to take Mary your wife home, for what has been conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
Matthew 1:21  She shall bear a Son, and you shall call His name Jesus, for He shall save His people from their sins.”
Matthew 1:22  All this has happened so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled:
Matthew 1:23  “Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall call His name Emmanuel”; which means “God with us.”
Matthew 1:24  When Joseph awoke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him and took his wife home.
Matthew 1:25  He did not have relations with her until she bore a Son; and he called His name Jesus.

Matthew 2
Matthew 2:1  After Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of King Herod, behold, magi from the east arrived in Jerusalem,
Matthew 2:2  saying, “Where is the One born King of the Jews? For we saw His star at its rising and have come to bow before Him.”
Matthew 2:3  When King Herod heard this, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
Matthew 2:4  He gathered all the chief priests and scribes of the people and asked them where the Christ was to be born.
Matthew 2:5  They told him, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for this is what has been written through the prophet:
Matthew 2:6  ‘And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for out of you will come a ruler who will shepherd My people Israel.’”
Matthew 2:7  Then Herod secretly called the magi and learned from them the exact time when the star appeared.
Matthew 2:8  He sent them to Bethlehem, saying, “Go and inquire carefully about the Child. When you find Him, report to me, so that I too may come and bow before Him.”
Matthew 2:9  After hearing the king, they went on their way. And behold, the star they had seen at its rising went ahead of them until it came and stood over the place where the Child was.
Matthew 2:10  When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.
Matthew 2:11  They entered the house and saw the Child with Mary His mother. Falling down, they bowed before Him; and opening their treasures, they offered Him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
Matthew 2:12  Having been warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they withdrew to their country by another way.
Matthew 2:13  After they withdrew, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, “Rise, take the Child and His mother, and flee to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you, for Herod is about to seek the Child to destroy Him.”
Matthew 2:14  He rose, took the Child and His mother by night, and withdrew to Egypt.
Matthew 2:15  He remained there until Herod’s death, so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled: “Out of Egypt I called My Son.”
Matthew 2:16  Then Herod, seeing that the magi had outwitted him, became exceedingly angry. He sent men and killed all the boys in Bethlehem and throughout its district who were two years old and under, according to the exact time he had learned from the magi.
Matthew 2:17  Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled:
Matthew 2:18  “A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and great lamentation: Rachel weeping for her children, and she would not be comforted, because they are no more.”
Matthew 2:19  After Herod died, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,
Matthew 2:20  saying, “Rise, take the Child and His mother, and go to the land of Israel, for those seeking the Child’s life have died.”
Matthew 2:21  He rose, took the Child and His mother, and entered the land of Israel.
Matthew 2:22  But hearing that Archelaus reigned over Judea in place of his father Herod, he feared to go there. Warned in a dream, he withdrew to the regions of Galilee.
Matthew 2:23  He came and settled in a city called Nazareth, so that what was spoken through the prophets might be fulfilled: “He will be called a Nazarene.”

Matthew 3
Matthew 3:1  In those days John the Baptist appeared, proclaiming in the wilderness of Judea
Matthew 3:2  and saying, “Repent, for the kingdom of the heavens has drawn near.”
Matthew 3:3  For this is the one spoken of through Isaiah the prophet: “A voice of one crying in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord; make His paths straight.’”
Matthew 3:4  John himself wore clothing of camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist; his food was locusts and wild honey.
Matthew 3:5  Then Jerusalem, all Judea, and all the region around the Jordan went out to him,
Matthew 3:6  and they were baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
Matthew 3:7  When he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them, “Brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
Matthew 3:8  Bear fruit, then, worthy of repentance,
Matthew 3:9  and do not suppose you can say among yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as father.’ For I tell you that God can raise up children for Abraham from these stones.
Matthew 3:10  Already the axe lies at the root of the trees. Every tree, therefore, that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into fire.
Matthew 3:11  I baptize you in water for repentance, but the One coming after me is stronger than I, whose sandals I am not fit to carry. He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire.
Matthew 3:12  His winnowing shovel is in His hand, and He will thoroughly clear His threshing floor and gather His wheat into the storehouse; but He will burn the chaff with unquenchable fire.”
Matthew 3:13  Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan, to John, to be baptized by him.
Matthew 3:14  John tried to prevent Him, saying, “I need to be baptized by Thee, and dost Thou come to me?”
Matthew 3:15  Jesus answered him, “Allow it now, for in this way it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness.” Then he allowed Him.
Matthew 3:16  When Jesus was baptized, He immediately came up from the water. And behold, the heavens were opened, and He saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming upon Him.
Matthew 3:17  And behold, a voice from the heavens said, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

Matthew 4
Matthew 4:1  Then Jesus was led up into the wilderness by the Spirit to be tempted by the devil.
Matthew 4:2  After fasting forty days and forty nights, He became hungry.
Matthew 4:3  The tempter came and said to Him, “If Thou art God’s Son, command these stones to become loaves of bread.”
Matthew 4:4  But He answered, “It is written: ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes forth through the mouth of God.’”
Matthew 4:5  Then the devil took Him into the holy city and set Him on the pinnacle of the temple,
Matthew 4:6  and said to Him, “If Thou art God’s Son, throw Thyself down. For it is written: ‘He will command His angels concerning Thee,’ and ‘They will lift Thee on their hands, lest Thou strike Thy foot against a stone.’”
Matthew 4:7  Jesus said to him, “Again it is written: ‘You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.’”
Matthew 4:8  Again the devil took Him to an exceedingly high mountain and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
Matthew 4:9  He said to Him, “I will give Thee all these things if Thou fall down and worship me.”
Matthew 4:10  Then Jesus said to him, “Go away, Satan! For it is written: ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and Him alone shall you serve.’”
Matthew 4:11  Then the devil left Him, and behold, angels came and ministered to Him.
Matthew 4:12  When He heard that John had been handed over, He withdrew to Galilee.
Matthew 4:13  Leaving Nazareth, He came and settled in Capernaum beside the sea, in the territories of Zebulun and Naphtali,
Matthew 4:14  so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled:
Matthew 4:15  “Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations:
Matthew 4:16  the people sitting in darkness saw a great light, and for those sitting in the region and shadow of death a light rose.”
Matthew 4:17  From then on Jesus began to proclaim, “Repent, for the kingdom of the heavens has drawn near.”
Matthew 4:18  As He walked beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw two brothers, Simon called Peter and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
Matthew 4:19  He said to them, “Come after Me, and I will make you fishers of people.”
Matthew 4:20  Immediately they left their nets and followed Him.
Matthew 4:21  Going on from there, He saw two other brothers, James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and He called them.
Matthew 4:22  Immediately they left the boat and their father and followed Him.
Matthew 4:23  He went throughout Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every infirmity among the people.
Matthew 4:24  The report about Him spread throughout Syria, and they brought Him all who were ill, afflicted with various diseases and torments, those oppressed by demons, those suffering seizures, and paralytics; and He healed them.
Matthew 4:25  Great crowds followed Him from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and beyond the Jordan.

Matthew 5
Matthew 5:1  And seeing the crowds, He went up the mountain; and when He had sat down, His disciples came to Him.
Matthew 5:2  And He opened His mouth and taught them, saying:
Matthew 5:3  “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of the heavens.
Matthew 5:4  Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.
Matthew 5:5  Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.
Matthew 5:6  Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled.
Matthew 5:7  Blessed are the merciful, for they shall receive mercy.
Matthew 5:8  Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.
Matthew 5:9  Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God.
Matthew 5:10  Blessed are those who have been persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the kingdom of the heavens.
Matthew 5:11  Blessed are you when they revile you and persecute you and falsely speak every evil thing against you for My sake.
Matthew 5:12  Rejoice and be glad, for great is your reward in the heavens; for thus they persecuted the prophets before you.
Matthew 5:13  You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt becomes tasteless, how shall it be made salty? It is no longer good for anything except to be thrown out and trampled underfoot by people.
Matthew 5:14  You are the light of the world. A city set upon a mountain cannot be hidden.
Matthew 5:15  Nor do people light a lamp and place it beneath the modius, but upon the lampstand; and it shines for everyone in the house.
Matthew 5:16  So let your light shine before people, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in the heavens.
Matthew 5:17  Do not think that I came to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I did not come to abolish, but to fulfil.
Matthew 5:18  For truly I tell you: until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota nor one stroke shall pass from the Law, until all things come to pass.
Matthew 5:19  Whoever therefore loosens one of these least commandments and teaches people to do so shall be called least in the kingdom of the heavens; but whoever does and teaches them shall be called great in the kingdom of the heavens.
Matthew 5:20  For I tell you: unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall by no means enter the kingdom of the heavens.
Matthew 5:21  You have heard that it was said to those of old: ‘You shall not murder’; and ‘whoever murders shall be liable to judgment.’
Matthew 5:22  But I tell you that everyone who is angry with his brother shall be liable to judgment; and whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ shall be liable to the council; and whoever says, ‘Fool,’ shall be liable to the Gehenna of fire.
Matthew 5:23  If therefore you offer your gift upon the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you,
Matthew 5:24  leave your gift there before the altar, and go; first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.
Matthew 5:25  Come to terms with your adversary quickly, while you are with him on the way, lest your adversary hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you be thrown into prison.
Matthew 5:26  Truly I tell you: you shall by no means come out of there until you have paid the last quadrans.
Matthew 5:27  You have heard that it was said: ‘You shall not commit adultery.’
Matthew 5:28  But I tell you that everyone who looks at a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
Matthew 5:29  If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body be thrown into Gehenna.
Matthew 5:30  And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body go into Gehenna.
Matthew 5:31  And it was said: ‘Whoever divorces his wife, let him give her a certificate of divorce.’
Matthew 5:32  But I tell you that everyone who divorces his wife, except on account of sexual immorality, causes her to commit adultery; and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
Matthew 5:33  Again, you have heard that it was said to those of old: ‘You shall not swear falsely, but shall fulfil your oaths to the Lord.’
Matthew 5:34  But I tell you: do not swear at all, neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God,
Matthew 5:35  nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of His feet, nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
Matthew 5:36  Nor shall you swear by your head, for you cannot make one hair white or black.
Matthew 5:37  But let your word be ‘Yes, yes’; ‘No, no.’ Whatever is beyond these is of evil.
Matthew 5:38  You have heard that it was said: ‘An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.’
Matthew 5:39  But I tell you: do not resist the evildoer; but whoever strikes you upon your right cheek, turn the other to him also.
Matthew 5:40  And if anyone would sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak also.
Matthew 5:41  And whoever compels you to go one Roman mile, go with him two.
Matthew 5:42  Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who would borrow from you.
Matthew 5:43  You have heard that it was said: ‘You shall love your neighbour and hate your enemy.’
Matthew 5:44  But I tell you: love your enemies, and pray for those who persecute you,
Matthew 5:45  that you may become sons of your Father who is in the heavens; for He makes His sun rise upon the evil and the good, and sends rain upon the righteous and the unrighteous.
Matthew 5:46  For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same?
Matthew 5:47  And if you greet only your brothers, what are you doing beyond others? Do not even the Gentiles do the same?
Matthew 5:48  You shall therefore be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.

Matthew 6
Matthew 6:1  Take care not to practice your righteousness before people in order to be seen by them; otherwise you have no reward with your Father in the heavens.
Matthew 6:2  So when you give alms, do not sound a trumpet before you as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and streets, so that people may glorify them. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.
Matthew 6:3  But when you give alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
Matthew 6:4  so that your almsgiving may be in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will repay you.
Matthew 6:5  And when you pray, you shall not be like the hypocrites, because they love to pray standing in synagogues and at street corners, so that people may see them. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.
Matthew 6:6  But you, when you pray, enter your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will repay you.
Matthew 6:7  When praying, do not babble like the Gentiles, for they think they will be heard through their many words.
Matthew 6:8  So do not become like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.
Matthew 6:9  Pray, then, in this way: ‘Our Father who art in the heavens, hallowed be Thy name.
Matthew 6:10  Thy kingdom come; Thy will be done, as in heaven, so also upon earth.
Matthew 6:11  Give us this day our daily bread;
Matthew 6:12  and forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors;
Matthew 6:13  and bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.’
Matthew 6:14  For if you forgive people their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
Matthew 6:15  But if you do not forgive people, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
Matthew 6:16  And when you fast, do not become gloomy like the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces so that people may see they are fasting. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.
Matthew 6:17  But you, when fasting, anoint your head and wash your face,
Matthew 6:18  so that your fasting may be seen by your Father who is in secret, rather than by people; and your Father who sees in secret will repay you.
Matthew 6:19  Do not store up treasures for yourselves upon earth, where moth and consumption destroy and where thieves break through and steal.
Matthew 6:20  But store up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where neither moth nor consumption destroys and where thieves neither break through nor steal.
Matthew 6:21  For where your treasure is, there your heart will also be.
Matthew 6:22  The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light.
Matthew 6:23  But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be dark. So if the light within you is darkness, how great is the darkness!
Matthew 6:24  No one can serve as a slave to two masters: for he will either hate the one and love the other, or hold to one and despise the other. You cannot serve as a slave to God and mammon.
Matthew 6:25  Therefore I tell you: do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat or what you will drink, or about your body, what you will wear. Is life not more than food, and the body more than clothing?
Matthew 6:26  Look at the birds of the sky: they do not sow or reap or gather into storehouses, yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth more than they?
Matthew 6:27  Which of you by being anxious can add one cubit to his lifespan?
Matthew 6:28  And why are you anxious about clothing? Observe the lilies of the field, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin.
Matthew 6:29  Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory clothed himself like one of these.
Matthew 6:30  If God so clothes the grass of the field, which exists today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, will He not much more clothe you, people of little faith?
Matthew 6:31  So do not be anxious, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’
Matthew 6:32  For the nations seek all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them all.
Matthew 6:33  But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.
Matthew 6:34  So do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious about itself. Sufficient for the day is its own trouble.

Matthew 7
Matthew 7:1  Do not judge, so that you may not be judged.
Matthew 7:2  For with the judgment you use, you will be judged, and with the measure you use, it will be measured to you.
Matthew 7:3  Why do you see the splinter in your brother’s eye, but do not notice the beam in your own eye?
Matthew 7:4  Or how will you say to your brother, ‘Let me remove the splinter from your eye,’ when behold, the beam is in your own eye?
Matthew 7:5  Hypocrite! First remove the beam from your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the splinter from your brother’s eye.
Matthew 7:6  Do not give what is holy to dogs or throw your pearls before pigs, lest they trample them with their feet and turn and tear you apart.
Matthew 7:7  Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
Matthew 7:8  For everyone who asks receives, the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.
Matthew 7:9  Or who among you, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone?
Matthew 7:10  Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a snake?
Matthew 7:11  If you, then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in the heavens give good things to those who ask Him!
Matthew 7:12  So in everything, whatever you wish people to do for you, you also do likewise for them; for this is the Law and the Prophets.
Matthew 7:13  Enter through the narrow gate, because the gate is wide and the road broad that leads to destruction, and many enter through it.
Matthew 7:14  How narrow is the gate and how constricted the road that leads to life, and few find it!
Matthew 7:15  Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves.
Matthew 7:16  You will recognize them by their fruits. Do people gather grapes from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
Matthew 7:17  In the same way, every good tree bears good fruit, but the rotten tree bears evil fruit.
Matthew 7:18  A good tree cannot bear evil fruit, nor can a rotten tree bear good fruit.
Matthew 7:19  Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into fire.
Matthew 7:20  So then, you will recognize them by their fruits.
Matthew 7:21  Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of the heavens, but the one who does the will of My Father in the heavens.
Matthew 7:22  Many will say to Me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Thy name, cast out demons in Thy name, and do many mighty works in Thy name?’
Matthew 7:23  Then I will declare to them, ‘I never knew you. Depart from Me, you who practice lawlessness.’
Matthew 7:24  Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and puts them into practice will be likened to a prudent man who built his house upon the rock.
Matthew 7:25  The rain came down, the rivers came, and the winds blew and fell upon that house, and it did not fall, for it had been founded upon the rock.
Matthew 7:26  And everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not put them into practice will be likened to a foolish man who built his house upon the sand.
Matthew 7:27  The rain came down, the rivers came, and the winds blew and struck that house, and it fell; and its fall was great.”
Matthew 7:28  When Jesus finished these words, the crowds were astonished at His teaching,
Matthew 7:29  for He taught them as One having authority, and not as their scribes.

Matthew 8
Matthew 8:1  When He came down from the mountain, great crowds followed Him.
Matthew 8:2  And behold, a leper came and bowed before Him, saying, “Lord, if Thou art willing, Thou canst cleanse me.”
Matthew 8:3  He stretched out His hand and touched him, saying, “I am willing; be cleansed.” Immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
Matthew 8:4  Jesus said to him, “See that you tell no one, but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift Moses commanded as a testimony to them.”
Matthew 8:5  When He entered Capernaum, a centurion came to Him, pleading with Him
Matthew 8:6  and saying, “Lord, my servant lies at home paralyzed, terribly tormented.”
Matthew 8:7  He said to him, “I will come and heal him.”
Matthew 8:8  The centurion answered, “Lord, I am not fit for Thee to enter under my roof. Only speak a word, and my servant will be healed.
Matthew 8:9  For I too am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I say to this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and to my slave, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
Matthew 8:10  When Jesus heard this, He marveled and said to those following, “Truly I tell you, with no one in Israel have I found such faith.
Matthew 8:11  I tell you that many will come from east and west and recline with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of the heavens,
Matthew 8:12  but the sons of the kingdom will be cast into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.”
Matthew 8:13  Jesus said to the centurion, “Go; as you have believed, let it happen for you.” And his servant was healed at that hour.
Matthew 8:14  Jesus entered Peter’s house and saw his mother-in-law lying down with a fever.
Matthew 8:15  He touched her hand, and the fever left her. She arose and served Him.
Matthew 8:16  When evening came, they brought Him many who were oppressed by demons. He cast out the spirits with a word and healed all who were ill,
Matthew 8:17  so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled: “He took our weaknesses and carried our diseases.”
Matthew 8:18  Seeing a crowd around Him, Jesus gave orders to depart to the other side.
Matthew 8:19  One scribe came and said to Him, “Teacher, I will follow Thee wherever Thou goest.”
Matthew 8:20  Jesus said to him, “Foxes have dens and the birds of the sky have resting places, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay His head.”
Matthew 8:21  Another of His disciples said to Him, “Lord, first permit me to go and bury my father.”
Matthew 8:22  But Jesus said to him, “Follow Me, and let the dead bury their own dead.”
Matthew 8:23  And when He entered the boat, His disciples followed Him.
Matthew 8:24  And behold, a great tempest arose in the sea, so that the boat was covered by the waves; but He was sleeping.
Matthew 8:25  And they came to Him and awoke Him, saying, “Lord, save; we are perishing.”
Matthew 8:26  And He says to them, “Why are you fearful, you of little faith?” Then He arose and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.
Matthew 8:27  And the men marvelled, saying, “What kind of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey Him?”
Matthew 8:28  When He came to the other side, to the country of the Gadarenes, two men oppressed by demons met Him, coming out of the tombs. They were exceedingly fierce, so that no one could pass by that road.
Matthew 8:29  And behold, they cried out, “What have we to do with Thee, Son of God? Hast Thou come here to torment us before the appointed time?”
Matthew 8:30  Far from them a herd of many pigs was feeding.
Matthew 8:31  The demons pleaded with Him, saying, “If Thou castest us out, send us into the herd of pigs.”
Matthew 8:32  He said to them, “Go.” They came out and went into the pigs. And behold, the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea and died in the waters.
Matthew 8:33  The herdsmen fled, and going into the city they reported everything, including what had happened to the men oppressed by demons.
Matthew 8:34  And behold, the whole city came out to meet Jesus. When they saw Him, they begged Him to depart from their territory.

Matthew 9
Matthew 9:1  He entered a boat, crossed over, and came to His own city.
Matthew 9:2  And behold, they brought Him a paralytic lying on a bed. Seeing their faith, Jesus said to the paralytic, “Take courage, child; your sins are forgiven.”
Matthew 9:3  And behold, some of the scribes said among themselves, “This Man blasphemes.”
Matthew 9:4  Seeing their thoughts, Jesus said, “Why do you think evil things in your hearts?
Matthew 9:5  For which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Rise and walk’?
Matthew 9:6  But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—then He said to the paralytic—“rise, take your bed, and go to your house.”
Matthew 9:7  He rose and went to his house.
Matthew 9:8  When the crowds saw this, they feared and glorified God, who had given such authority to human beings.
Matthew 9:9  As Jesus passed on from there, He saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax station, and He said to him, “Follow Me.” He rose and followed Him.
Matthew 9:10  As He reclined at table in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and reclined with Jesus and His disciples.
Matthew 9:11  When the Pharisees saw this, they said to His disciples, “Why does your Teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
Matthew 9:12  Hearing this, He said, “The strong have no need of a physician, but those who are ill do.
Matthew 9:13  Go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy and not sacrifice.’ For I did not come to call righteous people, but sinners.”
Matthew 9:14  Then John’s disciples came to Him, saying, “Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but Thy disciples do not fast?”
Matthew 9:15  Jesus said to them, “Can the wedding guests mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them? But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast.
Matthew 9:16  No one puts a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, for its patch pulls away from the garment, and a worse tear results.
Matthew 9:17  Nor do people put new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise the skins burst, the wine spills out, and the skins are ruined. Instead, they put new wine into fresh wineskins, and both are preserved.”
Matthew 9:18  While He was saying these things to them, behold, a ruler came and bowed before Him, saying, “My daughter has just died. But come, lay Thy hand upon her, and she will live.”
Matthew 9:19  Jesus rose and followed him, and so did His disciples.
Matthew 9:20  And behold, a woman who had suffered a flow of blood for twelve years came behind Him and touched the fringe of His garment.
Matthew 9:21  For she said within herself, “If I only touch His garment, I will be saved.”
Matthew 9:22  Jesus turned, saw her, and said, “Take courage, daughter; your faith has saved you.” And the woman was saved from that hour.
Matthew 9:23  When Jesus entered the ruler’s house and saw the flute players and the crowd in an uproar,
Matthew 9:24  He said, “Withdraw, for the girl has not died but is sleeping.” And they laughed at Him.
Matthew 9:25  When the crowd had been put outside, He entered and took her hand, and the girl arose.
Matthew 9:26  This report went out into all that land.
Matthew 9:27  As Jesus passed on from there, two blind men followed Him, crying out, “Have mercy on us, Son of David!”
Matthew 9:28  When He entered the house, the blind men came to Him, and Jesus said to them, “Do you believe that I can do this?” They said to Him, “Yes, Lord.”
Matthew 9:29  Then He touched their eyes, saying, “According to your faith, let it happen for you.”
Matthew 9:30  Their eyes were opened. Jesus sternly warned them, saying, “See that no one knows.”
Matthew 9:31  But they went out and spread the report about Him throughout all that land.
Matthew 9:32  As they were going out, behold, people brought Him a mute man oppressed by a demon.
Matthew 9:33  When the demon was cast out, the mute man spoke. The crowds marveled, saying, “Never has anything like this appeared in Israel.”
Matthew 9:34  But the Pharisees said, “By the ruler of the demons He casts out demons.”
Matthew 9:35  And Jesus went about all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues, proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every infirmity.
Matthew 9:36  And seeing the crowds, He was moved with compassion for them, because they were harassed and cast down, as sheep having no shepherd.
Matthew 9:37  Then He says to His disciples, “The harvest indeed is plentiful, but the labourers are few.
Matthew 9:38  Pray therefore to the Lord of the harvest, that He send out labourers into His harvest.”

Matthew 10
Matthew 10:1  He summoned His twelve disciples and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out and to heal every disease and every infirmity.
Matthew 10:2  These are the names of the twelve apostles: first Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;
Matthew 10:3  Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;
Matthew 10:4  Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, who also handed Him over.
Matthew 10:5  Jesus sent these twelve, commanding them, “Do not go along a road of the Gentiles, and do not enter a city of Samaritans.
Matthew 10:6  Go instead to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
Matthew 10:7  As you go, proclaim, ‘The kingdom of the heavens has drawn near.’
Matthew 10:8  Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse lepers, cast out demons. Freely you received; freely give.
Matthew 10:9  Do not acquire gold, silver, or copper for your belts,
Matthew 10:10  nor a bag for the journey, nor two tunics, nor sandals, nor a staff; for the worker is worthy of his food.
Matthew 10:11  Whatever city or village you enter, inquire who in it is worthy, and remain there until you leave.
Matthew 10:12  As you enter the house, greet it.
Matthew 10:13  If the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it; but if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.
Matthew 10:14  Whoever will not receive you or hear your words, as you leave that house or city, shake the dust off your feet.
Matthew 10:15  Truly I tell you, it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that city.
Matthew 10:16  Behold, I send you as sheep in the midst of wolves. So become prudent as snakes and innocent as doves.
Matthew 10:17  Beware of people, for they will hand you over to councils and flog you in their synagogues.
Matthew 10:18  You will also be brought before governors and kings because of Me, as a testimony to them and to the nations.
Matthew 10:19  When they hand you over, do not be anxious about how or what you should speak, for what you should speak will be given to you at that hour.
Matthew 10:20  For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you.
Matthew 10:21  Brother will hand brother over to death, and a father his child; children will rise against parents and have them put to death.
Matthew 10:22  You will be hated by all because of My name, but the one who endures to the end will be saved.
Matthew 10:23  When they persecute you in this city, flee to the other. For truly I tell you, you will certainly not finish going through the cities of Israel until the Son of Man comes.
Matthew 10:24  A disciple is not above the teacher, nor a slave above his master.
Matthew 10:25  It is enough for the disciple to become like his teacher, and the slave like his master. If they called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more his household members!
Matthew 10:26  So do not fear them. For nothing is covered that will not be revealed, or hidden that will not become known.
Matthew 10:27  What I tell you in the darkness, say in the light; and what you hear in the ear, proclaim upon the housetops.
Matthew 10:28  Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul; rather fear Him who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
Matthew 10:29  Are not two sparrows sold for an assarion? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground apart from your Father.
Matthew 10:30  Even the hairs of your head are all numbered.
Matthew 10:31  So do not fear; you are worth more than many sparrows.
Matthew 10:32  Therefore everyone who acknowledges Me before people, I too will acknowledge before My Father in the heavens.
Matthew 10:33  But whoever denies Me before people, I too will deny before My Father in the heavens.
Matthew 10:34  Do not suppose that I came to bring peace upon the earth. I did not come to bring peace, but a sword.
Matthew 10:35  For I came to divide a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law,
Matthew 10:36  and a person’s enemies will be the members of his own household.
Matthew 10:37  Whoever loves father or mother more than Me is not worthy of Me; and whoever loves son or daughter more than Me is not worthy of Me.
Matthew 10:38  Whoever does not take his cross and follow after Me is not worthy of Me.
Matthew 10:39  Whoever finds his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life because of Me will find it.
Matthew 10:40  Whoever receives you receives Me, and whoever receives Me receives the One who sent Me.
Matthew 10:41  Whoever receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward, and whoever receives a righteous person in the name of a righteous person will receive a righteous person’s reward.
Matthew 10:42  And whoever gives one of these little ones even a cup of cold water in the name of a disciple, truly I tell you, will certainly not lose his reward.”

Matthew 11
Matthew 11:1  When Jesus finished directing His twelve disciples, He moved on from there to teach and proclaim in their cities.
Matthew 11:2  John, hearing in prison about the works of the Christ, sent through his disciples
Matthew 11:3  and said to Him, “Art Thou the One who is coming, or should we expect another?”
Matthew 11:4  Jesus answered them, “Go and report to John what you hear and see:
Matthew 11:5  the blind receive sight and the lame walk, lepers are cleansed and the deaf hear, the dead are raised and the poor have good news proclaimed to them.
Matthew 11:6  And blessed is whoever does not stumble because of Me.”
Matthew 11:7  As they went away, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to behold? A reed shaken by the wind?
Matthew 11:8  But what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothing? Behold, those wearing soft clothing are in kings’ houses.
Matthew 11:9  But why did you go out? To see a prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
Matthew 11:10  This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I send My messenger before Thy face, who will prepare Thy way before Thee.’
Matthew 11:11  Truly I tell you, among those born of women none greater than John the Baptist has arisen; yet the least in the kingdom of the heavens is greater than he.
Matthew 11:12  From the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of the heavens suffers violence, and violent men seize it.
Matthew 11:13  For all the Prophets and the Law prophesied until John.
Matthew 11:14  And if you are willing to receive it, he is Elijah who is to come.
Matthew 11:15  Let the one who has ears hear.
Matthew 11:16  To what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplaces who call to the others,
Matthew 11:17  ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a lament, and you did not beat your breasts.’
Matthew 11:18  For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, ‘He has a demon.’
Matthew 11:19  The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Behold, a gluttonous man and a wine drinker, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ Yet wisdom was vindicated by her works.”
Matthew 11:20  Then He began to reproach the cities in which most of His mighty works had occurred, because they did not repent:
Matthew 11:21  “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works that occurred in you had occurred in Tyre and Sidon, they would long ago have repented in sackcloth and ashes.
Matthew 11:22  Nevertheless I tell you, it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.
Matthew 11:23  And you, Capernaum, will you be exalted to heaven? You will descend to Hades! For if the mighty works that occurred in you had occurred in Sodom, it would have remained until today.
Matthew 11:24  Nevertheless I tell you, it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom on the day of judgment than for you.”
Matthew 11:25  At that time Jesus answered, “I acknowledge Thee, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because Thou didst hide these things from the wise and understanding and reveal them to infants.
Matthew 11:26  Yes, Father, because this was pleasing before Thee.
Matthew 11:27  All things have been handed over to Me by My Father. No one knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone know the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son wishes to reveal Him.
Matthew 11:28  Come to Me, all you who labour and are burdened, and I will give you rest.
Matthew 11:29  Take My yoke upon you, and learn from Me; for I am meek and lowly in heart, and you shall find rest for your souls.
Matthew 11:30  For My yoke is easy, and My burden is light.”

Matthew 12
Matthew 12:1  At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the Sabbath; and His disciples grew hungry, and began to pluck heads of grain and eat.
Matthew 12:2  And the Pharisees, seeing it, said to Him, “Behold, Thy disciples do what is not lawful on the Sabbath.”
Matthew 12:3  He said to them, “Have you not read what David did when he and those with him became hungry:
Matthew 12:4  how he entered the house of God, and they ate the bread of the Presence, which it was not lawful for him or those with him to eat, but only for the priests?
Matthew 12:5  Or have you not read in the Law that on Sabbaths the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath and are guiltless?
Matthew 12:6  But I tell you that something greater than the temple is here.
Matthew 12:7  If you had known what ‘I desire mercy and not sacrifice’ means, you would not have condemned the guiltless.
Matthew 12:8  For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
Matthew 12:9  Moving on from there, He entered their synagogue.
Matthew 12:10  And behold, a man had a withered hand. They asked Him, “Is it lawful to heal on Sabbaths?” so that they might accuse Him.
Matthew 12:11  He said to them, “Who among you, if he has one sheep and it falls into a pit on a Sabbath, will not grasp it and lift it out?
Matthew 12:12  How much more valuable, then, is a human being than a sheep! So it is lawful to do good on Sabbaths.”
Matthew 12:13  Then He said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and it was restored, healthy like the other.
Matthew 12:14  The Pharisees went out and took counsel against Him, how they might destroy Him.
Matthew 12:15  But Jesus, knowing this, withdrew from there. Great crowds followed Him, and He healed them all.
Matthew 12:16  He sternly warned them not to make Him known,
Matthew 12:17  so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled:
Matthew 12:18  “Behold, My Servant whom I chose, My beloved in whom My soul was well pleased. I will put My Spirit upon Him, and He will proclaim justice to the nations.
Matthew 12:19  He will not quarrel or cry out, nor will anyone hear His voice in the streets.
Matthew 12:20  He will not break a bruised reed or extinguish a smoldering wick, until He brings justice forth to victory.
Matthew 12:21  And nations will hope in His name.”
Matthew 12:22  Then a man oppressed by a demon, blind and mute, was brought to Him. He healed him, so that the mute man spoke and saw.
Matthew 12:23  All the crowds were amazed and said, “Could this be the Son of David?”
Matthew 12:24  But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, “This Man casts out demons only by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons.”
Matthew 12:25  Knowing their thoughts, He said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.
Matthew 12:26  If Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then will his kingdom stand?
Matthew 12:27  And if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
Matthew 12:28  But if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
Matthew 12:29  Or how can someone enter the strong man’s house and seize his belongings unless he first binds the strong man? Then he will plunder his house.
Matthew 12:30  Whoever is not with Me is against Me, and whoever does not gather with Me scatters.
Matthew 12:31  Therefore I tell you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven people, but blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.
Matthew 12:32  Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the coming one.
Matthew 12:33  Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree rotten and its fruit rotten; for the tree is known by the fruit.
Matthew 12:34  Brood of vipers! How can you speak good things when you are evil? For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.
Matthew 12:35  The good person brings forth good things from the good treasure, and the evil person brings forth evil things from the evil treasure.
Matthew 12:36  But I tell you that people will give account on the day of judgment for every idle word they speak.
Matthew 12:37  For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”
Matthew 12:38  Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered Him, saying, “Teacher, we wish to see a sign from Thee.”
Matthew 12:39  He answered them, “An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, but no sign will be given it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.
Matthew 12:40  For just as Jonah was in the sea creature’s belly three days and three nights, so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.
Matthew 12:41  Men of Nineveh will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at Jonah’s proclamation; and behold, something greater than Jonah is here.
Matthew 12:42  The queen of the south will be raised at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon’s wisdom; and behold, something greater than Solomon is here.
Matthew 12:43  When the unclean spirit leaves a person, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, and finds none.
Matthew 12:44  Then it says, ‘I will return to my house from which I came.’ When it comes, it finds it vacant, swept, and put in order.
Matthew 12:45  Then it goes and takes with itself seven other spirits more evil than itself; they enter and dwell there, and that person’s last condition becomes worse than the first. So it will also be with this evil generation.”
Matthew 12:46  While He was still speaking to the crowds, behold, His mother and brothers stood outside, seeking to speak with Him.
Matthew 12:47  Someone said to Him, “Behold, Thy mother and Thy brothers stand outside, seeking to speak with Thee.”
Matthew 12:48  He answered the one speaking to Him, “Who is My mother, and who are My brothers?”
Matthew 12:49  Stretching out His hand toward His disciples, He said, “Behold, My mother and My brothers!
Matthew 12:50  For whoever does the will of My Father in the heavens is My brother and sister and mother.”

Matthew 13
Matthew 13:1  On that day Jesus went out of the house and sat beside the sea.
Matthew 13:2  Great crowds gathered to Him, so that He entered a boat and sat down, while all the crowd stood on the shore.
Matthew 13:3  He spoke many things to them in parables, saying, “Behold, the sower went out to sow.
Matthew 13:4  As he sowed, some seeds fell beside the road, and the birds came and devoured them.
Matthew 13:5  Others fell on rocky places, where they did not have much soil, and immediately sprang up because they had no depth of soil.
Matthew 13:6  But when the sun rose, they were scorched, and because they had no root they withered.
Matthew 13:7  Others fell among thorns; the thorns grew up and choked them.
Matthew 13:8  Others fell on the good soil and yielded fruit: some a hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold.
Matthew 13:9  Let the one who has ears hear.”
Matthew 13:10  The disciples came and said to Him, “Why dost Thou speak to them in parables?”
Matthew 13:11  He answered them, “To you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of the heavens, but to them it has not been given.
Matthew 13:12  For whoever has, to him more will be given, and he will have abundance; but whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken from him.
Matthew 13:13  Therefore I speak to them in parables, because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear or understand.
Matthew 13:14  In them is fulfilled Isaiah’s prophecy, which says: ‘You will hear and hear but certainly not understand; you will look and look but certainly not see.
Matthew 13:15  For the heart of this people has grown dull, and with their ears they heard but faintly, and their eyes they shut, lest they see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and turn, and I will heal them.’
Matthew 13:16  But blessed are your eyes, because they see, and your ears, because they hear.
Matthew 13:17  For truly I tell you, many prophets and righteous people desired to see what you see and did not see it, and to hear what you hear and did not hear it.
Matthew 13:18  You, then, hear the parable of the sower.
Matthew 13:19  When anyone hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand, the evil one comes and snatches what was sown in his heart. This is the one sown beside the road.
Matthew 13:20  The one sown on rocky places is the one who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy,
Matthew 13:21  yet has no root in himself, but lasts only a short time. When affliction or persecution arises because of the word, he immediately stumbles.
Matthew 13:22  The one sown among the thorns is the one who hears the word, but the anxiety of this age and the deceit of riches choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
Matthew 13:23  The one sown upon the good soil is the one who hears the word and understands; he indeed bears fruit and produces, some a hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold.”
Matthew 13:24  He set another parable before them, saying, “The kingdom of the heavens was likened to a man who sowed good seed in his field.
Matthew 13:25  While people slept, his enemy came and sowed darnel among the wheat and went away.
Matthew 13:26  When the crop sprouted and bore fruit, then the darnel appeared also.
Matthew 13:27  The householder’s slaves came and said to him, ‘Master, did you not sow good seed in your field? From where, then, does it have darnel?’
Matthew 13:28  He said to them, ‘An enemy did this.’ The slaves said to him, ‘Do you want us, then, to go and gather it?’
Matthew 13:29  He said, ‘No, lest while gathering the darnel you uproot the wheat with it.
Matthew 13:30  Let both grow together until the harvest. At harvest time I will tell the reapers: Gather the darnel first and bind it into bundles to burn it, but gather the wheat into my storehouse.’”
Matthew 13:31  He set another parable before them, saying, “The kingdom of the heavens is like a mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his field.
Matthew 13:32  It is smaller than all the seeds, but when it grows it is greater than the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and rest in its branches.”
Matthew 13:33  He spoke another parable to them: “The kingdom of the heavens is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three sata of flour until the whole was leavened.”
Matthew 13:34  Jesus spoke all these things to the crowds in parables, and He spoke nothing to them without a parable,
Matthew 13:35  so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled: “I will open My mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world.”
Matthew 13:36  Then He left the crowds and entered the house. His disciples came to Him, saying, “Explain to us the parable of the darnel in the field.”
Matthew 13:37  He answered, “The One sowing the good seed is the Son of Man.
Matthew 13:38  The field is the world; the good seed are the sons of the kingdom; the darnel are the sons of the evil one;
Matthew 13:39  the enemy who sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the consummation of the age; and the reapers are angels.
Matthew 13:40  Just as the darnel is gathered and burned with fire, so it will be at the consummation of the age.
Matthew 13:41  The Son of Man will send His angels, and they will gather from His kingdom all causes of stumbling and those who practice lawlessness.
Matthew 13:42  They will cast them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.
Matthew 13:43  Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Let the one who has ears hear.
Matthew 13:44  The kingdom of the heavens is like treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and hid. In his joy he goes and sells everything he has and buys that field.
Matthew 13:45  Again, the kingdom of the heavens is like a merchant seeking fine pearls.
Matthew 13:46  Finding one pearl of great value, he went and sold everything he had and bought it.
Matthew 13:47  Again, the kingdom of the heavens is like a dragnet cast into the sea and gathering fish of every kind.
Matthew 13:48  When it was full, they drew it onto the shore, sat down, and gathered the good into containers, but threw the rotten away.
Matthew 13:49  So it will be at the consummation of the age: the angels will go out and separate the evil from the midst of the righteous
Matthew 13:50  and cast them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.
Matthew 13:51  Have you understood all these things?” They said to Him, “Yes.”
Matthew 13:52  He said to them, “Therefore every scribe made a disciple for the kingdom of the heavens is like a householder who brings out of his treasure things new and old.”
Matthew 13:53  When Jesus finished these parables, He departed from there.
Matthew 13:54  Coming to His hometown, He taught them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished and said, “Where did this Man get this wisdom and these mighty works?
Matthew 13:55  Is He not the craftsman’s son? Is His mother not called Mary, and His brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas?
Matthew 13:56  And are not all His sisters with us? Where, then, did this Man get all these things?”
Matthew 13:57  They stumbled because of Him. But Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown and his own house.”
Matthew 13:58  He did not do many mighty works there because of their unbelief.

Matthew 14
Matthew 14:1  At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the report about Jesus
Matthew 14:2  and said to his attendants, “This is John the Baptist. He has been raised from the dead, and therefore the powers are at work in him.”
Matthew 14:3  For Herod had seized John, bound him, and put him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip.
Matthew 14:4  For John kept saying to him, “It is not lawful for you to have her.”
Matthew 14:5  Although he wanted to kill him, he feared the crowd, because they regarded him as a prophet.
Matthew 14:6  When Herod’s birthday celebration came, Herodias’s daughter danced in their midst and pleased Herod.
Matthew 14:7  Therefore he promised with an oath to give her whatever she asked.
Matthew 14:8  Prompted by her mother, she said, “Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist.”
Matthew 14:9  Although the king was grieved, because of his oaths and those reclining with him, he ordered it to be given.
Matthew 14:10  He sent and had John beheaded in the prison.
Matthew 14:11  His head was brought on a platter and given to the girl, and she brought it to her mother.
Matthew 14:12  His disciples came, took the corpse, and buried him; then they went and reported to Jesus.
Matthew 14:13  When Jesus heard this, He withdrew from there by boat to a deserted place privately. Hearing of it, the crowds followed Him on foot from the cities.
Matthew 14:14  Coming out, He saw a great crowd, was moved with compassion for them, and healed their sick.
Matthew 14:15  When evening came, the disciples approached Him, saying, “The place is deserted, and the hour has already passed. Dismiss the crowds so that they may go to the villages and buy food for themselves.”
Matthew 14:16  But Jesus said to them, “They have no need to go away. You give them something to eat.”
Matthew 14:17  They said to Him, “We have here only five loaves and two fish.”
Matthew 14:18  He said, “Bring them here to Me.”
Matthew 14:19  He ordered the crowds to recline on the grass. Taking the five loaves and the two fish, He looked up to heaven, blessed, broke the loaves, and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples to the crowds.
Matthew 14:20  They all ate and were filled, and they took up the surplus fragments: twelve baskets full.
Matthew 14:21  Those eating were about five thousand men, besides women and children.
Matthew 14:22  Immediately He compelled the disciples to enter a boat and go ahead of Him to the other side, while He dismissed the crowds.
Matthew 14:23  After dismissing the crowds, He went up the mountain privately to pray. When evening came, He was there alone.
Matthew 14:24  The boat was already many stadia from land, battered by the waves, for the wind was against them.
Matthew 14:25  In the fourth watch of the night He came toward them, walking upon the sea.
Matthew 14:26  When the disciples saw Him walking upon the sea, they were troubled and said, “It is an apparition!” They cried out in fear.
Matthew 14:27  Immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying, “Take courage; it is I. Do not fear.”
Matthew 14:28  Peter answered Him, “Lord, if it is Thou, command me to come to Thee upon the waters.”
Matthew 14:29  He said, “Come.” Peter got down from the boat, walked upon the waters, and came toward Jesus.
Matthew 14:30  But seeing the strong wind, he became afraid; beginning to sink, he cried out, “Lord, save me!”
Matthew 14:31  Immediately Jesus stretched out His hand, grasped him, and said to him, “You of little faith, why did you doubt?”
Matthew 14:32  When they climbed into the boat, the wind ceased.
Matthew 14:33  Those in the boat worshiped Him, saying, “Truly Thou art God’s Son.”
Matthew 14:34  Having crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret.
Matthew 14:35  The men of that place recognized Him and sent into all the surrounding region. They brought Him all who were ill
Matthew 14:36  and begged Him that they might only touch the fringe of His garment. As many as touched it were made well.

Matthew 15
Matthew 15:1  Then Pharisees and scribes from Jerusalem came to Jesus, saying,
Matthew 15:2  “Why do Thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread.”
Matthew 15:3  He answered them, “Why do you also transgress God’s commandment because of your tradition?
Matthew 15:4  For God said, ‘Honor father and mother,’ and ‘Whoever reviles father or mother must surely die.’
Matthew 15:5  But you say, ‘Whoever tells his father or mother, “Whatever benefit you might receive from me is a gift,”
Matthew 15:6  will certainly not honor his father.’ You have thus nullified the word of God because of your tradition.
Matthew 15:7  Hypocrites! Isaiah prophesied well about you, saying,
Matthew 15:8  ‘This people honors Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me.
Matthew 15:9  In vain do they worship Me, teaching human commands for doctrine.’”
Matthew 15:10  He summoned the crowd and said to them, “Hear and understand:
Matthew 15:11  what enters the mouth does not defile a person, but what comes out of the mouth—this defiles a person.”
Matthew 15:12  Then the disciples came and said to Him, “Dost Thou know that the Pharisees stumbled when they heard this saying?”
Matthew 15:13  He answered, “Every plant that My heavenly Father did not plant will be uprooted.
Matthew 15:14  Leave them; they are blind guides of the blind. If a blind person guides a blind person, both will fall into a pit.”
Matthew 15:15  Peter answered Him, “Explain this parable to us.”
Matthew 15:16  He said, “Are you also still without understanding?
Matthew 15:17  Do you not understand that everything entering the mouth goes into the stomach and is expelled into the latrine?
Matthew 15:18  But the things coming out of the mouth come from the heart, and those defile a person.
Matthew 15:19  For out of the heart come evil reasonings, murders, adulteries, sexual immoralities, thefts, false testimonies, and blasphemies.
Matthew 15:20  These are the things that defile a person, but eating with unwashed hands does not defile a person.”
Matthew 15:21  Jesus went out from there and withdrew to the regions of Tyre and Sidon.
Matthew 15:22  And behold, a Canaanite woman from those territories came out and cried, “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter is terribly oppressed by a demon.”
Matthew 15:23  But He did not answer her a word. His disciples came and asked Him, “Dismiss her, because she is crying out behind us.”
Matthew 15:24  He answered, “I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”
Matthew 15:25  She came and bowed before Him, saying, “Lord, help me.”
Matthew 15:26  He answered, “It is not good to take the children’s bread and throw it to the little dogs.”
Matthew 15:27  She said, “Yes, Lord, for even the little dogs eat from the crumbs falling from their masters’ table.”
Matthew 15:28  Then Jesus answered her, “Woman, great is your faith! Let it happen for you as you wish.” Her daughter was healed from that hour.
Matthew 15:29  Moving on from there, Jesus came beside the Sea of Galilee. He went up the mountain and sat there.
Matthew 15:30  Great crowds came to Him, bringing with them lame, blind, maimed, mute, and many others. They laid them at His feet, and He healed them,
Matthew 15:31  so that the crowd marveled when they saw mute people speaking, maimed people healthy, lame people walking, and blind people seeing. They glorified the God of Israel.
Matthew 15:32  Jesus summoned His disciples and said, “I am moved with compassion for the crowd, because they have already stayed with Me three days and have nothing to eat. I am unwilling to dismiss them fasting, lest they faint on the road.”
Matthew 15:33  The disciples said to Him, “Where can we get so many loaves in a deserted place, enough to fill so great a crowd?”
Matthew 15:34  Jesus said to them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven, and a few small fish.”
Matthew 15:35  He instructed the crowd to recline on the ground,
Matthew 15:36  took the seven loaves and the fish, gave thanks, broke them, and kept giving them to the disciples, and the disciples to the crowds.
Matthew 15:37  They all ate and were filled, and they took up the surplus fragments: seven large baskets full.
Matthew 15:38  Those eating were four thousand men, besides women and children.
Matthew 15:39  After dismissing the crowds, He entered the boat and came to the territory of Magadan.

Matthew 16
Matthew 16:1  The Pharisees and Sadducees came and, testing Him, asked Him to show them a sign from heaven.
Matthew 16:2  He answered them, “When evening comes, you say, ‘Fair weather, for the sky is red.’
Matthew 16:3  And in the morning, ‘Today a storm, for the sky is red and gloomy.’ You know how to distinguish the face of the sky, but can you not distinguish the signs of the times?
Matthew 16:4  An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, but no sign will be given it except the sign of Jonah.” He left them and went away.
Matthew 16:5  When the disciples came to the other side, they had forgotten to take bread.
Matthew 16:6  Jesus said to them, “Look out and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
Matthew 16:7  They reasoned among themselves, saying, “We did not take bread.”
Matthew 16:8  Knowing this, Jesus said, “Why do you reason among yourselves, people of little faith, because you have no bread?
Matthew 16:9  Do you not yet understand or remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many baskets you took up?
Matthew 16:10  Or the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many large baskets you took up?
Matthew 16:11  How do you not understand that I did not speak to you about bread? But beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
Matthew 16:12  Then they understood that He did not tell them to beware of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
Matthew 16:13  When Jesus came into the regions of Caesarea Philippi, He asked His disciples, “Who do people say the Son of Man is?”
Matthew 16:14  They said, “Some John the Baptist; others Elijah; still others Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”
Matthew 16:15  He said to them, “But you, who do you say I am?”
Matthew 16:16  Simon Peter answered, “Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
Matthew 16:17  Jesus answered him, “Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, because flesh and blood did not reveal this to you, but My Father in the heavens.
Matthew 16:18  And I tell you that you are Peter, and upon this rock I will build My Church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.
Matthew 16:19  I will give you the keys of the kingdom of the heavens. Whatever you bind upon earth will have been bound in the heavens, and whatever you loose upon earth will have been loosed in the heavens.”
Matthew 16:20  Then He instructed the disciples to tell no one that He was the Christ.
Matthew 16:21  From then on Jesus began to show His disciples that He must go to Jerusalem, suffer many things from the elders, chief priests, and scribes, be killed, and on the third day be raised.
Matthew 16:22  Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him, saying, “May mercy be Thine, Lord! This shall certainly never happen to Thee.”
Matthew 16:23  But He turned and said to Peter, “Get behind Me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to Me, because you do not set your mind on the things of God, but on the things of human beings.”
Matthew 16:24  Then Jesus said to His disciples, “If anyone wishes to come after Me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow Me.
Matthew 16:25  For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life because of Me will find it.
Matthew 16:26  For what will a person gain if he gains the whole world but forfeits his life? Or what will a person give in exchange for his life?
Matthew 16:27  For the Son of Man is to come in the glory of His Father with His angels, and then He will repay each person according to his conduct.
Matthew 16:28  Truly I tell you that some standing here will certainly not taste death until they see the Son of Man coming in His kingdom.”

Matthew 17
Matthew 17:1  After six days Jesus took Peter, James, and John his brother, and led them up a high mountain privately.
Matthew 17:2  He was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and His garments became white like the light.
Matthew 17:3  And behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to them, conversing with Him.
Matthew 17:4  Peter answered Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here. If Thou wishest, I will make three tents here: one for Thee, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
Matthew 17:5  While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them. And behold, a voice from the cloud said, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Hear Him.”
Matthew 17:6  When the disciples heard, they fell on their faces and were exceedingly afraid.
Matthew 17:7  Jesus came, touched them, and said, “Rise, and do not fear.”
Matthew 17:8  Lifting their eyes, they saw no one except Jesus Himself alone.
Matthew 17:9  As they came down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, “Tell the vision to no one until the Son of Man is raised from the dead.”
Matthew 17:10  The disciples asked Him, “Why, then, do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
Matthew 17:11  He answered, “Elijah indeed comes and will restore all things.
Matthew 17:12  But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wished. In the same way the Son of Man is also to suffer at their hands.”
Matthew 17:13  Then the disciples understood that He spoke to them about John the Baptist.
Matthew 17:14  When they came to the crowd, a man approached Him, kneeling before Him
Matthew 17:15  and saying, “Lord, have mercy on my son, because he suffers seizures and is badly afflicted; for he often falls into fire and often into water.
Matthew 17:16  I brought him to Thy disciples, but they could not heal him.”
Matthew 17:17  Jesus answered, “O faithless and perverted generation, how long will I be with you? How long will I bear with you? Bring him here to Me.”
Matthew 17:18  Jesus rebuked him, and the demon came out of him; the boy was healed from that hour.
Matthew 17:19  Then the disciples came to Jesus privately and said, “Why could we not cast it out?”
Matthew 17:20  He said to them, “Because of your little faith. For truly I tell you, if you have faith like a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you.”
Matthew 17:22  While they gathered in Galilee, Jesus said to them, “The Son of Man is about to be handed over into human hands.
Matthew 17:23  They will kill Him, and on the third day He will be raised.” They were exceedingly grieved.
Matthew 17:24  And when they came to Capernaum, those who collected the didrachmas came to Peter and said, “Does not your Teacher pay the didrachmas?”
Matthew 17:25  He says, “Yes.” And when he entered the house, Jesus spoke first to him, saying, “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth receive toll or tribute: from their sons, or from strangers?”
Matthew 17:26  And when he said, “From strangers,” Jesus said to him, “Then the sons are free.
Matthew 17:27  But lest we cause them to stumble, go to the sea and cast a hook, and take the first fish that comes up; and when you open its mouth, you will find a stater. Take it and give it to them for Me and you.”

Matthew 18
Matthew 18:1  At that hour the disciples came to Jesus, saying, “Who, then, is greatest in the kingdom of the heavens?”
Matthew 18:2  He called a child and stood the child in their midst,
Matthew 18:3  and said, “Truly I tell you, unless you turn and become like children, you will certainly not enter the kingdom of the heavens.
Matthew 18:4  Therefore whoever humbles himself like this child is greatest in the kingdom of the heavens.
Matthew 18:5  And whoever receives one such child in My name receives Me.
Matthew 18:6  But whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it is better for him that a donkey-driven millstone be hung around his neck and he be sunk in the open sea.
Matthew 18:7  Woe to the world because of stumbling blocks! For stumbling blocks must come, but woe to the person through whom the stumbling block comes!
Matthew 18:8  If your hand or foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter life maimed or lame than, having two hands or two feet, to be cast into the eternal fire.
Matthew 18:9  And if your eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter life with one eye than, having two eyes, to be cast into the Gehenna of fire.
Matthew 18:10  See that you do not despise one of these little ones, for I tell you that their angels in the heavens continually see the face of My Father in the heavens.
Matthew 18:12  What do you think? If someone has a hundred sheep and one of them strays, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the mountains and go seeking the one that strays?
Matthew 18:13  If he succeeds in finding it, truly I tell you that he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that have not strayed.
Matthew 18:14  In the same way, it is not the will of your Father in the heavens that one of these little ones perish.
Matthew 18:15  If your brother sins against you, go and reprove him between you and him alone. If he hears you, you have gained your brother.
Matthew 18:16  But if he does not hear, take one or two more with you, so that every matter may be established upon the mouth of two or three witnesses.
Matthew 18:17  If he refuses to hear them, tell the Church. And if he refuses to hear even the Church, let him be to you like the Gentile and the tax collector.
Matthew 18:18  Truly I tell you, whatever you bind upon earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever you loose upon earth will have been loosed in heaven.
Matthew 18:19  Again, truly I tell you that if two of you agree upon earth concerning any matter they ask, it will be done for them by My Father in the heavens.
Matthew 18:20  For where two or three are gathered into My name, there I am in their midst.”
Matthew 18:21  Then Peter came and said to Him, “Lord, how often will my brother sin against me and I forgive him? Up to seven times?”
Matthew 18:22  Jesus says to him, “I tell you, not up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven.
Matthew 18:23  Therefore the kingdom of the heavens was likened to a king who wished to settle accounts with his slaves.
Matthew 18:24  And when he began to settle them, one was brought to him who owed ten thousand talents.
Matthew 18:25  And since he did not have the means to repay, his master commanded that he be sold, with his wife and children and all that he had, and that payment be made.
Matthew 18:26  The slave therefore fell down and did him homage, saying, ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you everything.’
Matthew 18:27  And the master of that slave, moved with compassion, released him and forgave him the loan.
Matthew 18:28  But that slave went out and found one of his fellow slaves who owed him a hundred denarii. He seized him and began choking him, saying, ‘Repay whatever you owe.’
Matthew 18:29  So his fellow slave fell down and pleaded with him, saying, ‘Be patient with me, and I will repay you.’
Matthew 18:30  But he was unwilling. Instead, he went and threw him into prison until he repaid what was owed.
Matthew 18:31  When his fellow slaves saw what had happened, they were exceedingly grieved. They came and explained to their master everything that had happened.
Matthew 18:32  Then his master summoned him and said, ‘Evil slave! I forgave you all that debt because you pleaded with me.
Matthew 18:33  Should you not also have had mercy on your fellow slave, as I had mercy on you?’
Matthew 18:34  His master became angry and handed him over to the torturers until he repaid everything owed.
Matthew 18:35  So also My heavenly Father will do to you, unless each of you forgives his brother from your hearts.”

Matthew 19
Matthew 19:1  When Jesus finished these words, He departed from Galilee and came into the territories of Judea beyond the Jordan.
Matthew 19:2  Great crowds followed Him, and He healed them there.
Matthew 19:3  Pharisees came to Him, testing Him and saying, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any cause?”
Matthew 19:4  He answered, “Have you not read that the Creator from the beginning made them male and female,
Matthew 19:5  and said, ‘For this reason a man shall leave father and mother and cleave to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh’?
Matthew 19:6  So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has yoked together, let no human being separate.”
Matthew 19:7  They said to Him, “Why then did Moses command giving a certificate of divorce and divorcing her?”
Matthew 19:8  He said to them, “Because of your hardness of heart Moses permitted you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so.
Matthew 19:9  I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except on account of sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery.”
Matthew 19:10  His disciples said to Him, “If this is the situation of the man with the wife, it is better not to marry.”
Matthew 19:11  He said to them, “Not everyone can receive this saying, but only those to whom it has been given.
Matthew 19:12  For there are eunuchs who were born so from their mother’s womb, there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by human beings, and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs because of the kingdom of the heavens. Let the one able to receive it receive it.”
Matthew 19:13  Then children were brought to Him so that He might lay His hands upon them and pray. But the disciples rebuked them.
Matthew 19:14  Jesus said, “Let the children come, and do not hinder them from coming to Me, for the kingdom of the heavens belongs to such as these.”
Matthew 19:15  After laying His hands upon them, He went on from there.
Matthew 19:16  And behold, someone came and said to Him, “Teacher, what good thing shall I do to have eternal life?”
Matthew 19:17  He said to him, “Why do you ask Me about what is good? One is good. But if you wish to enter life, keep the commandments.”
Matthew 19:18  He said to Him, “Which ones?” Jesus said, “‘You shall not murder; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal; you shall not bear false witness;
Matthew 19:19  honor father and mother’; and ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’”
Matthew 19:20  The young man said to Him, “I have kept all these. What do I still lack?”
Matthew 19:21  Jesus said to him, “If you wish to be perfect, go, sell your belongings, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in the heavens. Then come, follow Me.”
Matthew 19:22  When the young man heard the saying, he went away grieved, for he had many properties.
Matthew 19:23  Jesus said to His disciples, “Truly I tell you that a rich person will enter the kingdom of the heavens with difficulty.
Matthew 19:24  Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to enter through the hole of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”
