Matthew 19:25  When the disciples heard this, they were exceedingly astonished, saying, “Who then can be saved?”
Matthew 19:26  Looking at them, Jesus said, “With human beings this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”
Matthew 19:27  Then Peter answered Him, “Behold, we have left everything and followed Thee. What then will there be for us?”
Matthew 19:28  Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you that you who have followed Me, in the regeneration, when the Son of Man sits upon the throne of His glory, shall also sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
Matthew 19:29  Everyone who has left houses, brothers, sisters, father, mother, children, or fields because of My name will receive a hundredfold and inherit eternal life.
Matthew 19:30  But many who are first will be last, and the last first.

Matthew 20
Matthew 20:1  For the kingdom of the heavens is like a householder who went out at dawn to hire labourers for his vineyard.
Matthew 20:2  And having agreed with the labourers for a denarius for the day, he sent them into his vineyard.
Matthew 20:3  And going out about the third hour, he saw others standing idle in the marketplace;
Matthew 20:4  and to them he said, ‘You also go into the vineyard, and whatever is just I will give you.’
Matthew 20:5  They went. Again he went out about the sixth and ninth hours and did the same.
Matthew 20:6  About the eleventh hour he went out and found others standing, and said to them, ‘Why have you stood here idle the whole day?’
Matthew 20:7  They said to him, ‘Because no one hired us.’ He said to them, ‘You also go into the vineyard.’
Matthew 20:8  When evening came, the master of the vineyard said to his steward, ‘Call the workers and pay them the wage, beginning with the last up to the first.’
Matthew 20:9  Those hired about the eleventh hour came and received a denarius each.
Matthew 20:10  When the first came, they supposed they would receive more, but they too received a denarius each.
Matthew 20:11  On receiving it, they grumbled against the householder,
Matthew 20:12  saying, ‘These last worked one hour, and you made them equal to us who bore the day’s burden and scorching heat.’
Matthew 20:13  He answered one of them, ‘Friend, I am not wronging you. Did you not agree with me for a denarius?
Matthew 20:14  Take what is yours and go. I wish to give to this last one the same as to you.
Matthew 20:15  Am I not permitted to do what I wish with what is mine? Or is your eye evil because I am good?’
Matthew 20:16  So the last will be first, and the first last.”
Matthew 20:17  As Jesus went up to Jerusalem, He took the twelve disciples privately, and on the road He said to them,
Matthew 20:18  “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes. They will condemn Him to death
Matthew 20:19  and hand Him over to the Gentiles to mock, flog, and crucify Him; and on the third day He will be raised.”
Matthew 20:20  Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons came to Him with her sons, bowing before Him and asking something from Him.
Matthew 20:21  He said to her, “What do you wish?” She said to Him, “Command that these two sons of mine sit, one at Thy right and one at Thy left, in Thy kingdom.”
Matthew 20:22  Jesus answered, “You do not know what you ask. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink?” They said to Him, “We are able.”
Matthew 20:23  He said to them, “You will indeed drink My cup, but to sit at My right and left is not Mine to give, except to those for whom it has been prepared by My Father.”
Matthew 20:24  When the ten heard, they became indignant about the two brothers.
Matthew 20:25  Jesus summoned them and said, “You know that the rulers of the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
Matthew 20:26  It shall not be so among you. Instead, whoever wishes to become great among you will be your servant,
Matthew 20:27  and whoever wishes to be first among you will be your slave,
Matthew 20:28  just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give His life as a ransom in place of many.”
Matthew 20:29  As they went out from Jericho, a great crowd followed Him.
Matthew 20:30  And behold, two blind men sitting beside the road heard that Jesus was passing by and cried out, “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!”
Matthew 20:31  The crowd rebuked them to make them silent, but they cried out all the more, “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!”
Matthew 20:32  Jesus stopped, called them, and said, “What do you wish Me to do for you?”
Matthew 20:33  They said to Him, “Lord, that our eyes may be opened.”
Matthew 20:34  Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes. Immediately they received sight and followed Him.

Matthew 21
Matthew 21:1  When they drew near Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, to the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples,
Matthew 21:2  saying to them, “Go into the village opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied up and a colt with her. Untie them and bring them to Me.
Matthew 21:3  If anyone says anything to you, say, ‘The Lord has need of them,’ and immediately he will send them.”
Matthew 21:4  This happened so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled:
Matthew 21:5  “Tell the daughter of Zion: ‘Behold, your King comes to you, meek and mounted upon a donkey, and upon a colt, the foal of a beast of burden.’”
Matthew 21:6  The disciples went and did as Jesus directed them.
Matthew 21:7  They brought the donkey and the colt, placed the garments upon them, and He sat upon them.
Matthew 21:8  Most of the crowd spread their garments on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.
Matthew 21:9  The crowds going before Him and those following cried out, “Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is the One coming in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”
Matthew 21:10  When He entered Jerusalem, the whole city was shaken, saying, “Who is this?”
Matthew 21:11  The crowds said, “This is the prophet Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.”
Matthew 21:12  Jesus entered the temple and cast out all those selling and buying in the temple. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.
Matthew 21:13  He said to them, “It is written, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer,’ but you make it a den of robbers.”
Matthew 21:14  Blind and lame people came to Him in the temple, and He healed them.
Matthew 21:15  But when the chief priests and scribes saw the wonders He did and the children crying in the temple, “Hosanna to the Son of David,” they became indignant
Matthew 21:16  and said to Him, “Dost Thou hear what these are saying?” Jesus said to them, “Yes. Have you never read, ‘Out of the mouth of infants and nursing children Thou didst prepare praise’?”
Matthew 21:17  Leaving them, He went outside the city to Bethany and spent the night there.
Matthew 21:18  In the morning, as He returned to the city, He became hungry.
Matthew 21:19  Seeing a fig tree beside the road, He came to it and found nothing on it except leaves alone. He said to it, “Let no fruit ever come from you again.” Immediately the fig tree withered.
Matthew 21:20  When the disciples saw it, they marveled, saying, “How did the fig tree wither immediately?”
Matthew 21:21  Jesus answered them, “Truly I tell you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you will do not only what was done to the fig tree; even if you say to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and cast into the sea,’ it will happen.
Matthew 21:22  Everything you ask in prayer, believing, you will receive.”
Matthew 21:23  When He entered the temple, the chief priests and elders of the people approached Him as He taught, saying, “By what authority dost Thou do these things? And who gave Thee this authority?”
Matthew 21:24  Jesus answered them, “I too will ask you one thing. If you tell Me, I too will tell you by what authority I do these things.
Matthew 21:25  John’s baptism—from where was it? From heaven or from human beings?” They reasoned among themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will say to us, ‘Why, then, did you not believe him?’
Matthew 21:26  But if we say, ‘From human beings,’ we fear the crowd, for all regard John as a prophet.”
Matthew 21:27  They answered Jesus, “We do not know.” He also said to them, “Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
Matthew 21:28  But what do you think? A man had two children. He came to the first and said, ‘Child, go work in the vineyard today.’
Matthew 21:29  He answered, ‘I do not want to,’ but afterward he changed his mind and went.
Matthew 21:30  He came to the second and said the same. He answered, ‘I will, sir,’ but did not go.
Matthew 21:31  Which of the two did the father’s will?” They said, “The first.” Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you that tax collectors and prostitutes go ahead of you into the kingdom of God.
Matthew 21:32  For John came to you in the way of righteousness and you did not believe him, but tax collectors and prostitutes believed him. Even after seeing this, you did not afterward change your minds and believe him.
Matthew 21:33  Hear another parable. A householder planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a winepress in it, and built a tower. He leased it to farmers and traveled abroad.
Matthew 21:34  When the season of fruits drew near, he sent his slaves to the farmers to receive his fruits.
Matthew 21:35  The farmers seized his slaves: one they beat, another they killed, another they stoned.
Matthew 21:36  Again he sent other slaves, more than the first, and they did the same to them.
Matthew 21:37  Last he sent his son to them, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’
Matthew 21:38  But when the farmers saw the son, they said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and take his inheritance.’
Matthew 21:39  They seized him, cast him outside the vineyard, and killed him.
Matthew 21:40  So when the master of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?”
Matthew 21:41  They said to Him, “He will miserably destroy those miserable men, and lease the vineyard to other farmers who will give him the fruits in their seasons.”
Matthew 21:42  Jesus said to them, “Have you never read in the Scriptures: ‘The stone that the builders rejected became the head of the corner; this came from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?
Matthew 21:43  Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken from you and given to a people producing its fruits.
Matthew 21:44  And the one falling upon this stone will be shattered; but on whomever it falls, it will crush him.”
Matthew 21:45  When the chief priests and Pharisees heard His parables, they knew He was speaking about them.
Matthew 21:46  Although they sought to seize Him, they feared the crowds, because they regarded Him as a prophet.

Matthew 22
Matthew 22:1  Jesus again answered them in parables, saying,
Matthew 22:2  “The kingdom of the heavens was likened to a king who made a wedding feast for his son.
Matthew 22:3  He sent his slaves to call those invited to the wedding feast, but they were unwilling to come.
Matthew 22:4  Again he sent other slaves, saying, ‘Tell those invited: Behold, I have prepared my meal. My bulls and fattened animals have been slaughtered, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding feast.’
Matthew 22:5  But they disregarded it and went away, one to his own field, another to his business.
Matthew 22:6  The rest seized his slaves, mistreated them, and killed them.
Matthew 22:7  The king became angry. He sent his troops, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.
Matthew 22:8  Then he said to his slaves, ‘The wedding feast is ready, but those invited were not worthy.
Matthew 22:9  So go to the outlets of the roads and invite to the wedding feast as many as you find.’
Matthew 22:10  Those slaves went out into the roads and gathered everyone they found, both evil and good, and the wedding feast was filled with people reclining.
Matthew 22:11  The king entered to see those reclining and saw there a man not clothed in a wedding garment.
Matthew 22:12  He said to him, ‘Friend, how did you enter here without a wedding garment?’ He was speechless.
Matthew 22:13  Then the king said to the attendants, ‘Bind his feet and hands and cast him into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.’
Matthew 22:14  For many are called, but few chosen.”
Matthew 22:15  Then the Pharisees went and took counsel how to trap Him in a statement.
Matthew 22:16  They sent Him their disciples with the Herodians, saying, “Teacher, we know that Thou art truthful and dost teach God’s way in truth. Thou art not swayed by anyone, for Thou dost not look at people’s outward status.
Matthew 22:17  Tell us, then, what Thou thinkest: is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or not?”
Matthew 22:18  Knowing their evil intent, Jesus said, “Why do you test Me, hypocrites?
Matthew 22:19  Show Me the coin of the tribute.” And they brought Him a denarius.
Matthew 22:20  And He says to them, “Whose image is this, and whose inscription?”
Matthew 22:21  They say to Him, “Caesar’s.” Then He says to them, “Render therefore to Caesar the things of Caesar, and to God the things of God.”
Matthew 22:22  When they heard, they marveled, left Him, and went away.
Matthew 22:23  On that day Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Him and questioned Him,
Matthew 22:24  saying, “Teacher, Moses said, ‘If someone dies without children, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’
Matthew 22:25  There were seven brothers among us. The first married and died, and having no offspring, left his wife to his brother.
Matthew 22:26  Likewise the second and the third, up to the seventh.
Matthew 22:27  Last of all, the woman died.
Matthew 22:28  In the resurrection, then, whose wife of the seven will she be? For all had her.”
Matthew 22:29  Jesus answered them, “You are mistaken, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God.
Matthew 22:30  For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.
Matthew 22:31  But concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what was spoken to you by God:
Matthew 22:32  ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? He is not God of the dead, but of the living.”
Matthew 22:33  When the crowds heard, they were astonished at His teaching.
Matthew 22:34  Hearing that He had silenced the Sadducees, the Pharisees gathered together.
Matthew 22:35  One of them, an expert in the Law, questioned Him to test Him:
Matthew 22:36  “Teacher, which commandment is great in the Law?”
Matthew 22:37  He said to him, “‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’
Matthew 22:38  This is the great and first commandment.
Matthew 22:39  A second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’
Matthew 22:40  On these two commandments hang the whole Law and the Prophets.”
Matthew 22:41  While the Pharisees were gathered, Jesus questioned them,
Matthew 22:42  saying, “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is He?” They said to Him, “David’s.”
Matthew 22:43  He said to them, “How then does David in the Spirit call Him Lord, saying,
Matthew 22:44  ‘The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at My right hand until I put Thy enemies beneath Thy feet’?
Matthew 22:45  If David calls Him Lord, how is He his son?”
Matthew 22:46  No one could answer Him a word, nor from that day did anyone dare question Him any longer.

Matthew 23
Matthew 23:1  Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and His disciples,
Matthew 23:2  saying, “The scribes and Pharisees have seated themselves in Moses’ chair.
Matthew 23:3  Therefore do and observe everything they tell you, but do not act according to their works, for they say and do not do.
Matthew 23:4  They bind heavy burdens, hard to carry, and lay them upon people’s shoulders, but they themselves are unwilling to move them with their finger.
Matthew 23:5  They do all their works to be seen by people. They broaden their phylacteries and enlarge their fringes.
Matthew 23:6  They love the foremost place at dinners and the foremost seats in the synagogues,
Matthew 23:7  greetings in the marketplaces, and being called ‘Rabbi’ by people.
Matthew 23:8  But you shall not be called ‘Rabbi,’ for One is your Teacher, and you are all brothers.
Matthew 23:9  And call no one upon earth your father, for One is your Father, the heavenly One.
Matthew 23:10  Nor shall you be called guides, because One is your Guide, the Christ.
Matthew 23:11  But the greatest among you will be your servant.
Matthew 23:12  Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
Matthew 23:13  Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you shut the kingdom of the heavens before people! For you do not enter, nor do you permit those entering to enter.
Matthew 23:15  Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you travel around sea and dry land to make one proselyte, and when he becomes one, you make him a son of Gehenna twice as much as yourselves!
Matthew 23:16  Woe to you, blind guides, who say, ‘Whoever swears by the sanctuary, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the sanctuary is bound.’
Matthew 23:17  Fools and blind men! For which is greater, the gold or the sanctuary that sanctified the gold?
Matthew 23:18  And, ‘Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift upon it is bound.’
Matthew 23:19  Blind men! For which is greater, the gift or the altar that sanctifies the gift?
Matthew 23:20  Therefore the one swearing by the altar swears by it and by everything upon it.
Matthew 23:21  The one swearing by the sanctuary swears by it and by the One dwelling in it.
Matthew 23:22  The one swearing by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the One seated upon it.
Matthew 23:23  Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you tithe mint, dill, and cumin, but have left aside the weightier matters of the Law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness! These you ought to have done without leaving those aside.
Matthew 23:24  Blind guides, straining out the gnat but swallowing the camel!
Matthew 23:25  Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you cleanse the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they are full of plunder and self-indulgence!
Matthew 23:26  Blind Pharisee, first cleanse the inside of the cup, so that its outside may also become clean.
Matthew 23:27  Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you resemble whitewashed tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but inwardly are full of dead people’s bones and all uncleanness!
Matthew 23:28  So you too outwardly appear righteous to people, but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
Matthew 23:29  Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you build the prophets’ tombs and adorn the monuments of the righteous,
Matthew 23:30  and say, ‘If we had lived in our fathers’ days, we would not have shared with them in the blood of the prophets.’
Matthew 23:31  So you testify concerning yourselves that you are sons of those who murdered the prophets.
Matthew 23:32  You, then, fill up the measure of your fathers!
Matthew 23:33  Snakes, brood of vipers! How will you flee from the judgment of Gehenna?
Matthew 23:34  Therefore behold, I send you prophets, wise people, and scribes. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and some you will flog in your synagogues and persecute from city to city,
Matthew 23:35  so that upon you may come all righteous blood poured out upon earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar.
Matthew 23:36  Truly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.
Matthew 23:37  Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her! How often I wished to gather your children as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you were unwilling!
Matthew 23:38  Behold, your house is left to you desolate.
Matthew 23:39  For I tell you, you will certainly not see Me from now until you say, ‘Blessed is the One coming in the name of the Lord.’”

Matthew 24
Matthew 24:1  Jesus went out from the temple and was going away, when His disciples came to show Him the temple buildings.
Matthew 24:2  He answered them, “Do you not see all these things? Truly I tell you, not one stone will be left here upon another that will not be thrown down.”
Matthew 24:3  As He sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately, saying, “Tell us, when will these things happen, and what is the sign of Thy coming and the consummation of the age?”
Matthew 24:4  Jesus answered them, “See that no one leads you astray.
Matthew 24:5  For many will come in My name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will lead many astray.
Matthew 24:6  You will hear wars and reports of wars. See that you are not alarmed, for these things must happen, but the end is not yet.
Matthew 24:7  For nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and earthquakes in various places.
Matthew 24:8  All these things are the beginning of birth pains.
Matthew 24:9  Then they will hand you over to affliction and kill you, and you will be hated by all nations because of My name.
Matthew 24:10  Then many will stumble, hand one another over, and hate one another.
Matthew 24:11  Many false prophets will arise and lead many astray.
Matthew 24:12  Because lawlessness increases, the love of many will grow cold.
Matthew 24:13  But the one who endures to the end will be saved.
Matthew 24:14  This good news of the kingdom will be proclaimed in the whole inhabited world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.
Matthew 24:15  So when you see the abomination of desolation spoken of through Daniel the prophet standing in a holy place—let the reader understand—
Matthew 24:16  then let those in Judea flee to the mountains.
Matthew 24:17  Let the one on the housetop not go down to take things from his house,
Matthew 24:18  and let the one in the field not turn back to take his cloak.
Matthew 24:19  Woe to those with child and those nursing infants in those days!
Matthew 24:20  Pray that your flight may not occur in winter or on a Sabbath.
Matthew 24:21  For then there will be great affliction such as has not happened from the beginning of the world until now, and certainly will never happen again.
Matthew 24:22  If those days had not been shortened, no flesh would have been saved; but because of the chosen, those days will be shortened.
Matthew 24:23  Then if anyone tells you, ‘Behold, here is the Christ!’ or ‘Here!’ do not believe it.
Matthew 24:24  For false christs and false prophets will arise and give great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen.
Matthew 24:25  Behold, I have told you beforehand.
Matthew 24:26  So if they tell you, ‘Behold, He is in the wilderness,’ do not go out; or ‘Behold, in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.
Matthew 24:27  For just as lightning comes from the east and shines to the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
Matthew 24:28  Wherever the corpse is, there the eagles will gather.
Matthew 24:29  Immediately after the affliction of those days, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its brightness, the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
Matthew 24:30  Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn; they will see the Son of Man coming upon the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
Matthew 24:31  He will send His angels with a great trumpet, and they will gather His chosen from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.
Matthew 24:32  Learn the parable from the fig tree: when its branch has already become tender and puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.
Matthew 24:33  So also you, when you see all these things, know that it is near, at the doors.
Matthew 24:34  Truly I tell you that this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things happen.
Matthew 24:35  Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will certainly not pass away.
Matthew 24:36  Concerning that day and hour, no one knows, not even the angels of the heavens, nor the Son, but the Father alone.
Matthew 24:37  For just as the days of Noah were, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
Matthew 24:38  For in those days before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark.
Matthew 24:39  They did not know until the flood came and took them all away. So also will be the coming of the Son of Man.
Matthew 24:40  Then two men will be in the field: one is taken and one is left.
Matthew 24:41  Two women will be grinding at the mill: one is taken and one is left.
Matthew 24:42  So keep watch, because you do not know on what day your Lord comes.
Matthew 24:43  But know this: if the householder had known in what watch the thief was coming, he would have kept watch and would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
Matthew 24:44  Therefore you too must be ready, because the Son of Man comes at an hour you do not expect.
Matthew 24:45  Who, then, is the faithful and prudent slave whom the master appointed over his household to give them food at the proper time?
Matthew 24:46  Blessed is that slave whom his master, when he comes, will find doing so.
Matthew 24:47  Truly I tell you that he will appoint him over all his belongings.
Matthew 24:48  But if that evil slave says in his heart, ‘My master delays,’
Matthew 24:49  and begins to beat his fellow slaves and eats and drinks with drunkards,
Matthew 24:50  the master of that slave will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know.
Matthew 24:51  He will cut him in two and assign his portion with the hypocrites. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.

Matthew 25
Matthew 25:1  Then the kingdom of the heavens will be likened to ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
Matthew 25:2  Five of them were foolish and five prudent.
Matthew 25:3  For the foolish took their lamps but did not take oil with them.
Matthew 25:4  The prudent took oil in containers along with their lamps.
Matthew 25:5  As the bridegroom delayed, they all became drowsy and slept.
Matthew 25:6  At midnight a cry arose: ‘Behold, the bridegroom! Come out to meet him.’
Matthew 25:7  Then all those virgins arose and put their lamps in order.
Matthew 25:8  The foolish said to the prudent, ‘Give us some of your oil, because our lamps are going out.’
Matthew 25:9  The prudent answered, ‘There may not be enough for us and you. Go instead to those selling and buy for yourselves.’
Matthew 25:10  While they went away to buy, the bridegroom came. Those who were ready entered with him into the wedding feast, and the door was shut.
Matthew 25:11  Afterward the other virgins also came, saying, ‘Lord, lord, open to us.’
Matthew 25:12  He answered, ‘Truly I tell you, I do not know you.’
Matthew 25:13  Therefore keep watch, because you know neither the day nor the hour.
Matthew 25:14  For it is like a man traveling abroad, who called his own slaves and handed over his belongings to them.
Matthew 25:15  To one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one, each according to his own ability, and traveled abroad. Immediately
Matthew 25:16  the one who received the five talents went and traded with them and gained another five.
Matthew 25:17  Likewise the one with two gained another two.
Matthew 25:18  But the one who received one went away, dug in the ground, and hid his master’s silver.
Matthew 25:19  After a long time, the master of those slaves came and settled accounts with them.
Matthew 25:20  The one who received five talents came and brought another five talents, saying, ‘Master, you handed over five talents to me. Look, I gained another five talents.’
Matthew 25:21  His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful slave. You were faithful over a few things; I will appoint you over many. Enter into your master’s joy.’
Matthew 25:22  The one with two talents also came and said, ‘Master, you handed over two talents to me. Look, I gained another two talents.’
Matthew 25:23  His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful slave. You were faithful over a few things; I will appoint you over many. Enter into your master’s joy.’
Matthew 25:24  The one who received one talent also came and said, ‘Master, I knew you to be a hard man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering from where you did not scatter.
Matthew 25:25  I was afraid, so I went away and hid your talent in the ground. Look, you have what is yours.’
Matthew 25:26  His master answered him, ‘Evil and idle slave! You knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather from where I did not scatter?
Matthew 25:27  Then you ought to have deposited my silver with the bankers, and when I came I would have recovered what is mine with interest.
Matthew 25:28  So take the talent from him and give it to the one who has the ten talents.
Matthew 25:29  For to everyone who has, more will be given and he will have abundance; but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken.
Matthew 25:30  Cast the useless slave into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.’
Matthew 25:31  When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, then He will sit upon the throne of His glory.
Matthew 25:32  All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate them from one another as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
Matthew 25:33  He will stand the sheep at His right and the young goats at His left.
Matthew 25:34  Then the King will say to those at His right, ‘Come, you blessed by My Father; inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
Matthew 25:35  For I was hungry and you gave Me food, I was thirsty and you gave Me drink, I was a stranger and you welcomed Me,
Matthew 25:36  naked and you clothed Me, I was sick and you visited Me, I was in prison and you came to Me.’
Matthew 25:37  Then the righteous will answer Him, ‘Lord, when did we see Thee hungry and feed Thee, or thirsty and give Thee drink?
Matthew 25:38  When did we see Thee a stranger and welcome Thee, or naked and clothe Thee?
Matthew 25:39  When did we see Thee sick or in prison and come to Thee?’
Matthew 25:40  The King will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did it to one of the least of these My brothers, you did it to Me.’
Matthew 25:41  Then He will also say to those at His left, ‘Depart from Me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
Matthew 25:42  For I was hungry and you did not give Me food, I was thirsty and you did not give Me drink,
Matthew 25:43  I was a stranger and you did not welcome Me, naked and you did not clothe Me, sick and in prison and you did not visit Me.’
Matthew 25:44  Then they too will answer, ‘Lord, when did we see Thee hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not serve Thee?’
Matthew 25:45  Then He will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did not do it to one of the least of these, neither did you do it to Me.’
Matthew 25:46  And these shall depart into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”

Matthew 26
Matthew 26:1  When Jesus finished all these words, He said to His disciples,
Matthew 26:2  “You know that after two days the Passover takes place, and the Son of Man is handed over to be crucified.”
Matthew 26:3  Then the chief priests and elders of the people gathered in the courtyard of the high priest called Caiaphas.
Matthew 26:4  They took counsel to seize Jesus by deceit and kill Him.
Matthew 26:5  But they said, “Not during the feast, lest an uproar occur among the people.”
Matthew 26:6  While Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
Matthew 26:7  a woman came to Him with an alabaster flask of very costly perfume and poured it upon His head as He reclined at table.
Matthew 26:8  Seeing it, the disciples became indignant, saying, “Why this waste?
Matthew 26:9  For this could have been sold for much and given to the poor.”
Matthew 26:10  Knowing this, Jesus said to them, “Why do you trouble the woman? For she has done a good work toward Me.
Matthew 26:11  For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have Me.
Matthew 26:12  By pouring this perfume upon My body, she did it to prepare Me for burial.
Matthew 26:13  Truly I tell you, wherever this good news is proclaimed in the whole world, what she did will also be told in remembrance of her.”
Matthew 26:14  Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
Matthew 26:15  and said, “What are you willing to give me, and I will hand Him over to you?” They weighed out for him thirty silver coins.
Matthew 26:16  From then on he sought a suitable opportunity to hand Him over.
Matthew 26:17  On the first day of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus, saying, “Where dost Thou wish us to prepare for Thee to eat the Passover?”
Matthew 26:18  He said, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, ‘The Teacher says: My appointed time is near. I keep the Passover at your house with My disciples.’”
Matthew 26:19  The disciples did as Jesus directed them, and prepared the Passover.
Matthew 26:20  When evening came, He reclined at table with the twelve.
Matthew 26:21  As they ate, He said, “Truly I tell you that one of you will hand Me over.”
Matthew 26:22  Exceedingly grieved, each began saying to Him, “Surely it is not I, Lord?”
Matthew 26:23  He answered, “The one who dipped his hand with Me in the dish will hand Me over.
Matthew 26:24  The Son of Man indeed goes as it is written concerning Him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is handed over! It would have been good for him if that man had not been born.”
Matthew 26:25  Judas, who was handing Him over, answered, “Surely it is not I, Rabbi?” He said to him, “You have said it.”
Matthew 26:26  And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and having blessed, He broke it; and giving it to the disciples, He said, “Take, eat; this is My body.”
Matthew 26:27  And He took a cup, and having given thanks, He gave it to them, saying, “Drink from it, all of you;
Matthew 26:28  for this is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for forgiveness of sins.
Matthew 26:29  And I tell you: from this time I shall by no means drink of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of My Father.”
Matthew 26:30  After singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Matthew 26:31  Then Jesus said to them, “All of you will stumble because of Me this night, for it is written: ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’
Matthew 26:32  But after I am raised, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.”
Matthew 26:33  Peter answered Him, “Even if everyone stumbles because of Thee, I will never stumble.”
Matthew 26:34  Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you that this night, before a rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.”
Matthew 26:35  Peter said to Him, “Even if I must die with Thee, I will certainly not deny Thee.” All the disciples said likewise.
Matthew 26:36  Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane, and said to the disciples, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”
Matthew 26:37  Taking Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, He began to be grieved and distressed.
Matthew 26:38  Then He said to them, “My soul is deeply grieved, even to death. Remain here and keep watch with Me.”
Matthew 26:39  Going forward a little, He fell upon His face and prayed, saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me. Nevertheless, not as I wish, but as Thou wishest.”
Matthew 26:40  He came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “So, could you not keep watch with Me for one hour?
Matthew 26:41  Keep watch and pray, so that you may not enter temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
Matthew 26:42  Again He went away a second time and prayed, saying, “My Father, if this cannot pass unless I drink it, let Thy will be done.”
Matthew 26:43  He came and again found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.
Matthew 26:44  He left them and went away again, praying a third time and saying the same words again.
Matthew 26:45  Then He came to the disciples and said to them, “Sleep on now and rest. Behold, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of Man is handed over into sinners’ hands.
Matthew 26:46  Rise, let us go. Behold, the one handing Me over has drawn near.”
Matthew 26:47  While He was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the twelve, came with a great crowd carrying swords and clubs, from the chief priests and elders of the people.
Matthew 26:48  The one handing Him over had given them a sign, saying, “The One I kiss is He; seize Him.”
Matthew 26:49  Immediately he came to Jesus and said, “Greetings, Rabbi,” and kissed Him.
Matthew 26:50  Jesus said to him, “Friend, do what you have come for.” Then they came forward, laid their hands upon Jesus, and seized Him.
Matthew 26:51  And behold, one of those with Jesus stretched out his hand, drew his sword, struck the high priest’s slave, and cut off his ear.
Matthew 26:52  Then Jesus said to him, “Return your sword to its place, for all who take a sword will perish by a sword.
Matthew 26:53  Or do you think I cannot plead with My Father, and He will provide Me at once more than twelve legions of angels?
Matthew 26:54  How, then, would the Scriptures be fulfilled, that it must happen this way?”
Matthew 26:55  At that hour Jesus said to the crowds, “Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs, to arrest Me? Daily I sat teaching in the temple, and you did not seize Me.
Matthew 26:56  But all this has happened so that the Scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples left Him and fled.
Matthew 26:57  Those who seized Jesus led Him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders had gathered.
Matthew 26:58  Peter followed Him at a distance as far as the high priest’s courtyard. Going inside, he sat with the officers to see the outcome.
Matthew 26:59  The chief priests and the whole council sought false testimony against Jesus to put Him to death,
Matthew 26:60  but found none, although many false witnesses came forward. Finally two came forward
Matthew 26:61  and said, “This Man said, ‘I can destroy God’s sanctuary and build it in three days.’”
Matthew 26:62  The high priest rose and said to Him, “Dost Thou answer nothing? What is this that they testify against Thee?”
Matthew 26:63  But Jesus remained silent. The high priest said to Him, “I adjure Thee by the living God to tell us whether Thou art the Christ, the Son of God.”
Matthew 26:64  Jesus said to him, “You have said it. Nevertheless I tell you, from now on you will see the Son of Man seated at the right of the Power and coming upon the clouds of heaven.”
Matthew 26:65  Then the high priest tore his garments, saying, “He has blasphemed! What further need do we have of witnesses? Look, now you heard the blasphemy.
Matthew 26:66  What do you think?” They answered, “He is liable to death.”
Matthew 26:67  Then they spat into His face and struck Him with their fists; others slapped Him,
Matthew 26:68  saying, “Prophesy to us, Christ! Who is the one who struck Thee?”
Matthew 26:69  Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard. One servant girl approached him, saying, “You too were with Jesus the Galilean.”
Matthew 26:70  But he denied it before everyone, saying, “I do not know what you are saying.”
Matthew 26:71  When he went out to the gateway, another girl saw him and said to those there, “This man was with Jesus the Nazarene.”
Matthew 26:72  Again he denied it with an oath: “I do not know the Man.”
Matthew 26:73  After a little while, those standing there came and said to Peter, “Truly you too are one of them, for even your speech makes you recognizable.”
Matthew 26:74  Then he began to invoke curses and swear, “I do not know the Man.” Immediately a rooster crowed.
Matthew 26:75  Peter remembered Jesus’ word: “Before a rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.” He went outside and wept bitterly.

Matthew 27
Matthew 27:1  When morning came, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put Him to death.
Matthew 27:2  They bound Him, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate the governor.
Matthew 27:3  Then Judas, who had handed Him over, saw that He had been condemned. Filled with regret, he returned the thirty silver coins to the chief priests and elders,
Matthew 27:4  saying, “I sinned by handing over innocent blood.” They said, “What is that to us? See to it yourself.”
Matthew 27:5  He threw the silver coins into the sanctuary and withdrew; then he went away and hanged himself.
Matthew 27:6  The chief priests took the silver coins and said, “It is not lawful to put them into the treasury, because they are the price of blood.”
Matthew 27:7  After taking counsel, they bought the potter’s field with them as a burial place for strangers.
Matthew 27:8  Therefore that field has been called Field of Blood until today.
Matthew 27:9  Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled: “They took the thirty silver coins, the price of the One priced, whom some of the sons of Israel priced,
Matthew 27:10  and gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord directed me.”
Matthew 27:11  Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor questioned Him, saying, “Art Thou the King of the Jews?” Jesus said, “You say it.”
Matthew 27:12  While He was accused by the chief priests and elders, He answered nothing.
Matthew 27:13  Then Pilate said to Him, “Dost Thou not hear how many things they testify against Thee?”
Matthew 27:14  He did not answer him even one word, so that the governor marveled greatly.
Matthew 27:15  At the feast the governor customarily released to the crowd one prisoner whom they wanted.
Matthew 27:16  At that time they had a notorious prisoner called Jesus Barabbas.
Matthew 27:17  So when they gathered, Pilate said to them, “Whom do you want me to release to you: Jesus Barabbas, or Jesus called Christ?”
Matthew 27:18  For he knew that they had handed Him over because of envy.
Matthew 27:19  While he sat on the judgment seat, his wife sent to him, saying, “Have nothing to do with that righteous Man, for I suffered many things today in a dream because of Him.”
Matthew 27:20  But the chief priests and elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and destroy Jesus.
Matthew 27:21  The governor answered them, “Which of the two do you want me to release to you?” They said, “Barabbas.”
Matthew 27:22  Pilate said to them, “What then shall I do with Jesus called Christ?” They all said, “Let Him be crucified!”
Matthew 27:23  He said, “Why, what evil did He do?” But they cried out all the more, “Let Him be crucified!”
Matthew 27:24  When Pilate saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but rather an uproar was arising, he took water and washed his hands before the crowd, saying, “I am innocent of this blood. See to it yourselves.”
Matthew 27:25  All the people answered, “His blood be upon us and upon our children.”
Matthew 27:26  Then he released Barabbas to them; after flogging Jesus, he handed Him over to be crucified.
Matthew 27:27  Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the praetorium and gathered the whole cohort around Him.
Matthew 27:28  They stripped Him and put a scarlet cloak around Him.
Matthew 27:29  They wove a crown from thorns, placed it upon His head, and put a reed in His right hand. Kneeling before Him, they mocked Him, saying, “Greetings, King of the Jews!”
Matthew 27:30  They spat on Him, took the reed, and kept striking Him upon the head.
Matthew 27:31  After mocking Him, they stripped off the cloak, dressed Him in His own garments, and led Him away to crucify Him.
Matthew 27:32  As they went out, they found a Cyrenian man named Simon. They compelled him to carry His cross.
Matthew 27:33  They came to a place called Golgotha, which is called Place of a Skull,
Matthew 27:34  and gave Him wine mixed with gall to drink. After tasting it, He was unwilling to drink.
Matthew 27:35  After crucifying Him, they divided His garments by casting a lot,
Matthew 27:36  and sat there keeping watch over Him.
Matthew 27:37  Above His head they placed the written charge against Him: “This is Jesus, the King of the Jews.”
Matthew 27:38  Then two robbers were crucified with Him, one at His right and one at His left.
Matthew 27:39  Those passing by reviled Him, shaking their heads
Matthew 27:40  and saying, “Thou who destroyest the sanctuary and buildest it in three days, save Thyself! If Thou art God’s Son, come down from the cross.”
Matthew 27:41  Likewise the chief priests, mocking with the scribes and elders, said,
Matthew 27:42  “He saved others; Himself He cannot save. He is King of Israel! Let Him come down from the cross now, and we will believe in Him.
Matthew 27:43  He trusts in God; let Him rescue Him now, if He desires Him, for He said, ‘I am God’s Son.’”
Matthew 27:44  The robbers crucified with Him also reproached Him in the same way.
Matthew 27:45  From the sixth hour darkness came upon all the land until the ninth hour.
Matthew 27:46  And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” That is, “My God, My God, why hast Thou forsaken Me?”
Matthew 27:47  Some standing there heard and said, “This Man is calling Elijah.”
Matthew 27:48  Immediately one of them ran, took a sponge, filled it with sour wine, placed it on a reed, and gave Him a drink.
Matthew 27:49  But the rest said, “Leave it; let us see whether Elijah comes to save Him.”
Matthew 27:50  Jesus again cried out with a loud voice and released His spirit.
Matthew 27:51  And behold, the veil of the sanctuary was torn in two from top to bottom. The earth shook, and the rocks split.
Matthew 27:52  The tombs were opened, and many bodies of the holy ones who had fallen asleep were raised.
Matthew 27:53  Coming out of the tombs after His rising, they entered the holy city and appeared to many.
Matthew 27:54  The centurion and those with him guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and what had happened, and were exceedingly afraid, saying, “Truly this was God’s Son.”
Matthew 27:55  Many women were there, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee, serving Him.
Matthew 27:56  Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee’s sons.
Matthew 27:57  When evening came, a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph came, who himself had also become Jesus’ disciple.
Matthew 27:58  He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Then Pilate ordered it to be given.
Matthew 27:59  Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth.
Matthew 27:60  He laid it in his own new tomb, which he had cut in the rock. Rolling a great stone to the tomb’s entrance, he went away.
Matthew 27:61  Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the tomb.
Matthew 27:62  On the next day, which was after the Preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees gathered before Pilate,
Matthew 27:63  saying, “Sir, we remembered that while He was still alive, that deceiver said, ‘After three days I am raised.’
Matthew 27:64  So command that the tomb be made secure until the third day, lest His disciples come, steal Him, and tell the people, ‘He has been raised from the dead,’ and the last deception will be worse than the first.”
Matthew 27:65  Pilate said to them, “You have a guard. Go and make it secure as you know how.”
Matthew 27:66  They went and secured the tomb by sealing the stone, with the guard.

Matthew 28
Matthew 28:1  After the Sabbath, as it dawned toward the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to view the tomb.
Matthew 28:2  And behold, a great earthquake occurred, for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven, came, rolled away the stone, and sat upon it.
Matthew 28:3  His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing white as snow.
Matthew 28:4  From fear of him the guards shook and became like dead men.
Matthew 28:5  The angel answered the women, “Do not be afraid, for I know that you seek Jesus who was crucified.
Matthew 28:6  He is not here, for He was raised, as He said. Come, see the place where He lay.
Matthew 28:7  Go quickly and tell His disciples that He was raised from the dead; and behold, He goes ahead of you to Galilee. There you will see Him. Behold, I have told you.”
Matthew 28:8  They departed quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy and ran to report to His disciples.
Matthew 28:9  And behold, Jesus met them, saying, “Greetings!” They came, grasped His feet, and worshiped Him.
Matthew 28:10  Then Jesus said to them, “Do not fear. Go and report to My brothers that they should go to Galilee, and there they will see Me.”
Matthew 28:11  As they went, behold, some of the guard came into the city and reported to the chief priests everything that had happened.
Matthew 28:12  They gathered with the elders and took counsel, then gave a considerable amount of silver to the soldiers,
Matthew 28:13  saying, “Say, ‘His disciples came by night and stole Him while we slept.’
Matthew 28:14  If this is heard before the governor, we will persuade him and make you free from worry.”
Matthew 28:15  They took the silver and did as they were instructed. This account was spread among Jews until this very day.
Matthew 28:16  The eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had directed them.
Matthew 28:17  When they saw Him, they worshiped, but some doubted.
Matthew 28:18  And Jesus came and spoke to them, saying, “All authority in heaven and upon earth has been given to Me.
Matthew 28:19  Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
Matthew 28:20  teaching them to keep all that I commanded you; and behold, I am with you all the days, until the consummation of the age.”

MARK

Mark 1
Mark 1:1  The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, Son of God.
Mark 1:2  As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: “Look, I send My messenger before Thy face, who will prepare Thy way;
Mark 1:3  a voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way of the Lord; make His paths straight.’”
Mark 1:4  John appeared, baptizing in the wilderness and proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
Mark 1:5  The whole Judean countryside and all the people of Jerusalem were going out to him. They were being baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
Mark 1:6  John was clothed in camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist, and ate locusts and wild honey.
Mark 1:7  He proclaimed, saying, “The One stronger than I is coming after me. I am not worthy to stoop down and untie the strap of His sandals.
Mark 1:8  I baptized you with water, but He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.”
Mark 1:9  In those days Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized in the Jordan by John.
Mark 1:10  Immediately as He came up out of the water, He saw the heavens being torn open and the Spirit descending like a dove into Him.
Mark 1:11  A voice came from the heavens: “Thou art My beloved Son; in Thee I am well pleased.”
Mark 1:12  Immediately the Spirit drove Him out into the wilderness.
Mark 1:13  He was in the wilderness forty days, being tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals, and the angels ministered to Him.
Mark 1:14  And after John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, proclaiming the gospel of God,
Mark 1:15  and saying, “The appointed time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near; repent, and believe in the gospel.”
Mark 1:16  And passing beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw Simon and Andrew the brother of Simon casting a net in the sea, for they were fishermen.
Mark 1:17  And He said to them, “Come after Me, and I will make you become fishers of men.”
Mark 1:18  Immediately they left their nets and followed Him.
Mark 1:19  Going a little farther, He saw James son of Zebedee and John his brother, who were also in the boat, putting the nets in order.
Mark 1:20  Immediately He called them. They left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers and went after Him.
Mark 1:21  They entered Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath He went into the synagogue and taught.
Mark 1:22  They were astonished at His teaching, for He taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
Mark 1:23  Immediately there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,
Mark 1:24  “What have we to do with Thee, Jesus of Nazareth? Hast Thou come to destroy us? I know who Thou art—the Holy One of God!”
Mark 1:25  Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be muzzled, and come out of him!”
Mark 1:26  The unclean spirit convulsed him, cried out with a loud voice, and came out of him.
Mark 1:27  They were all amazed, so that they discussed among themselves, saying, “What is this? A new teaching! With authority He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him.”
Mark 1:28  Immediately the report about Him went out everywhere through the whole surrounding region of Galilee.
Mark 1:29  Immediately after leaving the synagogue, they went into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
Mark 1:30  Simon’s mother-in-law was lying down with a fever, and immediately they told Him about her.
Mark 1:31  He came to her, took her by the hand, and raised her up. The fever left her, and she served them.
Mark 1:32  When evening came, after the sun had set, they brought to Him all who were ill and those possessed by demons.
Mark 1:33  The whole city had gathered at the door.
Mark 1:34  He healed many who were ill with various diseases and cast out many demons. He would not allow the demons to speak, because they knew Him.
Mark 1:35  Very early, while it was still dark, He arose, went out, and departed to a deserted place, and there He prayed.
Mark 1:36  Simon and those with him searched for Him
Mark 1:37  and found Him. They said to Him, “Everyone is looking for Thee.”
Mark 1:38  He said to them, “Let us go elsewhere, into the neighboring towns, so that I may proclaim there also, for that is why I came out.”
Mark 1:39  He went throughout all Galilee, proclaiming in their synagogues and casting out the demons.
Mark 1:40  A leper came to Him, pleading with Him, kneeling, and saying, “If Thou art willing, Thou canst cleanse me.”
Mark 1:41  And moved with compassion, He stretched out His hand and touched him, and says to him, “I will; be cleansed.”
Mark 1:42  Immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was cleansed.
Mark 1:43  Sternly warning him, He immediately drove him away
Mark 1:44  and said to him, “See that you say nothing to anyone. But go, show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”
Mark 1:45  But he went out and began proclaiming it widely and spreading the report, so that Jesus could no longer enter a city openly. He remained outside in deserted places, and they came to Him from every direction.

Mark 2
Mark 2:1  When He entered Capernaum again after some days, it was heard that He was at home.
Mark 2:2  Many gathered, so that there was no longer room, not even near the door, and He was speaking the word to them.
Mark 2:3  They came, bringing to Him a paralyzed man carried by four men.
Mark 2:4  Since they could not bring him to Jesus because of the crowd, they removed the roof above the place where He was. After digging through it, they lowered the mat on which the paralyzed man lay.
Mark 2:5  Jesus saw their faith and said to the paralyzed man, “Child, your sins are forgiven.”
Mark 2:6  Some of the scribes were sitting there and reasoning in their hearts,
Mark 2:7  “Why does this man speak this way? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins except the one God?”
Mark 2:8  Immediately Jesus knew in His spirit that they were reasoning this way within themselves. He said to them, “Why are you reasoning these things in your hearts?
Mark 2:9  Which is easier: to say to the paralyzed man, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Arise, take your mat, and walk’?
Mark 2:10  But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—He said to the paralyzed man—
Mark 2:11  “I say to you, arise, take your mat, and go to your house.”
Mark 2:12  He arose, immediately took up the mat, and went out before everyone. They were all amazed and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”
Mark 2:13  He went out again beside the sea. The whole crowd came to Him, and He taught them.
Mark 2:14  As He passed by, He saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax station. He said to him, “Follow Me.” He arose and followed Him.
Mark 2:15  As He reclined at table in his house, many tax collectors and sinners reclined with Jesus and His disciples, for there were many who followed Him.
Mark 2:16  The scribes of the Pharisees saw that He was eating with sinners and tax collectors and said to His disciples, “Why does He eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
Mark 2:17  Jesus heard and said to them, “The strong have no need of a physician, but those who are ill do. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”
Mark 2:18  John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting. They came and said to Him, “Why do John’s disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but Thy disciples do not fast?”
Mark 2:19  Jesus said to them, “Can the bridegroom’s companions fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
Mark 2:20  But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast on that day.
Mark 2:21  No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old garment. Otherwise the new patch pulls away from the old, and a worse tear results.
Mark 2:22  No one puts new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise the wine will burst the skins, and the wine is lost along with the skins. New wine belongs in fresh wineskins.”
Mark 2:23  He was passing through the grainfields on the Sabbath, and His disciples began to make their way, plucking the heads of grain.
Mark 2:24  The Pharisees said to Him, “Look! Why are they doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?”
Mark 2:25  He said to them, “Have you never read what David did when he was in need and hungry, he and those with him:
Mark 2:26  how he entered God’s house in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the loaves of presentation, which only priests may lawfully eat, and also gave them to those who were with him?”
Mark 2:27  And He said to them, “The Sabbath was made for man, and not man for the Sabbath.
Mark 2:28  So the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”

Mark 3
Mark 3:1  He entered a synagogue again, and a man with a withered hand was there.
Mark 3:2  They watched Him closely to see whether He would heal him on the Sabbath, so that they might accuse Him.
Mark 3:3  He said to the man with the withered hand, “Arise and come into the midst.”
Mark 3:4  He said to them, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to kill?” But they remained silent.
Mark 3:5  He looked around at them with anger, grieving at the hardness of their hearts, and said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
Mark 3:6  The Pharisees went out and immediately took counsel with the Herodians against Him, as to how they might destroy Him.
Mark 3:7  Jesus withdrew with His disciples to the sea, and a great multitude from Galilee followed; and from Judea,
Mark 3:8  Jerusalem, Idumea, beyond the Jordan, and the region of Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude heard all He was doing and came to Him.
Mark 3:9  He told His disciples to have a small boat ready for Him because of the crowd, so that they would not crush Him.
Mark 3:10  For He healed many, so that all who had afflictions pressed upon Him to touch Him.
Mark 3:11  Whenever the unclean spirits saw Him, they fell before Him and cried, “Thou art the Son of God!”
Mark 3:12  He sternly warned them not to make Him known.
Mark 3:13  He went up the mountain and called to Himself those He wanted, and they came to Him.
Mark 3:14  He appointed twelve, whom He also named apostles, to be with Him and to be sent out by Him to proclaim
Mark 3:15  and to have authority to cast out the demons.
Mark 3:16  He appointed the Twelve: Simon, to whom He gave the name Peter;
Mark 3:17  James son of Zebedee and John, James’s brother, to whom He gave the name Boanerges, that is, Sons of Thunder;
Mark 3:18  Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Cananaean,
Mark 3:19  and Judas Iscariot, who also handed Him over.
Mark 3:20  He came into a house, and the crowd gathered again, so that they could not even eat bread.
Mark 3:21  When His own people heard, they went out to take hold of Him, for they were saying, “He is out of His mind.”
Mark 3:22  The scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, “He has Beelzebul,” and, “By the ruler of the demons He casts out the demons.”
Mark 3:23  He called them to Himself and spoke to them in parables: “How can Satan cast out Satan?
Mark 3:24  If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
Mark 3:25  If a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.
Mark 3:26  If Satan has risen against himself and is divided, he cannot stand, but has come to an end.
Mark 3:27  No one can enter the strong man’s house and plunder his belongings unless he first binds the strong man. Then he will plunder his house.
Mark 3:28  Truly I tell you, people will be forgiven everything—their sins and whatever blasphemies they may utter.
Mark 3:29  But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit has no forgiveness for ever, but is liable for an eternal sin.”
Mark 3:30  For they were saying, “He has an unclean spirit.”
Mark 3:31  His mother and His brothers came. Standing outside, they sent to Him and called Him.
Mark 3:32  A crowd was sitting around Him. They said to Him, “Look! Thy mother and Thy brothers and Thy sisters are outside looking for Thee.”
Mark 3:33  He answered them, “Who is My mother, or who are My brothers?”
Mark 3:34  He looked around at those sitting in a circle about Him and said, “Look—My mother and My brothers!
Mark 3:35  For whoever does the will of God is My brother and sister and mother.”

Mark 4
Mark 4:1  Again He began teaching beside the sea. A very great crowd gathered around Him, so that He got into a boat on the sea and sat down, while the whole crowd was on the land beside the sea.
Mark 4:2  He taught them many things in parables, and in His teaching He said to them:
Mark 4:3  “Listen! Look, the sower went out to sow.
Mark 4:4  As he sowed, some fell beside the road, and the birds came and ate it up.
Mark 4:5  Other seed fell on rocky ground, where it had little soil, and immediately sprang up because the soil had no depth.
Mark 4:6  When the sun rose, it was scorched, and because it had no root, it withered.
Mark 4:7  Other seed fell among the thorns. The thorns grew up and choked it, and it gave no fruit.
Mark 4:8  Other seeds fell into the good soil and gave fruit, growing up and increasing; they yielded thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.”
Mark 4:9  He said, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”
Mark 4:10  When He was alone, those around Him, together with the Twelve, asked Him about the parables.
Mark 4:11  He said to them, “To you the mystery of the kingdom of God has been given. But for those outside, everything comes in parables,
Mark 4:12  so that, looking, they may look and not see, and hearing, they may hear and not understand, lest they turn back and be forgiven.”
Mark 4:13  He said to them, “Do you not understand this parable? Then how will you understand all the parables?
Mark 4:14  The sower sows the word.
Mark 4:15  These are the ones beside the road where the word is sown: whenever they hear, Satan immediately comes and takes away the word sown into them.
Mark 4:16  Likewise, these are the ones sown on the rocky places: whenever they hear the word, they immediately receive it with joy,
Mark 4:17  but they have no root in themselves and last only for a time. Then, when distress or persecution comes because of the word, they immediately stumble.
Mark 4:18  Others are the ones sown among the thorns. These are the ones who have heard the word,
Mark 4:19  but the cares of the age, the deceitfulness of riches, and desires for other things enter and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
Mark 4:20  Those sown on the good soil are the ones who hear the word, accept it, and bear fruit: thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.”
Mark 4:21  He said to them, “Does the lamp come to be put under the modius basket, or under the bed? Is it not to be put on the lampstand?
Mark 4:22  For nothing is hidden except to be revealed, nor has anything become secret except to come into the open.
Mark 4:23  If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.”
Mark 4:24  He said to them, “Pay attention to what you hear. With the measure you use, it will be measured to you, and more will be added to you.
Mark 4:25  For whoever has will be given more; and whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken from him.”
Mark 4:26  He said, “The kingdom of God is like this: a man casts seed on the ground,
Mark 4:27  and sleeps and rises, night and day, while the seed sprouts and grows—he himself does not know how.
Mark 4:28  The earth bears fruit of itself: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.
Mark 4:29  When the crop is ready, he immediately sends in the sickle, because the harvest has arrived.”
Mark 4:30  He said, “How shall we compare the kingdom of God, or in what parable shall we set it out?
Mark 4:31  It is like a mustard seed, which, when sown on the ground, is smaller than all the seeds on the earth.
Mark 4:32  Yet when sown, it grows up and becomes larger than all the garden plants, and makes great branches, so that the birds of the sky can shelter under its shade.”
Mark 4:33  With many such parables He spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear.
Mark 4:34  He did not speak to them without a parable, but privately He explained everything to His own disciples.
Mark 4:35  On that day, when evening came, He said to them, “Let us cross to the other side.”
Mark 4:36  Leaving the crowd, they took Him with them, just as He was, in the boat. Other boats were with Him.
Mark 4:37  A great windstorm arose, and the waves broke into the boat, so that the boat was already filling.
Mark 4:38  He was in the stern, asleep on the cushion. They woke Him and said to Him, “Teacher, dost Thou not care that we are perishing?”
Mark 4:39  And He awoke, rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Be silent; be still.” And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
Mark 4:40  He said to them, “Why are you cowardly? Do you still have no faith?”
Mark 4:41  They were greatly afraid and said to one another, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?”

Mark 5
Mark 5:1  They came to the other side of the sea, to the country of the Gerasenes.
Mark 5:2  As He stepped out of the boat, a man with an unclean spirit immediately met Him from the tombs.
Mark 5:3  He made his dwelling among the tombs, and no one could bind him anymore, even with a chain.
Mark 5:4  He had often been bound with fetters and chains, but he had torn the chains apart and shattered the fetters. No one had the strength to subdue him.
Mark 5:5  Continually, night and day, among the tombs and on the mountains, he cried out and cut himself with stones.
Mark 5:6  Seeing Jesus from far away, he ran and bowed before Him.
Mark 5:7  He cried out with a loud voice and said, “What hast Thou to do with me, Jesus, Son of God Most High? I adjure Thee by God: do not torment me!”
Mark 5:8  For He had been saying to him, “Come out of the man, unclean spirit!”
Mark 5:9  He asked him, “What is your name?” He said to Him, “Legion is my name, because we are many.”
Mark 5:10  He begged Him earnestly not to send them out of the country.
Mark 5:11  Now a large herd of pigs was feeding there near the mountain.
Mark 5:12  They begged Him, saying, “Send us into the pigs, so that we may enter them.”
Mark 5:13  He allowed them. The unclean spirits came out and entered the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea—about two thousand—and they drowned in the sea.
Mark 5:14  Those tending them fled and reported it in the city and in the fields. People came to see what had happened.
Mark 5:15  They came to Jesus and saw the demon-possessed man sitting, clothed and in his right mind—the one who had had the legion—and they were afraid.
Mark 5:16  Those who had seen it told them what had happened to the demon-possessed man and about the pigs.
Mark 5:17  They began begging Him to leave their territory.
Mark 5:18  As He was boarding the boat, the man who had been demon-possessed begged Him to let him be with Him.
Mark 5:19  He did not allow him, but said to him, “Go home to your own people and report to them how much the Lord has done for you and how He has had mercy on you.”
Mark 5:20  He went away and began proclaiming in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him, and everyone marveled.
Mark 5:21  When Jesus had crossed again in the boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered around Him, and He was beside the sea.
Mark 5:22  One of the synagogue rulers came, named Jairus. Seeing Him, he fell at His feet
Mark 5:23  and begged Him earnestly, saying, “My little daughter is at the point of death. Please come and lay Thy hands on her, so that she may be saved and live.”
Mark 5:24  He went with him. A large crowd followed Him and pressed against Him.
Mark 5:25  A woman who had had a flow of blood for twelve years,
Mark 5:26  and had suffered much under many physicians and spent everything she had, without any benefit but instead growing worse,
Mark 5:27  heard about Jesus. She came behind Him in the crowd and touched His garment.
Mark 5:28  For she was saying, “If I touch even His clothes, I will be saved.”
Mark 5:29  Immediately the source of her blood dried up, and she knew in her body that she was healed of the affliction.
Mark 5:30  Immediately Jesus, recognizing in Himself that power had gone out from Him, turned around in the crowd and said, “Who touched My clothes?”
Mark 5:31  His disciples said to Him, “Thou seest the crowd pressing against Thee, and Thou sayest, ‘Who touched Me?’”
Mark 5:32  He kept looking around to see the woman who had done this.
Mark 5:33  The woman, afraid and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell before Him and told Him the whole truth.
Mark 5:34  And He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has saved you; go in peace, and be well, free from your affliction.”
Mark 5:35  While He was still speaking, people came from the synagogue ruler’s house, saying, “Your daughter has died. Why trouble the Teacher any further?”
Mark 5:36  Jesus, overhearing the word being spoken, said to the synagogue ruler, “Do not fear; only believe.”
Mark 5:37  He allowed no one to accompany Him except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.
Mark 5:38  They came to the synagogue ruler’s house, and He saw a commotion, with people weeping and wailing loudly.
Mark 5:39  He went in and said to them, “Why are you making a commotion and weeping? The child has not died but is sleeping.”
Mark 5:40  They laughed at Him. But He put them all outside, took the child’s father and mother and those with Him, and went in where the child was.
Mark 5:41  Taking the child’s hand, He said to her, “Talitha koum,” which translated means, “Little girl, I say to you, arise!”
Mark 5:42  Immediately the little girl rose and walked around, for she was twelve years old. Immediately they were overcome with great amazement.
Mark 5:43  He gave them strict orders that no one should know this, and said that she should be given something to eat.

Mark 6
Mark 6:1  He left there and came to His hometown, and His disciples followed Him.
Mark 6:2  When the Sabbath came, He began teaching in the synagogue. The many who heard Him were astonished, saying, “Where did this Man get these things? What is this wisdom given to Him? And such mighty works taking place through His hands!
Mark 6:3  Is this not the carpenter, the Son of Mary and brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? Are not His sisters here with us?” They took offense at Him.
Mark 6:4  Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own house.”
Mark 6:5  He could do no mighty work there, except that He laid His hands on a few sick people and healed them.
Mark 6:6  He marveled at their unbelief. Then He went around the surrounding villages, teaching.
Mark 6:7  He called the Twelve to Him and began sending them out two by two, giving them authority over the unclean spirits.
Mark 6:8  He instructed them to take nothing for the journey except a staff alone: no bread, no bag, no copper money in their belt,
Mark 6:9  but to wear sandals, and, “Do not put on two tunics.”
Mark 6:10  He said to them, “Wherever you enter a house, remain there until you leave that place.
Mark 6:11  Whatever place does not receive you, and whose people do not listen to you, shake off the dust beneath your feet as you leave there, as a testimony to them.”
Mark 6:12  They went out and proclaimed that people should repent.
Mark 6:13  They cast out many demons, and anointed many sick people with oil and healed them.
Mark 6:14  King Herod heard of it, for His name had become known. People were saying, “John the baptizer has been raised from the dead, and that is why mighty powers are at work in Him.”
Mark 6:15  Others said, “He is Elijah.” Still others said, “He is a prophet, like one of the prophets.”
Mark 6:16  But when Herod heard, he said, “John, whom I beheaded—he has been raised!”
Mark 6:17  For Herod himself had sent men to seize John and bind him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, because he had married her.
Mark 6:18  For John had been saying to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”
Mark 6:19  Herodias held a grudge against him and wanted to kill him, but she could not.
Mark 6:20  For Herod feared John, knowing him to be a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. When he heard him, he was greatly perplexed, yet he listened to him gladly.
Mark 6:21  An opportune day came when Herod gave a dinner on his birthday for his dignitaries, commanders of thousands, and the leading men of Galilee.
Mark 6:22  His daughter Herodias came in and danced, pleasing Herod and those reclining with him. The king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”
Mark 6:23  He swore to her repeatedly, “Whatever you ask of me, I will give you, up to half my kingdom.”
Mark 6:24  She went out and said to her mother, “What should I ask for?” She said, “The head of John the baptizer.”
Mark 6:25  Immediately she hurried in to the king and made her request, saying, “I want you to give me at once, on a platter, the head of John the Baptist.”
Mark 6:26  The king became deeply grieved, but because of his oaths and those reclining at table, he did not want to refuse her.
Mark 6:27  Immediately the king sent an executioner and ordered him to bring John’s head. He went and beheaded him in prison,
Mark 6:28  brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the girl; the girl gave it to her mother.
Mark 6:29  When his disciples heard, they came and took his corpse and laid it in a tomb.
Mark 6:30  The apostles gathered around Jesus and reported to Him everything they had done and taught.
Mark 6:31  He said to them, “Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little.” For many were coming and going, and they did not even have an opportunity to eat.
Mark 6:32  They went away privately in the boat to a deserted place.
Mark 6:33  People saw them leaving, and many recognized them. They ran there together on foot from all the cities and arrived ahead of them.
Mark 6:34  As He stepped out, He saw a large crowd and was moved with compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. He began teaching them many things.
Mark 6:35  When the hour was already late, His disciples came to Him and said, “The place is deserted, and the hour is already late.
Mark 6:36  Dismiss them, so that they can go into the surrounding fields and villages and buy themselves something to eat.”
Mark 6:37  He answered them, “You give them something to eat.” They said to Him, “Should we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give them something to eat?”
Mark 6:38  He said to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go and see.” When they found out, they said, “Five, and two fish.”
Mark 6:39  He ordered them to have everyone recline in dining groups on the green grass.
Mark 6:40  They reclined in rows, by hundreds and by fifties.
Mark 6:41  He took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, pronounced a blessing, and broke the loaves. He kept giving them to His disciples to set before the people, and He divided the two fish among them all.
Mark 6:42  They all ate and were satisfied.
Mark 6:43  They took up broken pieces, twelve baskets full, and some of the fish.
Mark 6:44  Those who had eaten the loaves were five thousand men.
Mark 6:45  Immediately He compelled His disciples to board the boat and go ahead to the other side, toward Bethsaida, while He Himself dismissed the crowd.
Mark 6:46  After saying farewell to them, He went away to the mountain to pray.
Mark 6:47  When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and He was alone on the land.
Mark 6:48  Seeing them straining at the rowing, for the wind was against them, He came toward them about the fourth watch of the night, walking on the sea. He intended to pass by them.
Mark 6:49  When they saw Him walking on the sea, they thought it was a phantom and cried out,
Mark 6:50  for they all saw Him and were troubled. Immediately He spoke with them and said to them, “Take courage! It is I; do not fear.”
Mark 6:51  He climbed into the boat with them, and the wind ceased. They were utterly astounded within themselves,
Mark 6:52  for they had not understood about the loaves, but their heart was hardened.
Mark 6:53  When they crossed over to land, they came to Gennesaret and moored there.
Mark 6:54  As they stepped out of the boat, people immediately recognized Him
Mark 6:55  and ran through that whole country. They began carrying the sick around on their mats to wherever they heard He was.
Mark 6:56  Wherever He entered villages, cities, or fields, they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged Him to let them touch even the fringe of His garment. As many as touched Him were saved.

Mark 7
Mark 7:1  The Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Him.
Mark 7:2  They saw that some of His disciples were eating their bread with common hands—that is, unwashed.
Mark 7:3  For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands with the fist, holding to the tradition of the elders.
