Mark 7:4  On returning from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they wash themselves. There are many other things they received to observe: washings of cups, jugs, copper vessels, and couches.
Mark 7:5  The Pharisees and the scribes asked Him, “Why do Thy disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with common hands?”
Mark 7:6  He said to them, “Isaiah prophesied well about you hypocrites, as it is written: ‘This people honors Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me.
Mark 7:7  In vain do they worship Me, teaching human commands for doctrine.’
Mark 7:8  You abandon God’s commandment and hold to human tradition.”
Mark 7:9  He said to them, “You set aside God’s commandment very well indeed, so that you may establish your tradition!
Mark 7:10  For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘Let whoever speaks evil of father or mother surely die.’
Mark 7:11  But you say, ‘If a person says to his father or mother, “Whatever benefit you might receive from me is Corban”—that is, a gift—’
Mark 7:12  you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or mother,
Mark 7:13  making void the word of God by your tradition that you have handed down. You do many similar things.”
Mark 7:14  Calling the crowd to Him again, He said to them, “Listen to Me, all of you, and understand.
Mark 7:15  There is nothing outside a person that, by entering him, can defile him. Rather, the things coming out of a person are what defile the person.”
Mark 7:17  When He entered a house away from the crowd, His disciples asked Him about the parable.
Mark 7:18  He said to them, “Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not grasp that everything entering a person from outside cannot defile him,
Mark 7:19  because it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and goes out into the latrine?”—thus cleansing all foods.
Mark 7:20  He said, “What comes out of a person is what defiles the person.
Mark 7:21  For from within, out of people’s hearts, come evil reasonings, acts of sexual immorality, thefts, murders,
Mark 7:22  adulteries, acts of greed, wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, slander, arrogance, foolishness.
Mark 7:23  All these evil things come out from within and defile the person.”
Mark 7:24  He rose from there and went away into the territory of Tyre. He entered a house and wanted no one to know, but He could not remain hidden.
Mark 7:25  Immediately a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit heard about Him, came, and fell at His feet.
Mark 7:26  The woman was Greek, Syrophoenician by birth. She asked Him to cast the demon out of her daughter.
Mark 7:27  He said to her, “Let the children first be satisfied, for it is not good to take the children’s bread and throw it to the little dogs.”
Mark 7:28  She answered and said to Him, “Lord, even the little dogs under the table eat some of the children’s crumbs.”
Mark 7:29  He said to her, “Because of this word, go; the demon has gone out of your daughter.”
Mark 7:30  She went home and found the child lying on the bed, and the demon gone.
Mark 7:31  Leaving the territory of Tyre again, He came through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the middle of the territory of the Decapolis.
Mark 7:32  They brought Him a man who was deaf and had difficulty speaking, and begged Him to lay His hand on him.
Mark 7:33  Taking him aside privately, away from the crowd, He put His fingers into his ears, spat, and touched his tongue.
Mark 7:34  Looking up to heaven, He sighed and said to him, “Ephphatha,” that is, “Be opened.”
Mark 7:35  Immediately his ears were opened, the bond of his tongue was loosened, and he spoke correctly.
Mark 7:36  He ordered them to tell no one. But the more He ordered them, the more abundantly they proclaimed it.
Mark 7:37  They were astonished beyond measure, saying, “He has done everything well! He even makes the deaf hear and the speechless speak.”

Mark 8
Mark 8:1  In those days, when there was again a large crowd and they had nothing to eat, He called the disciples to Him and said to them,
Mark 8:2  “I have compassion on the crowd, because they have already remained with Me for three days and have nothing to eat.
Mark 8:3  If I send them home fasting, they will collapse on the way; and some of them have come from far away.”
Mark 8:4  His disciples answered Him, “Where can anyone get enough bread to satisfy these people here in a wilderness?”
Mark 8:5  He asked them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven.”
Mark 8:6  He instructed the crowd to recline on the ground. Taking the seven loaves, He gave thanks, broke them, and kept giving them to His disciples to set before the people; they set them before the crowd.
Mark 8:7  They also had a few small fish. He blessed them and said to set these before them as well.
Mark 8:8  They ate and were satisfied. They took up seven hampers of leftover pieces.
Mark 8:9  There were about four thousand people. He dismissed them.
Mark 8:10  Immediately He boarded the boat with His disciples and came to the district of Dalmanutha.
Mark 8:11  The Pharisees came out and began disputing with Him, seeking from Him a sign from heaven, to test Him.
Mark 8:12  He sighed deeply in His spirit and said, “Why does this generation seek a sign? Truly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.”
Mark 8:13  Leaving them, He boarded again and went away to the other side.
Mark 8:14  They had forgotten to take bread, and had only one loaf with them in the boat.
Mark 8:15  He warned them, saying, “Watch out! Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod.”
Mark 8:16  They reasoned with one another that they had no bread.
Mark 8:17  Aware of this, He said to them, “Why are you reasoning that you have no bread? Do you not yet grasp or understand? Is your heart hardened?
Mark 8:18  Having eyes, do you not see? Having ears, do you not hear? And do you not remember,
Mark 8:19  when I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of pieces you took up?” They said to Him, “Twelve.”
Mark 8:20  “And when I broke the seven for the four thousand, how many hampers full of pieces did you take up?” They said to Him, “Seven.”
Mark 8:21  He said to them, “Do you not yet understand?”
Mark 8:22  They came to Bethsaida. People brought Him a blind man and begged Him to touch him.
Mark 8:23  Taking the blind man by the hand, He led him out of the village. He spat into his eyes, laid His hands on him, and asked him, “Do you see anything?”
Mark 8:24  He looked up and said, “I see people, for I see them like trees, walking.”
Mark 8:25  Then He laid His hands on his eyes again. The man saw clearly and was restored, and could see everything distinctly.
Mark 8:26  He sent him home, saying, “Do not even enter the village.”
Mark 8:27  Jesus and His disciples went out to the villages of Caesarea Philippi. On the way He questioned His disciples, saying to them, “Who do people say that I am?”
Mark 8:28  They answered Him, saying, “John the Baptist; others, Elijah; and still others, one of the prophets.”
Mark 8:29  He asked them, “But you—who do you say that I am?” Peter answered Him, “Thou art the Christ.”
Mark 8:30  He strictly warned them to tell no one about Him.
Mark 8:31  He began teaching them that the Son of Man must suffer many things, be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, be killed, and rise after three days.
Mark 8:32  He spoke this word openly. Peter took Him aside and began rebuking Him.
Mark 8:33  But He turned, saw His disciples, and rebuked Peter, saying, “Go behind Me, Satan! For you are not setting your mind on God’s things, but on human things.”
Mark 8:34  Calling the crowd to Him with His disciples, He said to them, “If anyone wants to follow behind Me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow Me.
Mark 8:35  For whoever wants to save his life will lose it; but whoever loses his life for My sake and for the gospel will save it.
Mark 8:36  For what does it benefit a person to gain the whole world and forfeit his life?
Mark 8:37  For what can a person give in exchange for his life?
Mark 8:38  Whoever is ashamed of Me and My words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when He comes in the glory of His Father with the holy angels.”

Mark 9
Mark 9:1  He said to them, “Truly I tell you, some standing here will certainly not taste death until they see that the kingdom of God has come in power.”
Mark 9:2  After six days, Jesus took Peter, James, and John with Him and brought them up a high mountain privately, alone. He was transfigured before them,
Mark 9:3  and His clothes became gleaming, exceedingly white, as no cloth bleacher on earth could whiten them.
Mark 9:4  Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus.
Mark 9:5  Peter answered Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three tents: one for Thee, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
Mark 9:6  For he did not know what to answer, because they had become terrified.
Mark 9:7  A cloud came, overshadowing them, and a voice came from the cloud: “This is My beloved Son; listen to Him.”
Mark 9:8  Suddenly, looking around, they no longer saw anyone with them except Jesus alone.
Mark 9:9  As they came down from the mountain, He ordered them to tell no one what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
Mark 9:10  They kept the word to themselves, discussing what rising from the dead meant.
Mark 9:11  They questioned Him, saying, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
Mark 9:12  He said to them, “Elijah indeed comes first and restores all things. Yet how is it written of the Son of Man that He should suffer many things and be treated with contempt?
Mark 9:13  But I tell you that Elijah has also come, and they did to him whatever they wanted, just as it is written of him.”
Mark 9:14  When they came to the disciples, they saw a large crowd around them and scribes disputing with them.
Mark 9:15  Immediately the whole crowd saw Him and was greatly astonished. They ran up and greeted Him.
Mark 9:16  He asked them, “What are you disputing with them?”
Mark 9:17  One from the crowd answered Him, “Teacher, I brought Thee my son, who has a speechless spirit.
Mark 9:18  Wherever it seizes him, it dashes him down; he foams, grinds his teeth, and becomes rigid. I told Thy disciples to cast it out, but they did not have the strength.”
Mark 9:19  He answered them, “O unbelieving generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him to Me.”
Mark 9:20  They brought him to Him. When the spirit saw Him, it immediately convulsed the boy; falling on the ground, he rolled about, foaming.
Mark 9:21  He asked his father, “How long has this been happening to him?” He said, “From childhood.
Mark 9:22  Often it has thrown him both into fire and into water, to destroy him. But if Thou canst do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”
Mark 9:23  Jesus said to him, “‘If Thou canst’! All things are possible for the one who believes.”
Mark 9:24  Immediately the father of the child cried out and said, “I believe; help my unbelief!”
Mark 9:25  Seeing that a crowd was running together, Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, “Speechless and deaf spirit, I command you: come out of him, and enter him no more.”
Mark 9:26  Crying out and convulsing him violently, it came out. The boy became like a dead person, so that most of them said, “He has died.”
Mark 9:27  But Jesus took him by the hand and raised him, and he stood up.
Mark 9:28  When He entered a house, His disciples asked Him privately, “Why could we not cast it out?”
Mark 9:29  He said to them, “This kind can come out by nothing except prayer.”
Mark 9:30  They left there and passed through Galilee, and He did not want anyone to know.
Mark 9:31  For He was teaching His disciples and saying to them, “The Son of Man is being handed over into human hands, and they will kill Him. After He is killed, He will rise after three days.”
Mark 9:32  But they did not understand the saying, and were afraid to ask Him.
Mark 9:33  They came to Capernaum. When He was in the house, He asked them, “What were you discussing on the way?”
Mark 9:34  They remained silent, for on the way they had discussed with one another who was greatest.
Mark 9:35  He sat down, called the Twelve, and said to them, “If anyone wants to be first, he shall be last of all and servant of all.”
Mark 9:36  He took a child, stood the child among them, and, embracing the child, said to them,
Mark 9:37  “Whoever receives one such child in My name receives Me; and whoever receives Me does not receive Me but the One who sent Me.”
Mark 9:38  John said to Him, “Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in Thy name, and we tried to stop him, because he was not following us.”
Mark 9:39  Jesus said, “Do not stop him, for no one who does a mighty work in My name will be able soon afterward to speak evil of Me.
Mark 9:40  For whoever is not against us is for us.
Mark 9:41  Whoever gives you a cup of water to drink in recognition that you belong to Christ, truly I tell you, will certainly not lose his reward.
Mark 9:42  Whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble—it would be better for him if a donkey-driven millstone were placed around his neck and he were thrown into the sea.
Mark 9:43  If your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life maimed than to have two hands and go away into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire.
Mark 9:45  If your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to have two feet and be thrown into Gehenna.
Mark 9:47  If your eye causes you to stumble, cast it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into Gehenna,
Mark 9:48  where their worm does not die and the fire is not extinguished.
Mark 9:49  For everyone will be salted with fire.
Mark 9:50  Salt is good; but if salt becomes saltless, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”

Mark 10
Mark 10:1  He rose from there and came into the territory of Judea and beyond the Jordan. Crowds gathered to Him again, and as was His custom, He again taught them.
Mark 10:2  Pharisees came to Him and asked whether it was lawful for a man to divorce his wife, testing Him.
Mark 10:3  He answered them, “What did Moses command you?”
Mark 10:4  They said, “Moses permitted a man to write a certificate of divorce and dismiss her.”
Mark 10:5  Jesus said to them, “Because of your hardness of heart he wrote you this commandment.
Mark 10:6  But from the beginning of creation, ‘He made them male and female.’
Mark 10:7  ‘For this reason a man shall leave his father and mother and cleave to his wife,
Mark 10:8  and the two shall become one flesh.’ So they are no longer two, but one flesh.
Mark 10:9  Therefore, what God has yoked together, let no human separate.”
Mark 10:10  In the house, the disciples asked Him about this again.
Mark 10:11  He said to them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her.
Mark 10:12  And if she divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery.”
Mark 10:13  People brought children to Him so that He might touch them, but the disciples rebuked them.
Mark 10:14  When Jesus saw it, He was indignant and said to them, “Let the children come to Me; do not stop them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
Mark 10:15  Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will certainly not enter it.”
Mark 10:16  He embraced them and blessed them, laying His hands on them.
Mark 10:17  As He was setting out on the road, a man ran up, knelt before Him, and asked Him, “Good Teacher, what should I do to inherit eternal life?”
Mark 10:18  Jesus said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good except One—God.
Mark 10:19  You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder; do not commit adultery; do not steal; do not bear false witness; do not defraud; honor your father and mother.’”
Mark 10:20  He said to Him, “Teacher, I have kept all these from my youth.”
Mark 10:21  Jesus looked at him, loved him, and said to him, “You lack one thing. Go, sell what you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”
Mark 10:22  But his face fell at the word, and he went away grieved, for he had many possessions.
Mark 10:23  Jesus looked around and said to His disciples, “How hard it will be for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!”
Mark 10:24  The disciples were astounded at His words. But Jesus answered them again, “Children, how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God!
Mark 10:25  It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”
Mark 10:26  They were exceedingly astonished and said to one another, “Then who can be saved?”
Mark 10:27  Jesus looked at them and said, “With humans it is impossible, but not with God; for all things are possible with God.”
Mark 10:28  Peter began saying to Him, “Look, we have left everything and followed Thee.”
Mark 10:29  Jesus said, “Truly I tell you, there is no one who has left house, brothers, sisters, mother, father, children, or fields for My sake and for the sake of the gospel,
Mark 10:30  who will not receive a hundredfold now, in this time—houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and fields, with persecutions—and in the coming age, eternal life.
Mark 10:31  But many who are first will be last, and the last first.”
Mark 10:32  They were on the road going up to Jerusalem. Jesus was going ahead of them, and they were astounded, while those following were afraid. Taking the Twelve aside again, He began telling them what was going to happen to Him:
Mark 10:33  “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes. They will condemn Him to death and hand Him over to the Gentiles.
Mark 10:34  They will mock Him, spit on Him, flog Him, and kill Him, and after three days He will rise.”
Mark 10:35  James and John, the sons of Zebedee, approached Him and said to Him, “Teacher, we want Thee to do for us whatever we ask Thee.”
Mark 10:36  He said to them, “What do you want Me to do for you?”
Mark 10:37  They said to Him, “Grant us to sit, one at Thy right and one at Thy left, in Thy glory.”
Mark 10:38  Jesus said to them, “You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I drink, or be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?”
Mark 10:39  They said to Him, “We can.” Jesus said to them, “You will drink the cup that I drink, and you will be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized.
Mark 10:40  But to sit at My right or at My left is not Mine to give; it is for those for whom it has been prepared.”
Mark 10:41  When the ten heard, they began to be indignant with James and John.
Mark 10:42  Jesus called them to Him and said to them, “You know that those regarded as rulers of the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
Mark 10:43  But it is not so among you. Whoever wants to become great among you shall be your servant,
Mark 10:44  and whoever wants to be first among you shall be slave of all.
Mark 10:45  For even the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom in exchange for many.”
Mark 10:46  They came to Jericho. As He was leaving Jericho with His disciples and a considerable crowd, Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.
Mark 10:47  Hearing that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began crying out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Mark 10:48  Many rebuked him so that he would be silent, but he cried out much more, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Mark 10:49  Jesus stopped and said, “Call him.” They called the blind man, saying to him, “Take courage! Get up; He is calling you.”
Mark 10:50  He threw off his garment, sprang up, and came to Jesus.
Mark 10:51  Jesus answered him, “What do you want Me to do for you?” The blind man said to Him, “Rabbouni, that I may see again.”
Mark 10:52  Jesus said to him, “Go; your faith has saved you.” Immediately he saw again and followed Him on the road.

Mark 11
Mark 11:1  As they drew near Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, He sent two of His disciples
Mark 11:2  and said to them, “Go into the village opposite you. Immediately on entering it, you will find a colt tied, on which no human has ever sat. Untie it and bring it.
Mark 11:3  If anyone says to you, ‘Why are you doing this?’ say, ‘The Lord has need of it, and He will send it back here immediately.’”
Mark 11:4  They went away and found a colt tied at a door outside on the street, and untied it.
Mark 11:5  Some of those standing there said to them, “What are you doing, untying the colt?”
Mark 11:6  They answered them just as Jesus had said, and the people let them go.
Mark 11:7  They brought the colt to Jesus, threw their garments on it, and He sat on it.
Mark 11:8  Many spread their garments on the road; others spread leafy branches they had cut from the fields.
Mark 11:9  Those going ahead and those following cried out, “Hosanna! Blessed is the One who comes in the name of the Lord!
Mark 11:10  Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!”
Mark 11:11  He entered Jerusalem, into the temple. After looking around at everything, since the hour was already late, He went out to Bethany with the Twelve.
Mark 11:12  On the next day, as they came out from Bethany, He became hungry.
Mark 11:13  Seeing from far away a fig tree with leaves, He came to see whether He might find anything on it. When He reached it, He found nothing but leaves, for it was not the season for figs.
Mark 11:14  He addressed it, “May no one ever eat fruit from you again.” His disciples heard it.
Mark 11:15  They came to Jerusalem. He entered the temple and began driving out those selling and those buying in the temple. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves,
Mark 11:16  and would not allow anyone to carry a vessel through the temple.
Mark 11:17  He taught and said to them, “Is it not written, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations’? But you have made it a den of robbers.”
Mark 11:18  The chief priests and the scribes heard, and sought how to destroy Him; for they feared Him, because the whole crowd was astonished at His teaching.
Mark 11:19  Whenever evening came, they went out of the city.
Mark 11:20  Passing by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots.
Mark 11:21  Peter remembered and said to Him, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree that Thou didst curse has withered.”
Mark 11:22  Jesus answered them, “Have faith in God.
Mark 11:23  Truly I tell you, whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that what he says is happening, it will be his.
Mark 11:24  Therefore I tell you, everything you pray and ask for—believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.
Mark 11:25  Whenever you stand praying, forgive if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father in the heavens may also forgive your trespasses.”
Mark 11:27  They came again to Jerusalem. As He walked in the temple, the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders came to Him
Mark 11:28  and said to Him, “By what authority art Thou doing these things? Or who gave Thee this authority to do them?”
Mark 11:29  Jesus said to them, “I will ask you one question. Answer Me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
Mark 11:30  Was John’s baptism from heaven or from humans? Answer Me.”
Mark 11:31  They reasoned with one another, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will say, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’
Mark 11:32  But should we say, ‘From humans’?” They feared the crowd, for everyone held that John truly was a prophet.
Mark 11:33  They answered Jesus, “We do not know.” Jesus said to them, “Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.”

Mark 12
Mark 12:1  He began speaking to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a winepress vat, and built a tower. He leased it to tenant farmers and went abroad.
Mark 12:2  At the proper season he sent a slave to the farmers, to receive from them some of the vineyard’s fruit.
Mark 12:3  They seized him, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.
Mark 12:4  Again he sent another slave to them; they struck that one on the head and dishonored him.
Mark 12:5  He sent another, and they killed that one; and many others—some they beat, and others they killed.
Mark 12:6  He still had one, a beloved son. He sent him to them last, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’
Mark 12:7  But those farmers said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
Mark 12:8  They seized him, killed him, and threw him outside the vineyard.
Mark 12:9  What, then, will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the farmers and give the vineyard to others.
Mark 12:10  Have you not even read this Scripture: ‘The stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner.
Mark 12:11  This came from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?”
Mark 12:12  They sought to seize Him, but feared the crowd, for they knew that He had spoken the parable against them. They left Him and went away.
Mark 12:13  They sent some of the Pharisees and the Herodians to Him, to catch Him in a word.
Mark 12:14  They came and said to Him, “Teacher, we know that Thou art truthful and dost not defer to anyone, for Thou dost not look at people’s outward standing, but dost teach God’s way in truth. Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar or not? Should we give it or not?”
Mark 12:15  Knowing their hypocrisy, He said to them, “Why are you testing Me? Bring Me a denarius so that I may see it.”
Mark 12:16  They brought one. He said to them, “Whose image and inscription is this?” They said to Him, “Caesar’s.”
Mark 12:17  Jesus said to them, “Give back Caesar’s things to Caesar, and God’s things to God.” They marveled greatly at Him.
Mark 12:18  Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Him and questioned Him, saying,
Mark 12:19  “Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if someone’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no child, his brother should take the wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
Mark 12:20  There were seven brothers. The first took a wife, and died leaving no offspring.
Mark 12:21  The second took her and died leaving no offspring, and the third likewise.
Mark 12:22  The seven left no offspring. Last of all, the woman also died.
Mark 12:23  In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be? For the seven had her as wife.”
Mark 12:24  Jesus said to them, “Is this not why you are mistaken: you know neither the Scriptures nor God’s power?
Mark 12:25  For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in the heavens.
Mark 12:26  As for the dead being raised, have you not read in the book of Moses, in the passage about the bush, how God spoke to him, saying, ‘I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob’?
Mark 12:27  He is not God of the dead, but of the living. You are greatly mistaken.”
Mark 12:28  One of the scribes approached, having heard them disputing and seen that He had answered them well. He asked Him, “Which commandment is first of all?”
Mark 12:29  Jesus answered, “The first is, ‘Hear, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.
Mark 12:30  You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart, with your whole soul, with your whole mind, and with your whole strength.’
Mark 12:31  The second is this: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”
Mark 12:32  The scribe said to Him, “Well said, Teacher! Thou hast truly said that He is one, and there is no other besides Him.
Mark 12:33  To love Him with the whole heart, with the whole understanding, and with the whole strength, and to love one’s neighbor as oneself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
Mark 12:34  Seeing that he answered thoughtfully, Jesus said to him, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” No one dared to question Him any further.
Mark 12:35  Jesus responded as He taught in the temple, “How do the scribes say that the Christ is David’s son?
Mark 12:36  David himself said in the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at My right hand until I put Thy enemies beneath Thy feet.’
Mark 12:37  David himself calls Him Lord; how then is He his son?” The large crowd listened to Him gladly.
Mark 12:38  In His teaching He said, “Beware of the scribes who like to walk about in long robes and receive greetings in the marketplaces,
Mark 12:39  the foremost seats in the synagogues, and the foremost reclining places at dinners.
Mark 12:40  They devour widows’ houses and make long prayers as a pretense. These will receive greater judgment.”
Mark 12:41  He sat opposite the treasury and watched how the crowd put copper money into the treasury. Many rich people put in much.
Mark 12:42  And one poor widow came and put in two lepta, which make a quadrans.
Mark 12:43  He called His disciples to Him and said to them, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all those putting into the treasury.
Mark 12:44  For they all put in from their surplus, but she, from her need, put in everything she had—her whole livelihood.”

Mark 13
Mark 13:1  As He was leaving the temple, one of His disciples said to Him, “Teacher, look! What stones and what buildings!”
Mark 13:2  Jesus said to him, “Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone will be left here on another that will not be torn down.”
Mark 13:3  As He sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew questioned Him privately:
Mark 13:4  “Tell us, when will these things be, and what will be the sign when all these things are about to be fulfilled?”
Mark 13:5  Jesus began saying to them, “Watch out that no one leads you astray.
Mark 13:6  Many will come in My name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and will lead many astray.
Mark 13:7  When you hear of wars and reports of wars, do not be alarmed. These must happen, but the end is not yet.
Mark 13:8  For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places; there will be famines. These things are the beginning of birth pains.
Mark 13:9  But watch yourselves. They will hand you over to councils; you will be beaten in synagogues, and you will stand before governors and kings for My sake, as a testimony to them.
Mark 13:10  The gospel must first be proclaimed to all the nations.
Mark 13:11  When they lead you away to hand you over, do not worry beforehand about what to say. Whatever is given you in that hour, say that; for it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.
Mark 13:12  Brother will hand brother over to death, and a father his child. Children will rise against parents and have them put to death.
Mark 13:13  You will be hated by all because of My name. But the one who endures to the end will be saved.
Mark 13:14  When you see the abomination of desolation standing where it must not—let the reader understand—then let those in Judea flee to the mountains.
Mark 13:15  Let the one on the housetop not go down or enter to take anything from his house,
Mark 13:16  and let the one in the field not turn back to take his garment.
Mark 13:17  Woe to those who are pregnant and those nursing infants in those days!
Mark 13:18  Pray that it does not happen in winter.
Mark 13:19  For those days will be distress such as has not occurred from the beginning of the creation that God created until now, and certainly will not occur again.
Mark 13:20  If the Lord had not shortened the days, no flesh would have been saved. But for the sake of the chosen, whom He chose, He shortened the days.
Mark 13:21  Then if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ do not believe it.
Mark 13:22  For false christs and false prophets will arise and give signs and wonders to lead astray, if possible, the chosen.
Mark 13:23  But you, watch out! I have told you everything beforehand.
Mark 13:24  But in those days, after that distress, the sun will be darkened and the moon will not give its light.
Mark 13:25  The stars will be falling from heaven, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.
Mark 13:26  Then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
Mark 13:27  Then He will send the angels and gather His chosen from the four winds, from the end of the earth to the end of heaven.
Mark 13:28  Learn the parable from the fig tree: when its branch has already become tender and puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.
Mark 13:29  So also, when you see these things happening, know that it is near, at the doors.
Mark 13:30  Truly I tell you, this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things happen.
Mark 13:31  Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will certainly not pass away.
Mark 13:32  But concerning that day or hour, no one knows—not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son—except the Father.
Mark 13:33  Watch out; stay awake, for you do not know when the time is.
Mark 13:34  It is like a man going abroad who left his house and gave his slaves authority, each his own work, and commanded the doorkeeper to keep watch.
Mark 13:35  Therefore keep watch, for you do not know when the master of the house is coming: in the evening, at midnight, at cockcrow, or in the morning.
Mark 13:36  Otherwise he may come suddenly and find you sleeping.
Mark 13:37  What I say to you, I say to all: keep watch!”

Mark 14
Mark 14:1  The Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread were two days away. The chief priests and the scribes sought how to seize Him by deceit and kill Him.
Mark 14:2  For they said, “Not during the feast, lest there be a disturbance among the people.”
Mark 14:3  While He was in Bethany, reclining in the house of Simon the leper, a woman came with an alabaster jar of very costly ointment of pure nard. She broke the alabaster jar and poured it over His head.
Mark 14:4  Some were indignant among themselves: “Why has this ointment been wasted?
Mark 14:5  For this ointment could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor.” They scolded her harshly.
Mark 14:6  Jesus said, “Leave her alone. Why are you troubling her? She has done a good work for Me.
Mark 14:7  For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you want, you can do good to them; but you do not always have Me.
Mark 14:8  She did what she could. She has anointed My body beforehand for burial.
Mark 14:9  Truly I tell you, wherever the gospel is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will also be told in remembrance of her.”
Mark 14:10  Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went away to the chief priests to hand Him over to them.
Mark 14:11  When they heard, they rejoiced and promised to give him silver money. He sought how to hand Him over at a suitable time.
Mark 14:12  On the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they sacrificed the Passover, His disciples said to Him, “Where dost Thou want us to go and prepare the Passover for Thee to eat?”
Mark 14:13  He sent two of His disciples and said to them, “Go into the city, and a man carrying an earthenware jar of water will meet you. Follow him.
Mark 14:14  Wherever he enters, say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says: Where is My guest room, where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?’
Mark 14:15  He will show you a large upper room, furnished and ready. Prepare for us there.”
Mark 14:16  The disciples went out, came to the city, and found it just as He had told them. They prepared the Passover.
Mark 14:17  When evening came, He arrived with the Twelve.
Mark 14:18  As they reclined and ate, Jesus said, “Truly I tell you, one of you will hand Me over—one who is eating with Me.”
Mark 14:19  They began to be grieved and said to Him one by one, “Surely not I?”
Mark 14:20  He said to them, “One of the Twelve, the one dipping with Me into the dish.
Mark 14:21  For the Son of Man goes just as it is written about Him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is handed over! It would have been good for that man if he had not been born.”
Mark 14:22  As they ate, He took bread, pronounced a blessing, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “Take; this is My body.”
Mark 14:23  He took a cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
Mark 14:24  He said to them, “This is My blood of the covenant, poured out for many.
Mark 14:25  Truly I tell you, I will certainly no longer drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.”
Mark 14:26  After singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Mark 14:27  Jesus said to them, “You will all stumble, because it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’
Mark 14:28  But after I am raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”
Mark 14:29  Peter said to Him, “Even if all stumble, I will not.”
Mark 14:30  Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, today, this very night, before a rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.”
Mark 14:31  He spoke all the more insistently, “Even if I must die with Thee, I will certainly not deny Thee.” They all said the same.
Mark 14:32  They came to a place whose name was Gethsemane. He said to His disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”
Mark 14:33  He took Peter, James, and John with Him, and began to be deeply alarmed and distressed.
Mark 14:34  He said to them, “My soul is deeply grieved, to the point of death. Remain here and keep watch.”
Mark 14:35  Going forward a little, He fell on the ground and prayed that, if possible, the hour might pass from Him.
Mark 14:36  He said, “Abba, Father, all things are possible for Thee. Take this cup away from Me. Yet not what I will, but what Thou wilt.”
Mark 14:37  He came and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “Simon, are you sleeping? Could you not keep watch for one hour?
Mark 14:38  Keep watch and pray, so that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
Mark 14:39  Again He went away and prayed, saying the same word.
Mark 14:40  Again He came and found them sleeping, for their eyes were weighed down, and they did not know what to answer Him.
Mark 14:41  He came the third time and said to them, “Sleep on now and rest. It is enough. The hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.
Mark 14:42  Rise; let us go. Look, the one handing Me over has drawn near.”
Mark 14:43  Immediately, while He was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived, and with him a crowd with swords and clubs from the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders.
Mark 14:44  The one handing Him over had given them an agreed sign, saying, “The One I kiss is He. Seize Him and lead Him away securely.”
Mark 14:45  He came and immediately approached Him, saying, “Rabbi!” Then he kissed Him.
Mark 14:46  They laid their hands on Him and seized Him.
Mark 14:47  One of those standing nearby drew his sword, struck the high priest’s slave, and cut off his ear.
Mark 14:48  Jesus answered them, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me as though against a robber?
Mark 14:49  Day after day I was with you in the temple, teaching, and you did not seize Me. But this is so that the Scriptures may be fulfilled.”
Mark 14:50  They all left Him and fled.
Mark 14:51  A certain young man was following Him, wearing a linen cloth over his naked body. They seized him,
Mark 14:52  but he left the linen cloth behind and fled naked.
Mark 14:53  They led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests, the elders, and the scribes assembled.
Mark 14:54  Peter followed Him from a distance, as far as inside the high priest’s courtyard. He sat with the attendants and warmed himself at the firelight.
Mark 14:55  The chief priests and the whole council sought testimony against Jesus to put Him to death, but found none.
Mark 14:56  For many bore false witness against Him, but their testimonies did not agree.
Mark 14:57  Some stood up and bore false witness against Him, saying,
Mark 14:58  “We heard Him say, ‘I will tear down this sanctuary made by hands, and in three days I will build another not made by hands.’”
Mark 14:59  Yet even in this their testimony did not agree.
Mark 14:60  The high priest stood up in the midst and questioned Jesus, saying, “Dost Thou answer nothing? What is it these men testify against Thee?”
Mark 14:61  He remained silent and answered nothing. Again the high priest questioned Him and said to Him, “Art Thou the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”
Mark 14:62  Jesus said, “I am. And you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right of the Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”
Mark 14:63  The high priest tore his tunics and said, “What further need have we of witnesses?
Mark 14:64  You heard the blasphemy. What is your judgment?” They all condemned Him as deserving death.
Mark 14:65  Some began spitting on Him, covering His face, striking Him with their fists, and saying to Him, “Prophesy!” The attendants received Him with slaps.
Mark 14:66  While Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the high priest’s female slaves came.
Mark 14:67  Seeing Peter warming himself, she looked at him and said, “You too were with Jesus the Nazarene.”
Mark 14:68  He denied it, saying, “I neither know nor understand what you are saying.” He went outside into the forecourt, and a rooster crowed.
Mark 14:69  The female slave saw him and again began saying to those standing nearby, “This man is one of them.”
Mark 14:70  Again he denied it. After a little while, those standing nearby again said to Peter, “Truly you are one of them, for you are a Galilean.”
Mark 14:71  He began invoking a curse and swearing, “I do not know this Man you are speaking of.”
Mark 14:72  Immediately a rooster crowed a second time. Peter remembered the word Jesus had spoken to him: “Before a rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.” He broke down and wept.

Mark 15
Mark 15:1  Immediately in the morning, the chief priests held a consultation with the elders, the scribes, and the whole council. They bound Jesus, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate.
Mark 15:2  Pilate questioned Him, “Art Thou the King of the Jews?” He answered him, “You say so.”
Mark 15:3  The chief priests accused Him of many things.
Mark 15:4  Pilate questioned Him again, saying, “Dost Thou answer nothing? Look how many accusations they bring against Thee.”
Mark 15:5  But Jesus gave no further answer, so that Pilate marveled.
Mark 15:6  At the feast he used to release for them one prisoner whom they requested.
Mark 15:7  The man called Barabbas was imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder in the uprising.
Mark 15:8  The crowd came up and began asking him to do as he usually did for them.
Mark 15:9  Pilate answered them, “Do you want me to release for you the King of the Jews?”
Mark 15:10  For he knew that the chief priests had handed Him over out of envy.
Mark 15:11  But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas for them instead.
Mark 15:12  Pilate answered them again, “Then what do you want me to do with the One you call the King of the Jews?”
Mark 15:13  They cried out again, “Crucify Him!”
Mark 15:14  Pilate said to them, “Why, what evil has He done?” They cried out all the more, “Crucify Him!”
Mark 15:15  Pilate, wanting to satisfy the crowd, released Barabbas for them. After having Jesus scourged, he handed Him over to be crucified.
Mark 15:16  The soldiers led Him inside the courtyard—that is, the praetorium—and called together the whole cohort.
Mark 15:17  They clothed Him in purple and, after weaving a crown of thorns, put it on Him.
Mark 15:18  They began saluting Him, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
Mark 15:19  They kept striking His head with a reed and spitting on Him, and knelt down to bow before Him.
Mark 15:20  After they had mocked Him, they stripped off the purple and put His own garments on Him. They led Him out to crucify Him.
Mark 15:21  They compelled a passerby, Simon of Cyrene, coming from the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry His cross.
Mark 15:22  They brought Him to the place Golgotha, which translated means Place of a Skull.
Mark 15:23  They offered Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He did not take it.
Mark 15:24  They crucified Him and divided His garments, casting a lot over them to determine who would take what.
Mark 15:25  It was the third hour when they crucified Him.
Mark 15:26  The inscription of the charge against Him was written: “The King of the Jews.”
Mark 15:27  They crucified two robbers with Him, one at His right and one at His left.
Mark 15:29  Those passing by reviled Him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! Thou who dost tear down the sanctuary and build it in three days,
Mark 15:30  save Thyself by coming down from the cross!”
Mark 15:31  Likewise the chief priests, mocking Him among themselves with the scribes, said, “He saved others; He cannot save Himself.
Mark 15:32  Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe.” Those crucified with Him also reproached Him.
Mark 15:33  When the sixth hour came, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
Mark 15:34  At the ninth hour, Jesus cried out with a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which translated means, “My God, My God, why hast Thou forsaken Me?”
Mark 15:35  Some of those standing nearby heard and said, “Look, He is calling Elijah.”
Mark 15:36  Someone ran, filled a sponge with sour wine, placed it on a reed, and gave Him a drink, saying, “Leave Him; let us see whether Elijah comes to take Him down.”
Mark 15:37  Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed His last.
Mark 15:38  The curtain of the sanctuary was torn in two from top to bottom.
Mark 15:39  When the centurion standing opposite Him saw that He breathed His last in this way, he said, “Truly this Man was God’s Son.”
Mark 15:40  There were also women watching from a distance, among them Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the Little and Joses, and Salome.
Mark 15:41  When He was in Galilee, they had followed Him and served Him; there were also many other women who had come up with Him to Jerusalem.
Mark 15:42  Evening had already come, and since it was Preparation—that is, the day before the Sabbath—
Mark 15:43  Joseph of Arimathea, a respected council member who himself was also awaiting the kingdom of God, came and dared to enter before Pilate and ask for Jesus’ body.
Mark 15:44  Pilate marveled that He was already dead. Calling the centurion to him, he asked whether He had died some time ago.
Mark 15:45  When he learned from the centurion, he granted the corpse to Joseph.
Mark 15:46  Joseph bought a linen cloth, took Him down, wrapped Him in the cloth, and laid Him in a tomb cut out of rock. He rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.
Mark 15:47  Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses watched where He was laid.

Mark 16
Mark 16:1  When the Sabbath had passed, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices so that they might come and anoint Him.
Mark 16:2  Very early on the first day of the week, they came to the tomb when the sun had risen.
Mark 16:3  They said to one another, “Who will roll the stone away from the entrance of the tomb for us?”
Mark 16:4  Looking up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away, for it was very large.
Mark 16:5  They entered the tomb and saw a young man sitting on the right, clothed in a white robe, and they were greatly alarmed.
Mark 16:6  He said to them, “Do not be alarmed. You seek Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified. He has been raised; He is not here. Look, the place where they laid Him.
Mark 16:7  But go, tell His disciples and Peter, ‘He is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see Him, just as He told you.’”
Mark 16:8  They went out and fled from the tomb, for trembling and astonishment held them. They said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.
Mark 16:9  ⟦After He had risen early on the first day of the week, He appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom He had cast out seven demons.
Mark 16:10  She went and reported to those who had been with Him, as they mourned and wept.
Mark 16:11  When they heard that He was alive and had been seen by her, they disbelieved.
Mark 16:12  After these things, He appeared in another form to two of them as they were walking, going into the country.
Mark 16:13  They went away and reported to the rest; they did not believe them either.
Mark 16:14  Later He appeared to the Eleven themselves as they reclined at table, and reproached their unbelief and hardness of heart because they had not believed those who had seen Him raised.
Mark 16:15  He said to them, “Go into the whole world and proclaim the gospel to all creation.
Mark 16:16  The one who believes and is baptized will be saved; the one who disbelieves will be condemned.
Mark 16:17  These signs will accompany those who believe: in My name they will cast out demons; they will speak in new tongues;
Mark 16:18  and with their hands they will pick up snakes; and if they drink anything deadly, it will certainly not harm them; they will lay hands on the sick, and they will be well.”
Mark 16:19  So the Lord Jesus, after speaking to them, was taken up into heaven and sat at the right of God.
Mark 16:20  They went out and proclaimed everywhere, while the Lord worked with them and confirmed the word through the accompanying signs.⟧

LUKE

Luke 1
Luke 1:1  Since many have undertaken to compile an account of the events fulfilled among us,
Luke 1:2  just as those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and servants of the word handed them down to us,
Luke 1:3  it seemed good to me also, having followed everything carefully from the beginning, to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus,
Luke 1:4  so that you may know the certainty of the matters in which you have been instructed.
Luke 1:5  In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah, of the division of Abijah. He had a wife from the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
Luke 1:6  Both were righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the Lord’s commandments and ordinances.
Luke 1:7  They had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and both were advanced in years.
Luke 1:8  While he was serving as priest before God in the order of his division,
Luke 1:9  according to the priesthood’s custom, he was chosen by lot to enter the Lord’s sanctuary and burn incense.
Luke 1:10  The whole multitude of the people was praying outside at the hour of incense.
Luke 1:11  An angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right of the altar of incense.
Luke 1:12  Zechariah was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him.
Luke 1:13  But the angel said to him, “Do not fear, Zechariah, for your petition has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall name him John.
Luke 1:14  You will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth,
Luke 1:15  for he will be great before the Lord. He will certainly drink neither wine nor strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb.
Luke 1:16  He will turn many of the sons of Israel to the Lord their God.
Luke 1:17  He himself will go before Him in Elijah’s spirit and power, to turn fathers’ hearts toward children and the disobedient to the understanding of the righteous, to prepare for the Lord a people made ready.”
Luke 1:18  Zechariah said to the angel, “How will I know this? For I am an old man, and my wife is advanced in years.”
Luke 1:19  The angel answered him, “I am Gabriel, who stands before God, and I was sent to speak to you and announce this good news to you.
Luke 1:20  And behold, you will be silent and unable to speak until the day these things happen, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled at their appointed time.”
Luke 1:21  The people were waiting for Zechariah and wondering at his delay in the sanctuary.
Luke 1:22  When he came out, he could not speak to them, and they realized that he had seen a vision in the sanctuary. He kept making signs to them and remained mute.
Luke 1:23  When the days of his service were completed, he went home.
Luke 1:24  After those days his wife Elizabeth conceived, and she kept herself secluded for five months, saying,
Luke 1:25  “This is what the Lord has done for me in these days, when He looked upon me to take away my disgrace among people.”
Luke 1:26  In the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee named Nazareth,
Luke 1:27  to a virgin betrothed to a man named Joseph, of David’s house. The virgin’s name was Mary.
Luke 1:28  And he entered and said to her, “Rejoice, you who have been favoured! The Lord is with you.”
Luke 1:29  She was greatly troubled at the saying and considered what sort of greeting this might be.
Luke 1:30  The angel said to her, “Do not fear, Mary, for you have found grace with God.
Luke 1:31  And behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a Son, and you shall name Him Jesus.
Luke 1:32  He will be great and will be called Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give Him the throne of His father David,
Luke 1:33  and He will reign over Jacob’s house forever, and His kingdom will have no end.”
Luke 1:34  Mary said to the angel, “How will this be, since I do not know a man?”
Luke 1:35  The angel answered her, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; and so the holy One to be born will be called Son of God.
Luke 1:36  And behold, your relative Elizabeth has also conceived a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month for her who was called barren,
Luke 1:37  for no word from God will be powerless.”
Luke 1:38  Mary said, “Behold, I am the Lord’s servant. May it happen to me according to your word.” Then the angel departed from her.
Luke 1:39  In those days Mary arose and went in haste into the hill country, to a city of Judah.
Luke 1:40  She entered Zechariah’s house and greeted Elizabeth.
Luke 1:41  When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the infant leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
Luke 1:42  She cried out with a loud shout and said, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
Luke 1:43  And how is it that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
Luke 1:44  For behold, when the sound of your greeting entered my ears, the infant in my womb leaped with gladness.
Luke 1:45  And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of the things spoken to her from the Lord.”
Luke 1:46  Mary said, “My soul magnifies the Lord,
Luke 1:47  and my spirit rejoiced in God my Savior,
Luke 1:48  because He looked upon the lowly condition of His servant. For behold, from now on all generations will call me blessed,
Luke 1:49  because the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is His name.
Luke 1:50  His mercy is for generations and generations upon those who fear Him.
Luke 1:51  He has performed a mighty deed with His arm; He scattered the proud in the thought of their heart.
Luke 1:52  He brought rulers down from thrones and raised up the lowly.
Luke 1:53  He filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty.
Luke 1:54  He helped Israel His servant, remembering mercy,
Luke 1:55  as He spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and his offspring forever.”
Luke 1:56  Mary stayed with her about three months and returned to her home.
Luke 1:57  When Elizabeth’s time to give birth had come, she bore a son.
Luke 1:58  Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had magnified His mercy toward her, and they rejoiced with her.
Luke 1:59  On the eighth day they came to circumcise the child and were calling him Zechariah after his father’s name.
Luke 1:60  But his mother answered, “No; he shall be called John.”
Luke 1:61  They said to her, “No one among your relatives is called by this name.”
Luke 1:62  They made signs to his father to ask what he wanted the child to be called.
Luke 1:63  He asked for a writing tablet and wrote, “His name is John.” And they all wondered.
Luke 1:64  Immediately his mouth and tongue were opened, and he spoke, blessing God.
Luke 1:65  Fear came upon all who lived around them, and all these matters were discussed throughout the whole hill country of Judea.
Luke 1:66  Everyone who heard took these matters to heart, saying, “What then will this child become?” For the Lord’s hand was indeed with him.
Luke 1:67  His father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying,
Luke 1:68  “Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, because He has visited and accomplished redemption for His people,
Luke 1:69  and has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of David His servant,
Luke 1:70  as He spoke through the mouth of His holy prophets from long ago:
Luke 1:71  salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us,
Luke 1:72  to show mercy to our fathers and remember His holy covenant,
Luke 1:73  the oath He swore to Abraham our father, to grant us
Luke 1:74  that, rescued from our enemies’ hand, we might serve Him without fear,
Luke 1:75  in holiness and righteousness before Him all our days.
Luke 1:76  And you also, child, will be called prophet of the Most High, for you will go before the Lord to prepare His ways,
Luke 1:77  to give His people knowledge of salvation in the forgiveness of their sins,
Luke 1:78  through the tender mercy of our God, by which the dawn from on high will visit us,
Luke 1:79  to shine upon those who sit in darkness and death’s shadow, to direct our feet into a way of peace.”
Luke 1:80  The child grew and became strong in spirit. He remained in the wilderness until the day of his public appearance to Israel.

Luke 2
Luke 2:1  In those days a decree went out from Caesar Augustus for all the inhabited world to be registered.
Luke 2:2  This first registration took place while Quirinius was governing Syria.
Luke 2:3  Everyone went to be registered, each to his own city.
Luke 2:4  Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the city of Nazareth, into Judea, to David’s city, which is called Bethlehem, because he belonged to David’s house and family,
Luke 2:5  to be registered with Mary, who was betrothed to him and was pregnant.
Luke 2:6  While they were there, the time came for her to give birth.
Luke 2:7  She bore her firstborn Son, wrapped Him in swaddling cloths, and laid Him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the lodging place.
Luke 2:8  In that same region there were shepherds living in the fields and keeping watch over their flock through the watches of the night.
Luke 2:9  An angel of the Lord stood beside them, and the Lord’s glory shone around them; they feared with a great fear.
Luke 2:10  The angel said to them, “Do not fear, for behold, I announce to you good news of great joy, which will be for all the people:
Luke 2:11  today in David’s city a Savior has been born for you, who is Christ the Lord.
Luke 2:12  This is the sign for you: you will find an infant wrapped in swaddling cloths and lying in a manger.”
Luke 2:13  Suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army, praising God and saying,
Luke 2:14  “Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace among people of His favour.”
Luke 2:15  When the angels had departed from them into heaven, the shepherds said to one another, “Let us go over to Bethlehem and see this event that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”
Luke 2:16  They came in haste and found Mary and Joseph, and the infant lying in the manger.
Luke 2:17  When they saw Him, they made known the saying spoken to them about this Child.
Luke 2:18  Everyone who heard wondered at what the shepherds told them.
Luke 2:19  But Mary kept all these matters, pondering them in her heart.
Luke 2:20  The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for everything they had heard and seen, just as it had been spoken to them.
Luke 2:21  When eight days were completed for His circumcision, He was named Jesus, the name given by the angel before He was conceived in the womb.
Luke 2:22  When the days of their purification according to Moses’ law were completed, they brought Him up to Jerusalem to present Him to the Lord,
Luke 2:23  as it is written in the Lord’s law: “Every male opening the womb shall be called holy to the Lord,”
Luke 2:24  and to give a sacrifice according to what is said in the Lord’s law: “A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”
Luke 2:25  And behold, there was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon. This man was righteous and devout, awaiting Israel’s consolation, and the Holy Spirit was upon him.
Luke 2:26  It had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before he saw the Lord’s Christ.
Luke 2:27  He came in the Spirit into the temple. When the parents brought in the Child Jesus to do for Him what was customary under the law,
Luke 2:28  he received Him into his arms, blessed God, and said,
Luke 2:29  “Now, Master, Thou art releasing Thy servant in peace according to Thy word,
Luke 2:30  because my eyes have seen Thy salvation,
Luke 2:31  which Thou didst prepare in the sight of all peoples:
Luke 2:32  a light for revelation to the nations and glory for Thy people Israel.”
Luke 2:33  His father and mother were wondering at what was being said about Him.
Luke 2:34  Simeon blessed them and said to His mother Mary, “Behold, this One is appointed for the fall and rising of many in Israel, and for a sign spoken against—
Luke 2:35  and a sword will pass through your own soul also—so that thoughts from many hearts may be revealed.”
Luke 2:36  There was also a prophetess, Anna, daughter of Phanuel, from the tribe of Asher. She was very old. She had lived with her husband for seven years after marrying as a virgin,
Luke 2:37  and had been a widow until the age of eighty-four. She did not leave the temple, serving with fasts and petitions night and day.
Luke 2:38  Coming up at that very hour, she gave thanks to God and spoke about Him to everyone awaiting Jerusalem’s redemption.
Luke 2:39  When they had completed everything according to the Lord’s law, they returned to Galilee, to their own city of Nazareth.
Luke 2:40  The Child grew and became strong, being filled with wisdom, and God’s grace was upon Him.
Luke 2:41  His parents went each year to Jerusalem for the Festival of Passover.
Luke 2:42  When He became twelve years old, they went up according to the festival’s custom.
Luke 2:43  When the festival days were over and they were returning, the boy Jesus remained in Jerusalem, and His parents did not know.
Luke 2:44  Supposing Him to be in the traveling company, they went a day’s journey and searched for Him among their relatives and acquaintances.
Luke 2:45  When they did not find Him, they returned to Jerusalem searching for Him.
Luke 2:46  After three days they found Him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and questioning them.
Luke 2:47  All who heard Him were astonished at His understanding and answers.
Luke 2:48  When His parents saw Him, they were overwhelmed. His mother said to Him, “Child, why hast Thou treated us this way? Behold, Thy father and I have been searching for Thee in anguish.”
Luke 2:49  He said to them, “Why were you searching for Me? Did you not know that I must be in what belongs to My Father?”
Luke 2:50  But they did not understand the saying He spoke to them.
Luke 2:51  He went down with them and came to Nazareth, and He remained subject to them. His mother kept all these matters in her heart.
Luke 2:52  Jesus advanced in wisdom and age, and in favor with God and people.

Luke 3
Luke 3:1  In the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar’s rule, when Pontius Pilate governed Judea, Herod was tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip tetrarch of the region of Iturea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,
Luke 3:2  during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, God’s word came to John, Zechariah’s son, in the wilderness.
Luke 3:3  He went into all the region around the Jordan, proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins,
Luke 3:4  as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet: “A voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the Lord’s way; make His paths straight.
Luke 3:5  Every ravine will be filled, and every mountain and hill brought low. The crooked will become straight, and the rough ways smooth roads,
Luke 3:6  and all flesh will see God’s salvation.”
Luke 3:7  So he said to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him, “Brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee the coming wrath?
Luke 3:8  Produce fruits worthy of repentance, and do not begin saying among yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as father.’ For I tell you that God can raise up children for Abraham from these stones.
Luke 3:9  Already the axe also lies at the root of the trees. Therefore every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into fire.”
Luke 3:10  The crowds asked him, “What then should we do?”
Luke 3:11  He answered them, “Let the one who has two tunics share with the one who has none, and let the one who has food do likewise.”
Luke 3:12  Tax collectors also came to be baptized and said to him, “Teacher, what should we do?”
Luke 3:13  He said to them, “Collect nothing beyond what has been appointed for you.”
Luke 3:14  Soldiers also asked him, “And we, what should we do?” He said to them, “Extort from no one, do not make false accusations, and be content with your pay.”
Luke 3:15  As the people were waiting expectantly and everyone was considering in their hearts whether John might be the Christ,
Luke 3:16  John answered them all, “I baptize you with water, but One stronger than I is coming, whose sandal strap I am not worthy to untie. He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire.
Luke 3:17  His winnowing fork is in His hand, to cleanse His threshing floor thoroughly and gather the wheat into His storehouse; but the chaff He will burn with unquenchable fire.”
Luke 3:18  With many other exhortations also, he announced good news to the people.
Luke 3:19  But Herod the tetrarch, rebuked by him concerning Herodias, his brother’s wife, and all the evil things Herod had done,
Luke 3:20  added this also to them all: he shut John up in prison.
Luke 3:21  When all the people were baptized, and Jesus also had been baptized and was praying, heaven was opened,
Luke 3:22  and the Holy Spirit descended upon Him in bodily form like a dove. A voice came from heaven: “Thou art My beloved Son; in Thee I have taken delight.”
Luke 3:23  Jesus Himself was about thirty years old when He began His ministry. He was the son, as was supposed, of Joseph, of Heli,
Luke 3:24  of Matthat, of Levi, of Melchi, of Jannai, of Joseph,
Luke 3:25  of Mattathias, of Amos, of Nahum, of Esli, of Naggai,
Luke 3:26  of Maath, of Mattathias, of Semein, of Josech, of Joda,
Luke 3:27  of Joanan, of Rhesa, of Zerubbabel, of Shealtiel, of Neri,
Luke 3:28  of Melchi, of Addi, of Cosam, of Elmadam, of Er,
Luke 3:29  of Jesus, of Eliezer, of Jorim, of Matthat, of Levi,
Luke 3:30  of Simeon, of Judah, of Joseph, of Jonam, of Eliakim,
Luke 3:31  of Melea, of Menna, of Mattatha, of Nathan, of David,
Luke 3:32  of Jesse, of Obed, of Boaz, of Sala, of Nahshon,
Luke 3:33  of Amminadab, of Admin, of Arni, of Hezron, of Perez, of Judah,
Luke 3:34  of Jacob, of Isaac, of Abraham, of Terah, of Nahor,
Luke 3:35  of Serug, of Reu, of Peleg, of Eber, of Shelah,
Luke 3:36  of Cainan, of Arphaxad, of Shem, of Noah, of Lamech,
Luke 3:37  of Methuselah, of Enoch, of Jared, of Mahalalel, of Cainan,
Luke 3:38  of Enosh, of Seth, of Adam, of God.

Luke 4
Luke 4:1  Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led in the Spirit in the wilderness
Luke 4:2  for forty days, being tested by the devil. He ate nothing during those days, and when they were completed He was hungry.
Luke 4:3  The devil said to Him, “If Thou art God’s Son, tell this stone to become bread.”
Luke 4:4  Jesus answered him, “It is written: ‘Man shall not live by bread alone.’”
Luke 4:5  Taking Him up, the devil showed Him all the kingdoms of the inhabited world in a moment of time.
Luke 4:6  The devil said to Him, “I will give Thee all this authority and their glory, because it has been handed over to me, and I give it to whomever I wish.
Luke 4:7  Therefore, if Thou dost bow down before me, it will all be Thine.”
Luke 4:8  Jesus answered him, “It is written: ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and Him alone shall you serve.’”
Luke 4:9  He brought Him to Jerusalem, placed Him on the temple’s pinnacle, and said to Him, “If Thou art God’s Son, throw Thyself down from here,
Luke 4:10  for it is written: ‘He will command His angels concerning Thee, to guard Thee,’
Luke 4:11  and, ‘They will lift Thee upon their hands, lest Thou strike Thy foot against a stone.’”
Luke 4:12  Jesus answered him, “It has been said: ‘You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.’”
Luke 4:13  Having completed every test, the devil departed from Him until an opportune time.
Luke 4:14  Jesus returned in the Spirit’s power into Galilee, and a report about Him spread throughout the whole surrounding region.
Luke 4:15  He taught in their synagogues, being glorified by everyone.
Luke 4:16  He came to Nazareth, where He had been brought up, and according to His custom entered the synagogue on the Sabbath day. He stood up to read.
Luke 4:17  The scroll of the prophet Isaiah was given to Him. Unrolling it, He found the place where it was written:
Luke 4:18  “The Spirit of the Lord is upon Me, because He anointed Me to proclaim good news to the poor. He has sent Me to proclaim release to captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to let the crushed go free,
Luke 4:19  to proclaim the Lord’s year of favor.”
Luke 4:20  He rolled up the scroll, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down. The eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed on Him.
Luke 4:21  He began to say to them, “Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your ears.”
Luke 4:22  All bore witness to Him and wondered at the words of grace coming from His mouth. They said, “Is this not Joseph’s son?”
Luke 4:23  He said to them, “Surely you will tell Me this proverb: ‘Physician, heal yourself.’ ‘Do here in Thy homeland also everything we heard happened in Capernaum.’”
Luke 4:24  He said, “Amen, I tell you, no prophet is acceptable in his homeland.
Luke 4:25  But in truth I tell you, there were many widows in Israel in Elijah’s days, when heaven was shut for three years and six months and a great famine came over the whole land.
Luke 4:26  Yet Elijah was sent to none of them except to a widow at Zarephath in Sidon’s territory.
Luke 4:27  And there were many leprous people in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, but none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian.”
Luke 4:28  Everyone in the synagogue was filled with anger when they heard these things.
Luke 4:29  They rose, threw Him out of the city, and led Him to the brow of the hill on which their city was built, intending to hurl Him down.
Luke 4:30  But He passed through their midst and went on His way.
Luke 4:31  He went down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and was teaching them on the Sabbaths.
Luke 4:32  They were overwhelmed at His teaching, because His word was with authority.
Luke 4:33  In the synagogue was a man who had the spirit of an unclean demon. He cried out with a loud voice,
Luke 4:34  “Ah! What have we to do with Thee, Jesus of Nazareth? Hast Thou come to destroy us? I know who Thou art: God’s Holy One.”
Luke 4:35  Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent and come out of him!” The demon threw him down in their midst and came out of him without harming him.
Luke 4:36  Amazement came upon everyone, and they said to one another, “What is this word? With authority and power He commands the unclean spirits, and they come out!”
Luke 4:37  A report about Him went out into every place in the surrounding region.
Luke 4:38  Leaving the synagogue, He entered Simon’s house. Simon’s mother-in-law was gripped by a high fever, and they asked Him about her.
Luke 4:39  Standing over her, He rebuked the fever, and it left her. Immediately she rose and served them.
Luke 4:40  As the sun was setting, everyone who had people sick with various diseases brought them to Him. He laid His hands on each one and healed them.
Luke 4:41  Demons also came out of many, crying, “Thou art God’s Son!” He rebuked them and would not let them speak, because they knew He was the Christ.
Luke 4:42  When day came, He went out to a deserted place. The crowds searched for Him, came to Him, and tried to keep Him from departing from them.
Luke 4:43  But He said to them, “I must announce the good news of God’s kingdom to the other cities also, because for this I was sent.”
Luke 4:44  And He continued proclaiming in the synagogues of Judea.

Luke 5
Luke 5:1  As the crowd pressed upon Him to hear God’s word, He was standing beside the lake of Gennesaret.
Luke 5:2  He saw two boats beside the lake; the fishermen had left them and were washing their nets.
Luke 5:3  He entered one of the boats, which belonged to Simon, and asked him to put out a little from the land. Sitting down, He taught the crowds from the boat.
Luke 5:4  When He finished speaking, He said to Simon, “Put out into the deep water, and let down your nets for a catch.”
Luke 5:5  Simon answered, “Master, we labored through the whole night and caught nothing, but at Thy word I will let down the nets.”
Luke 5:6  When they did this, they enclosed a great multitude of fish, and their nets began to tear.
Luke 5:7  They signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them. They came and filled both boats, so that they began to sink.
Luke 5:8  When Simon Peter saw it, he fell at Jesus’ knees, saying, “Depart from me, Lord, because I am a sinful man.”
Luke 5:9  For amazement had seized him and everyone with him at the catch of fish they had taken,
Luke 5:10  and likewise James and John, Zebedee’s sons, who were Simon’s partners. Jesus said to Simon, “Do not fear. From now on you will be catching people alive.”
Luke 5:11  They brought the boats to land, left everything, and followed Him.
Luke 5:12  While He was in one of the cities, behold, there was a man full of leprosy. Seeing Jesus, he fell on his face and petitioned Him, saying, “Lord, if Thou art willing, Thou canst cleanse me.”
Luke 5:13  Stretching out His hand, He touched him and said, “I am willing; be cleansed.” Immediately the leprosy departed from him.
Luke 5:14  He commanded him to tell no one: “But go, show yourself to the priest, and make the offering for your cleansing as Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.”
Luke 5:15  Yet the report about Him spread all the more, and large crowds gathered to hear and to be healed of their illnesses.
Luke 5:16  But He kept withdrawing to deserted places and praying.
Luke 5:17  On one of those days He was teaching, and Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there. They had come from every village of Galilee and Judea and from Jerusalem; and the Lord’s power was present for Him to heal.
Luke 5:18  And behold, men were carrying on a bed a man who was paralyzed. They sought to bring him in and place him before Him.
Luke 5:19  Finding no way to bring him in because of the crowd, they went up onto the roof and lowered him through the tiles with his little bed into their midst, before Jesus.
Luke 5:20  Seeing their faith, He said, “Man, your sins are forgiven you.”
Luke 5:21  The scribes and Pharisees began to reason, saying, “Who is this who speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins except God alone?”
Luke 5:22  Jesus recognized their thoughts and answered them, “What are you reasoning in your hearts?
Luke 5:23  Which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven you,’ or to say, ‘Rise and walk’?
Luke 5:24  But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—He said to the paralyzed man—“I tell you, rise, take up your little bed, and go home.”
Luke 5:25  Immediately he rose before them, took up what he had been lying on, and went home glorifying God.
Luke 5:26  Astonishment seized everyone, and they glorified God and were filled with fear, saying, “We have seen extraordinary things today.”
Luke 5:27  After this He went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth, and said to him, “Follow Me.”
Luke 5:28  Leaving everything, he rose and followed Him.
Luke 5:29  Levi gave a great reception for Him in his house. A large crowd of tax collectors and others was reclining with them.
Luke 5:30  The Pharisees and their scribes grumbled to His disciples, saying, “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”
Luke 5:31  Jesus answered them, “Those who are healthy have no need of a physician, but those who are ill do.
Luke 5:32  I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
Luke 5:33  They said to Him, “John’s disciples fast often and offer petitions, and likewise those of the Pharisees, but Thine eat and drink.”
Luke 5:34  Jesus said to them, “Can you make the bridegroom’s companions fast while the bridegroom is with them?
Luke 5:35  But days will come, and when the bridegroom is taken from them, then they will fast in those days.”
Luke 5:36  He also told them a parable: “No one tears a patch from a new garment and puts it on an old garment. Otherwise he will tear the new one, and the patch from the new will not match the old.
Luke 5:37  And no one puts new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise the new wine will burst the skins, and it will be poured out and the skins destroyed.
Luke 5:38  But new wine must be put into fresh wineskins.
Luke 5:39  And no one who has drunk old wine desires new, for he says, ‘The old is good.’”

Luke 6
Luke 6:1  On a Sabbath He was passing through grainfields. His disciples plucked the ears, rubbed them in their hands, and ate.
Luke 6:2  Some of the Pharisees said, “Why are you doing what is not lawful on the Sabbaths?”
Luke 6:3  Jesus answered them, “Have you not even read what David did when he and those with him were hungry,
Luke 6:4  how he entered God’s house, took and ate the loaves of the presentation, and gave them to those with him, although no one except the priests alone may lawfully eat them?”
Luke 6:5  He said to them, “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
Luke 6:6  On another Sabbath He entered the synagogue and taught. A man was there whose right hand was withered.
Luke 6:7  The scribes and Pharisees watched closely to see whether He would heal on the Sabbath, so that they might find a way to accuse Him.
Luke 6:8  But He knew their thoughts and said to the man with the withered hand, “Rise and stand in the middle.” He rose and stood.
Luke 6:9  Jesus said to them, “I ask you: Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or do evil, to save a life or destroy it?”
Luke 6:10  Looking around at all of them, He said to him, “Stretch out your hand.” He did so, and his hand was restored.
Luke 6:11  They were filled with mindless anger and discussed with one another what they might do to Jesus.
Luke 6:12  In those days He went out to the mountain to pray, and spent the night in prayer to God.
