Luke 6:13  When day came, He called His disciples and chose twelve from them, whom He also named apostles:
Luke 6:14  Simon, whom He also named Peter, and his brother Andrew, and James and John, and Philip and Bartholomew,
Luke 6:15  and Matthew and Thomas, and James son of Alphaeus, and Simon called the Zealot,
Luke 6:16  and Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.
Luke 6:17  He came down with them and stood on a level place. There was a large crowd of His disciples and a great multitude of the people from all Judea, Jerusalem, and the coastal region of Tyre and Sidon.
Luke 6:18  They had come to hear Him and be healed of their diseases; those troubled by unclean spirits were also healed.
Luke 6:19  The whole crowd sought to touch Him, because power went out from Him and healed everyone.
Luke 6:20  Lifting His eyes toward His disciples, He said, “Blessed are you who are poor, because yours is God’s kingdom.
Luke 6:21  Blessed are you who hunger now, because you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, because you will laugh.
Luke 6:22  Blessed are you when people hate you, when they exclude you, reproach you, and cast out your name as evil because of the Son of Man.
Luke 6:23  Rejoice on that day and leap, for behold, your reward is great in heaven; their fathers treated the prophets in the same way.
Luke 6:24  But woe to you who are rich, because you have received your consolation.
Luke 6:25  Woe to you who are filled now, because you will hunger. Woe to you who laugh now, because you will mourn and weep.
Luke 6:26  Woe when all people speak well of you, for their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way.
Luke 6:27  But I say to you who hear: Love your enemies; do good to those who hate you.
Luke 6:28  Bless those who curse you; pray for those who mistreat you.
Luke 6:29  Offer the other cheek also to the one striking you on the cheek; and from the one taking your cloak, do not withhold your tunic also.
Luke 6:30  Give to everyone who asks you, and do not demand back your belongings from the one who takes them.
Luke 6:31  As you wish people to do to you, do likewise to them.
Luke 6:32  If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.
Luke 6:33  If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do the same.
Luke 6:34  If you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners to receive the equivalent back.
Luke 6:35  But love your enemies, do good, and lend, expecting nothing back. Your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, because He is kind to the ungrateful and evil.
Luke 6:36  Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
Luke 6:37  Do not judge, and you will certainly not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will certainly not be condemned. Release, and you will be released.
Luke 6:38  Give, and it will be given to you. They will put into your lap a good measure, pressed down, shaken together, overflowing; for by the measure you measure, it will be measured back to you.”
Luke 6:39  He also told them a parable: “Can a blind person guide a blind person? Will they not both fall into a pit?
Luke 6:40  A disciple is not above the teacher, but everyone fully trained will be like his teacher.
Luke 6:41  Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?
Luke 6:42  How can you say to your brother, ‘Brother, let me take out the speck in your eye,’ when you yourself do not see the beam in your own eye? Hypocrite! First take the beam out of your eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother’s eye.
Luke 6:43  For no good tree produces rotten fruit, nor again does a rotten tree produce good fruit.
Luke 6:44  Each tree is known by its own fruit. People do not gather figs from thorns, nor harvest grapes from a bramble.
Luke 6:45  The good person brings out good from the good treasure of his heart, and the evil person brings out evil from the evil treasure; for his mouth speaks from the heart’s abundance.
Luke 6:46  Why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and not do what I say?
Luke 6:47  Everyone who comes to Me, hears My words and does them—I will show you whom he resembles.
Luke 6:48  He resembles a man building a house, who dug and went deep and laid a foundation on the rock. When a flood came, the river burst against that house but could not shake it, because it had been well built.
Luke 6:49  But the one who heard and did not act resembles a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation. The river burst against it, and immediately it collapsed; the ruin of that house was great.”

Luke 7
Luke 7:1  When He had finished all His sayings in the people’s hearing, He entered Capernaum.
Luke 7:2  A certain centurion had a slave who was ill and about to die, and who was precious to him.
Luke 7:3  Hearing about Jesus, he sent elders of the Jews to Him, asking Him to come and save his slave.
Luke 7:4  When they reached Jesus, they urged Him earnestly, saying, “He is worthy for Thee to grant him this,
Luke 7:5  for he loves our nation, and he himself built our synagogue for us.”
Luke 7:6  Jesus went with them. When He was already not far from the house, the centurion sent friends, saying to Him, “Lord, do not trouble Thyself, for I am not worthy for Thee to enter under my roof.
Luke 7:7  Therefore I did not even consider myself worthy to come to Thee. But speak a word, and let my servant be healed.
Luke 7:8  For I too am a man placed under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and my slave, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
Luke 7:9  When Jesus heard this, He marveled at him. Turning to the crowd following Him, He said, “I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such faith.”
Luke 7:10  Those who had been sent returned to the house and found the slave in good health.
Luke 7:11  Afterward He went to a city called Nain, and His disciples and a large crowd traveled with Him.
Luke 7:12  As He approached the city’s gate, behold, a dead man was being carried out, his mother’s only son. She was a widow, and a considerable crowd from the city was with her.
Luke 7:13  When the Lord saw her, He was moved with compassion for her and said, “Do not weep.”
Luke 7:14  He approached and touched the bier; the bearers stood still. He said, “Young man, I tell you, rise.”
Luke 7:15  The dead man sat up and began speaking, and He gave him to his mother.
Luke 7:16  Fear seized everyone, and they glorified God, saying, “A great prophet has arisen among us,” and, “God has visited His people.”
Luke 7:17  This report about Him spread throughout all Judea and all the surrounding region.
Luke 7:18  John’s disciples reported all these things to him. John called two of his disciples
Luke 7:19  and sent them to the Lord, saying, “Art Thou the One who is coming, or should we expect another?”
Luke 7:20  When the men came to Him, they said, “John the Baptist sent us to Thee, saying, ‘Art Thou the One who is coming, or should we expect another?’”
Luke 7:21  At that hour He healed many of diseases, afflictions and evil spirits, and graciously gave sight to many blind people.
Luke 7:22  He answered them, “Go and report to John what you have seen and heard: the blind recover sight, the lame walk, leprous people are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor receive good news.
Luke 7:23  And blessed is whoever does not stumble because of Me.”
Luke 7:24  When John’s messengers had departed, He began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to behold? A reed shaken by the wind?
Luke 7:25  But what did you go out to see? A man clothed in soft garments? Behold, those who live in splendid clothing and luxury are in royal palaces.
Luke 7:26  But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
Luke 7:27  This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I send My messenger before Thy face, who will prepare Thy way ahead of Thee.’
Luke 7:28  I tell you, among those born of women no one is greater than John; yet the lesser one in God’s kingdom is greater than he.”
Luke 7:29  When all the people and the tax collectors heard, they acknowledged God’s righteousness, having been baptized with John’s baptism.
Luke 7:30  But the Pharisees and experts in the law rejected God’s purpose for themselves, not having been baptized by him.
Luke 7:31  “To what, then, shall I compare the people of this generation, and what are they like?
Luke 7:32  They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling to one another, saying, ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we lamented, and you did not weep.’
Luke 7:33  For John the Baptist has come neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon.’
Luke 7:34  The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Behold, a glutton and wine-drinker, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.’
Luke 7:35  Yet wisdom was justified by all her children.”
Luke 7:36  One of the Pharisees asked Him to eat with him. He entered the Pharisee’s house and reclined at table.
Luke 7:37  And behold, a woman in the city who was a sinner learned that He was reclining in the Pharisee’s house. She brought an alabaster vessel of perfume
Luke 7:38  and stood behind Him at His feet, weeping. She began to wet His feet with her tears and wiped them with the hair of her head. She kept kissing His feet and anointing them with the perfume.
Luke 7:39  When the Pharisee who had invited Him saw it, he said within himself, “If this man were a prophet, He would know who and what sort of woman is touching Him, that she is a sinner.”
Luke 7:40  Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to say to you.” He said, “Teacher, say it.”
Luke 7:41  “A certain lender had two debtors. One owed five hundred denarii and the other fifty.
Luke 7:42  Since they had nothing with which to repay, he graciously forgave them both. Which of them, then, will love him more?”
Luke 7:43  Simon answered, “I suppose the one to whom he forgave more.” He said to him, “You judged correctly.”
Luke 7:44  Turning toward the woman, He said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I entered your house; you gave Me no water for My feet, but she wet My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
Luke 7:45  You gave Me no kiss, but from the time I entered she has not stopped kissing My feet.
Luke 7:46  You did not anoint My head with oil, but she anointed My feet with perfume.
Luke 7:47  For this reason I tell you: her many sins are forgiven, because she loved much. But the one who is forgiven little loves little.”
Luke 7:48  He said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”
Luke 7:49  Those reclining with Him began to say within themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”
Luke 7:50  And He said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”

Luke 8
Luke 8:1  After this He traveled through cities and villages, proclaiming and announcing the good news of God’s kingdom. The Twelve were with Him,
Luke 8:2  and certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and illnesses: Mary called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out,
Luke 8:3  Joanna, wife of Chuza, Herod’s steward, Susanna, and many others, who served them out of their own belongings.
Luke 8:4  When a large crowd was gathering and people from each city were coming to Him, He spoke through a parable:
Luke 8:5  “The sower went out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell beside the road, was trampled, and the birds of the sky ate it.
Luke 8:6  Other seed fell on the rock, and when it sprouted it withered because it had no moisture.
Luke 8:7  Other seed fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up with it and choked it.
Luke 8:8  Other seed fell into good soil, sprouted and produced fruit a hundredfold.” As He said these things, He called out, “Let the one who has ears to hear listen.”
Luke 8:9  His disciples asked Him what this parable meant.
Luke 8:10  He said, “To you it has been given to know the mysteries of God’s kingdom, but to the rest in parables, so that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.
Luke 8:11  This is the parable: the seed is God’s word.
Luke 8:12  Those beside the road are the ones who have heard; then the devil comes and takes the word from their heart, so that they may not believe and be saved.
Luke 8:13  Those on the rock are the ones who, when they hear, receive the word with joy. They have no root; they believe for a time and fall away in a time of testing.
Luke 8:14  What fell among thorns represents those who have heard, but as they go along they are choked by life’s cares, wealth and pleasures, and do not bring fruit to maturity.
Luke 8:15  What is in the good soil represents those who hear the word in a noble and good heart, hold it fast, and bear fruit with endurance.
Luke 8:16  No one lights a lamp and covers it with a vessel or puts it under a bed, but places it on a lampstand, so that those entering may see the light.
Luke 8:17  For nothing is hidden that will not become manifest, nor concealed that will not be known and come into the open.
Luke 8:18  Therefore watch how you hear. For whoever has will be given more, and whoever does not have will have even what he thinks he has taken from him.”
Luke 8:19  His mother and brothers came to Him but could not reach Him because of the crowd.
Luke 8:20  It was reported to Him, “Thy mother and Thy brothers are standing outside, wanting to see Thee.”
Luke 8:21  He answered them, “My mother and My brothers are these who hear God’s word and do it.”
Luke 8:22  On one of those days He entered a boat with His disciples and said to them, “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.” They put out.
Luke 8:23  As they sailed, He fell asleep. A windstorm came down upon the lake, and they were being swamped and were in danger.
Luke 8:24  They came and woke Him, saying, “Master, Master, we are perishing!” He awoke and rebuked the wind and the surging water. They ceased, and there was calm.
Luke 8:25  He said to them, “Where is your faith?” Afraid, they marveled and said to one another, “Who then is this, that He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him?”
Luke 8:26  They sailed into the country of the Gerasenes, which lies opposite Galilee.
Luke 8:27  When He stepped onto the land, a man from the city who had demons met Him. For a considerable time he had worn no garment and had not lived in a house, but among the tombs.
Luke 8:28  Seeing Jesus, he cried out, fell before Him, and said with a loud voice, “What have I to do with Thee, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg Thee, do not torment me!”
Luke 8:29  For He was commanding the unclean spirit to leave the man. It had seized him many times; he was bound with chains and shackles and kept under guard, but he broke the bonds and was driven by the demon into deserted places.
Luke 8:30  Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” He said, “Legion,” because many demons had entered him.
Luke 8:31  They begged Him not to command them to go away into the abyss.
Luke 8:32  A herd of many pigs was feeding there on the hillside. They begged Him to permit them to enter those pigs, and He permitted them.
Luke 8:33  The demons came out of the man and entered the pigs. The herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.
Luke 8:34  When the herdsmen saw what had happened, they fled and reported it in the city and in the fields.
Luke 8:35  People came out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had gone out sitting at Jesus’ feet, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.
Luke 8:36  Those who had seen reported to them how the demon-possessed man had been saved.
Luke 8:37  The whole multitude of the surrounding country of the Gerasenes asked Him to depart from them, because they were gripped by great fear. He entered a boat and returned.
Luke 8:38  The man from whom the demons had gone out begged to be with Him, but He sent him away, saying,
Luke 8:39  “Return to your home and recount everything God has done for you.” He went away proclaiming throughout the whole city everything Jesus had done for him.
Luke 8:40  When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed Him, for they were all awaiting Him.
Luke 8:41  And behold, a man named Jairus came, who was a ruler of the synagogue. Falling at Jesus’ feet, he begged Him to enter his house,
Luke 8:42  because he had an only daughter, about twelve years old, and she was dying. As He went, the crowds pressed closely around Him.
Luke 8:43  A woman had suffered a flow of blood for twelve years. She had spent her whole livelihood on physicians, but could not be healed by anyone.
Luke 8:44  Coming up behind Him, she touched the fringe of His garment, and immediately her flow of blood stopped.
Luke 8:45  Jesus said, “Who touched Me?” When everyone denied it, Peter said, “Master, the crowds surround Thee and press against Thee.”
Luke 8:46  Jesus said, “Someone touched Me, for I knew that power had gone out from Me.”
Luke 8:47  When the woman saw that she had not escaped notice, she came trembling and fell before Him. Before all the people she reported why she had touched Him and how she had been healed immediately.
Luke 8:48  He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has saved you; go in peace.”
Luke 8:49  While He was still speaking, someone came from the synagogue ruler’s house, saying, “Your daughter has died. Do not trouble the Teacher any longer.”
Luke 8:50  Jesus heard and answered him, “Do not fear; only believe, and she will be saved.”
Luke 8:51  When He came to the house, He allowed no one to enter with Him except Peter, John and James, and the child’s father and mother.
Luke 8:52  Everyone was weeping and beating themselves in mourning for her. He said, “Do not weep, for she has not died, but is sleeping.”
Luke 8:53  They laughed at Him, knowing that she had died.
Luke 8:54  But He took her hand and called, “Child, rise.”
Luke 8:55  Her spirit returned, and she rose immediately. He ordered that she be given something to eat.
Luke 8:56  Her parents were astonished, but He commanded them to tell no one what had happened.

Luke 9
Luke 9:1  Calling the Twelve together, He gave them power and authority over all demons and to heal diseases.
Luke 9:2  He sent them to proclaim God’s kingdom and heal the sick.
Luke 9:3  He said to them, “Take nothing for the journey: neither a staff nor a bag nor bread nor silver; neither are you to have two tunics each.
Luke 9:4  Whatever house you enter, remain there and depart from there.
Luke 9:5  Wherever people do not receive you, as you leave that city shake the dust from your feet as a testimony against them.”
Luke 9:6  They went out and passed through the villages, announcing good news and healing everywhere.
Luke 9:7  Herod the tetrarch heard of everything that was happening and was perplexed, because some were saying that John had been raised from the dead,
Luke 9:8  others that Elijah had appeared, and others that one of the ancient prophets had arisen.
Luke 9:9  Herod said, “John I beheaded. But who is this about whom I hear such things?” And he sought to see Him.
Luke 9:10  When the apostles returned, they recounted to Him everything they had done. Taking them with Him, He withdrew privately to a city called Bethsaida.
Luke 9:11  The crowds learned of it and followed Him. He welcomed them, spoke to them about God’s kingdom, and healed those needing a cure.
Luke 9:12  The day was beginning to draw to a close. The Twelve approached and said to Him, “Dismiss the crowd, so that they may go into the surrounding villages and countryside, find lodging and obtain provisions, because we are here in a deserted place.”
Luke 9:13  He said to them, “You give them something to eat.” They said, “We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless we ourselves go and buy food for all these people.”
Luke 9:14  For there were about five thousand men. He said to His disciples, “Have them recline in groups of about fifty each.”
Luke 9:15  They did so and had everyone recline.
Luke 9:16  Taking the five loaves and the two fish, He looked up to heaven, blessed them, broke them, and kept giving them to the disciples to set before the crowd.
Luke 9:17  They all ate and were filled, and the leftover fragments were gathered up: twelve baskets.
Luke 9:18  While He was praying apart, His disciples were with Him, and He asked them, “Who do the crowds say I am?”
Luke 9:19  They answered, “John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and others that one of the ancient prophets has arisen.”
Luke 9:20  He said to them, “But you, who do you say I am?” Peter answered, “God’s Christ.”
Luke 9:21  He sternly commanded them to tell this to no one,
Luke 9:22  saying, “The Son of Man must suffer many things, be rejected by the elders, chief priests and scribes, be killed, and on the third day be raised.”
Luke 9:23  He said to everyone, “If anyone wishes to come after Me, let him deny himself, take up his cross daily, and follow Me.
Luke 9:24  For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake will save it.
Luke 9:25  For what benefit is there for a person to gain the whole world but destroy or forfeit himself?
Luke 9:26  Whoever is ashamed of Me and My words, of him the Son of Man will be ashamed when He comes in His glory and that of the Father and the holy angels.
Luke 9:27  But truly I tell you, some standing here will certainly not taste death until they see God’s kingdom.”
Luke 9:28  About eight days after these sayings, He took Peter, John and James and went up the mountain to pray.
Luke 9:29  As He prayed, the appearance of His face became different, and His clothing became white and flashing like lightning.
Luke 9:30  And behold, two men were speaking with Him, who were Moses and Elijah.
Luke 9:31  Appearing in glory, they spoke of His departure, which He was about to fulfill in Jerusalem.
Luke 9:32  Peter and those with him were weighed down with sleep, but when fully awake they saw His glory and the two men standing with Him.
Luke 9:33  As they were parting from Him, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three tents, one for Thee, one for Moses and one for Elijah,” not knowing what he was saying.
Luke 9:34  While he said this, a cloud came and overshadowed them, and they were afraid as they entered the cloud.
Luke 9:35  A voice came from the cloud, saying, “This is My Son, the chosen One; listen to Him.”
Luke 9:36  When the voice came, Jesus was found alone. They kept silent and in those days reported to no one anything they had seen.
Luke 9:37  On the following day, when they came down from the mountain, a large crowd met Him.
Luke 9:38  And behold, a man from the crowd cried out, “Teacher, I beg Thee to look upon my son, because he is my only child.
Luke 9:39  Behold, a spirit seizes him, and suddenly he cries out. It convulses him with foaming and scarcely leaves him, bruising him.
Luke 9:40  I begged Thy disciples to cast it out, but they could not.”
Luke 9:41  Jesus answered, “O faithless and distorted generation, how long shall I be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here.”
Luke 9:42  While he was still approaching, the demon dashed him down and convulsed him. Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
Luke 9:43  Everyone was overwhelmed at God’s majesty. While they all marveled at everything He was doing, He said to His disciples,
Luke 9:44  “You, place these words in your ears: the Son of Man is about to be handed over into human hands.”
Luke 9:45  But they did not understand this saying; it was veiled from them so that they might not perceive it, and they were afraid to ask Him about it.
Luke 9:46  A discussion arose among them about which of them might be greatest.
Luke 9:47  Jesus knew the thought of their heart. He took a child and placed him beside Himself,
Luke 9:48  and said to them, “Whoever receives this child in My name receives Me; whoever receives Me receives the One who sent Me. For the one who is least among you all is great.”
Luke 9:49  John answered, “Master, we saw someone casting out demons in Thy name and tried to stop him, because he does not follow with us.”
Luke 9:50  Jesus said to him, “Do not stop him, for whoever is not against you is for you.”
Luke 9:51  As the days for His being taken up approached their fulfillment, He firmly set His face to go to Jerusalem.
Luke 9:52  He sent messengers before His face. They went and entered a Samaritan village to prepare for Him.
Luke 9:53  But they did not receive Him, because His face was set toward Jerusalem.
Luke 9:54  Seeing this, the disciples James and John said, “Lord, dost Thou wish us to command fire to come down from heaven and consume them?”
Luke 9:55  But He turned and rebuked them.
Luke 9:56  And they went to another village.
Luke 9:57  As they traveled on the road, someone said to Him, “I will follow Thee wherever Thou goest.”
Luke 9:58  Jesus said to him, “Foxes have dens and the birds of the sky have dwelling places, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay His head.”
Luke 9:59  He said to another, “Follow Me.” But he said, “Lord, permit me first to go and bury my father.”
Luke 9:60  He said to him, “Let the dead bury their own dead; but you go and proclaim God’s kingdom.”
Luke 9:61  Another also said, “I will follow Thee, Lord; but first permit me to say farewell to those in my house.”
Luke 9:62  Jesus said to him, “No one who puts his hand to a plow and looks backward is fit for God’s kingdom.”

Luke 10
Luke 10:1  After this the Lord appointed seventy-two others also, and sent them two by two before His face into every city and place where He Himself was about to go.
Luke 10:2  He said to them, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few. Therefore petition the Lord of the harvest to send workers out into His harvest.
Luke 10:3  Go; behold, I send you as lambs among wolves.
Luke 10:4  Carry no purse, no bag, no sandals, and greet no one along the road.
Luke 10:5  Whatever house you enter, first say, ‘Peace to this house.’
Luke 10:6  If a son of peace is there, your peace will rest upon him; otherwise it will return to you.
Luke 10:7  Remain in that same house, eating and drinking what they provide, for the worker is worthy of his pay. Do not move from house to house.
Luke 10:8  Whatever city you enter and they receive you, eat what is set before you.
Luke 10:9  Heal the sick in it and say to them, ‘God’s kingdom has drawn near to you.’
Luke 10:10  But whatever city you enter and they do not receive you, go out into its streets and say,
Luke 10:11  ‘Even the dust from your city that clings to our feet we wipe off against you. Nevertheless know this: God’s kingdom has drawn near.’
Luke 10:12  I tell you, it will be more bearable for Sodom on that day than for that city.
Luke 10:13  Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty deeds performed among you had happened in Tyre and Sidon, they would long ago have repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
Luke 10:14  Nevertheless, it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you.
Luke 10:15  And you, Capernaum, will you be exalted as far as heaven? You will go down as far as Hades.
Luke 10:16  The one who hears you hears Me, and the one who rejects you rejects Me; the one who rejects Me rejects the One who sent Me.”
Luke 10:17  The seventy-two returned with joy, saying, “Lord, even the demons submit to us in Thy name.”
Luke 10:18  He said to them, “I was watching Satan fall from heaven like lightning.
Luke 10:19  Behold, I have given you authority to tread upon snakes and scorpions, and over all the enemy’s power, and nothing will ever harm you.
Luke 10:20  Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names have been written in the heavens.”
Luke 10:21  At that very hour He rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, “I acknowledge Thee, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because Thou didst hide these things from the wise and understanding and reveal them to infants. Yes, Father, for such was Thy good pleasure.
Luke 10:22  Everything has been handed over to Me by My Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, or who the Father is except the Son and anyone to whom the Son wishes to reveal Him.”
Luke 10:23  Turning privately to the disciples, He said, “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.
Luke 10:24  For I tell you that many prophets and kings wished to see what you see, and did not see it, and to hear what you hear, and did not hear it.”
Luke 10:25  And behold, an expert in the law stood up to test Him, saying, “Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”
Luke 10:26  He said to him, “What is written in the law? How do you read it?”
Luke 10:27  He answered, “You shall love the Lord your God from your whole heart, with your whole soul, with your whole strength and with your whole mind, and your neighbor as yourself.”
Luke 10:28  He said to him, “You answered correctly. Do this and you will live.”
Luke 10:29  But wishing to justify himself, he said to Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”
Luke 10:30  Jesus replied, “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers. They stripped him, inflicted blows, and went away, leaving him half dead.
Luke 10:31  By coincidence a certain priest was going down that road. He saw him and passed by on the opposite side.
Luke 10:32  Likewise a Levite also came to the place, saw him, and passed by on the opposite side.
Luke 10:33  But a certain Samaritan, traveling, came upon him. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion.
Luke 10:34  He approached and bound his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He placed him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and cared for him.
Luke 10:35  On the next day he took out two denarii, gave them to the innkeeper, and said, ‘Care for him, and whatever more you spend I will repay you when I return.’
Luke 10:36  Which of these three seems to you to have become a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers?”
Luke 10:37  He said, “The one who showed him mercy.” Jesus said to him, “Go, and you do likewise.”
Luke 10:38  As they traveled, He entered a certain village. A woman named Martha welcomed Him.
Luke 10:39  She had a sister called Mary, who also sat at the Lord’s feet and listened to His word.
Luke 10:40  But Martha was distracted by much serving. She came up and said, “Lord, dost Thou not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her, then, to help me.”
Luke 10:41  The Lord answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things,
Luke 10:42  but one thing is needed; for Mary has chosen the good portion, which shall not be taken from her.”

Luke 11
Luke 11:1  And it happened that He was praying in a certain place. When He stopped, one of His disciples said to Him, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his disciples.”
Luke 11:2  He said to them, “When you pray, say: ‘Father, let Thy name be hallowed. Let Thy kingdom come.
Luke 11:3  Give us day by day our daily bread.
Luke 11:4  And forgive us our sins, for we ourselves also forgive everyone who owes us. And do not bring us into testing.’”
Luke 11:5  And He said to them, “Which of you will have a friend and go to him at midnight and say to him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves,
Luke 11:6  since a friend of mine has arrived at my home from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him,’
Luke 11:7  and that man will answer from inside, ‘Do not trouble me. The door is already shut, and my children are in bed with me. I cannot get up and give you anything’?
Luke 11:8  I tell you, even if he will not get up and give to him because he is his friend, yet because of his shameless insistence he will rise and give him as much as he needs.
Luke 11:9  And I tell you: ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
Luke 11:10  For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.
Luke 11:11  What father among you, if his son asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead of a fish?
Luke 11:12  Or again, if he asks for an egg, will he give him a scorpion?
Luke 11:13  So if you, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father from heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!”
Luke 11:14  And He was driving out a mute demon. When the demon came out, the mute man spoke, and the crowds marveled.
Luke 11:15  But some of them said, “He drives out the demons by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons.”
Luke 11:16  Others, testing Him, were seeking from Him a sign from heaven.
Luke 11:17  But He, knowing their thoughts, said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and house falls upon house.
Luke 11:18  And if Satan also is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say that I drive out the demons by Beelzebul.
Luke 11:19  But if I drive out the demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
Luke 11:20  But if I drive out the demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
Luke 11:21  When the strong man, fully armed, guards his own courtyard, his possessions are at peace.
Luke 11:22  But when someone stronger than he attacks and defeats him, he takes away the full armor in which he trusted and distributes his spoils.
Luke 11:23  Whoever is not with Me is against Me, and whoever does not gather with Me scatters.
Luke 11:24  When the unclean spirit comes out of a person, it passes through waterless places seeking rest. Finding none, it then says, ‘I will return to my house from which I came.’
Luke 11:25  And when it comes, it finds it swept and put in order.
Luke 11:26  Then it goes and takes seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they enter and dwell there. And the last state of that person becomes worse than the first.”
Luke 11:27  While He was saying these things, a woman from the crowd raised her voice and said to Him, “Blessed is the womb that bore Thee and the breasts at which Thou didst nurse!”
Luke 11:28  But He said, “Rather, blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it!”
Luke 11:29  As the crowds were gathering in greater numbers, He began to say, “This generation is an evil generation. It seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah.
Luke 11:30  For just as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will also be to this generation.
Luke 11:31  The queen of the south will be raised at the judgment with the men of this generation and will condemn them, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and behold, something greater than Solomon is here.
Luke 11:32  The men of Nineveh will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at the proclamation of Jonah, and behold, something greater than Jonah is here.
Luke 11:33  No one who lights a lamp puts it in a hidden place or under the modius basket, but on the lampstand, so that those who enter may see its light.
Luke 11:34  Your eye is the lamp of the body. When your eye is single, your whole body is also full of light; but when it is evil, your body is also dark.
Luke 11:35  Watch, therefore, that the light within you is not darkness.
Luke 11:36  So if your whole body is full of light, with no part of it dark, it will be wholly full of light, as when a lamp illumines you with its radiance.”
Luke 11:37  As He was speaking, a Pharisee invited Him to dine with him. He went in and reclined at the table.
Luke 11:38  But the Pharisee, seeing this, marveled that He had not first washed before the meal.
Luke 11:39  And the Lord said to him, “Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and the dish, but your inside is full of plunder and wickedness.
Luke 11:40  Fools! Did not the One who made the outside also make the inside?
Luke 11:41  But give what is within as alms, and behold, everything is clean for you.
Luke 11:42  But woe to you Pharisees, because you tithe mint and rue and every garden herb, and pass by justice and the love of God! You ought to have done these things without leaving those undone.
Luke 11:43  Woe to you Pharisees, because you love the foremost seat in the synagogues and greetings in the marketplaces!
Luke 11:44  Woe to you, because you are like unmarked tombs, and the people who walk over them do not know it!”
Luke 11:45  One of the experts in the Law answered Him, “Teacher, by saying these things Thou dost insult us also.”
Luke 11:46  But He said, “Woe also to you experts in the Law, because you load people with burdens hard to carry, and you yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers!
Luke 11:47  Woe to you, because you build the tombs of the prophets, but your fathers killed them!
Luke 11:48  So you are witnesses and approve the deeds of your fathers: they killed them, and you build.
Luke 11:49  For this reason the wisdom of God also said, ‘I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of these they will kill and persecute,’
Luke 11:50  so that the blood of all the prophets poured out since the foundation of the world may be required of this generation,
Luke 11:51  from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who perished between the altar and the house. Yes, I tell you, it will be required of this generation.
Luke 11:52  Woe to you experts in the Law, because you have taken away the key of knowledge! You did not enter yourselves, and you hindered those who were entering.”
Luke 11:53  When He went out from there, the scribes and Pharisees began to press Him fiercely and question Him closely about many things,
Luke 11:54  lying in wait for Him to catch something from His mouth.

Luke 12
Luke 12:1  Meanwhile, as the crowd gathered in its tens of thousands, so that they were trampling one another, He began to speak first to His disciples: “Guard yourselves against the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
Luke 12:2  Nothing is covered up that will not be uncovered, or hidden that will not become known.
Luke 12:3  Therefore whatever you have said in the darkness will be heard in the light, and what you have spoken into the ear in the inner rooms will be proclaimed on the housetops.
Luke 12:4  I tell you, My friends, do not fear those who kill the body and after that have nothing more they can do.
Luke 12:5  But I will show you whom to fear: fear the One who, after killing, has authority to cast into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear Him.
Luke 12:6  Are not five sparrows sold for two assaria? Yet not one of them is forgotten before God.
Luke 12:7  Indeed, even the hairs of your head are all numbered. Do not fear; you are worth more than many sparrows.
Luke 12:8  And I tell you, everyone who acknowledges Me before people, the Son of Man will also acknowledge before the angels of God.
Luke 12:9  But whoever denies Me before people will be denied before the angels of God.
Luke 12:10  And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
Luke 12:11  When they bring you before the synagogues and the rulers and authorities, do not be anxious about how or what you should say in your defense, or what you should say,
Luke 12:12  for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that very hour what must be said.”
Luke 12:13  Someone from the crowd said to Him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
Luke 12:14  But He said to him, “Man, who appointed Me a judge or divider over you?”
Luke 12:15  And He said to them, “See to it that you guard against every kind of greed, because a person’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.”
Luke 12:16  Then He told them a parable: “The land of a certain rich man yielded abundantly.
Luke 12:17  And he reasoned within himself, saying, ‘What shall I do, since I have nowhere to gather my crops?’
Luke 12:18  And he said, ‘This is what I will do: I will pull down my storehouses and build larger ones, and gather all the grain and my goods there.
Luke 12:19  And I will say to my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Rest, eat, drink, be glad!”’
Luke 12:20  But God said to him, ‘Fool, this very night they demand your soul from you; and the things you have prepared—whose will they be?’
Luke 12:21  So it is with the one who stores up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.”
Luke 12:22  And He said to His disciples, “For this reason I tell you: do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.
Luke 12:23  For life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.
Luke 12:24  Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap, and they have neither storeroom nor storehouse, yet God feeds them. How much more valuable you are than the birds!
Luke 12:25  And which of you by being anxious can add a cubit to his span of life?
Luke 12:26  So if you cannot do even the smallest thing, why are you anxious about the rest?
Luke 12:27  Consider the lilies, how they grow. They neither toil nor spin. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
Luke 12:28  But if God so clothes the grass that is in the field today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more will He clothe you, you of little faith!
Luke 12:29  And do not seek what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not be unsettled,
Luke 12:30  for the nations of the world seek after all these things, and your Father knows that you need them.
Luke 12:31  But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added to you.
Luke 12:32  Do not fear, little flock, because your Father was pleased to give you the kingdom.
Luke 12:33  Sell your possessions and give alms. Make for yourselves purses that do not wear out, an unfailing treasure in the heavens, where no thief draws near and no moth destroys.
Luke 12:34  For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
Luke 12:35  Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning,
Luke 12:36  and be like people waiting for their own master to return from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks, they may open to him at once.
Luke 12:37  Blessed are those slaves whom the master finds keeping watch when he comes. Amen, I tell you: he will gird himself, have them recline at table, and come and serve them.
Luke 12:38  Whether he comes in the second watch or in the third and finds them so, blessed are they.
Luke 12:39  But know this: if the master of the house had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
Luke 12:40  You also must be ready, because the Son of Man comes at an hour you do not expect.”
Luke 12:41  Peter said, “Lord, art Thou telling this parable to us, or also to everyone?”
Luke 12:42  And the Lord said, “Who, then, is the faithful steward, the prudent one, whom his master will appoint over his household staff to give out their ration of grain at the proper time?
Luke 12:43  Blessed is that slave whom his master finds doing so when he comes.
Luke 12:44  Truly, I tell you, he will appoint him over all his possessions.
Luke 12:45  But if that slave says in his heart, ‘My master is taking a long time to come,’ and begins to beat the male and female servants, and to eat and drink and become drunk,
Luke 12:46  the master of that slave will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in two and assign his portion with the unfaithful.
Luke 12:47  That slave who knew his master’s will and did not prepare or act according to his will shall receive many blows.
Luke 12:48  But the one who did not know and did things deserving blows shall receive few. From everyone to whom much was given, much will be required; and from the one to whom they entrusted much, they will ask all the more.
Luke 12:49  I came to cast fire upon the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!
Luke 12:50  But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how I am constrained until it is accomplished!
Luke 12:51  Do you think I have come to give peace on earth? No, I tell you, but division.
Luke 12:52  For from now on five in one house will be divided, three against two and two against three.
Luke 12:53  They will be divided: father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.”
Luke 12:54  He also said to the crowds, “When you see a cloud rising in the west, you say at once, ‘A rainstorm is coming,’ and so it happens.
Luke 12:55  And when you see a south wind blowing, you say, ‘There will be scorching heat,’ and it happens.
Luke 12:56  Hypocrites! You know how to assess the appearance of the earth and the sky, but how is it that you do not know how to assess this time?
Luke 12:57  And why do you not also judge for yourselves what is right?
Luke 12:58  For as you go with your adversary before a ruler, make an effort on the way to be released from him, lest he drag you before the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
Luke 12:59  I tell you, you will certainly not come out from there until you have paid even the last lepton.”

Luke 13
Luke 13:1  At that very time some people were present who told Him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
Luke 13:2  And He answered them, “Do you think these Galileans were greater sinners than all the other Galileans because they suffered these things?
Luke 13:3  No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all likewise perish.
Luke 13:4  Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you think they were greater debtors than all the people living in Jerusalem?
Luke 13:5  No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.”
Luke 13:6  And He told this parable: “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard. He came looking for fruit on it and found none.
Luke 13:7  So he said to the vineyard worker, ‘Behold, for three years I have been coming to look for fruit on this fig tree and have found none. Cut it down, then! Why should it also make the ground unproductive?’
Luke 13:8  But he answered him, ‘Master, leave it this year also, until I dig around it and put on manure.
Luke 13:9  And if it produces fruit in the coming year—but if not, you shall cut it down.’”
Luke 13:10  Now He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.
Luke 13:11  And behold, there was a woman who had had a spirit of weakness for eighteen years. She was bent over and could not straighten up completely.
Luke 13:12  When Jesus saw her, He called to her and said, “Woman, you have been released from your weakness.”
Luke 13:13  And He laid His hands on her, and at once she was made straight, and she glorified God.
Luke 13:14  But the synagogue ruler, indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, said to the crowd, “There are six days on which work ought to be done. So come and be healed on those days, and not on the Sabbath day.”
Luke 13:15  But the Lord answered him, “Hypocrites! Does not each of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or donkey from the manger and lead it away to give it water?
Luke 13:16  And this woman, who is a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan bound for, behold, eighteen years—ought she not to have been released from this bond on the Sabbath day?”
Luke 13:17  As He said these things, all who opposed Him were put to shame, and the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things being done by Him.
Luke 13:18  So He said, “What is the kingdom of God like, and to what shall I compare it?
Luke 13:19  It is like a mustard seed that a man took and cast into his own garden. It grew and became a tree, and the birds of the sky nested in its branches.”
Luke 13:20  And again He said, “To what shall I compare the kingdom of God?
Luke 13:21  It is like leaven that a woman took and hid in three sata of flour, until the whole was leavened.”
Luke 13:22  And He traveled through cities and villages, teaching and making His journey toward Jerusalem.
Luke 13:23  Someone said to Him, “Lord, are those who are being saved few?” And He said to them,
Luke 13:24  “Strive to enter through the narrow door, because many, I tell you, will seek to enter and will not be able,
Luke 13:25  once the master of the house rises and shuts the door. Then you will begin to stand outside and knock at the door, saying, ‘Lord, open to us!’ And he will answer you, ‘I do not know you or where you come from.’
Luke 13:26  Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.’
Luke 13:27  And he will say to you, ‘I do not know you or where you come from. Depart from me, all you workers of unrighteousness!’
Luke 13:28  There will be weeping and grinding of teeth there, when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but yourselves being thrown outside.
Luke 13:29  And people will come from east and west and from north and south and recline at table in the kingdom of God.
Luke 13:30  And behold, there are last who will be first, and there are first who will be last.”
Luke 13:31  At that very hour some Pharisees approached and said to Him, “Leave and go away from here, because Herod wants to kill Thee.”
Luke 13:32  And He said to them, “Go and tell that fox, ‘Behold, I drive out demons and accomplish healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I am brought to completion.’
Luke 13:33  Nevertheless, I must travel today and tomorrow and the day following, because it is not possible for a prophet to perish outside Jerusalem.
Luke 13:34  Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her! How often I wanted to gather your children as a bird gathers her own brood under her wings, and you were not willing!
Luke 13:35  Behold, your house is left to you. And I tell you, you will certainly not see Me until the time comes when you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!’”

Luke 14
Luke 14:1  And it happened that He went into the house of one of the leaders of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, and they were watching Him closely.
Luke 14:2  And behold, a certain man suffering from dropsy was before Him.
Luke 14:3  Jesus spoke to the experts in the Law and the Pharisees, saying, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath, or not?”
Luke 14:4  But they were silent. And He took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him away.
Luke 14:5  And He said to them, “Which of you, if his son or ox falls into a well, will not pull him out at once on the Sabbath day?”
Luke 14:6  And they were unable to answer these things.
Luke 14:7  He told a parable to those who had been invited, noticing how they chose the foremost places at table. He said to them,
Luke 14:8  “When someone invites you to a wedding feast, do not recline in the foremost place. Someone more honored than you may have been invited by him,
Luke 14:9  and the one who invited you both will come and say to you, ‘Give this man your place.’ Then you will begin, with shame, to occupy the last place.
Luke 14:10  But when you are invited, go and recline in the last place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he will say to you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will have honor before all who recline at table with you.
Luke 14:11  For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”
Luke 14:12  He also said to the one who had invited Him, “When you give a midday meal or a supper, do not invite your friends or your brothers or your relatives or rich neighbors, lest they also invite you in return and you receive repayment.
Luke 14:13  But when you give a reception, invite the poor, the disabled, the lame, and the blind.
Luke 14:14  And you will be blessed, because they have nothing with which to repay you; for you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”
Luke 14:15  When one of those reclining at table heard these things, he said to Him, “Blessed is whoever shall eat bread in the kingdom of God!”
Luke 14:16  But He said to him, “A certain man was giving a great supper, and he invited many.
Luke 14:17  At the hour of the supper he sent his slave to tell those who had been invited, ‘Come, because things are now ready.’
Luke 14:18  And they all alike began to excuse themselves. The first said to him, ‘I bought a field, and I need to go out and see it. I ask you to excuse me.’
Luke 14:19  And another said, ‘I bought five pairs of oxen, and I am going to test them. I ask you to excuse me.’
Luke 14:20  And another said, ‘I married a wife, and for this reason I cannot come.’
Luke 14:21  The slave returned and reported these things to his master. Then the master of the house became angry and said to his slave, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring the poor, the disabled, the blind, and the lame in here.’
Luke 14:22  And the slave said, ‘Master, what you commanded has been done, and there is still room.’
Luke 14:23  And the master said to the slave, ‘Go out into the roads and along the fences, and compel people to come in, so that my house may be filled.
Luke 14:24  For I tell you, none of those men who were invited will taste my supper.’”
Luke 14:25  Now great crowds were traveling with Him. He turned and said to them,
Luke 14:26  “If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, and even his own life, he cannot be My disciple.
Luke 14:27  Whoever does not carry his own cross and come after Me cannot be My disciple.
Luke 14:28  For which of you, wanting to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate the expense, whether he has enough to finish it?
Luke 14:29  Otherwise, when he has laid a foundation and is unable to complete it, all who see it may begin to mock him,
Luke 14:30  saying, ‘This man began to build and was unable to finish.’
Luke 14:31  Or what king, going to meet another king in war, will not first sit down and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
Luke 14:32  And if not, while the other is still far away, he sends a delegation and asks for terms of peace.
Luke 14:33  So, therefore, every one of you who does not renounce all his own possessions cannot be My disciple.
Luke 14:34  Salt, then, is good. But if even the salt becomes tasteless, with what will it be seasoned?
Luke 14:35  It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure heap; they throw it outside. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”

Luke 15
Luke 15:1  Now all the tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to hear Him.
Luke 15:2  And both the Pharisees and the scribes grumbled, saying, “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.”
Luke 15:3  So He told them this parable:
Luke 15:4  “What man among you, having a hundred sheep and losing one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the lost one until he finds it?
Luke 15:5  And when he finds it, he lays it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
Luke 15:6  When he comes home, he calls his friends and neighbors together and says to them, ‘Rejoice with me, because I found my sheep that was lost!’
Luke 15:7  I tell you, in the same way there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous people who have no need of repentance.
Luke 15:8  Or what woman, having ten drachmas, if she loses one drachma, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and search carefully until she finds it?
Luke 15:9  And when she finds it, she calls her women friends and neighbors together, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, because I found the drachma that I lost!’
Luke 15:10  In the same way, I tell you, there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents.”
Luke 15:11  And He said, “A certain man had two sons.
Luke 15:12  The younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me the share of the property that falls to me.’ And he divided his livelihood between them.
Luke 15:13  Not many days later, the younger son gathered everything together and traveled to a distant country. There he scattered his property by living recklessly.
Luke 15:14  When he had spent everything, a severe famine arose throughout that country, and he began to be in need.
Luke 15:15  So he went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that country, who sent him into his fields to feed pigs.
Luke 15:16  And he longed to be filled with the carob pods the pigs were eating, and no one gave him anything.
Luke 15:17  But when he came to himself, he said, ‘How many of my father’s hired workers have bread to spare, while I am perishing here from hunger!
Luke 15:18  I will rise and go to my father and say to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you.
Luke 15:19  I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired workers.”’
Luke 15:20  And he rose and came to his own father. But while he was still far away, his father saw him and was moved with compassion. He ran, fell upon his neck, and kissed him tenderly.
Luke 15:21  And the son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you; I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
Luke 15:22  But the father said to his slaves, ‘Quickly bring out the best robe, and clothe him; and put a ring on his hand, and sandals on his feet.
Luke 15:23  And bring the fattened calf, and slaughter it; and let us eat and rejoice,
Luke 15:24  because this son of mine was dead and came to life again; he was lost and was found.’ And they began to be glad.
Luke 15:25  Now his older son was in the field. As he came and drew near the house, he heard music and dancing.
Luke 15:26  And he called one of the servants and asked what these things might mean.
Luke 15:27  He said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father slaughtered the fattened calf because he received him back in good health.’
Luke 15:28  But he became angry and was unwilling to enter. His father came out and pleaded with him.
Luke 15:29  But he answered his father, ‘Behold, all these years I have served you as a slave, and I never disobeyed your command; yet you never gave me a young goat so that I might be glad with my friends.
Luke 15:30  But when this son of yours came, who devoured your livelihood with prostitutes, you slaughtered the fattened calf for him!’
Luke 15:31  And he said to him, ‘Child, you are always with me, and everything of mine is yours.
Luke 15:32  But we had to be glad and rejoice, because this brother of yours was dead and came to life; he was lost and was found.’”

Luke 16
Luke 16:1  He also said to the disciples, “There was a certain rich man who had a steward, and this man was accused before him of scattering his possessions.
Luke 16:2  He called him and said to him, ‘What is this I hear about you? Give an account of your stewardship, for you can no longer be steward.’
Luke 16:3  And the steward said within himself, ‘What shall I do, since my master is taking the stewardship away from me? I am not strong enough to dig; I am ashamed to beg.
Luke 16:4  I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from the stewardship, they may welcome me into their own houses.’
Luke 16:5  And he called each one of his own master’s debtors and said to the first, ‘How much do you owe my master?’
Luke 16:6  He said, ‘A hundred baths of oil.’ And he said to him, ‘Take your document, sit down quickly, and write fifty.’
Luke 16:7  Then he said to another, ‘And how much do you owe?’ He said, ‘A hundred kors of wheat.’ He said to him, ‘Take your document and write eighty.’
Luke 16:8  And the master praised the unrighteous steward because he had acted prudently. For the sons of this age are more prudent toward their own generation than the sons of light.
Luke 16:9  And I tell you, make friends for yourselves from the mammon of unrighteousness, so that when it fails, they may welcome you into the eternal tents.
Luke 16:10  The one who is faithful in the least is faithful also in much, and the one who is unrighteous in the least is unrighteous also in much.
Luke 16:11  So if you have not been faithful with unrighteous mammon, who will entrust the true riches to you?
Luke 16:12  And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to another, who will give you what is your own?
Luke 16:13  No household servant can serve two masters as a slave. For either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.”
Luke 16:14  Now the Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all these things and sneered at Him.
Luke 16:15  And He said to them, “You are those who justify yourselves before people, but God knows your hearts, because what is exalted among people is an abomination before God.
Luke 16:16  The Law and the Prophets were until John. From that time the kingdom of God is proclaimed as good news, and everyone presses into it.
Luke 16:17  But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one small stroke of the Law to fall.
Luke 16:18  Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery, and the one who marries a woman divorced from a husband commits adultery.
Luke 16:19  Now there was a certain rich man, and he clothed himself in purple and fine linen, enjoying himself in splendor every day.
Luke 16:20  And a certain poor man named Lazarus had been laid at his gateway, covered with sores
Luke 16:21  and longing to be filled with what fell from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.
Luke 16:22  And it happened that the poor man died and was carried away by the angels to Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died and was buried.
Luke 16:23  And in Hades, being in torment, he lifted his eyes and saw Abraham far away and Lazarus in his bosom.
Luke 16:24  And he called out, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I am in pain in this flame.’
Luke 16:25  But Abraham said, ‘Child, remember that you received your good things during your life, and Lazarus likewise bad things. But now he is comforted here, and you are in pain.
Luke 16:26  And besides all this, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that those who want to cross from here to you cannot, nor may they cross over from there to us.’
Luke 16:27  And he said, ‘Then I ask you, father, to send him to my father’s house,
Luke 16:28  for I have five brothers, so that he may solemnly warn them, lest they also come to this place of torment.’
Luke 16:29  But Abraham said, ‘They have Moses and the Prophets; let them hear them.’
Luke 16:30  But he said, ‘No, father Abraham; but if someone goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’
Luke 16:31  And he said to him, ‘If they do not hear Moses and the Prophets, neither will they be persuaded if someone rises from the dead.’”

Luke 17
Luke 17:1  And He said to His disciples, “It is impossible for stumbling blocks not to come, but woe to the one through whom they come!
Luke 17:2  It would be better for him to have a millstone placed around his neck and be thrown into the sea than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.
Luke 17:3  Watch yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.
Luke 17:4  And if he sins against you seven times in the day and turns back to you seven times, saying, ‘I repent,’ you shall forgive him.”
Luke 17:5  And the apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith.”
Luke 17:6  And the Lord said, “If you have faith like a mustard seed, you would say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.
Luke 17:7  Which of you, having a slave plowing or tending sheep, will say to him when he comes in from the field, ‘Come at once and recline at table’?
Luke 17:8  Will he not instead say to him, ‘Prepare something for my supper, gird yourself, and serve me while I eat and drink; and after that you shall eat and drink’?
Luke 17:9  Does he thank the slave because he did what was commanded?
Luke 17:10  So you also, when you have done everything commanded you, say, ‘We are unprofitable slaves; we have done what we ought to have done.’”
Luke 17:11  And it happened that, as He was traveling to Jerusalem, He passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.
Luke 17:12  As He entered a certain village, ten men with leprosy met Him. They stood at a distance
Luke 17:13  and raised their voices, saying, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
Luke 17:14  When He saw them, He said to them, “Go and show yourselves to the priests.” And it happened that as they went, they were cleansed.
Luke 17:15  One of them, seeing that he had been healed, returned, glorifying God with a loud voice.
Luke 17:16  And he fell on his face at His feet, giving Him thanks; and he was a Samaritan.
Luke 17:17  Jesus answered, “Were not the ten cleansed? But where are the nine?
Luke 17:18  Were none found returning to give glory to God except this foreigner?”
Luke 17:19  And He said to him, “Rise and go; your faith has saved you.”
Luke 17:20  When the Pharisees asked Him when the kingdom of God was coming, He answered them, “The kingdom of God does not come in a way that can be observed,
Luke 17:21  nor will they say, ‘Behold, here!’ or ‘There!’ For behold, the kingdom of God is within you.”
Luke 17:22  And He said to the disciples, “Days will come when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
Luke 17:23  And they will say to you, ‘Behold, there!’ or ‘Behold, here!’ Do not go away or pursue them.
Luke 17:24  For just as lightning flashes and shines from one region under heaven to another under heaven, so will the Son of Man be in His day.
Luke 17:25  But first He must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
Luke 17:26  And just as it happened in the days of Noah, so it will also be in the days of the Son of Man.
Luke 17:27  They were eating, drinking, marrying, and being given in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark, and the flood came and destroyed them all.
Luke 17:28  Likewise, just as it happened in the days of Lot: they were eating, drinking, buying, selling, planting, and building;
Luke 17:29  but on the day Lot went out from Sodom, fire and sulfur rained from heaven and destroyed them all.
Luke 17:30  It will be the same on the day the Son of Man is revealed.
Luke 17:31  On that day, whoever is on the housetop, with his belongings in the house, must not go down to take them; likewise, whoever is in the field must not turn back.
Luke 17:32  Remember Lot’s wife.
Luke 17:33  Whoever seeks to preserve his life will lose it, but whoever loses it will keep it alive.
Luke 17:34  I tell you, on that night two will be on one bed: one will be taken and the other left.
Luke 17:35  Two women will be grinding together: one will be taken and the other left.”
Luke 17:37  And they answered Him, “Where, Lord?” He said to them, “Where the body is, there the eagles will also gather.”

Luke 18
Luke 18:1  And He told them a parable about their need to pray always and not lose heart,
Luke 18:2  saying, “There was a certain judge in a certain city who neither feared God nor respected any person.
Luke 18:3  And there was a widow in that city who kept coming to him, saying, ‘Give me justice against my adversary.’
Luke 18:4  For a time he was unwilling. But afterward he said within himself, ‘Even though I do not fear God or respect any person,
Luke 18:5  yet because this widow troubles me, I will give her justice, lest by coming continually she wear me down.’”
Luke 18:6  And the Lord said, “Hear what the unrighteous judge says.
Luke 18:7  And will not God bring about justice for His chosen ones who cry to Him day and night? And will He delay over them?
Luke 18:8  I tell you, He will bring about justice for them speedily. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will He find faith on the earth?”
Luke 18:9  He also told this parable to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and regarded the rest as nothing:
Luke 18:10  “Two men went up into the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
Luke 18:11  The Pharisee stood and prayed these things to himself: ‘God, I thank Thee that I am not like the rest of humanity—plunderers, unrighteous people, adulterers—or even like this tax collector.
Luke 18:12  I fast twice a week; I tithe everything I acquire.’
Luke 18:13  But the tax collector, standing far away, would not even lift his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, the sinner.’
Luke 18:14  I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”
Luke 18:15  And they were bringing even infants to Him so that He might touch them. But when the disciples saw it, they rebuked them.
Luke 18:16  But Jesus called the children to Himself, saying, “Let the children come to Me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
Luke 18:17  Amen, I tell you: whoever does not receive the kingdom of God as a child will certainly not enter it.”
Luke 18:18  And a certain ruler questioned Him, saying, “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
Luke 18:19  Jesus said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good except One—God.
Luke 18:20  You know the commandments: ‘Do not commit adultery; do not murder; do not steal; do not bear false witness; honor your father and mother.’”
Luke 18:21  And he said, “All these things I have kept from my youth.”
Luke 18:22  When Jesus heard this, He said to him, “You still lack one thing: sell everything you have and distribute it to the poor, and you will have treasure in the heavens; and come, follow Me.”
Luke 18:23  But when he heard these things, he became deeply grieved, for he was exceedingly rich.
Luke 18:24  Seeing that he had become deeply grieved, Jesus said, “How difficult it is for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!
Luke 18:25  For it is easier for a camel to enter through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”
Luke 18:26  And those who heard said, “Then who can be saved?”
Luke 18:27  But He said, “The things impossible with people are possible with God.”
Luke 18:28  And Peter said, “Behold, we have left what was our own and followed Thee.”
Luke 18:29  And He said to them, “Amen, I tell you: there is no one who has left house or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
Luke 18:30  who will not certainly receive many times as much in this time, and in the age to come eternal life.”
Luke 18:31  Taking the Twelve aside, He said to them, “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything written through the prophets will be accomplished for the Son of Man.
Luke 18:32  For He will be handed over to the nations and will be mocked and insulted and spat upon.
Luke 18:33  And after flogging Him, they will kill Him, and on the third day He will rise.”
Luke 18:34  But they understood none of these things. This saying was hidden from them, and they did not understand what was being said.
Luke 18:35  And it happened that as He drew near to Jericho, a certain blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.
Luke 18:36  Hearing a crowd passing through, he asked what this might be.
Luke 18:37  They told him, “Jesus the Nazarene is passing by.”
Luke 18:38  And he cried out, saying, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Luke 18:39  Those going ahead rebuked him so that he would be silent, but he cried out much more, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Luke 18:40  Jesus stopped and commanded that he be brought to Him. When he drew near, He asked him,
Luke 18:41  “What do you want Me to do for you?” And he said, “Lord, that I may receive my sight.”
Luke 18:42  And Jesus said to him, “Receive your sight; your faith has saved you.”
Luke 18:43  And at once he received his sight and followed Him, glorifying God. And all the people, seeing this, gave praise to God.

Luke 19
Luke 19:1  And He entered Jericho and was passing through it.
Luke 19:2  And behold, there was a man called Zacchaeus, who was a chief tax collector and was rich.
Luke 19:3  He was seeking to see who Jesus was, but could not because of the crowd, since he was short in stature.
Luke 19:4  So he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore fig tree to see Him, because He was about to pass that way.
Luke 19:5  When Jesus came to the place, He looked up and said to him, “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay in your house.”
Luke 19:6  And he hurried down and welcomed Him, rejoicing.
Luke 19:7  When they saw this, they all grumbled, saying, “He has gone in to lodge with a sinful man.”
Luke 19:8  But Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, “Behold, Lord, I give half of my possessions to the poor, and if I have extorted anything from anyone, I repay it fourfold.”
Luke 19:9  Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham.
Luke 19:10  For the Son of Man came to seek and to save what was lost.”
Luke 19:11  While they were hearing these things, He went on to tell a parable, because He was near Jerusalem and they thought that the kingdom of God was about to appear immediately.
Luke 19:12  So He said, “A certain nobleman went to a distant country to receive a kingdom for himself and return.
Luke 19:13  He called ten of his own slaves, gave them ten minas, and said to them, ‘Do business until I come.’
Luke 19:14  But his citizens hated him and sent a delegation after him, saying, ‘We do not want this man to reign over us.’
Luke 19:15  And it happened that when he returned, having received the kingdom, he ordered those slaves to whom he had given the money to be called to him, so that he might know what business they had done.
Luke 19:16  The first came, saying, ‘Master, your mina has gained ten minas.’
Luke 19:17  And he said to him, ‘Well done, good slave! Because you have been faithful in a very small thing, have authority over ten cities.’
Luke 19:18  The second came, saying, ‘Your mina, master, has made five minas.’
Luke 19:19  And he said to this one also, ‘You too shall be over five cities.’
Luke 19:20  And the other came, saying, ‘Master, behold your mina, which I kept laid away in a cloth.
Luke 19:21  For I was afraid of you, because you are a severe man: you take up what you did not lay down and reap what you did not sow.’
Luke 19:22  He said to him, ‘From your own mouth I will judge you, evil slave. You knew that I am a severe man, taking up what I did not lay down and reaping what I did not sow?
Luke 19:23  Then why did you not put my money on deposit? And when I came, I would have collected it with interest.’
Luke 19:24  And he said to those standing by, ‘Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has the ten minas.’
Luke 19:25  And they said to him, ‘Master, he has ten minas!’
Luke 19:26  ‘I tell you that to everyone who has, more will be given; but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away.
Luke 19:27  But those enemies of mine who did not want me to reign over them—bring them here and slaughter them before me.’”
Luke 19:28  And after saying these things, He went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
Luke 19:29  And it happened that as He drew near Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount called Olivet, He sent two of the disciples,
Luke 19:30  saying, “Go into the village opposite. As you enter it, you will find a colt tied, on which no person has ever sat. Untie it and bring it.
Luke 19:31  And if anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?’ you shall say this: ‘The Lord has need of it.’”
Luke 19:32  Those who were sent went away and found it just as He had told them.
Luke 19:33  As they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, “Why are you untying the colt?”
Luke 19:34  And they said, “The Lord has need of it.”
Luke 19:35  They brought it to Jesus, threw their garments on the colt, and set Jesus upon it.
Luke 19:36  As He went, they spread their own garments on the road.
Luke 19:37  As He was already drawing near the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works they had seen,
Luke 19:38  saying, “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!”
Luke 19:39  And some of the Pharisees from the crowd said to Him, “Teacher, rebuke Thy disciples.”
Luke 19:40  And He answered, “I tell you, if these fall silent, the stones will cry out.”
Luke 19:41  As He drew near and saw the city, He wept over it,
Luke 19:42  saying, “If only you too had known on this day the things that lead to peace—but now they have been hidden from your eyes.
Luke 19:43  For days will come upon you when your enemies will build a siege barrier around you and surround you and hem you in on every side.
Luke 19:44  They will dash you to the ground, and your children within you, and will not leave stone upon stone within you, because you did not know the time of your visitation.”
Luke 19:45  And He entered the temple and began to drive out those who were selling,
Luke 19:46  saying to them, “It is written, ‘And My house shall be a house of prayer,’ but you have made it a den of robbers.”
Luke 19:47  And He was teaching daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes, and the leading men of the people, were seeking to destroy Him.
Luke 19:48  Yet they could not find what to do, for all the people hung on His words as they listened.

Luke 20
Luke 20:1  And it happened on one of the days, as He was teaching the people in the temple and proclaiming good news, that the chief priests and the scribes came up with the elders
Luke 20:2  and said to Him, “Tell us by what authority Thou doest these things, or who it is that gave Thee this authority.”
Luke 20:3  He answered them, “I too will ask you a question; tell Me:
Luke 20:4  was John’s baptism from heaven or from people?”
Luke 20:5  And they reasoned among themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will say, ‘Why did you not believe him?’
Luke 20:6  But if we say, ‘From people,’ all the people will stone us, for they are convinced that John was a prophet.”
Luke 20:7  So they answered that they did not know where it was from.
Luke 20:8  And Jesus said to them, “Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
Luke 20:9  And He began to tell the people this parable: “A certain man planted a vineyard, leased it to tenant farmers, and went away for a considerable time.
Luke 20:10  At the proper season he sent a slave to the farmers, so that they would give him some of the vineyard’s fruit. But the farmers beat him and sent him away empty.
Luke 20:11  And he went on to send another slave. But they beat and dishonored that one also and sent him away empty.
Luke 20:12  And he went on to send a third. But they wounded that one also and threw him out.
Luke 20:13  Then the master of the vineyard said, ‘What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will respect him.’
Luke 20:14  But when the farmers saw him, they reasoned with one another, saying, ‘This is the heir. Let us kill him, so that the inheritance may become ours.’
Luke 20:15  And they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What, then, will the master of the vineyard do to them?
