Luke 20:16  He will come and destroy those farmers and give the vineyard to others.” When they heard this, they said, “May it never happen!”
Luke 20:17  But He looked at them and said, “What, then, is this that is written: ‘The stone the builders rejected—this became the head of the corner’?
Luke 20:18  Everyone who falls upon that stone will be shattered; but whoever it falls upon, it will crush him.”
Luke 20:19  And the scribes and the chief priests sought to lay hands on Him at that very hour, but they feared the people, for they knew that He had spoken this parable against them.
Luke 20:20  And keeping watch, they sent spies who pretended to be righteous, so that they might seize on something He said and hand Him over to the rule and authority of the governor.
Luke 20:21  They questioned Him, saying, “Teacher, we know that Thou speakest and teachest rightly and dost not show partiality, but teachest the way of God in truth.
Luke 20:22  Is it lawful for us to give tribute to Caesar, or not?”
Luke 20:23  But perceiving their cunning, He said to them,
Luke 20:24  “Show Me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it have?” They answered, “Caesar’s.”
Luke 20:25  And He said to them, “Then give back to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”
Luke 20:26  And they were unable to seize on the saying before the people. Marveling at His answer, they fell silent.
Luke 20:27  Some of the Sadducees, who deny that there is a resurrection, came up and questioned Him,
Luke 20:28  saying, “Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies, having a wife but being childless, his brother should take the wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
Luke 20:29  Now there were seven brothers. The first took a wife and died childless,
Luke 20:30  and the second,
Luke 20:31  and the third took her. Likewise, all seven left no children and died.
Luke 20:32  Afterward the woman also died.
Luke 20:33  So in the resurrection, whose wife does the woman become? For all seven had her as wife.”
Luke 20:34  And Jesus said to them, “The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage.
Luke 20:35  But those counted worthy to attain that age and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage.
Luke 20:36  For they can no longer die either, because they are equal to angels and are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.
Luke 20:37  And that the dead are raised, even Moses disclosed in the passage about the bush, when he calls the Lord the God of Abraham and God of Isaac and God of Jacob.
Luke 20:38  Now He is God not of the dead but of the living, for all live to Him.”
Luke 20:39  And some of the scribes answered, “Teacher, Thou hast spoken well.”
Luke 20:40  For they no longer dared to question Him about anything.
Luke 20:41  But He said to them, “How do they say that the Christ is David’s son?
Luke 20:42  For David himself says in the book of Psalms, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand
Luke 20:43  until I make Thy enemies a footstool for Thy feet.”’
Luke 20:44  David therefore calls Him Lord; how, then, is He his son?”
Luke 20:45  While all the people were listening, He said to His disciples,
Luke 20:46  “Beware of the scribes who want to walk about in robes and love greetings in the marketplaces and foremost seats in the synagogues and foremost places at suppers,
Luke 20:47  who devour widows’ houses and pray at length for a pretext. These will receive greater judgment.”

Luke 21
Luke 21:1  Looking up, He saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury.
Luke 21:2  And He saw a certain needy widow putting two lepta in there.
Luke 21:3  And He said, “Truly, I tell you, this poor widow put in more than all of them.
Luke 21:4  For all these put into the gifts out of their abundance, but she, out of her lack, put in all she had to live on.”
Luke 21:5  And as some were speaking about the temple, how it was adorned with beautiful stones and dedicated offerings, He said,
Luke 21:6  “As for these things you see, days will come in which stone will not be left upon stone without being torn down.”
Luke 21:7  They questioned Him, saying, “Teacher, when, then, will these things be, and what will be the sign when these things are about to happen?”
Luke 21:8  And He said, “See that you are not led astray. For many will come in My name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and, ‘The time has drawn near.’ Do not go after them.
Luke 21:9  When you hear of wars and disturbances, do not be terrified, for these things must happen first, but the end will not come immediately.”
Luke 21:10  Then He said to them, “Nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom.
Luke 21:11  There will be great earthquakes, and famines and plagues in various places. There will also be terrors and great signs from heaven.
Luke 21:12  But before all these things they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, handing you over to synagogues and prisons, and you will be led before kings and governors because of My name.
Luke 21:13  It will turn out as an opportunity for you to bear witness.
Luke 21:14  Therefore settle it in your hearts not to rehearse beforehand how to defend yourselves,
Luke 21:15  for I will give you a mouth and wisdom that all who oppose you will be unable to resist or contradict.
Luke 21:16  You will be handed over even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and they will put some of you to death.
Luke 21:17  And you will be hated by all because of My name.
Luke 21:18  Yet certainly not a hair from your head will perish.
Luke 21:19  By your endurance gain your souls.
Luke 21:20  But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that her desolation has drawn near.
Luke 21:21  Then let those in Judea flee to the mountains, and let those within her depart, and let those in the countryside not enter her,
Luke 21:22  because these are days of vengeance, for all that is written to be fulfilled.
Luke 21:23  Woe to those who are pregnant and those nursing infants in those days! For there will be great distress upon the land and wrath against this people.
Luke 21:24  They will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive into all the nations. And Jerusalem will be trampled by nations until the times of nations are fulfilled.
Luke 21:25  And there will be signs in sun and moon and stars, and on the earth distress among nations in perplexity at the roar of the sea and its surging,
Luke 21:26  people fainting from fear and expectation of what is coming upon the inhabited world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
Luke 21:27  And then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
Luke 21:28  But when these things begin to happen, straighten up and lift your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.”
Luke 21:29  And He told them a parable: “Look at the fig tree and all the trees.
Luke 21:30  When they already put out shoots, you see and know for yourselves that summer is already near.
Luke 21:31  So also you, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.
Luke 21:32  Amen, I tell you: this generation will certainly not pass away until all things happen.
Luke 21:33  Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will certainly not pass away.
Luke 21:34  But watch yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down with carousing and drunkenness and the cares of life, and that day come upon you suddenly
Luke 21:35  like a trap. For it will come upon all who dwell on the face of the whole earth.
Luke 21:36  But stay awake at every season, praying that you may have strength to escape all these things that are about to happen and to stand before the Son of Man.”
Luke 21:37  By day He was teaching in the temple, but at night He went out and lodged on the mount called Olivet.
Luke 21:38  And all the people would come early in the morning to Him in the temple to hear Him.

Luke 22
Luke 22:1  Now the feast of Unleavened Bread, called Passover, was drawing near.
Luke 22:2  And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how to kill Him, for they feared the people.
Luke 22:3  Then Satan entered Judas, who was called Iscariot and was one of the number of the Twelve.
Luke 22:4  He went away and spoke with the chief priests and the captains about how he might hand Him over to them.
Luke 22:5  And they rejoiced and agreed to give him money.
Luke 22:6  He consented, and sought an opportunity to hand Him over to them when no crowd was present.
Luke 22:7  Then the day of Unleavened Bread came, on which the Passover sacrifice had to be slaughtered.
Luke 22:8  And He sent Peter and John, saying, “Go and prepare the Passover for us, so that we may eat.”
Luke 22:9  They said to Him, “Where dost Thou want us to prepare it?”
Luke 22:10  He said to them, “Behold, as you enter the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him into the house he enters.
Luke 22:11  And you shall say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says to you, “Where is the lodging room in which I may eat the Passover with My disciples?”’
Luke 22:12  And he will show you a large, furnished upper room. Prepare it there.”
Luke 22:13  They went and found things just as He had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
Luke 22:14  When the hour came, He reclined at table, and the apostles with Him.
Luke 22:15  And He said to them, “With desire I have desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.
Luke 22:16  For I tell you that I will certainly not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.”
Luke 22:17  And He received a cup, gave thanks, and said, “Take this and divide it among yourselves.
Luke 22:18  For I tell you, from now on I will certainly not drink from the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.”
Luke 22:19  And He took bread, and having given thanks, He broke it and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body, which is given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”
Luke 22:20  And likewise the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, poured out for you.
Luke 22:21  But behold, the hand of the one who hands Me over is with Me on the table.
Luke 22:22  For the Son of Man indeed goes according to what has been determined, but woe to that man through whom He is handed over!”
Luke 22:23  And they began to discuss among themselves which of them it could be who was about to do this.
Luke 22:24  A dispute also arose among them about which of them was considered to be greatest.
Luke 22:25  But He said to them, “The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who exercise authority over them are called benefactors.
Luke 22:26  But you are not to be so. Rather, let the greatest among you become as the youngest, and the leader as the one who serves.
Luke 22:27  For who is greater, the one reclining at table or the one serving? Is it not the one reclining? But I am among you as the One who serves.
Luke 22:28  And you are those who have remained with Me in My trials.
Luke 22:29  And I assign to you a kingdom, just as My Father assigned one to Me,
Luke 22:30  so that you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom, and you will sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
Luke 22:31  Simon, Simon, behold, Satan demanded to have you all, to sift you like wheat.
Luke 22:32  But I prayed for you, that your faith might not fail; and you, once you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.”
Luke 22:33  He said to Him, “Lord, I am ready to go with Thee both to prison and to death.”
Luke 22:34  But He said, “I tell you, Peter, a rooster will not crow today until you deny three times that you know Me.”
Luke 22:35  And He said to them, “When I sent you without purse and bag and sandals, did you lack anything?” They said, “Nothing.”
Luke 22:36  And He said to them, “But now let the one who has a purse take it, and likewise a bag; and let the one who does not have sell his garment and buy a sword.
Luke 22:37  For I tell you that this which is written must be accomplished in Me: ‘And He was numbered with the lawless.’ For what concerns Me is reaching its completion.”
Luke 22:38  They said, “Lord, behold, here are two swords.” And He said to them, “It is enough.”
Luke 22:39  And He went out and traveled, as was His custom, to the Mount of Olives; and the disciples also followed Him.
Luke 22:40  When He came to the place, He said to them, “Pray that you may not enter into testing.”
Luke 22:41  And He withdrew from them about a stone’s throw, knelt down, and prayed,
Luke 22:42  saying, “Father, if Thou art willing, remove this cup from Me. Nevertheless, let not My will but Thine be done.”
Luke 22:43  And an angel from heaven appeared to Him, strengthening Him.
Luke 22:44  And being in agony, He prayed more earnestly, and His sweat became like clots of blood falling to the ground.
Luke 22:45  Rising from prayer, He came to the disciples and found them sleeping from grief.
Luke 22:46  And He said to them, “Why are you sleeping? Rise and pray, so that you may not enter into testing.”
Luke 22:47  While He was still speaking, behold, a crowd came, and the one called Judas, one of the Twelve, was going before them. He drew near to Jesus to kiss Him.
Luke 22:48  But Jesus said to him, “Judas, do you hand over the Son of Man with a kiss?”
Luke 22:49  When those around Him saw what was about to happen, they said, “Lord, shall we strike with a sword?”
Luke 22:50  And one of them struck the high priest’s slave and took off his right ear.
Luke 22:51  But Jesus answered, “Allow this much.” And He touched the ear and healed him.
Luke 22:52  And Jesus said to the chief priests and captains of the temple and elders who had come against Him, “Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs?
Luke 22:53  When I was with you daily in the temple, you did not stretch out your hands against Me. But this is your hour and the authority of darkness.”
Luke 22:54  They seized Him and led Him away and brought Him into the high priest’s house. But Peter was following at a distance.
Luke 22:55  When they had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter sat among them.
Luke 22:56  A certain servant girl saw him sitting by the light and, looking intently at him, said, “This man also was with Him.”
Luke 22:57  But he denied it, saying, “I do not know Him, woman.”
Luke 22:58  After a short time another saw him and said, “You too are one of them.” But Peter said, “Man, I am not.”
Luke 22:59  After about one hour had passed, someone else insisted, saying, “Truly, this man also was with Him, for he too is a Galilean.”
Luke 22:60  But Peter said, “Man, I do not know what you are saying.” And at once, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
Luke 22:61  And the Lord turned and looked at Peter. And Peter remembered the Lord’s word, how He had said to him, “Before a rooster crows today, you will deny Me three times.”
Luke 22:62  And he went outside and wept bitterly.
Luke 22:63  Now the men who were holding Him mocked Him and beat Him.
Luke 22:64  They blindfolded Him and questioned Him, saying, “Prophesy! Who is it that struck Thee?”
Luke 22:65  And they spoke many other things against Him, blaspheming.
Luke 22:66  When day came, the council of elders of the people gathered, both chief priests and scribes, and they led Him into their council,
Luke 22:67  saying, “If Thou art the Christ, tell us.” But He said to them, “If I tell you, you will certainly not believe.
Luke 22:68  And if I ask, you will certainly not answer.
Luke 22:69  But from now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”
Luke 22:70  They all said, “Then art Thou the Son of God?” And He said to them, “You say that I am.”
Luke 22:71  They said, “What further need do we have of testimony? For we ourselves have heard from His own mouth.”

Luke 23
Luke 23:1  Then their whole assembly rose and led Him before Pilate.
Luke 23:2  And they began to accuse Him, saying, “We found this man turning our nation astray and forbidding tribute to be given to Caesar, and saying that He Himself is Christ, a king.”
Luke 23:3  Pilate questioned Him, saying, “Art Thou the King of the Jews?” He answered him, “You say so.”
Luke 23:4  And Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, “I find no ground for a charge against this man.”
Luke 23:5  But they insisted, saying, “He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee even to this place.”
Luke 23:6  When Pilate heard this, he asked whether the man was a Galilean.
Luke 23:7  And learning that He belonged to Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent Him to Herod, who was himself also in Jerusalem in those days.
Luke 23:8  When Herod saw Jesus, he rejoiced greatly, for he had long wanted to see Him because he had heard about Him, and he hoped to see some sign performed by Him.
Luke 23:9  He questioned Him at length, but He gave him no answer.
Luke 23:10  And the chief priests and scribes stood there, accusing Him vehemently.
Luke 23:11  Herod also, with his troops, treated Him with contempt and mocked Him. He clothed Him in splendid clothing and sent Him back to Pilate.
Luke 23:12  Herod and Pilate became friends with one another on that very day, for previously they had been at enmity with each other.
Luke 23:13  Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people
Luke 23:14  and said to them, “You brought this man to me as one turning the people astray. And behold, I examined Him before you and found no ground in this man for the accusations you bring against Him.
Luke 23:15  Nor did Herod, for he sent Him back to us. And behold, nothing deserving death has been done by Him.
Luke 23:16  Therefore I will punish Him and release Him.”
Luke 23:18  But they cried out all together, saying, “Take this man away, and release Barabbas to us!”
Luke 23:19  He had been thrown into prison for a certain uprising that took place in the city and for murder.
Luke 23:20  Pilate addressed them again, wanting to release Jesus.
Luke 23:21  But they kept shouting, saying, “Crucify, crucify Him!”
Luke 23:22  And for the third time he said to them, “Why, what evil has this man done? I found no ground for death in Him. Therefore I will punish Him and release Him.”
Luke 23:23  But they pressed him with loud voices, demanding that He be crucified, and their voices prevailed.
Luke 23:24  And Pilate decided that their demand should be granted.
Luke 23:25  He released the man who had been thrown into prison for uprising and murder, whom they were demanding; but he handed Jesus over to their will.
Luke 23:26  As they led Him away, they seized a certain Simon of Cyrene coming from the countryside, and laid the cross on him to carry behind Jesus.
Luke 23:27  And a great multitude of the people followed Him, and women who beat themselves in mourning and lamented Him.
Luke 23:28  But Jesus turned toward them and said, “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep over Me, but weep over yourselves and over your children.
Luke 23:29  For behold, days are coming in which they will say, ‘Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that did not bear, and the breasts that did not nourish.’
Luke 23:30  Then they will begin to say to the mountains, ‘Fall upon us,’ and to the hills, ‘Cover us.’
Luke 23:31  For if they do these things with the green wood, what will happen with the dry?”
Luke 23:32  Two others also, criminals, were being led with Him to be put to death.
Luke 23:33  When they came to the place called Skull, there they crucified Him and the criminals, one on the right and the other on the left.
Luke 23:34  But Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” And dividing His garments, they cast lots.
Luke 23:35  The people stood watching. The rulers also sneered, saying, “He saved others; let Him save Himself, if this is the Christ of God, the chosen One.”
Luke 23:36  The soldiers also mocked Him, coming up and offering Him sour wine
Luke 23:37  and saying, “If Thou art the King of the Jews, save Thyself.”
Luke 23:38  There was also an inscription above Him: “This is the King of the Jews.”
Luke 23:39  One of the criminals who were hanging there blasphemed Him, saying, “Art Thou not the Christ? Save Thyself and us!”
Luke 23:40  But the other answered, rebuking him, “Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same judgment?
Luke 23:41  And we justly so, for we receive what our deeds deserve. But this man did nothing out of place.”
Luke 23:42  And he said, “Jesus, remember me when Thou comest into Thy kingdom.”
Luke 23:43  And He said to him, “Amen, I tell you: today you will be with Me in Paradise.”
Luke 23:44  And it was already about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour,
Luke 23:45  as the sun’s light failed. And the curtain of the sanctuary was split down the middle.
Luke 23:46  And Jesus cried out with a loud voice and said, “Father, into Thy hands I entrust My spirit.” Having said this, He breathed His last.
Luke 23:47  When the centurion saw what had happened, he glorified God, saying, “Truly, this man was righteous.”
Luke 23:48  And all the crowds who had gathered for this spectacle, seeing what had happened, returned beating their breasts.
Luke 23:49  All His acquaintances stood at a distance, and the women who had followed Him from Galilee, watching these things.
Luke 23:50  And behold, there was a man named Joseph, a council member, a good and righteous man.
Luke 23:51  He had not consented to their decision and action. He was from Arimathea, a city of the Jews, and was awaiting the kingdom of God.
Luke 23:52  This man approached Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
Luke 23:53  Taking it down, he wrapped it in linen and laid Him in a rock-cut tomb where no one had yet been laid.
Luke 23:54  It was the day of Preparation, and the Sabbath was beginning.
Luke 23:55  The women who had come with Him from Galilee followed and saw the tomb and how His body was laid.
Luke 23:56  Then they returned and prepared spices and perfumed ointments. And on the Sabbath they rested according to the commandment.

Luke 24
Luke 24:1  But on the first day of the week, at early dawn, they came to the tomb, carrying the spices they had prepared.
Luke 24:2  They found the stone rolled away from the tomb,
Luke 24:3  but when they entered, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
Luke 24:4  And it happened that, while they were perplexed about this, behold, two men stood beside them in flashing clothing.
Luke 24:5  They became afraid and bowed their faces to the ground, and the men said to them, “Why do you seek the living One among the dead?
Luke 24:6  He is not here, but has been raised. Remember how He spoke to you while He was still in Galilee,
Luke 24:7  saying that the Son of Man must be handed over into the hands of sinful people and be crucified and rise on the third day.”
Luke 24:8  And they remembered His words,
Luke 24:9  and returned from the tomb and reported all these things to the Eleven and to all the rest.
Luke 24:10  It was Mary Magdalene and Joanna and Mary of James and the other women with them who told these things to the apostles.
Luke 24:11  But these words seemed to them like nonsense, and they did not believe the women.
Luke 24:12  Yet Peter rose and ran to the tomb. Stooping to look in, he saw the linen cloths alone, and went away, wondering to himself at what had happened.
Luke 24:13  And behold, two of them were traveling that same day to a village named Emmaus, sixty stadia away from Jerusalem.
Luke 24:14  They were talking with one another about all these things that had happened.
Luke 24:15  And it happened that, as they talked and discussed, Jesus Himself drew near and traveled with them.
Luke 24:16  But their eyes were held back from recognizing Him.
Luke 24:17  And He said to them, “What are these words you are exchanging with one another as you walk?” And they stood still, downcast.
Luke 24:18  One named Cleopas answered Him, “Art Thou the only visitor in Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in these days?”
Luke 24:19  And He said to them, “What things?” They said to Him, “The things concerning Jesus the Nazarene, who was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people,
Luke 24:20  and how our chief priests and rulers handed Him over to a judgment of death and crucified Him.
Luke 24:21  But we were hoping that He was the One about to redeem Israel. Yet indeed, besides all these things, this is the third day since these things happened.
Luke 24:22  Moreover, some women from among us astonished us. They went to the tomb early
Luke 24:23  and did not find His body, and came saying that they had also seen a vision of angels who say that He is alive.
Luke 24:24  And some of those with us went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but Him they did not see.”
Luke 24:25  And He said to them, “O foolish ones, and slow in heart to believe all that the prophets spoke!
Luke 24:26  Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and enter into His glory?”
Luke 24:27  And beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, He interpreted to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning Himself.
Luke 24:28  They drew near the village to which they were traveling, and He acted as though He would travel farther.
Luke 24:29  But they urged Him strongly, saying, “Stay with us, because it is toward evening and the day has already waned.” And He went in to stay with them.
Luke 24:30  And it happened that as He reclined at table with them, He took the bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them.
Luke 24:31  Then their eyes were opened and they recognized Him, and He vanished from their sight.
Luke 24:32  And they said to one another, “Was not our heart burning within us as He spoke to us on the road, as He opened the Scriptures to us?”
Luke 24:33  They rose that very hour and returned to Jerusalem, and found the Eleven and those with them gathered together,
Luke 24:34  saying, “The Lord has truly been raised and has appeared to Simon!”
Luke 24:35  And they related the things that happened on the road, and how He was made known to them in the breaking of the bread.
Luke 24:36  While they were speaking these things, He Himself stood among them and said to them, “Peace be with you.”
Luke 24:37  But they were startled and became afraid, thinking they were seeing a spirit.
Luke 24:38  And He said to them, “Why are you troubled, and why do doubts arise in your heart?
Luke 24:39  See My hands and My feet, that it is I Myself. Feel Me and see, because a spirit does not have flesh and bones as you see that I have.”
Luke 24:40  And having said this, He showed them His hands and feet.
Luke 24:41  While they still did not believe for joy and were marveling, He said to them, “Do you have anything to eat here?”
Luke 24:42  They gave Him a portion of broiled fish.
Luke 24:43  And He took it and ate before them.
Luke 24:44  And He said to them, “These are My words that I spoke to you while I was still with you: everything written about Me in the Law of Moses and the Prophets and Psalms must be fulfilled.”
Luke 24:45  Then He opened their mind to understand the Scriptures
Luke 24:46  and said to them, “Thus it is written that the Christ should suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,
Luke 24:47  and that repentance for the forgiveness of sins should be proclaimed in His name to all the nations—beginning from Jerusalem.
Luke 24:48  You are witnesses of these things.
Luke 24:49  And behold, I am sending out the promise of My Father upon you; but remain in the city until you are clothed with power from on high.”
Luke 24:50  And He led them out as far as toward Bethany, and lifted His hands and blessed them.
Luke 24:51  And it happened that while He blessed them, He parted from them and was carried up into heaven.
Luke 24:52  And they, having worshiped Him, returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
Luke 24:53  and were continually in the temple, blessing God.

JOHN

John 1
John 1:1  In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
John 1:2  He was in the beginning with God.
John 1:3  All things came into being through Him, and without Him not one thing came into being. What has come into being
John 1:4  in Him was life, and the life was the light of humankind.
John 1:5  And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it.
John 1:6  There came a man sent from God; his name was John.
John 1:7  He came as a witness, to bear witness concerning the Light, so that all might believe through him.
John 1:8  He was not the Light, but came to bear witness concerning the Light.
John 1:9  The true Light, which gives light to every person, was coming into the world.
John 1:10  He was in the world, and the world came into being through Him, and the world did not know Him.
John 1:11  He came to what was His own, and His own people did not receive Him.
John 1:12  But to all who received Him, He gave authority to become children of God—to those who believe in His name,
John 1:13  who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of a man, but of God.
John 1:14  And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld His glory, glory as of the Only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth.
John 1:15  John bears witness concerning Him and has cried out, saying, “This was He of whom I said, ‘The One who comes after me has taken precedence over me, because He was before me.’”
John 1:16  For from His fullness we all received, even grace in place of grace.
John 1:17  For the Law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
John 1:18  No one has ever seen God; the Only-begotten God, who is in the bosom of the Father, has made Him known.
John 1:19  And this is the testimony of John, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to him, to ask him, “Who are you?”
John 1:20  And he confessed and did not deny, and confessed, “I am not the Christ.”
John 1:21  They asked him, “What, then? Are you Elijah?” And he said, “I am not.” “Are you the Prophet?” And he answered, “No.”
John 1:22  So they said to him, “Who are you, so that we may give an answer to those who sent us? What do you say about yourself?”
John 1:23  He said, “I am a voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way of the Lord,’ just as Isaiah the prophet said.”
John 1:24  Now those sent were from the Pharisees.
John 1:25  And they questioned him and said to him, “Why, then, do you baptize if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?”
John 1:26  John answered them, saying, “I baptize in water. Among you stands One whom you do not know,
John 1:27  the One coming after me, whose sandal strap I am not worthy to untie.”
John 1:28  These things happened in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
John 1:29  The next day he saw Jesus coming toward him and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!
John 1:30  This is He of whom I said, ‘After me comes a man who has taken precedence over me, because He was before me.’
John 1:31  And I did not know Him, but I came baptizing in water for this reason: so that He might be revealed to Israel.”
John 1:32  And John testified, saying, “I have beheld the Spirit descending like a dove from heaven, and He remained upon Him.
John 1:33  And I did not know Him, but the One who sent me to baptize in water said to me, ‘The One upon whom you see the Spirit descending and remaining—this is the One who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.’
John 1:34  And I have seen and have testified that this is the Son of God.”
John 1:35  The next day John was standing there again, and two of his disciples,
John 1:36  and looking at Jesus as He walked, he said, “Behold, the Lamb of God!”
John 1:37  The two disciples heard him speaking and followed Jesus.
John 1:38  Jesus turned and, seeing them following, said to them, “What do you seek?” They said to Him, “Rabbi”—which, translated, means Teacher—“where art Thou staying?”
John 1:39  He said to them, “Come, and you will see.” So they came and saw where He was staying, and stayed with Him that day. It was about the tenth hour.
John 1:40  Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, was one of the two who heard from John and followed Him.
John 1:41  He first found his own brother Simon and said to him, “We have found the Messiah”—which, translated, is Christ.
John 1:42  He brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, “You are Simon, the son of John; you shall be called Cephas”—which is translated Peter.
John 1:43  The next day He wanted to go out into Galilee. And He found Philip, and Jesus said to him, “Follow Me.”
John 1:44  Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.
John 1:45  Philip found Nathanael and said to him, “We have found the One of whom Moses wrote in the Law, and the prophets also: Jesus, the son of Joseph, from Nazareth.”
John 1:46  Nathanael said to him, “Can anything good come from Nazareth?” Philip said to him, “Come and see.”
John 1:47  Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward Him and said concerning him, “Behold, truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit!”
John 1:48  Nathanael said to Him, “How dost Thou know me?” Jesus answered him, “Before Philip called you, while you were under the fig tree, I saw you.”
John 1:49  Nathanael answered Him, “Rabbi, Thou art the Son of God; Thou art the King of Israel.”
John 1:50  Jesus answered him, “Because I told you that I saw you beneath the fig tree, do you believe? You will see greater things than these.”
John 1:51  And He said to him, “Amen, amen, I tell you all: you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.”

John 2
John 2:1  And on the third day a wedding took place in Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there.
John 2:2  Jesus and His disciples were also invited to the wedding.
John 2:3  When the wine ran short, the mother of Jesus said to Him, “They have no wine.”
John 2:4  And Jesus said to her, “What is this to Me and to you, woman? My hour has not yet come.”
John 2:5  His mother said to the servants, “Whatever He tells you, do.”
John 2:6  Now six stone water jars were set there for the purification of the Jews, each holding two or three metretes.
John 2:7  Jesus said to them, “Fill the jars with water.” And they filled them to the top.
John 2:8  And He said to them, “Draw some out now and take it to the master of the feast.” And they took it.
John 2:9  When the master of the feast tasted the water that had become wine and did not know where it came from—though the servants who had drawn the water knew—the master of the feast called the bridegroom
John 2:10  and said to him, “Everyone sets out the good wine first, and when people have become drunk, the inferior wine. You have kept the good wine until now.”
John 2:11  Jesus did this as the beginning of His signs in Cana of Galilee and manifested His glory, and His disciples believed in Him.
John 2:12  After this He went down to Capernaum, He and His mother and His brothers and His disciples, and they stayed there not many days.
John 2:13  Now the Passover of the Jews was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
John 2:14  And He found in the temple those selling oxen and sheep and doves, and the money changers seated there.
John 2:15  Making a whip from cords, He drove them all out of the temple, both the sheep and the oxen, and poured out the money changers’ coins and overturned their tables.
John 2:16  And He said to those selling the doves, “Take these things away from here. Do not make My Father’s house a house of trade.”
John 2:17  His disciples remembered that it is written, “Zeal for Thy house will consume Me.”
John 2:18  So the Jews answered Him, “What sign dost Thou show us, since Thou doest these things?”
John 2:19  Jesus answered them, “Destroy this sanctuary, and in three days I will raise it.”
John 2:20  So the Jews said, “This sanctuary was built in forty-six years, and wilt Thou raise it in three days?”
John 2:21  But He was speaking about the sanctuary of His body.
John 2:22  When, therefore, He was raised from the dead, His disciples remembered that He had said this, and they believed the Scripture and the word Jesus had spoken.
John 2:23  While He was in Jerusalem at the Passover, during the feast, many believed in His name, seeing the signs He was doing.
John 2:24  But Jesus Himself did not entrust Himself to them, because He knew everyone
John 2:25  and because He had no need for anyone to testify concerning humanity, for He Himself knew what was within a person.

John 3
John 3:1  Now there was a man from the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews.
John 3:2  He came to Him at night and said to Him, “Rabbi, we know that Thou hast come from God as a teacher, for no one can do these signs that Thou doest unless God is with him.”
John 3:3  Jesus answered and said to him, “Amen, amen, I tell you: unless someone is born from above, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”
John 3:4  Nicodemus said to Him, “How can a person be born when he is old? Can he enter his mother’s womb a second time and be born?”
John 3:5  Jesus answered, “Amen, amen, I tell you: unless someone is born from water and Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God.
John 3:6  What is born from the flesh is flesh, and what is born from the Spirit is spirit.
John 3:7  Do not marvel that I said to you, ‘You all must be born from above.’
John 3:8  The wind blows where it wills, and you hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes; so it is with everyone born of the Spirit.”
John 3:9  Nicodemus answered Him, “How can these things happen?”
John 3:10  Jesus answered him, “Are you the teacher of Israel, and do you not understand these things?
John 3:11  Amen, amen, I tell you: we speak what we know and bear witness to what we have seen, and you all do not receive our testimony.
John 3:12  If I told you earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things?
John 3:13  And no one has ascended into heaven except the One who descended from heaven, the Son of Man.
John 3:14  And just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up,
John 3:15  so that everyone who believes may have eternal life in Him.
John 3:16  For God loved the world in this way: He gave the only-begotten Son, so that everyone who believes in Him might not perish but have eternal life.
John 3:17  For God did not send the Son into the world to judge the world, but so that the world might be saved through Him.
John 3:18  The one who believes in Him is not judged; but the one who does not believe has already been judged, because he has not believed in the name of the only-begotten Son of God.
John 3:19  And this is the judgment: the Light has come into the world, and people loved the darkness more than the Light, for their deeds were evil.
John 3:20  For everyone who practices base things hates the light and does not come to the light, so that his deeds may not be exposed.
John 3:21  But the one who does the truth comes to the light, so that his deeds may be manifested, because they have been done in God.”
John 3:22  After these things Jesus and His disciples came into the Judean countryside, and there He stayed with them and was baptizing.
John 3:23  John was also baptizing in Aenon near Salim, because there was much water there, and people came and were baptized.
John 3:24  For John had not yet been thrown into prison.
John 3:25  Then a discussion arose between John’s disciples and a Jew concerning purification.
John 3:26  And they came to John and said to him, “Rabbi, He who was with you beyond the Jordan, to whom you testified—behold, He is baptizing, and everyone is coming to Him.”
John 3:27  John answered, “A person can receive not even one thing unless it has been given to him from heaven.
John 3:28  You yourselves bear witness for me that I said, ‘I am not the Christ, but I have been sent before Him.’
John 3:29  The one who has the bride is the bridegroom. But the bridegroom’s friend, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom’s voice. So this joy of mine has been fulfilled.
John 3:30  He must increase, but I must decrease.”
John 3:31  The One coming from above is above all. The one who is from the earth is from the earth and speaks from the earth. The One coming from heaven is above all.
John 3:32  What He has seen and heard, this He testifies, and no one receives His testimony.
John 3:33  The one who has received His testimony has set his seal that God is true.
John 3:34  For the One whom God sent speaks the words of God, for He gives the Spirit without measure.
John 3:35  The Father loves the Son and has given all things into His hand.
John 3:36  The one who believes in the Son has eternal life; but the one who disobeys the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him.

John 4
John 4:1  So when Jesus learned that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John—
John 4:2  although Jesus Himself was not baptizing, but His disciples—
John 4:3  He left Judea and went away again into Galilee.
John 4:4  And He had to pass through Samaria.
John 4:5  So He came to a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the plot of land Jacob gave to his son Joseph.
John 4:6  Jacob’s spring was there. Jesus, therefore, wearied from the journey, sat down as He was by the spring. It was about the sixth hour.
John 4:7  A woman from Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her, “Give Me a drink.”
John 4:8  For His disciples had gone away into the city to buy food.
John 4:9  So the Samaritan woman said to Him, “How dost Thou, being a Jew, ask a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.
John 4:10  Jesus answered her, “If you knew the gift of God and who it is who says to you, ‘Give Me a drink,’ you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water.”
John 4:11  The woman said to Him, “Sir, Thou hast no vessel for drawing water, and the well is deep. Where, then, dost Thou get this living water?
John 4:12  Art Thou greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well and drank from it himself, and his sons and his livestock?”
John 4:13  Jesus answered her, “Everyone who drinks from this water will thirst again.
John 4:14  But whoever drinks from the water that I will give him will certainly never thirst; rather, the water I will give him will become in him a spring of water leaping up into eternal life.”
John 4:15  The woman said to Him, “Sir, give me this water, so that I may not thirst or come here to draw.”
John 4:16  He said to her, “Go, call your husband, and come here.”
John 4:17  The woman answered Him, “I have no husband.” Jesus said to her, “You have spoken well in saying, ‘I have no husband,’
John 4:18  for you have had five husbands, and the one you have now is not your husband. This you have spoken truly.”
John 4:19  The woman said to Him, “Sir, I see that Thou art a prophet.
John 4:20  Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, and you all say that in Jerusalem is the place where one must worship.”
John 4:21  Jesus said to her, “Believe Me, woman, an hour is coming when neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem will you worship the Father.
John 4:22  You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, because salvation is from the Jews.
John 4:23  But an hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth; for the Father seeks such people to worship Him.
John 4:24  God is spirit, and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and truth.”
John 4:25  The woman said to Him, “I know that Messiah is coming, the One called Christ. When He comes, He will announce all things to us.”
John 4:26  Jesus said to her, “I am He, the One speaking to you.”
John 4:27  At this His disciples came and marveled that He was speaking with a woman. Yet no one said, “What dost Thou seek?” or, “Why art Thou speaking with her?”
John 4:28  So the woman left her water jar and went away into the city and said to the people,
John 4:29  “Come, see a man who told me everything I did. Could this be the Christ?”
John 4:30  They went out of the city and were coming to Him.
John 4:31  Meanwhile the disciples urged Him, saying, “Rabbi, eat.”
John 4:32  But He said to them, “I have food to eat that you do not know.”
John 4:33  So the disciples said to one another, “Has someone brought Him something to eat?”
John 4:34  Jesus said to them, “My food is to do the will of the One who sent Me and to complete His work.
John 4:35  Do you not say, ‘There are still four months, and the harvest comes’? Behold, I tell you, lift your eyes and look at the fields, for they are white for harvest. Already
John 4:36  the one who reaps receives wages and gathers fruit for eternal life, so that the one who sows and the one who reaps may rejoice together.
John 4:37  For in this the saying is true: ‘One is the sower and another the reaper.’
John 4:38  I sent you to reap what you have not labored for. Others have labored, and you have entered into their labor.”
John 4:39  Many of the Samaritans from that city believed in Him because of the word of the woman, who testified, “He told me everything I did.”
John 4:40  So when the Samaritans came to Him, they asked Him to stay with them, and He stayed there two days.
John 4:41  And many more believed because of His word.
John 4:42  They said to the woman, “We no longer believe because of your speech, for we ourselves have heard and know that this is truly the Savior of the world.”
John 4:43  After the two days He went out from there into Galilee.
John 4:44  For Jesus Himself had testified that a prophet has no honor in his own homeland.
John 4:45  So when He came into Galilee, the Galileans welcomed Him, having seen everything He did in Jerusalem at the feast, for they too had gone to the feast.
John 4:46  So He came again to Cana of Galilee, where He made the water wine. And there was a certain royal official whose son was ill in Capernaum.
John 4:47  When this man heard that Jesus had come from Judea into Galilee, he went to Him and asked Him to come down and heal his son, for he was about to die.
John 4:48  So Jesus said to him, “Unless you all see signs and wonders, you will certainly not believe.”
John 4:49  The royal official said to Him, “Sir, come down before my little child dies.”
John 4:50  Jesus said to him, “Go; your son lives.” The man believed the word Jesus spoke to him and went on his way.
John 4:51  While he was already going down, his slaves met him, saying that his boy was alive.
John 4:52  So he asked them the hour when he had begun to improve. They said to him, “Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.”
John 4:53  So the father knew that it was in that hour when Jesus said to him, “Your son lives,” and he believed, he and his whole household.
John 4:54  This again was the second sign Jesus did when He came from Judea into Galilee.

John 5
John 5:1  After these things there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
John 5:2  Now in Jerusalem by the Sheep Gate there is a pool called Bethzatha in Hebrew, having five porticoes.
John 5:3  In these lay a multitude of the sick, the blind, the lame, and those with withered limbs.
John 5:5  And a certain man was there who had been ill for thirty-eight years.
John 5:6  Jesus, seeing him lying there and knowing that he had already been that way a long time, said to him, “Do you want to become well?”
John 5:7  The sick man answered Him, “Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred. While I am coming, someone else goes down before me.”
John 5:8  Jesus said to him, “Rise, take up your mat, and walk.”
John 5:9  And at once the man became well, took up his mat, and walked. Now it was a Sabbath on that day.
John 5:10  So the Jews said to the man who had been healed, “It is a Sabbath, and it is not lawful for you to take up the mat.”
John 5:11  But he answered them, “The One who made me well said to me, ‘Take up your mat and walk.’”
John 5:12  So they asked him, “Who is the man who told you, ‘Take it up and walk’?”
John 5:13  But the man who had been healed did not know who He was, for Jesus had slipped away, since there was a crowd in the place.
John 5:14  After these things Jesus found him in the temple and said to him, “Behold, you have become well. Sin no more, so that something worse may not happen to you.”
John 5:15  The man went away and reported to the Jews that it was Jesus who made him well.
John 5:16  And for this reason the Jews persecuted Jesus, because He did these things on a Sabbath.
John 5:17  But Jesus answered them, “My Father is working even now, and I am working.”
John 5:18  For this reason, therefore, the Jews sought all the more to kill Him, because He not only broke the Sabbath, but also called God His own Father, making Himself equal to God.
John 5:19  So Jesus answered them, “Amen, amen, I tell you: the Son can do nothing from Himself unless He sees the Father doing it. For whatever He does, the Son also does these things in the same way.
John 5:20  For the Father loves the Son and shows Him everything He Himself does, and He will show Him works greater than these, so that you may marvel.
John 5:21  For just as the Father raises the dead and gives life, so also the Son gives life to whom He wills.
John 5:22  For the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son,
John 5:23  so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. The one who does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent Him.
John 5:24  Amen, amen, I tell you: the one who hears My word and believes the One who sent Me has eternal life, and does not come into judgment, but has passed from death into life.
John 5:25  Amen, amen, I tell you: an hour is coming, and now is, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.
John 5:26  For just as the Father has life in Himself, so He also gave the Son to have life in Himself.
John 5:27  And He gave Him authority to execute judgment, because He is the Son of Man.
John 5:28  Do not marvel at this, because an hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs will hear His voice
John 5:29  and come out: those who did good things to a resurrection of life, but those who practiced base things to a resurrection of judgment.
John 5:30  I can do nothing from Myself. As I hear, I judge, and My judgment is righteous, because I do not seek My own will, but the will of the One who sent Me.
John 5:31  If I bear witness concerning Myself, My testimony is not true.
John 5:32  There is Another who bears witness concerning Me, and I know that the testimony He bears concerning Me is true.
John 5:33  You have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.
John 5:34  But I do not receive testimony from a person; rather, I say these things so that you may be saved.
John 5:35  He was the lamp that burned and shone, and you were willing to rejoice for an hour in his light.
John 5:36  But I have testimony greater than John’s: for the works the Father has given Me to complete, the very works I do, bear witness concerning Me that the Father has sent Me.
John 5:37  And the Father who sent Me has Himself testified concerning Me. You have never heard His voice or seen His form,
John 5:38  and you do not have His word remaining in you, because you do not believe the One He sent.
John 5:39  You search the Scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life; and it is they that bear witness concerning Me.
John 5:40  Yet you are unwilling to come to Me so that you may have life.
John 5:41  I do not receive glory from people,
John 5:42  but I know you, that you do not have the love of God within yourselves.
John 5:43  I have come in My Father’s name, and you do not receive Me. If another comes in his own name, you will receive him.
John 5:44  How can you believe, receiving glory from one another, and not seeking the glory that comes from the only God?
John 5:45  Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father. There is one who accuses you: Moses, in whom you have set your hope.
John 5:46  For if you believed Moses, you would believe Me, for he wrote concerning Me.
John 5:47  But if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe My words?”

John 6
John 6:1  After these things Jesus went away across the Sea of Galilee, the Sea of Tiberias.
John 6:2  A great crowd followed Him, because they were seeing the signs He did upon the sick.
John 6:3  Jesus went up the mountain and sat there with His disciples.
John 6:4  Now the Passover, the feast of the Jews, was near.
John 6:5  So Jesus lifted His eyes and, seeing that a great crowd was coming toward Him, said to Philip, “Where are we to buy loaves so that these people may eat?”
John 6:6  He said this to test him, for He Himself knew what He was about to do.
John 6:7  Philip answered Him, “Two hundred denarii worth of loaves are not enough for them, so that each may receive even a little.”
John 6:8  One of His disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to Him,
John 6:9  “There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two small fish. But what are these among so many?”
John 6:10  Jesus said, “Have the people recline.” Now there was much grass in the place. So the men reclined, about five thousand in number.
John 6:11  Then Jesus took the loaves, gave thanks, and distributed them to those reclining, and likewise from the fish, as much as they wanted.
John 6:12  When they were filled, He said to His disciples, “Gather the remaining fragments, so that nothing may be lost.”
John 6:13  So they gathered them and filled twelve baskets with fragments from the five barley loaves that remained over from those who had eaten.
John 6:14  When the people saw the sign He did, they said, “This is truly the Prophet who is coming into the world.”
John 6:15  So Jesus, knowing that they were about to come and seize Him to make Him king, withdrew again to the mountain, Himself alone.
John 6:16  When evening came, His disciples went down to the sea.
John 6:17  They entered a boat and were going across the sea toward Capernaum. Darkness had already come, and Jesus had not yet come to them,
John 6:18  and the sea was being stirred up by a strong wind blowing.
John 6:19  So when they had rowed about twenty-five or thirty stadia, they saw Jesus walking upon the sea and drawing near the boat, and they were afraid.
John 6:20  But He said to them, “It is I; do not fear.”
John 6:21  Then they were willing to receive Him into the boat, and at once the boat was at the land to which they were going.
John 6:22  The next day, the crowd standing across the sea saw that there had been no other small boat there except one, and that Jesus had not entered the boat with His disciples, but His disciples had gone away alone.
John 6:23  Other small boats came from Tiberias near the place where they ate the bread after the Lord had given thanks.
John 6:24  So when the crowd saw that Jesus was not there, nor His disciples, they themselves entered the small boats and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus.
John 6:25  Finding Him across the sea, they said to Him, “Rabbi, when didst Thou come here?”
John 6:26  Jesus answered them, “Amen, amen, I tell you: you seek Me not because you saw signs, but because you ate from the loaves and were filled.
John 6:27  Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that remains for eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you; for upon Him the Father, God, has set His seal.”
John 6:28  So they said to Him, “What are we to do, so that we may work the works of God?”
John 6:29  Jesus answered them, “This is the work of God: that you believe in the One He sent.”
John 6:30  So they said to Him, “What sign, then, dost Thou perform, so that we may see and believe Thee? What work dost Thou do?
John 6:31  Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, just as it is written, ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’”
John 6:32  So Jesus said to them, “Amen, amen, I tell you: Moses has not given you the bread from heaven, but My Father gives you the true bread from heaven.
John 6:33  For the bread of God is the One who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.”
John 6:34  So they said to Him, “Lord, always give us this bread.”
John 6:35  Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life; the one who comes to Me will certainly never hunger, and the one who believes in Me will certainly never thirst.
John 6:36  But I told you that you have both seen Me and do not believe.
John 6:37  Everything the Father gives Me will come to Me, and the one who comes to Me I will certainly not cast out,
John 6:38  because I have come down from heaven not to do My own will, but the will of the One who sent Me.
John 6:39  And this is the will of the One who sent Me: that of everything He has given Me I should lose nothing, but raise it up on the last day.
John 6:40  For this is My Father’s will: that everyone who beholds the Son and believes in Him should have eternal life, and I Myself will raise him up on the last day.”
John 6:41  So the Jews grumbled concerning Him, because He said, “I am the bread that came down from heaven.”
John 6:42  And they said, “Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How does He now say, ‘I have come down from heaven’?”
John 6:43  Jesus answered them, “Do not grumble among yourselves.
John 6:44  No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him, and I will raise him up on the last day.
John 6:45  It is written in the Prophets, ‘And they shall all be taught by God.’ Everyone who has heard from the Father and learned comes to Me.
John 6:46  Not that anyone has seen the Father except the One who is from God; He has seen the Father.
John 6:47  Amen, amen, I tell you: the one who believes has eternal life.
John 6:48  I am the bread of life.
John 6:49  Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness and died.
John 6:50  This is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that someone may eat from it and not die.
John 6:51  I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats from this bread, he will live forever. And the bread that I will give is My flesh, for the life of the world.”
John 6:52  So the Jews disputed with one another, saying, “How can this man give us His flesh to eat?”
John 6:53  So Jesus said to them, “Amen, amen, I tell you: unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood, you have no life in yourselves.
John 6:54  The one who eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.
John 6:55  For My flesh is true food, and My blood is true drink.
John 6:56  The one who eats My flesh and drinks My blood remains in Me, and I in him.
John 6:57  Just as the living Father sent Me and I live because of the Father, so the one who eats Me will also live because of Me.
John 6:58  This is the bread that came down from heaven, not as the fathers ate and died. The one who eats this bread will live forever.”
John 6:59  He said these things while teaching in a synagogue in Capernaum.
John 6:60  So many of His disciples, when they heard, said, “This saying is hard. Who can hear it?”
John 6:61  But Jesus, knowing within Himself that His disciples were grumbling about this, said to them, “Does this cause you to stumble?
John 6:62  Then what if you see the Son of Man ascending where He was before?
John 6:63  The Spirit is the One who gives life; the flesh benefits nothing. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and are life.
John 6:64  But there are some among you who do not believe.” For Jesus knew from the beginning who those were who did not believe and who it was who would hand Him over.
John 6:65  And He said, “For this reason I have told you that no one can come to Me unless it has been given to him from the Father.”
John 6:66  From this, many of His disciples went back and no longer walked with Him.
John 6:67  So Jesus said to the Twelve, “Do you also want to go away?”
John 6:68  Simon Peter answered Him, “Lord, to whom shall we go? Thou hast words of eternal life.
John 6:69  And we have believed and have known that Thou art the Holy One of God.”
John 6:70  Jesus answered them, “Did I not choose you, the Twelve? Yet one of you is a devil.”
John 6:71  He was speaking of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, for this man was about to hand Him over, one of the Twelve.

John 7
John 7:1  After these things Jesus walked about in Galilee, for He did not want to walk about in Judea, because the Jews were seeking to kill Him.
John 7:2  Now the feast of the Jews, the feast of Booths, was near.
John 7:3  So His brothers said to Him, “Leave here and go into Judea, so that Thy disciples also may see the works Thou doest.
John 7:4  For no one acts in secret while seeking to be known publicly. If Thou doest these things, reveal Thyself to the world.”
John 7:5  For not even His brothers believed in Him.
John 7:6  So Jesus said to them, “My time is not yet here, but your time is always ready.
John 7:7  The world cannot hate you, but it hates Me, because I testify concerning it that its works are evil.
John 7:8  You go up to the feast. I am not going up to this feast, because My time has not yet been fulfilled.”
John 7:9  Having said these things, He remained in Galilee.
John 7:10  But when His brothers had gone up to the feast, then He also went up, not openly, but as in secret.
John 7:11  So the Jews sought Him at the feast and said, “Where is He?”
John 7:12  And there was much grumbling about Him among the crowds. Some said, “He is good,” but others said, “No, He leads the crowd astray.”
John 7:13  Yet no one spoke openly about Him because of fear of the Jews.
John 7:14  When the feast was already halfway through, Jesus went up into the temple and taught.
John 7:15  So the Jews marveled, saying, “How does this man know the writings without having studied?”
John 7:16  So Jesus answered them, “My teaching is not Mine, but belongs to the One who sent Me.
John 7:17  If anyone wills to do His will, he will know concerning the teaching whether it is from God or whether I speak from Myself.
John 7:18  The one who speaks from himself seeks his own glory. But the one who seeks the glory of the one who sent him is true, and there is no unrighteousness in him.
John 7:19  Has not Moses given you the Law? Yet none of you keeps the Law. Why do you seek to kill Me?”
John 7:20  The crowd answered, “Thou hast a demon! Who seeks to kill Thee?”
John 7:21  Jesus answered them, “I did one work, and you all marvel.
John 7:22  For this reason Moses has given you circumcision—not that it is from Moses, but from the fathers—and on a Sabbath you circumcise a person.
John 7:23  If a person receives circumcision on a Sabbath so that the Law of Moses may not be broken, are you angry with Me because I made a whole person well on a Sabbath?
John 7:24  Do not judge according to appearance, but judge with righteous judgment.”
John 7:25  So some of the Jerusalem residents said, “Is this not the man they are seeking to kill?
John 7:26  And behold, He speaks openly, and they say nothing to Him. Could the rulers truly have recognized that this is the Christ?
John 7:27  But we know where this man is from; when the Christ comes, no one knows where He is from.”
John 7:28  So Jesus cried out as He taught in the temple, saying, “You both know Me and know where I am from. Yet I have not come from Myself, but the One who sent Me is true, whom you do not know.
John 7:29  I know Him, because I am from Him and He sent Me.”
John 7:30  So they sought to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him, because His hour had not yet come.
John 7:31  But many from the crowd believed in Him and said, “When the Christ comes, will He do more signs than this man has done?”
John 7:32  The Pharisees heard the crowd grumbling these things about Him, and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to seize Him.
John 7:33  So Jesus said, “I am with you for a little time longer, and I go to the One who sent Me.
John 7:34  You will seek Me and will not find Me, and where I am, you cannot come.”
John 7:35  So the Jews said among themselves, “Where is this man about to go that we will not find Him? Is He about to go to the Dispersion among the Greeks and teach the Greeks?
John 7:36  What is this saying He spoke: ‘You will seek Me and will not find Me, and where I am, you cannot come’?”
John 7:37  On the last day, the great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried out, saying, “If anyone thirsts, let him come to Me and drink.
John 7:38  The one who believes in Me—as the Scripture said, rivers of living water will flow from his belly.”
John 7:39  He said this concerning the Spirit, whom those who believed in Him were about to receive; for the Spirit was not yet, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.
[EDITORIAL NOTE: Reading note on John 7:39 — editorial. “The Spirit was not yet” concerns the giving or reception of the Spirit in relation to Jesus’ glorification, as the surrounding verse explains; it is not a statement that the Holy Spirit did not exist. Some English translations supply “given.” The reading text preserves the selected Greek wording. See the linked comparison edition for its textual explanation. This note is separate from the verse.]
John 7:40  So some from the crowd, hearing these words, said, “This is truly the Prophet.”
John 7:41  Others said, “This is the Christ.” But some said, “Surely the Christ does not come from Galilee?
John 7:42  Has not the Scripture said that the Christ comes from the offspring of David and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?”
John 7:43  So a division arose in the crowd because of Him.
John 7:44  Some of them wanted to seize Him, but no one laid hands on Him.
John 7:45  So the officers came to the chief priests and Pharisees, and these said to them, “Why did you not bring Him?”
John 7:46  The officers answered, “Never has a person spoken in this way.”
John 7:47  So the Pharisees answered them, “Have you also been led astray?
John 7:48  Has any of the rulers believed in Him, or any of the Pharisees?
John 7:49  But this crowd that does not know the Law is accursed.”
John 7:50  Nicodemus, who had come to Him earlier and was one of them, said to them,
John 7:51  “Does our Law judge a person unless it first hears from him and knows what he does?”
John 7:52  They answered him, “Are you also from Galilee? Search and see that a prophet does not arise from Galilee.”
John 7:53  ⟦And each went to his own house.

John 8
John 8:1  But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
John 8:2  At dawn He came again into the temple, and all the people were coming to Him; and He sat down and taught them.
John 8:3  And the scribes and the Pharisees brought a woman caught in adultery, and set her in the midst.
John 8:4  They said to Him, “Teacher, this woman was caught in the very act of committing adultery.
John 8:5  Now in the Law Moses commanded us that such women be stoned. What, then, dost Thou say?”
John 8:6  They said this to test Him, so that they might have something with which to accuse Him. But Jesus bent down and wrote with His finger on the ground.
John 8:7  As they persisted in questioning Him, He straightened up and said to them, “Let the one among you who is without sin be first to cast a stone at her.”
John 8:8  And again He bent down and wrote on the ground.
John 8:9  But when they heard, they went out one by one, beginning with the older ones. And Jesus was left alone, and the woman standing in the midst.
John 8:10  Jesus straightened up and said to her, “Woman, where are they? Has no one condemned you?”
John 8:11  She said, “No one, Lord.” Jesus said, “Neither do I condemn you. Go, and from now on sin no more.”⟧
John 8:12  Then Jesus spoke to them again, saying, “I am the Light of the world. The one who follows Me will certainly not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”
John 8:13  So the Pharisees said to Him, “Thou bearest witness concerning Thyself; Thy testimony is not true.”
John 8:14  Jesus answered them, “Even if I bear witness concerning Myself, My testimony is true, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I come from or where I am going.
John 8:15  You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one.
John 8:16  But even if I judge, My judgment is true, because I am not alone, but I and the Father who sent Me.
John 8:17  And in your own Law it is written that the testimony of two people is true.
John 8:18  I am the One who bears witness concerning Myself, and the Father who sent Me bears witness concerning Me.”
John 8:19  So they said to Him, “Where is Thy Father?” Jesus answered, “You know neither Me nor My Father. If you knew Me, you would also know My Father.”
John 8:20  He spoke these words at the treasury as He taught in the temple, and no one seized Him, because His hour had not yet come.
John 8:21  So He said to them again, “I am going away, and you will seek Me, and you will die in your sin. Where I go, you cannot come.”
John 8:22  So the Jews said, “Will He kill Himself, since He says, ‘Where I go, you cannot come’?”
John 8:23  And He said to them, “You are from below; I am from above. You are from this world; I am not from this world.
John 8:24  Therefore I told you that you will die in your sins; for unless you believe that I am, you will die in your sins.”
John 8:25  So they said to Him, “Who art Thou?” Jesus said to them, “Why do I even speak to you at all?
John 8:26  I have many things to speak and judge concerning you. But the One who sent Me is true, and what I heard from Him, these things I speak to the world.”
John 8:27  They did not understand that He was speaking to them about the Father.
John 8:28  So Jesus said to them, “When you lift up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am, and that I do nothing from Myself, but speak these things just as the Father taught Me.
John 8:29  And the One who sent Me is with Me. He has not left Me alone, because I always do the things pleasing to Him.”
John 8:30  As He spoke these things, many believed in Him.
John 8:31  So Jesus said to the Jews who had believed Him, “If you remain in My word, you are truly My disciples,
John 8:32  and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”
John 8:33  They answered Him, “We are Abraham’s offspring and have never been slaves to anyone. How dost Thou say, ‘You will become free’?”
John 8:34  Jesus answered them, “Amen, amen, I tell you: everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin.
John 8:35  But the slave does not remain in the house forever; the son remains forever.
John 8:36  So if the Son sets you free, you will truly be free.
John 8:37  I know that you are Abraham’s offspring. Yet you seek to kill Me, because My word has no room in you.
John 8:38  I speak what I have seen with the Father, and you therefore do what you have heard from the father.”
John 8:39  They answered Him, “Our father is Abraham.” Jesus said to them, “If you are Abraham’s children, you would be doing Abraham’s works.
John 8:40  But now you seek to kill Me, a man who has spoken to you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham did not do this.
John 8:41  You do the works of your father.” Then they said to Him, “We were not born from sexual immorality. We have one Father, God.”
John 8:42  Jesus said to them, “If God were your Father, you would love Me, for I came out from God and have come here. For I have not come from Myself, but He sent Me.
John 8:43  Why do you not understand My speech? Because you cannot hear My word.
John 8:44  You are from your father, the devil, and you want to carry out your father’s desires. He was a murderer from the beginning and has not stood in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks the lie, he speaks from what is his own, because he is a liar and its father.
John 8:45  But because I speak the truth, you do not believe Me.
John 8:46  Which of you convicts Me of sin? If I speak truth, why do you not believe Me?
John 8:47  The one who is from God hears the words of God. For this reason you do not hear, because you are not from God.”
John 8:48  The Jews answered Him, “Do we not rightly say that Thou art a Samaritan and hast a demon?”
John 8:49  Jesus answered, “I do not have a demon, but I honor My Father, and you dishonor Me.
John 8:50  But I do not seek My own glory. There is One who seeks it and judges.
John 8:51  Amen, amen, I tell you: if anyone keeps My word, he will certainly never behold death.”
John 8:52  So the Jews said to Him, “Now we know that Thou hast a demon. Abraham died, and the prophets also, and Thou sayest, ‘If anyone keeps My word, he will certainly never taste death.’
John 8:53  Art Thou greater than our father Abraham, who died? The prophets also died. Who dost Thou make Thyself out to be?”
John 8:54  Jesus answered, “If I glorify Myself, My glory is nothing. It is My Father who glorifies Me, of whom you say, ‘He is our God.’
John 8:55  Yet you have not known Him, but I know Him. And if I say that I do not know Him, I will be a liar like you. But I know Him and keep His word.
John 8:56  Abraham your father rejoiced to see My day, and he saw it and was glad.”
John 8:57  So the Jews said to Him, “Thou art not yet fifty years old, and hast Thou seen Abraham?”
John 8:58  Jesus said to them, “Amen, amen, I tell you: before Abraham came into being, I am.”
John 8:59  So they took up stones to cast at Him, but Jesus hid Himself and went out of the temple.

John 9
John 9:1  And as He passed by, He saw a man blind from birth.
John 9:2  His disciples asked Him, saying, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, so that he was born blind?”
John 9:3  Jesus answered, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned, but this was so that the works of God might be revealed in him.
John 9:4  We must work the works of the One who sent Me while it is day. Night is coming, when no one can work.
John 9:5  While I am in the world, I am the Light of the world.”
John 9:6  Having said these things, He spat on the ground and made mud from the spittle, and spread the mud upon his eyes.
John 9:7  And He said to him, “Go, wash in the pool of Siloam”—which is translated Sent. So he went away and washed, and came back seeing.
John 9:8  Then the neighbors and those who had seen him before as a beggar said, “Is this not the one who sat and begged?”
John 9:9  Some said, “This is he.” Others said, “No, but he is like him.” He said, “I am he.”
John 9:10  So they said to him, “How, then, were your eyes opened?”
John 9:11  He answered, “The man called Jesus made mud and spread it on my eyes and said to me, ‘Go to Siloam and wash.’ So I went away and washed, and received my sight.”
John 9:12  And they said to him, “Where is He?” He said, “I do not know.”
John 9:13  They brought the man who had formerly been blind to the Pharisees.
John 9:14  Now it was a Sabbath on the day when Jesus made the mud and opened his eyes.
John 9:15  So the Pharisees also asked him again how he received his sight. He said to them, “He put mud on my eyes, and I washed, and I see.”
John 9:16  Then some of the Pharisees said, “This man is not from God, because He does not keep the Sabbath.” But others said, “How can a sinful man do such signs?” And there was division among them.
John 9:17  So they said to the blind man again, “What do you say about Him, since He opened your eyes?” He said, “He is a prophet.”
John 9:18  So the Jews did not believe concerning him that he had been blind and received his sight, until they called the parents of the man who had received his sight
John 9:19  and asked them, saying, “Is this your son, whom you say was born blind? How, then, does he now see?”
John 9:20  His parents answered, “We know that this is our son and that he was born blind.
John 9:21  But how he now sees we do not know, or who opened his eyes we do not know. Ask him; he is of age. He will speak for himself.”
John 9:22  His parents said these things because they feared the Jews, for the Jews had already agreed that if anyone confessed Him as Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue.
John 9:23  For this reason his parents said, “He is of age; ask him.”
John 9:24  So for the second time they called the man who had been blind and said to him, “Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner.”
John 9:25  He answered, “Whether He is a sinner I do not know. One thing I know: though I was blind, now I see.”
John 9:26  So they said to him, “What did He do to you? How did He open your eyes?”
John 9:27  He answered them, “I told you already, and you did not hear. Why do you want to hear again? Do you also want to become His disciples?”
John 9:28  They reviled him and said, “You are that man’s disciple, but we are Moses’ disciples.
John 9:29  We know that God has spoken to Moses, but this man—we do not know where He is from.”
John 9:30  The man answered them, “Why, this is the marvelous thing: you do not know where He is from, and He opened my eyes!
John 9:31  We know that God does not hear sinners, but if anyone worships God and does His will, He hears that person.
John 9:32  Since the age began, no one has heard of anyone opening the eyes of a person born blind.
John 9:33  If this man were not from God, He could do nothing.”
John 9:34  They answered him, “You were born entirely in sins, and do you teach us?” And they cast him out.
John 9:35  Jesus heard that they had cast him out, and when He found him, He said, “Do you believe in the Son of Man?”
John 9:36  He answered, “And who is He, Sir, so that I may believe in Him?”
John 9:37  Jesus said to him, “You have both seen Him, and the One speaking with you is He.”
John 9:38  He said, “I believe, Lord,” and worshiped Him.
John 9:39  And Jesus said, “For judgment I came into this world, so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind.”
John 9:40  Some of the Pharisees who were with Him heard these things and said to Him, “Are we also blind?”
John 9:41  Jesus said to them, “If you were blind, you would not have sin. But now you say, ‘We see’; your sin remains.”

John 10
John 10:1  “Amen, amen, I tell you: the one who does not enter the sheepfold through the door, but climbs in from elsewhere, is a thief and a robber.
John 10:2  But the one who enters through the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
John 10:3  To him the doorkeeper opens, and the sheep hear his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
John 10:4  When he has brought all his own out, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice.
John 10:5  But they will certainly not follow a stranger; rather, they will flee from him, because they do not know the voice of strangers.”
John 10:6  Jesus spoke this figure of speech to them, but they did not understand what He was saying to them.
John 10:7  So Jesus spoke to them again: “Amen, amen, I tell you that I am the door of the sheep.
John 10:8  All who came before Me are thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not hear them.
John 10:9  I am the door. If anyone enters through Me, he will be saved, and will go in and go out and find pasture.
John 10:10  The thief comes only to steal and slaughter and destroy. I came so that they may have life and have abundance.
John 10:11  I am the good Shepherd; the good Shepherd lays down His life for the sheep.
John 10:12  The hired worker, who is not a shepherd and does not own the sheep, sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep and flees—and the wolf seizes them and scatters them—
John 10:13  because he is a hired worker and does not care for the sheep.
John 10:14  I am the good Shepherd, and I know My own, and My own know Me,
