John 10:15  just as the Father knows Me and I know the Father; and I lay down My life for the sheep.
John 10:16  And I have other sheep that are not from this fold. I must bring them also, and they will hear My voice, and they will become one flock, one shepherd.
John 10:17  For this reason the Father loves Me, because I lay down My life, so that I may take it again.
John 10:18  No one takes it from Me, but I lay it down of My own accord. I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it again. This command I received from My Father.”
John 10:19  Division arose again among the Jews because of these words.
John 10:20  Many of them said, “He has a demon and is mad. Why do you listen to Him?”
John 10:21  Others said, “These are not the words of a demon-possessed person. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?”
John 10:22  Then the feast of Dedication took place in Jerusalem. It was winter,
John 10:23  and Jesus was walking in the temple, in Solomon’s Portico.
John 10:24  So the Jews surrounded Him and said to Him, “How long wilt Thou keep our soul in suspense? If Thou art the Christ, tell us openly.”
John 10:25  Jesus answered them, “I told you, and you do not believe. The works I do in My Father’s name bear witness concerning Me.
John 10:26  But you do not believe, because you are not from My sheep.
John 10:27  My sheep hear My voice, and I know them, and they follow Me.
John 10:28  And I give them eternal life, and they will certainly never perish, and no one will snatch them from My hand.
John 10:29  What My Father has given Me is greater than all, and no one can snatch from the Father’s hand.
John 10:30  I and the Father are one.”
John 10:31  Then the Jews took up stones again to stone Him.
John 10:32  Jesus answered them, “I showed you many good works from the Father. For which work among them do you stone Me?”
John 10:33  The Jews answered Him, “We do not stone Thee for a good work, but for blasphemy, and because Thou, being a man, makest Thyself God.”
John 10:34  Jesus answered them, “Is it not written in your Law, ‘I said, you are gods’?
John 10:35  If He called them gods, to whom the word of God came—and the Scripture cannot be broken—
John 10:36  do you say to the One whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, ‘Thou blasphemest,’ because I said, ‘I am the Son of God’?
John 10:37  If I do not do My Father’s works, do not believe Me.
John 10:38  But if I do them, even if you do not believe Me, believe the works, so that you may know and continue to know that the Father is in Me and I in the Father.”
John 10:39  So they sought again to seize Him, and He went out from their hand.
John 10:40  And He went away again beyond the Jordan, to the place where John was first baptizing, and remained there.
John 10:41  Many came to Him and said, “John indeed did no sign, but everything John said concerning this man was true.”
John 10:42  And many believed in Him there.

John 11
John 11:1  Now a certain man was ill, Lazarus of Bethany, from the village of Mary and her sister Martha.
John 11:2  It was Mary who anointed the Lord with perfumed ointment and wiped His feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was ill.
John 11:3  So the sisters sent to Him, saying, “Lord, behold, the one Thou lovest is ill.”
John 11:4  When Jesus heard, He said, “This illness is not for death, but for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.”
John 11:5  Now Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.
John 11:6  So when He heard that he was ill, He then remained two days in the place where He was.
John 11:7  After this He said to the disciples, “Let us go into Judea again.”
John 11:8  The disciples said to Him, “Rabbi, the Jews were just now seeking to stone Thee, and art Thou going there again?”
John 11:9  Jesus answered, “Are there not twelve hours of the day? If anyone walks in the day, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world.
John 11:10  But if anyone walks in the night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him.”
John 11:11  He said these things, and after this He said to them, “Lazarus our friend has fallen asleep, but I am going to awaken him.”
John 11:12  So the disciples said to Him, “Lord, if he has fallen asleep, he will be saved.”
John 11:13  But Jesus had spoken of his death, while they thought He was speaking of resting in sleep.
John 11:14  So then Jesus told them openly, “Lazarus died,
John 11:15  and for your sake I rejoice that I was not there, so that you may believe. But let us go to him.”
John 11:16  Then Thomas, who was called Didymus, said to his fellow disciples, “Let us also go, so that we may die with Him.”
John 11:17  So when Jesus came, He found that he had already been in the tomb four days.
John 11:18  Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away.
John 11:19  Many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to console them concerning their brother.
John 11:20  When Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went to meet Him, but Mary remained seated in the house.
John 11:21  So Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if Thou hadst been here, my brother would not have died.
John 11:22  But even now I know that whatever Thou askest of God, God will give Thee.”
John 11:23  Jesus said to her, “Your brother will rise.”
John 11:24  Martha said to Him, “I know that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day.”
John 11:25  Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life; the one who believes in Me will live, even if he dies,
John 11:26  and everyone who lives and believes in Me will certainly never die. Do you believe this?”
John 11:27  She said to Him, “Yes, Lord. I have believed that Thou art the Christ, the Son of God, the One coming into the world.”
John 11:28  Having said this, she went away and called her sister Mary secretly, saying, “The Teacher is here and calls you.”
John 11:29  When she heard, she rose quickly and came to Him.
John 11:30  Now Jesus had not yet entered the village, but was still at the place where Martha had met Him.
John 11:31  So the Jews who were with her in the house consoling her, seeing that Mary rose quickly and went out, followed her, thinking that she was going to the tomb to weep there.
John 11:32  When Mary came where Jesus was and saw Him, she fell at His feet and said to Him, “Lord, if Thou hadst been here, my brother would not have died.”
John 11:33  So when Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her weeping, He was indignant in spirit and troubled Himself.
John 11:34  And He said, “Where have you laid him?” They said to Him, “Lord, come and see.”
John 11:35  Jesus wept.
John 11:36  So the Jews said, “Behold, how He loved him!”
John 11:37  But some of them said, “Could not this man, who opened the blind man’s eyes, have kept this man from dying too?”
John 11:38  Then Jesus, again indignant within Himself, came to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone lay against it.
John 11:39  Jesus said, “Take away the stone.” Martha, the dead man’s sister, said to Him, “Lord, there is already a smell, for he has been dead four days.”
John 11:40  Jesus said to her, “Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?”
John 11:41  So they took away the stone. Jesus lifted His eyes upward and said, “Father, I thank Thee that Thou didst hear Me.
John 11:42  I knew that Thou always hearest Me, but I said this because of the crowd standing around, so that they may believe that Thou didst send Me.”
John 11:43  Having said these things, He cried out with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”
John 11:44  The dead man came out, his feet and hands bound with strips of cloth, and his face wrapped with a cloth. Jesus said to them, “Unbind him, and let him go.”
John 11:45  So many of the Jews who had come to Mary and beheld what He did believed in Him.
John 11:46  But some of them went away to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus did.
John 11:47  Then the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered a council and said, “What are we doing? For this man does many signs.
John 11:48  If we leave Him like this, everyone will believe in Him, and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.”
John 11:49  But a certain one of them, Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them, “You know nothing,
John 11:50  nor do you consider that it is better for you for one man to die for the people than for the whole nation to perish.”
John 11:51  He did not say this from himself, but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus was about to die for the nation,
John 11:52  and not for the nation alone, but also to gather into one the children of God who had been scattered.
John 11:53  So from that day they planned to kill Him.
John 11:54  Therefore Jesus no longer walked openly among the Jews, but went away from there into the region near the wilderness, to a city called Ephraim, and stayed there with the disciples.
John 11:55  Now the Passover of the Jews was near, and many went up to Jerusalem from the countryside before the Passover to purify themselves.
John 11:56  So they sought Jesus and said to one another as they stood in the temple, “What do you think? Surely He will not come to the feast?”
John 11:57  The chief priests and the Pharisees had given orders that if anyone knew where He was, he should disclose it, so that they might seize Him.

John 12
John 12:1  So six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, whom Jesus had raised from the dead.
John 12:2  They made a supper for Him there, and Martha served, while Lazarus was one of those reclining at table with Him.
John 12:3  Then Mary took a litra of costly perfume of genuine nard, anointed Jesus’ feet, and wiped His feet with her hair. And the house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.
John 12:4  But Judas Iscariot, one of His disciples, who was about to hand Him over, said,
John 12:5  “Why was this perfume not sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?”
John 12:6  He said this not because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief, and having the money box, he used to carry off what was put into it.
John 12:7  So Jesus said, “Leave her, so that she may keep it for the day of My burial.
John 12:8  For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have Me.”
John 12:9  A great crowd of the Jews learned that He was there, and they came not because of Jesus alone, but also to see Lazarus, whom He raised from the dead.
John 12:10  But the chief priests planned to kill Lazarus also,
John 12:11  because on his account many of the Jews were going away and believing in Jesus.
John 12:12  The next day, the great crowd that had come to the feast, hearing that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem,
John 12:13  took branches of the palm trees and went out to meet Him, and cried out, “Hosanna! Blessed is the One who comes in the name of the Lord, even the King of Israel!”
John 12:14  Jesus found a young donkey and sat upon it, just as it is written,
John 12:15  “Do not fear, daughter Zion. Behold, your King comes, sitting upon a donkey’s colt.”
John 12:16  His disciples did not understand these things at first. But when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that these things were written about Him and that they had done these things to Him.
John 12:17  So the crowd that was with Him when He called Lazarus from the tomb and raised him from the dead bore witness.
John 12:18  For this reason the crowd also met Him, because they heard that He had done this sign.
John 12:19  So the Pharisees said among themselves, “You see that you accomplish nothing. Behold, the world has gone after Him.”
John 12:20  Now there were some Greeks among those going up to worship at the feast.
John 12:21  These approached Philip, who was from Bethsaida of Galilee, and asked him, saying, “Sir, we want to see Jesus.”
John 12:22  Philip came and told Andrew; Andrew and Philip came and told Jesus.
John 12:23  Jesus answered them, saying, “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
John 12:24  Amen, amen, I tell you: unless the grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
John 12:25  The one who loves his life loses it, and the one who hates his life in this world will keep it for eternal life.
John 12:26  If anyone serves Me, let him follow Me; and where I am, there My servant will be also. If anyone serves Me, the Father will honor him.
John 12:27  Now My soul is troubled, and what shall I say? Father, save Me from this hour? Yet for this reason I came to this hour.
John 12:28  Father, glorify Thy name.” Then a voice came from heaven: “I both glorified it and will glorify it again.”
John 12:29  So the crowd standing there and hearing it said that it had thundered. Others said, “An angel has spoken to Him.”
John 12:30  Jesus answered, “This voice has come not for My sake, but for yours.
John 12:31  Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will be cast out.
John 12:32  And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to Myself.”
John 12:33  He said this to signify by what kind of death He was about to die.
John 12:34  So the crowd answered Him, “We have heard from the Law that the Christ remains forever. How dost Thou say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?”
John 12:35  Then Jesus said to them, “For a little time longer the Light is among you. Walk while you have the Light, so that darkness may not overtake you. The one walking in the darkness does not know where he is going.
John 12:36  While you have the Light, believe in the Light, so that you may become sons of light.” Jesus spoke these things, and went away and hid Himself from them.
John 12:37  Though He had done so many signs before them, they did not believe in Him,
John 12:38  so that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spoke: “Lord, who believed our report? And to whom was the arm of the Lord revealed?”
John 12:39  For this reason they could not believe, because Isaiah said again,
John 12:40  “He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, so that they may not see with the eyes and understand with the heart and turn—and I will heal them.”
John 12:41  Isaiah said these things because he saw His glory and spoke concerning Him.
John 12:42  Nevertheless, many even from the rulers believed in Him, but because of the Pharisees they did not confess Him, so that they might not be put out of the synagogue,
John 12:43  for they loved the glory of people more than the glory of God.
John 12:44  And Jesus cried out and said, “The one who believes in Me believes not in Me, but in the One who sent Me.
John 12:45  And the one who beholds Me beholds the One who sent Me.
John 12:46  I have come as Light into the world, so that everyone who believes in Me may not remain in the darkness.
John 12:47  And if anyone hears My words and does not keep them, I do not judge him; for I did not come to judge the world, but to save the world.
John 12:48  The one who rejects Me and does not receive My words has one who judges him: the word that I spoke will judge him on the last day.
John 12:49  Because I have not spoken from Myself, but the Father who sent Me has Himself given Me a command about what I should say and what I should speak.
John 12:50  And I know that His command is eternal life. So the things I speak, just as the Father has told Me, thus I speak.”

John 13
John 13:1  Before the feast of the Passover, Jesus, knowing that His hour had come to pass from this world to the Father, having loved His own who were in the world, loved them to the end.
John 13:2  And while supper was taking place, the devil having already put it into the heart that Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, should hand Him over,
John 13:3  knowing that the Father had given all things into His hands, and that He came out from God and was going to God,
John 13:4  He rose from supper and laid aside His garments, and took a towel and tied it around Himself.
John 13:5  Then He poured water into the basin and began to wash the disciples’ feet and wipe them with the towel He had tied around Himself.
John 13:6  So He came to Simon Peter, who said to Him, “Lord, dost Thou wash my feet?”
John 13:7  Jesus answered him, “What I do you do not understand now, but you will understand after these things.”
John 13:8  Peter said to Him, “Thou wilt certainly never wash my feet.” Jesus answered him, “Unless I wash you, you have no share with Me.”
John 13:9  Simon Peter said to Him, “Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head!”
John 13:10  Jesus said to him, “The one who has bathed has no need to wash except the feet, but is wholly clean. And you are clean, but not all.”
John 13:11  For He knew the one who was handing Him over; for this reason He said, “Not all of you are clean.”
John 13:12  So when He had washed their feet and taken His garments and reclined again, He said to them, “Do you understand what I have done to you?
John 13:13  You call Me the Teacher and the Lord, and you speak well, for I am.
John 13:14  So if I, the Lord and the Teacher, washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet.
John 13:15  For I have given you an example, so that you also may do just as I did to you.
John 13:16  Amen, amen, I tell you: a slave is not greater than his master, nor a messenger greater than the one who sent him.
John 13:17  If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.
John 13:18  I do not speak about all of you. I know whom I chose. But so that the Scripture may be fulfilled: ‘The one eating My bread lifted his heel against Me.’
John 13:19  From now on I tell you before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe that I am.
John 13:20  Amen, amen, I tell you: the one who receives anyone I send receives Me, and the one who receives Me receives the One who sent Me.”
John 13:21  Having said these things, Jesus was troubled in spirit and testified, saying, “Amen, amen, I tell you that one of you will hand Me over.”
John 13:22  The disciples looked at one another, perplexed about whom He was speaking.
John 13:23  One of His disciples, whom Jesus loved, was reclining in Jesus’ bosom.
John 13:24  So Simon Peter signaled to this one to ask whom He was speaking about.
John 13:25  Leaning back thus upon Jesus’ chest, he said to Him, “Lord, who is it?”
John 13:26  Jesus answered, “It is the one for whom I will dip the morsel and give it to him.” So He dipped the morsel, took it, and gave it to Judas, son of Simon Iscariot.
John 13:27  And after the morsel, then Satan entered him. So Jesus said to him, “What you do, do more quickly.”
John 13:28  But none of those reclining knew for what purpose He said this to him.
John 13:29  For some thought, since Judas had the money box, that Jesus was telling him, “Buy what we need for the feast,” or that he should give something to the poor.
John 13:30  So, having received the morsel, he went out at once. And it was night.
John 13:31  When he had gone out, Jesus said, “Now the Son of Man was glorified, and God was glorified in Him.
John 13:32  If God was glorified in Him, God will also glorify Him in Himself, and will glorify Him at once.
John 13:33  Little children, I am with you a little longer. You will seek Me, and just as I told the Jews, ‘Where I go, you cannot come,’ I now tell you also.
John 13:34  I give you a new commandment: that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also are to love one another.
John 13:35  By this everyone will know that you are My disciples, if you have love among one another.”
John 13:36  Simon Peter said to Him, “Lord, where art Thou going?” Jesus answered him, “Where I go, you cannot follow Me now, but you will follow later.”
John 13:37  Peter said to Him, “Lord, why can I not follow Thee now? I will lay down my life for Thee.”
John 13:38  Jesus answered, “Will you lay down your life for Me? Amen, amen, I tell you: a rooster will certainly not crow until you deny Me three times.”

John 14
John 14:1  “Do not let your heart be troubled. Believe in God, and believe also in Me.
John 14:2  In My Father’s house are many dwelling places. If it were not so, would I have told you that I am going to prepare a place for you?
John 14:3  And if I go and prepare a place for you, I am coming again and will take you to Myself, so that where I am, you also may be.
John 14:4  And you know the way to where I am going.”
John 14:5  Thomas says to Him, “Lord, we do not know where Thou art going. How can we know the way?”
John 14:6  Jesus says to him, “I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.
John 14:7  If you have known Me, you will also know My Father. From now on you know Him and have seen Him.”
John 14:8  Philip says to Him, “Lord, show us the Father, and it is enough for us.”
John 14:9  Jesus says to him, “Have I been with you for so long a time, and you have not known Me, Philip? The one who has seen Me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?
John 14:10  Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me? The words that I say to you I do not speak from Myself; but the Father, who remains in Me, does His works.
John 14:11  Believe Me that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me. But if not, believe because of the works themselves.
John 14:12  Amen, amen, I say to you: the one who believes in Me will also do the works that I do, and will do greater works than these, because I am going to the Father.
John 14:13  And whatever you ask in My name, this I will do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
John 14:14  If you ask Me anything in My name, I will do it.
John 14:15  “If you love Me, you will keep My commandments.
John 14:16  And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate, so that He may be with you forever:
John 14:17  the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither beholds Him nor knows Him. You know Him, because He remains with you and will be in you.
John 14:18  I will not leave you orphans; I am coming to you.
John 14:19  Yet a little while, and the world no longer beholds Me, but you behold Me. Because I live, you also will live.
John 14:20  On that day you will know that I am in My Father, and you in Me, and I in you.
John 14:21  The one who has My commandments and keeps them is the one who loves Me. And the one who loves Me will be loved by My Father, and I will love him and reveal Myself to him.”
John 14:22  Judas—not the Iscariot—says to Him, “Lord, what then has happened that Thou art going to reveal Thyself to us and not to the world?”
John 14:23  Jesus answered and said to him, “If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word, and My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our dwelling with him.
John 14:24  The one who does not love Me does not keep My words. And the word that you hear is not Mine, but the Father’s who sent Me.
John 14:25  “These things I have spoken to you while remaining with you.
John 14:26  But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in My name, He will teach you all things and remind you of all that I said to you.
John 14:27  Peace I leave with you; My peace I give you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your heart be troubled or afraid.
John 14:28  You heard that I said to you, ‘I am going away, and I am coming to you.’ If you loved Me, you would have rejoiced that I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I.
John 14:29  And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe.
John 14:30  I will no longer speak much with you, for the ruler of the world is coming, and he has nothing in Me.
John 14:31  But so that the world may know that I love the Father, I do just as the Father commanded Me. Rise, let us go from here.”

John 15
John 15:1  “I am the true vine, and My Father is the vinegrower.
John 15:2  Every branch in Me that does not bear fruit He takes away; and every one that bears fruit He prunes, so that it may bear more fruit.
John 15:3  You are already clean because of the word that I have spoken to you.
John 15:4  Remain in Me, and I in you. Just as the branch cannot bear fruit from itself unless it remains in the vine, neither can you unless you remain in Me.
John 15:5  I am the vine; you are the branches. The one who remains in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit, because apart from Me you can do nothing.
John 15:6  If anyone does not remain in Me, he is thrown outside like the branch and withers; and they gather them and throw them into the fire, and they are burned.
John 15:7  If you remain in Me and My words remain in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you.
John 15:8  In this My Father has been glorified: that you bear much fruit and become My disciples.
John 15:9  Just as the Father loved Me, I also loved you. Remain in My love.
John 15:10  If you keep My commandments, you will remain in My love, just as I have kept My Father’s commandments and remain in His love.
John 15:11  These things I have spoken to you so that My joy may be in you and your joy may be made full.
John 15:12  “This is My commandment: that you love one another just as I loved you.
John 15:13  No one has greater love than this: that someone should lay down his life for his friends.
John 15:14  You are My friends if you do what I command you.
John 15:15  I no longer call you slaves, because the slave does not know what his master is doing; but I have called you friends, because I have made known to you everything that I heard from My Father.
John 15:16  You did not choose Me, but I chose you, and appointed you so that you should go and bear fruit and your fruit should remain, so that whatever you ask the Father in My name He may give you.
John 15:17  These things I command you, so that you love one another.
John 15:18  “If the world hates you, know that it has hated Me before you.
John 15:19  If you were from the world, the world would love its own. But because you are not from the world, but I chose you out of the world, for this reason the world hates you.
John 15:20  Remember the word that I said to you: ‘A slave is not greater than his master.’ If they persecuted Me, they will also persecute you; if they kept My word, they will also keep yours.
John 15:21  But they will do all these things to you because of My name, because they do not know the One who sent Me.
John 15:22  If I had not come and spoken to them, they would have no sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin.
John 15:23  The one who hates Me hates My Father also.
John 15:24  If I had not done among them the works that no one else did, they would have no sin; but now they have both seen and hated both Me and My Father.
John 15:25  But this is so that the word written in their law might be fulfilled: ‘They hated Me without cause.’
John 15:26  “When the Advocate comes, whom I will send you from the Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father, He will bear witness about Me.
John 15:27  And you also bear witness, because you have been with Me from the beginning.

John 16
John 16:1  “These things I have spoken to you so that you may not stumble.
John 16:2  They will put you out of the synagogues; indeed, an hour is coming when everyone who kills you will think he is offering worship to God.
John 16:3  And they will do these things because they have known neither the Father nor Me.
John 16:4  But these things I have spoken to you so that, when their hour comes, you may remember that I told you about them. I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you.
John 16:5  But now I am going to the One who sent Me, and none of you asks Me, ‘Where art Thou going?’
John 16:6  But because I have spoken these things to you, sorrow has filled your heart.
John 16:7  Yet I tell you the truth: it is better for you that I go away. For if I do not go away, the Advocate certainly will not come to you; but if I go, I will send Him to you.
John 16:8  And when He comes, He will convict the world concerning sin and concerning righteousness and concerning judgment:
John 16:9  concerning sin, because they do not believe in Me;
John 16:10  concerning righteousness, because I am going to the Father and you no longer behold Me;
John 16:11  and concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has been judged.
John 16:12  “I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now.
John 16:13  But when He comes, the Spirit of truth, He will guide you in all the truth; for He will not speak from Himself, but will speak whatever He hears, and will announce to you the things to come.
John 16:14  He will glorify Me, because He will receive from what is Mine and announce it to you.
John 16:15  Everything that the Father has is Mine. For this reason I said that He receives from what is Mine and will announce it to you.
John 16:16  “A little while, and you no longer behold Me; and again a little while, and you will see Me.”
John 16:17  Then some of His disciples said to one another, “What is this that He says to us: ‘A little while, and you do not behold Me; and again a little while, and you will see Me,’ and, ‘Because I am going to the Father’?”
John 16:18  So they were saying, “What is this ‘little while’ that He speaks of? We do not know what He is saying.”
John 16:19  Jesus knew that they wanted to ask Him, and said to them, “Are you seeking an answer among yourselves about this, because I said, ‘A little while, and you do not behold Me; and again a little while, and you will see Me’?
John 16:20  Amen, amen, I say to you that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will become joy.
John 16:21  When a woman is giving birth, she has sorrow because her hour has come; but when she has borne the child, she no longer remembers the anguish because of the joy that a human being has been born into the world.
John 16:22  So you too now have sorrow; but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one takes your joy away from you.
John 16:23  And on that day you will ask Me nothing. Amen, amen, I say to you: if you ask the Father anything, He will give it to you in My name.
John 16:24  Until now you have asked nothing in My name. Ask, and you will receive, so that your joy may be made full.
John 16:25  “These things I have spoken to you in figures of speech. An hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in figures of speech, but will tell you plainly about the Father.
John 16:26  On that day you will ask in My name; and I do not say to you that I will ask the Father concerning you,
John 16:27  for the Father Himself loves you, because you have loved Me and have believed that I came forth from God.
John 16:28  I came forth from the Father and have come into the world. Again, I am leaving the world and going to the Father.”
John 16:29  His disciples say, “See, now Thou speakest plainly and usest no figure of speech.
John 16:30  Now we know that Thou knowest all things, and hast no need for anyone to question Thee. By this we believe that Thou didst come forth from God.”
John 16:31  Jesus answered them, “Do you now believe?
John 16:32  Behold, an hour is coming, and has come, when you will be scattered, each to his own, and will leave Me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with Me.
John 16:33  These things I have spoken to you so that in Me you may have peace. In the world you have affliction; but take courage: I have overcome the world.”

John 17
John 17:1  Jesus spoke these things, and, lifting His eyes to heaven, said, “Father, the hour has come. Glorify Thy Son, so that the Son may glorify Thee,
John 17:2  just as Thou gavest Him authority over all flesh, so that He may give eternal life to them—to all that Thou hast given Him.
John 17:3  And this is eternal life: that they know Thee, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom Thou didst send.
John 17:4  I glorified Thee on the earth, having completed the work that Thou hast given Me to do.
John 17:5  And now, Father, glorify Me with Thyself, with the glory that I had with Thee before the world existed.
John 17:6  “I revealed Thy name to the people whom Thou gavest Me out of the world. They were Thine, and Thou gavest them to Me, and they have kept Thy word.
John 17:7  Now they have known that everything Thou hast given Me is from Thee,
John 17:8  because the words that Thou gavest Me I have given them; and they received them and truly knew that I came forth from Thee, and believed that Thou didst send Me.
John 17:9  I ask concerning them. I do not ask concerning the world, but concerning those whom Thou hast given Me, because they are Thine;
John 17:10  and all that is Mine is Thine, and what is Thine is Mine, and I have been glorified in them.
John 17:11  And I am no longer in the world, but they are in the world, and I am coming to Thee. Holy Father, keep them in Thy name, which Thou hast given Me, so that they may be one just as We are.
John 17:12  When I was with them, I kept them in Thy name, which Thou hast given Me, and guarded them; and not one of them perished except the son of destruction, so that the Scripture might be fulfilled.
John 17:13  But now I am coming to Thee, and I speak these things in the world so that they may have My joy made full within themselves.
John 17:14  I have given them Thy word, and the world hated them, because they are not from the world, just as I am not from the world.
John 17:15  I do not ask that Thou take them out of the world, but that Thou keep them from the evil one.
John 17:16  They are not from the world, just as I am not from the world.
John 17:17  Sanctify them in the truth; Thy word is truth.
John 17:18  Just as Thou didst send Me into the world, I also sent them into the world;
John 17:19  and for their sake I sanctify Myself, so that they also may be sanctified in truth.
John 17:20  “And I ask not only concerning these, but also concerning those who believe in Me through their word,
John 17:21  so that they may all be one, just as Thou, Father, art in Me and I in Thee, so that they also may be in Us, so that the world may believe that Thou didst send Me.
John 17:22  And the glory that Thou hast given Me I have given them, so that they may be one just as We are one:
John 17:23  I in them and Thou in Me, so that they may be made completely one, so that the world may know that Thou didst send Me and didst love them just as Thou didst love Me.
John 17:24  Father, as for what Thou hast given Me, I desire that they too may be with Me where I am, so that they may behold My glory, which Thou hast given Me, because Thou didst love Me before the foundation of the world.
John 17:25  Righteous Father, although the world did not know Thee, I knew Thee, and these knew that Thou didst send Me;
John 17:26  and I made Thy name known to them, and will make it known, so that the love with which Thou didst love Me may be in them, and I in them.”

John 18
John 18:1  Having said these things, Jesus went out with His disciples beyond the winter-stream Kidron, where there was a garden, into which He and His disciples entered.
John 18:2  Now Judas, who was handing Him over, also knew the place, because Jesus had often gathered there with His disciples.
John 18:3  So Judas, taking the cohort and officers from the chief priests and from the Pharisees, comes there with lanterns and torches and weapons.
John 18:4  Then Jesus, knowing everything that was coming upon Him, went out and says to them, “Whom do you seek?”
John 18:5  They answered Him, “Jesus the Nazarene.” He says to them, “I am.” Now Judas, who was handing Him over, was also standing with them.
John 18:6  So when He said to them, “I am,” they went backward and fell to the ground.
John 18:7  Then He asked them again, “Whom do you seek?” And they said, “Jesus the Nazarene.”
John 18:8  Jesus answered, “I told you that I am. So if you seek Me, let these go away,”
John 18:9  so that the word that He spoke might be fulfilled: “Of those whom Thou hast given Me, I lost not one.”
John 18:10  Then Simon Peter, having a sword, drew it and struck the high priest’s slave and cut off his right ear. The slave’s name was Malchus.
John 18:11  So Jesus said to Peter, “Put the sword into the sheath. The cup that the Father has given Me—shall I not drink it?”
John 18:12  Then the cohort and the commander and the officers of the Jews arrested Jesus and bound Him,
John 18:13  and led Him first to Annas, for he was father-in-law to Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
John 18:14  Now Caiaphas was the one who advised the Jews that it was better for them for one person to die for the people.
John 18:15  And Simon Peter and another disciple were following Jesus. That disciple was known to the high priest, and entered with Jesus into the high priest’s courtyard;
John 18:16  but Peter was standing outside at the door. So the other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the woman keeping the door, and brought Peter in.
John 18:17  Then the slave girl keeping the door says to Peter, “You are not also one of this Man’s disciples, are you?” He says, “I am not.”
John 18:18  Now the slaves and the officers were standing there, having made a charcoal fire because it was cold, and they were warming themselves. Peter too was with them, standing and warming himself.
John 18:19  Then the high priest questioned Jesus about His disciples and about His teaching.
John 18:20  Jesus answered him, “I have spoken openly to the world. I always taught in a synagogue and in the temple, where all the Jews gather, and I spoke nothing in secret.
John 18:21  Why do you question Me? Question those who have heard what I spoke to them. See, these know what I said.”
John 18:22  When He said these things, one of the officers standing nearby gave Jesus a slap, saying, “Is this how Thou answerest the high priest?”
John 18:23  Jesus answered him, “If I spoke wrongly, bear witness about the wrong; but if rightly, why do you beat Me?”
John 18:24  So Annas sent Him bound to Caiaphas the high priest.
John 18:25  Now Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. So they said to him, “You are not also one of His disciples, are you?” He denied it and said, “I am not.”
John 18:26  One of the high priest’s slaves, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, says, “Did I not see you in the garden with Him?”
John 18:27  Then Peter denied it again, and immediately a rooster crowed.
John 18:28  Then they lead Jesus from Caiaphas into the praetorium. It was early morning, and they themselves did not enter the praetorium, so that they might not be defiled, but might eat the Passover.
John 18:29  So Pilate went outside to them and says, “What accusation do you bring against this Man?”
John 18:30  They answered and said to him, “If this Man were not doing evil, we would not have handed Him over to you.”
John 18:31  Then Pilate said to them, “Take Him yourselves, and judge Him according to your law.” The Jews said to him, “It is not lawful for us to put anyone to death,”
John 18:32  so that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled, which He spoke to indicate by what kind of death He was going to die.
John 18:33  Then Pilate entered the praetorium again, called Jesus, and said to Him, “Art Thou the King of the Jews?”
John 18:34  Jesus answered, “Do you say this from yourself, or did others tell you about Me?”
John 18:35  Pilate answered, “I am not a Jew, am I? Thy own nation and the chief priests handed Thee over to me. What hast Thou done?”
John 18:36  Jesus answered, “My kingdom is not from this world. If My kingdom were from this world, My attendants would be fighting so that I would not be handed over to the Jews. But as it is, My kingdom is not from here.”
John 18:37  Then Pilate said to Him, “So then, Thou art a king?” Jesus answered, “You say that I am a king. For this I have been born, and for this I have come into the world: to bear witness to the truth. Everyone who is from the truth hears My voice.”
John 18:38  Pilate says to Him, “What is truth?” And having said this, he went out again to the Jews, and says to them, “I find no charge against Him.
John 18:39  But you have a custom that I release one person to you at the Passover. So do you wish me to release to you the King of the Jews?”
John 18:40  Then they cried out again, saying, “Not this Man, but Barabbas!” Now Barabbas was a bandit.

John 19
John 19:1  Then Pilate took Jesus and had Him scourged.
John 19:2  And the soldiers, weaving a crown from thorns, put it on His head and clothed Him in a purple garment;
John 19:3  and they kept coming to Him and saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” And they gave Him slaps.
John 19:4  And Pilate went outside again and says to them, “See, I am bringing Him outside to you so that you may know that I find no charge against Him.”
John 19:5  Then Jesus came outside, wearing the thorny crown and the purple garment. And he says to them, “Behold the Man!”
John 19:6  So when the chief priests and the officers saw Him, they cried out, saying, “Crucify! Crucify!” Pilate says to them, “Take Him yourselves and crucify Him, for I find no charge against Him.”
John 19:7  The Jews answered him, “We have a law, and according to the law He ought to die, because He made Himself Son of God.”
John 19:8  So when Pilate heard this word, he was more afraid,
John 19:9  and entered the praetorium again and says to Jesus, “Where art Thou from?” But Jesus gave him no answer.
John 19:10  Then Pilate says to Him, “Dost Thou not speak to me? Dost Thou not know that I have authority to release Thee, and I have authority to crucify Thee?”
John 19:11  Jesus answered him, “You would have no authority against Me unless it had been given you from above. For this reason the one who handed Me over to you has greater sin.”
John 19:12  From this Pilate sought to release Him; but the Jews cried out, saying, “If you release this Man, you are not Caesar’s friend. Everyone who makes himself a king speaks against Caesar.”
John 19:13  So Pilate, hearing these words, brought Jesus outside and sat on the judgment seat at a place called Stone Pavement, and in Hebrew, Gabbatha.
John 19:14  Now it was the Preparation of the Passover; it was about the sixth hour. And he says to the Jews, “Behold your King!”
John 19:15  Then they cried out, “Take Him away! Take Him away! Crucify Him!” Pilate says to them, “Shall I crucify your King?” The chief priests answered, “We have no king except Caesar.”
John 19:16  Then he handed Him over to them to be crucified. So they took Jesus;
John 19:17  and, bearing the cross for Himself, He went out to what is called the Place of a Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha,
John 19:18  where they crucified Him, and with Him two others, one on either side, and Jesus in the middle.
John 19:19  And Pilate also wrote an inscription and put it on the cross. It was written: “Jesus the Nazarene, the King of the Jews.”
John 19:20  Then many of the Jews read this inscription, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city; and it was written in Hebrew, in Latin, in Greek.
John 19:21  So the chief priests of the Jews were saying to Pilate, “Do not write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but that He said, ‘I am King of the Jews.’”
John 19:22  Pilate answered, “What I have written, I have written.”
John 19:23  Then the soldiers, when they crucified Jesus, took His garments and made four parts, a part for each soldier, and also took the tunic. Now the tunic was seamless, woven from the top throughout.
John 19:24  So they said to one another, “Let us not tear it, but cast lots for it, to decide whose it will be,” so that the Scripture might be fulfilled which says, “They divided My garments among themselves, and for My clothing they cast a lot.” So the soldiers did these things.
John 19:25  But standing beside Jesus’ cross were His mother and His mother’s sister, Mary of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
John 19:26  Then Jesus, seeing His mother and the disciple whom He loved standing nearby, says to His mother, “Woman, behold your son.”
John 19:27  Then He says to the disciple, “Behold your mother.” And from that hour the disciple took her into his own home.
John 19:28  After this, Jesus, knowing that all things had already been completed, says, so that the Scripture might be brought to completion, “I thirst.”
John 19:29  A vessel full of sour wine was standing there. So, putting a sponge full of the sour wine on hyssop, they brought it to His mouth.
John 19:30  When therefore Jesus had received the sour wine, He said, “It is finished.” And bowing His head, He gave up His spirit.
John 19:31  Then, because it was Preparation, the Jews asked Pilate to have their legs broken and their bodies taken away, so that the bodies would not remain on the cross on the Sabbath—for that Sabbath was a great day.
John 19:32  So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man and of the other who was crucified with Him;
John 19:33  but when they came to Jesus, as they saw that He was already dead, they did not break His legs.
John 19:34  But one of the soldiers pierced His side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.
John 19:35  And the one who has seen has borne witness, and his testimony is true; and he knows that he speaks the truth, so that you also may believe.
John 19:36  For these things happened so that the Scripture might be fulfilled: “A bone of His will not be broken.”
John 19:37  And again another Scripture says, “They will look on the One whom they pierced.”
John 19:38  And after these things Joseph from Arimathea, being a disciple of Jesus but secretly because of fear of the Jews, asked Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus; and Pilate permitted it. So he came and took away His body.
John 19:39  And Nicodemus also came, the one who had first come to Him by night, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred litrai.
John 19:40  So they took the body of Jesus and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, as is the Jews’ custom for burial.
John 19:41  Now in the place where He was crucified there was a garden, and in the garden a new tomb, in which no one had yet been laid.
John 19:42  So there, because of the Jews’ Preparation, since the tomb was nearby, they laid Jesus.

John 20
John 20:1  Now on the first day of the week Mary Magdalene comes early to the tomb, while it is still dark, and sees the stone taken away from the tomb.
John 20:2  So she runs and comes to Simon Peter and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, and says to them, “They took the Lord out of the tomb, and we do not know where they laid Him.”
John 20:3  Then Peter and the other disciple went out, and they were coming to the tomb.
John 20:4  The two were running together, and the other disciple ran ahead faster than Peter and came to the tomb first;
John 20:5  and, stooping to look in, he sees the linen cloths lying there; yet he did not enter.
John 20:6  Then Simon Peter also comes, following him, and entered the tomb; and he beholds the linen cloths lying there,
John 20:7  and the face cloth that had been on His head, not lying with the linen cloths, but wrapped up separately in one place.
John 20:8  Then the other disciple who had come to the tomb first also entered, and he saw and believed;
John 20:9  for they did not yet know the Scripture, that He must rise from the dead.
John 20:10  Then the disciples went back to their own place.
John 20:11  But Mary was standing outside beside the tomb, weeping. So, as she wept, she stooped to look into the tomb,
John 20:12  and beholds two angels in white, sitting one at the head and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain.
John 20:13  And they say to her, “Woman, why do you weep?” She says to them, “They took my Lord, and I do not know where they laid Him.”
John 20:14  Having said these things, she turned backward and beholds Jesus standing there, and did not know that it was Jesus.
John 20:15  Jesus says to her, “Woman, why do you weep? Whom do you seek?” She, supposing that He is the gardener, says to Him, “Sir, if Thou didst carry Him away, tell me where Thou didst lay Him, and I will take Him away.”
John 20:16  Jesus says to her, “Mary.” Turning, she says to Him in Hebrew, “Rabbouni!”—which means Teacher.
John 20:17  Jesus says to her, “Do not cling to Me, for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go to My brothers and tell them, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, and My God and your God.’”
John 20:18  Mary Magdalene comes, announcing to the disciples, “I have seen the Lord,” and that He said these things to her.
John 20:19  Then, when it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and the doors were shut where the disciples were, because of fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the midst, and says to them, “Peace to you.”
John 20:20  And having said this, He showed them His hands and His side. Then the disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord.
John 20:21  Then Jesus said to them again, “Peace to you. Just as the Father has sent Me, I also send you.”
John 20:22  And having said this, He breathed and says to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit.
John 20:23  If you forgive the sins of any, they have been forgiven them; if you retain those of any, they have been retained.”
John 20:24  But Thomas, one of the Twelve, who was called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.
John 20:25  So the other disciples were saying to him, “We have seen the Lord.” But he said to them, “Unless I see in His hands the mark of the nails and put my finger into the mark of the nails and put my hand into His side, I certainly will not believe.”
John 20:26  And after eight days His disciples were inside again, and Thomas with them. Jesus comes, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst and said, “Peace to you.”
John 20:27  Then He says to Thomas, “Bring your finger here and see My hands, and bring your hand and put it into My side; and do not become unbelieving, but believing.”
John 20:28  Thomas answered and said to Him, “My Lord and my God!”
John 20:29  Jesus says to him, “Because you have seen Me, have you believed? Blessed are those who have not seen and have believed.”
John 20:30  Now Jesus also did many other signs before His disciples, which are not written in this book;
John 20:31  but these have been written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and so that, believing, you may have life in His name.

John 21
John 21:1  After these things Jesus revealed Himself again to the disciples at the Sea of Tiberias, and He revealed Himself in this way.
John 21:2  Simon Peter and Thomas, who was called Didymus, and Nathanael from Cana of Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two others of His disciples were together.
John 21:3  Simon Peter says to them, “I am going fishing.” They say to him, “We also are coming with you.” They went out and got into the boat, and during that night they caught nothing.
John 21:4  But when morning had already come, Jesus stood on the shore; yet the disciples did not know that it was Jesus.
John 21:5  Then Jesus says to them, “Children, you do not have any fish to eat, do you?” They answered Him, “No.”
John 21:6  And He said to them, “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” So they cast it, and were no longer strong enough to draw it in because of the multitude of fish.
John 21:7  Then that disciple whom Jesus loved says to Peter, “It is the Lord.” So Simon Peter, hearing that it is the Lord, tied his outer garment around himself—for he was naked—and threw himself into the sea.
John 21:8  But the other disciples came in the little boat, dragging the net of fish, for they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits away.
John 21:9  So when they got out onto the land, they see a charcoal fire laid there, and fish lying on it, and bread.
John 21:10  Jesus says to them, “Bring some of the fish that you have just caught.”
John 21:11  So Simon Peter went up and drew the net onto the land, full of large fish, a hundred and fifty-three; and though there were so many, the net was not torn.
John 21:12  Jesus says to them, “Come, have breakfast.” But none of the disciples dared to question Him, “Who art Thou?” knowing that it was the Lord.
John 21:13  Jesus comes and takes the bread and gives it to them, and the fish likewise.
John 21:14  This was now the third time Jesus was revealed to the disciples after being raised from the dead.
John 21:15  So when they had eaten breakfast, Jesus says to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me more than these?” He says to Him, “Yes, Lord, Thou knowest that I love Thee.” He says to him, “Feed My lambs.”
John 21:16  He says to him again a second time, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me?” He says to Him, “Yes, Lord, Thou knowest that I love Thee.” He says to him, “Shepherd My sheep.”
John 21:17  He says to him the third time, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me?” Peter was grieved because He said to him the third time, “Do you love Me?” And he said to Him, “Lord, Thou knowest all things; Thou knowest that I love Thee.” Jesus says to him, “Feed My sheep.
John 21:18  Amen, amen, I say to you: when you were younger, you tied your belt around yourself and walked where you wished; but when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will tie your belt around you and carry you where you do not wish.”
John 21:19  Now He said this to indicate by what kind of death he would glorify God. And having said this, He says to him, “Follow Me.”
John 21:20  Turning, Peter sees the disciple whom Jesus loved following, the one who also leaned back at the supper upon His chest and said, “Lord, who is the one handing Thee over?”
John 21:21  So Peter, seeing him, says to Jesus, “Lord, and what about this man?”
John 21:22  Jesus says to him, “If I wish him to remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow Me.”
John 21:23  So this word went out among the brothers, that this disciple does not die. But Jesus did not say to him that he does not die, but, “If I wish him to remain until I come, what is that to you?”
John 21:24  This is the disciple who bears witness about these things and who wrote these things; and we know that his testimony is true.
John 21:25  And there are also many other things that Jesus did, which, if each one were written, I suppose that even the world itself would not contain the books being written.

ACTS

Acts 1
Acts 1:1  In my first account, Theophilus, I wrote about all that Jesus began both to do and to teach
Acts 1:2  until the day when, after giving instructions through the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom He had chosen, He was taken up.
Acts 1:3  To them He also presented Himself alive after His suffering, with many proofs, appearing to them over forty days and speaking about the kingdom of God.
Acts 1:4  While gathered with them, He ordered them not to leave Jerusalem, but to wait for the Father’s promise, “which,” He said, “you heard from Me;
Acts 1:5  for John baptized with water, but you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit not many days from now.”
Acts 1:6  So those who had come together asked Him, “Lord, is this the time when Thou art restoring the kingdom to Israel?”
Acts 1:7  He said to them, “It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has set by His own authority.
Acts 1:8  But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you, and you will be My witnesses in Jerusalem and [in] all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.”
Acts 1:9  After saying these things, He was lifted up as they watched, and a cloud took Him from their sight.
Acts 1:10  As they were gazing into heaven while He went, look—two men stood beside them in white garments.
Acts 1:11  They said, “Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw Him go into heaven.”
Acts 1:12  Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mountain called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem, a Sabbath’s journey away.
Acts 1:13  When they entered, they went up to the upper room where they were staying: Peter and John and James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James.
Acts 1:14  All these devoted themselves with one accord to prayer, together with women, Mary the mother of Jesus, and His brothers.
Acts 1:15  In those days Peter stood up among the brothers and said—about a hundred and twenty people were gathered together—
Acts 1:16  “Men, brothers, the Scripture had to be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit spoke beforehand through David’s mouth concerning Judas, who became a guide to those who arrested Jesus;
Acts 1:17  for he was counted among us and received his allotted share in this ministry.”
Acts 1:18  Now this man acquired a field from the wages of wrongdoing, and falling headlong, he burst open in the middle, and all his entrails poured out.
Acts 1:19  This became known to all who lived in Jerusalem, so that the field was called in their own language Hakeldamach—that is, Field of Blood.
Acts 1:20  “For it is written in the book of Psalms: ‘Let his dwelling become deserted, and let there be no one living in it,’ and, ‘Let another take his office of oversight.’
Acts 1:21  Therefore, of the men who accompanied us throughout the time when the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,
Acts 1:22  beginning with John’s baptism until the day when He was taken up from us, one of these must become with us a witness of His resurrection.”
Acts 1:23  They put forward two: Joseph called Barsabbas, who was also named Justus, and Matthias.
Acts 1:24  They prayed and said, “Thou, Lord, who knowest everyone’s heart, show which one of these two Thou hast chosen
Acts 1:25  to take the place in this ministry and apostleship from which Judas turned aside to go to his own place.”
Acts 1:26  They cast lots for them, and the lot fell on Matthias, and he was counted with the eleven apostles.

Acts 2
Acts 2:1  When the day of Pentecost arrived, they were all together in the same place.
Acts 2:2  Suddenly a sound came from heaven like a violent wind rushing along, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.
Acts 2:3  Tongues like fire appeared to them, separating and settling on each one of them.
Acts 2:4  They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.
Acts 2:5  Now there were Jews living in Jerusalem, devout men from every nation under heaven.
Acts 2:6  When this sound occurred, the crowd came together and was bewildered, because each one heard them speaking in his own language.
Acts 2:7  They were astonished and amazed, saying, “Look, are not all these people who are speaking Galileans?
Acts 2:8  How is it, then, that each of us hears in our own native language?
Acts 2:9  Parthians, Medes, and Elamites; those living in Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia,
Acts 2:10  Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya around Cyrene; visitors from Rome,
Acts 2:11  both Jews and converts; Cretans and Arabs—we hear them speaking in our own tongues about the mighty deeds of God.”
Acts 2:12  They were all astonished and perplexed, saying to one another, “What does this mean?”
Acts 2:13  But others mocked them and said, “They are full of sweet wine.”
Acts 2:14  Peter stood with the eleven, raised his voice, and addressed them: “Men of Judea and all who live in Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and listen closely to my words.
Acts 2:15  These people are not drunk, as you suppose, for it is the third hour of the day.
Acts 2:16  Rather, this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel:
Acts 2:17  ‘And it shall come to pass in the last days, says God, that I will pour out of My Spirit upon all flesh. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy, your young men will see visions, and your elders will dream dreams.
Acts 2:18  Even upon My male slaves and My female slaves in those days I will pour out of My Spirit, and they will prophesy.
Acts 2:19  And I will give wonders in heaven above and signs on the earth below: blood and fire and a vapor of smoke.
Acts 2:20  The sun will be changed into darkness and the moon into blood before the great and manifest day of the Lord comes.
Acts 2:21  And it shall come to pass that everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.’
Acts 2:22  Men of Israel, hear these words: Jesus the Nazarene was a man attested to you by God through mighty works, wonders, and signs that God did through Him in your midst, as you yourselves know.
Acts 2:23  This man, handed over according to God’s determined purpose and foreknowledge, you nailed up and killed through the hands of lawless men.
Acts 2:24  God raised Him, releasing Him from the pangs of death, because it was impossible for Him to be held by it.
Acts 2:25  For David says concerning Him, ‘I saw the Lord ever before me, for He is at my right hand, that I may not be shaken.
Acts 2:26  Therefore my heart rejoiced, and my tongue exulted; indeed, even my flesh will dwell in hope,
Acts 2:27  for Thou wilt not abandon my soul to Hades, nor let Thy Holy One see decay.
Acts 2:28  Thou hast made known to me the paths of life; Thou wilt fill me with gladness in Thy presence.’
Acts 2:29  Men, brothers, I may speak openly to you about the patriarch David: he both died and was buried, and his tomb is among us to this day.
Acts 2:30  Since he was a prophet and knew that God had sworn an oath to him to seat one from the fruit of his loins upon his throne,
Acts 2:31  he foresaw and spoke about the resurrection of the Christ: He was neither abandoned to Hades, nor did His flesh see decay.
Acts 2:32  God raised this Jesus, and all of us are witnesses of it.
Acts 2:33  Therefore, exalted to God’s right hand and having received from the Father the promised Holy Spirit, He has poured out what you both see and hear.
Acts 2:34  For David did not ascend into the heavens, but he himself says, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand
Acts 2:35  until I make Thy enemies a footstool for Thy feet.”’
Acts 2:36  Therefore let the whole house of Israel know with certainty that God has made Him both Lord and Christ—this Jesus whom you crucified.”
Acts 2:37  When they heard this, they were pierced to the heart and said to Peter and the other apostles, “Men, brothers, what should we do?”
Acts 2:38  Peter said to them, “Repent, and let each one of you be baptized upon the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
Acts 2:39  For the promise is for you, for your children, and for all who are far away—as many as the Lord our God calls to Himself.”
Acts 2:40  With many other words he bore solemn witness and urged them, saying, “Be saved from this crooked generation.”
Acts 2:41  So those who welcomed his word were baptized, and about three thousand persons were added that day.
Acts 2:42  They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to the prayers.
Acts 2:43  Awe came upon everyone, and many wonders and signs took place through the apostles.
Acts 2:44  All who believed were together and held everything in common.
Acts 2:45  They would sell their properties and possessions and distribute the proceeds to all, as anyone had need.
Acts 2:46  Day by day they devoted themselves with one accord to gathering in the temple, and breaking bread in their homes, they shared food with gladness and simplicity of heart,
Acts 2:47  praising God and enjoying favor with all the people. And day by day the Lord added those who were being saved to their gathering.

Acts 3
Acts 3:1  Peter and John were going up to the temple at the ninth hour, the hour of prayer.
Acts 3:2  A man unable to walk from his mother’s womb was being carried there. They used to place him each day at the temple gate called Beautiful, to ask for alms from those entering the temple.
Acts 3:3  When he saw Peter and John about to enter the temple, he asked to receive alms.
Acts 3:4  Peter, together with John, looked intently at him and said, “Look at us.”
Acts 3:5  He paid attention to them, expecting to receive something from them.
Acts 3:6  But Peter said, “Silver and gold I do not have, but what I have I give you: in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, get up and walk.”
Acts 3:7  Taking him by the right hand, he raised him up. At once his feet and ankles were strengthened.
Acts 3:8  Leaping up, he stood and began walking. He entered the temple with them, walking and leaping and praising God.
Acts 3:9  All the people saw him walking and praising God.
Acts 3:10  They recognized him as the one who used to sit for alms at the temple’s Beautiful Gate, and they were filled with wonder and astonishment at what had happened to him.
Acts 3:11  As he held on to Peter and John, all the people ran together to them at the portico called Solomon’s, utterly astonished.
Acts 3:12  When Peter saw this, he addressed the people: “Men of Israel, why do you marvel at this, or why do you stare at us as though we had made him walk by our own power or godliness?
Acts 3:13  The God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified His Servant Jesus, whom you handed over and denied before Pilate, when he had decided to release Him.
Acts 3:14  But you denied the Holy and Righteous One and asked for a murderer to be granted to you.
Acts 3:15  You killed the Author of life, whom God raised from the dead; we are witnesses of this.
Acts 3:16  Through faith in His name, His name has strengthened this man whom you see and know; and the faith that is through Him has given him this complete health before all of you.
Acts 3:17  And now, brothers, I know that you acted in ignorance, as did your rulers.
Acts 3:18  But what God announced beforehand through the mouth of all the prophets—that His Christ would suffer—He has fulfilled in this way.
Acts 3:19  Repent, therefore, and turn back, so that your sins may be wiped away,
Acts 3:20  so that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord, and He may send the Christ appointed for you, Jesus,
Acts 3:21  whom heaven must receive until the times of restoration of all things of which God spoke through the mouth of His holy prophets from long ago.
Acts 3:22  Moses said, ‘The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. You shall listen to him in everything he says to you.
Acts 3:23  Every person who does not listen to that prophet will be destroyed from among the people.’
Acts 3:24  And all the prophets, from Samuel and those who followed—as many as spoke—also announced these days.
Acts 3:25  You are sons of the prophets and of the covenant God made with your fathers, saying to Abraham, ‘In your seed all the families of the earth will be blessed.’
Acts 3:26  God raised up His Servant and sent Him first to you, to bless you by turning each of you away from your wicked deeds.”

Acts 4
Acts 4:1  While they were speaking to the people, the priests, the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees came upon them,
Acts 4:2  greatly troubled because they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection from the dead.
Acts 4:3  They laid hands on them and placed them in custody until the next day, for it was already evening.
Acts 4:4  But many of those who heard the word believed, and the number of the men came to about five thousand.
Acts 4:5  The next day their rulers, elders, and scribes gathered in Jerusalem,
Acts 4:6  together with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and all who belonged to the high-priestly family.
Acts 4:7  They made them stand in their midst and asked, “By what power or by what name did you do this?”
Acts 4:8  Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, “Rulers of the people and elders,
Acts 4:9  if we are being examined today concerning a good deed done to a disabled man, and by what means he has been made well,
Acts 4:10  let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead—in Him this man stands before you in good health.
Acts 4:11  He is the stone despised by you, the builders, which has become the cornerstone.
Acts 4:12  Salvation is in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among human beings by which we must be saved.”
Acts 4:13  When they observed Peter’s and John’s boldness and realized that they were unlettered, ordinary men, they were amazed. They also recognized that they had been with Jesus.
Acts 4:14  Seeing the man who had been healed standing with them, they had nothing to say against it.
Acts 4:15  They ordered them to leave the council and conferred with one another,
Acts 4:16  saying, “What should we do with these men? That a notable sign has taken place through them is evident to everyone living in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it.
Acts 4:17  But so that it spreads no further among the people, let us warn them with threats not to speak to anyone in this name again.”
Acts 4:18  They called them in and ordered them neither to speak nor to teach at all in the name of Jesus.
Acts 4:19  Peter and John answered them, “Judge whether it is right before God to listen to you rather than to God;
Acts 4:20  for we cannot keep from speaking about what we have seen and heard.”
Acts 4:21  After further threats, they released them, finding no way to punish them because of the people, since everyone was glorifying God for what had happened.
Acts 4:22  For the man in whom this sign of healing had occurred was more than forty years old.
Acts 4:23  After their release, they went to their own people and reported all that the chief priests and elders had said to them.
Acts 4:24  On hearing it, they lifted their voice together to God and said, “Master, Thou art the One who made heaven and earth and the sea and everything in them,
Acts 4:25  who through the Holy Spirit, by the mouth of our father David, Thy servant, said, ‘Why did nations rage and peoples devise empty things?
Acts 4:26  The kings of the earth took their stand, and the rulers gathered together against the Lord and against His Christ.’
Acts 4:27  For truly, in this city, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles and the peoples of Israel, gathered against Thy holy Servant Jesus, whom Thou didst anoint,
Acts 4:28  to do whatever Thy hand and Thy purpose had determined beforehand should happen.
Acts 4:29  And now, Lord, look upon their threats, and grant Thy servants to speak Thy word with all boldness,
Acts 4:30  while Thou stretchest out Thy hand for healing, and signs and wonders take place through the name of Thy holy Servant Jesus.”
Acts 4:31  When they had prayed, the place where they were gathered was shaken. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke God’s word with boldness.
Acts 4:32  The multitude of those who believed was of one heart and soul. Not one of them claimed that anything he possessed was his own, but they held everything in common.
Acts 4:33  With great power the apostles gave their testimony to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace was upon them all.
Acts 4:34  For there was not a needy person among them: all who owned lands or houses would sell them and bring the proceeds of what was sold,
Acts 4:35  laying them at the apostles’ feet; distribution was made to each as anyone had need.
Acts 4:36  Joseph, whom the apostles called Barnabas—which means Son of Encouragement—a Levite and a native of Cyprus,
Acts 4:37  sold a field he owned, brought the money, and laid it at the apostles’ feet.

Acts 5
Acts 5:1  A man named Ananias, together with his wife Sapphira, sold a property.
Acts 5:2  He secretly kept back part of the price, with his wife also knowing about it, and brought a portion and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
Acts 5:3  Peter said, “Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart, so that you lied to the Holy Spirit and secretly kept back part of the price of the land?
Acts 5:4  While it remained unsold, did it not remain yours? And after it was sold, was it not under your authority? Why have you put this deed in your heart? You have not lied to human beings but to God.”
Acts 5:5  When Ananias heard these words, he fell down and breathed his last. Great fear came upon all who heard.
Acts 5:6  The younger men rose, wrapped him up, carried him out, and buried him.
Acts 5:7  About three hours later, his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.
Acts 5:8  Peter said to her, “Tell me, did you sell the land for this amount?” She said, “Yes, for that amount.”
Acts 5:9  Peter said to her, “Why did you both agree to test the Spirit of the Lord? Look, the feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.”
Acts 5:10  At once she fell at his feet and breathed her last. When the young men came in, they found her dead; they carried her out and buried her beside her husband.
Acts 5:11  Great fear came upon the whole Church and upon all who heard these things.
Acts 5:12  Many signs and wonders were taking place among the people through the apostles’ hands. They were all together with one accord in Solomon’s Portico.
Acts 5:13  None of the rest dared to join them, but the people held them in high esteem.
Acts 5:14  More and more believers were added to the Lord, multitudes of both men and women,
Acts 5:15  so that they even carried the sick into the streets and laid them on small beds and mats, so that as Peter came by, at least his shadow might fall upon one of them.
Acts 5:16  The crowd also came together from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those troubled by unclean spirits, and they were all healed.
Acts 5:17  The high priest and all who were with him—the party of the Sadducees—rose up, filled with jealousy.
Acts 5:18  They laid hands on the apostles and placed them in the public prison.
Acts 5:19  But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the prison doors, led them out, and said,
Acts 5:20  “Go, stand in the temple, and speak to the people all the words of this life.”
Acts 5:21  When they heard this, they entered the temple at daybreak and began teaching. The high priest and those with him arrived, called together the council and the whole assembly of elders of the sons of Israel, and sent to the jail to have them brought in.
Acts 5:22  But when the officers arrived, they did not find them in the prison. They returned and reported,
Acts 5:23  “We found the jail securely locked and the guards standing at the doors, but when we opened it, we found no one inside.”
Acts 5:24  When the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard these words, they were perplexed about them, wondering what this would come to.
Acts 5:25  Then someone came and reported to them, “Look, the men you put in prison are standing in the temple and teaching the people.”
Acts 5:26  The captain then went with the officers and brought them, without force, for they feared the people might stone them.
Acts 5:27  They brought them and made them stand before the council. The high priest questioned them,
Acts 5:28  saying, “Did we not strictly command you not to teach in this name? Yet look—you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching and intend to bring this man’s blood upon us.”
Acts 5:29  Peter and the apostles answered, “We must obey God rather than human beings.
Acts 5:30  The God of our fathers raised Jesus, whom you killed by hanging Him on a tree.
Acts 5:31  God exalted Him to His right hand as Leader and Savior, to grant repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins.
Acts 5:32  We are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey Him.”
Acts 5:33  When they heard this, they were enraged and wanted to kill them.
Acts 5:34  But a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law honored by all the people, stood in the council and ordered the men to be taken outside briefly.
Acts 5:35  He said to them, “Men of Israel, take care what you are about to do to these men.
Acts 5:36  For before these days Theudas arose, claiming to be somebody, and about four hundred men joined him. He was killed, and all who followed him were dispersed and came to nothing.
Acts 5:37  After him Judas the Galilean arose in the days of the registration and drew people away after him. He too perished, and all who followed him were scattered.
Acts 5:38  And now I tell you, keep away from these men and leave them alone. For if this plan or this work is of human origin, it will be overthrown;
Acts 5:39  but if it is from God, you will not be able to overthrow them. You might even be found fighting against God.” They were persuaded by him.
Acts 5:40  They summoned the apostles, beat them, ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and released them.
Acts 5:41  So they left the council rejoicing that they had been counted worthy to suffer dishonor for the Name.
Acts 5:42  Every day, in the temple and in their homes, they never ceased teaching and proclaiming the good news of Jesus the Christ.

Acts 6
Acts 6:1  In those days, as the disciples increased in number, a complaint arose from the Hellenists against the Hebrews, because their widows were being overlooked in the daily service.
Acts 6:2  The twelve called the multitude of the disciples together and said, “It is not fitting for us to leave the word of God to serve tables.
Acts 6:3  So, brothers, select from among you seven men of good reputation, full of the Spirit and wisdom, whom we will put in charge of this task.
Acts 6:4  But we will devote ourselves to prayer and to the service of the word.”
Acts 6:5  The proposal pleased the whole multitude. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a convert from Antioch.
Acts 6:6  They presented them before the apostles, who prayed and laid their hands upon them.
Acts 6:7  The word of God grew, and the number of disciples in Jerusalem increased greatly. A large number of the priests also became obedient to the faith.
Acts 6:8  Stephen, full of grace and power, was doing great wonders and signs among the people.
Acts 6:9  But some from the synagogue called the Freedmen’s, including Cyrenians and Alexandrians and people from Cilicia and Asia, rose up and disputed with Stephen.
Acts 6:10  They could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke.
Acts 6:11  Then they secretly persuaded men to say, “We have heard him speaking blasphemous words against Moses and God.”
Acts 6:12  They stirred up the people, the elders, and the scribes, and came upon him, seized him, and brought him to the council.
Acts 6:13  They set up false witnesses who said, “This man never stops speaking words against this holy place and the law.
Acts 6:14  For we have heard him say that this Jesus the Nazarene will destroy this place and change the customs Moses handed down to us.”
Acts 6:15  All who were seated in the council looked intently at him and saw his face like the face of an angel.

Acts 7
Acts 7:1  The high priest said, “Are these things true?”
Acts 7:2  He answered, “Men, brothers and fathers, listen. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran,
Acts 7:3  and said to him, ‘Leave your land and your relatives, and come to the land I will show you.’
Acts 7:4  Then he left the land of the Chaldeans and lived in Haran. From there, after his father died, God moved him to this land in which you now live.
