Acts 23:6  When Paul perceived that one part consisted of Sadducees and the other of Pharisees, he cried out in the council, “Men, brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. I am being judged concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead.”
Acts 23:7  As he said this, dissension arose between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the multitude was divided.
Acts 23:8  For the Sadducees say there is no resurrection, nor angel nor spirit, but the Pharisees acknowledge both.
Acts 23:9  A great outcry arose, and some scribes of the Pharisees’ party stood up and argued fiercely, saying, “We find nothing wrong in this man. But what if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him?”
Acts 23:10  As the dispute intensified, the tribune feared Paul would be torn apart by them. He ordered the troops to go down, snatch him from their midst, and bring him into the barracks.
Acts 23:11  The following night the Lord stood beside him and said, “Take courage, for as you have borne solemn witness about Me in Jerusalem, so you must also testify in Rome.”
Acts 23:12  When day came, the Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves under a curse, saying they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.
Acts 23:13  More than forty had made this conspiracy.
Acts 23:14  They went to the chief priests and elders and said, “We have bound ourselves under a solemn curse to taste nothing until we have killed Paul.
Acts 23:15  Now, therefore, you and the council should inform the tribune to bring him down to you, as though you intended to determine his case more accurately. We are ready to kill him before he comes near.”
Acts 23:16  Paul’s sister’s son heard about the ambush, came and entered the barracks, and reported it to Paul.
Acts 23:17  Paul called one of the centurions and said, “Take this young man to the tribune, for he has something to report to him.”
Acts 23:18  So he took him and brought him to the tribune, saying, “The prisoner Paul called me and asked me to bring this young man to you, since he has something to tell you.”
Acts 23:19  The tribune took him by the hand, withdrew privately, and asked, “What is it that you have to report to me?”
Acts 23:20  He said, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the council tomorrow, as though it intended to inquire more accurately about him.
Acts 23:21  But do not be persuaded by them, for more than forty men among them are lying in wait for him. They have bound themselves under a curse neither to eat nor to drink until they kill him, and now they are ready, awaiting your agreement.”
Acts 23:22  The tribune dismissed the young man, ordering him, “Tell no one that you have disclosed these things to me.”
Acts 23:23  He called two of the centurions and said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea, with seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen, leaving at the third hour of the night.”
Acts 23:24  He also ordered mounts to be provided so that they could put Paul on them and bring him safely to Felix the governor.
Acts 23:25  He wrote a letter in this form:
Acts 23:26  “Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix: greetings.
Acts 23:27  This man was seized by the Jews and was about to be killed by them when I came with the troops and rescued him, having learned that he was a Roman.
Acts 23:28  Wishing to learn the reason they accused him, I brought him down to their council.
Acts 23:29  I found him accused over questions of their law, but under no charge deserving death or imprisonment.
Acts 23:30  When a plot against the man was disclosed to me, I immediately sent him to you, also ordering his accusers to state their case against him before you.”
Acts 23:31  So the soldiers, according to their orders, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.
Acts 23:32  The next day they left the horsemen to go on with him and returned to the barracks.
Acts 23:33  When the horsemen entered Caesarea, they delivered the letter to the governor and also presented Paul before him.
Acts 23:34  He read it, asked what province Paul was from, and learned that he was from Cilicia.
Acts 23:35  He said, “I will hear you fully when your accusers also arrive,” and ordered him kept under guard in Herod’s praetorium.

Acts 24
Acts 24:1  After five days the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and an advocate named Tertullus. They presented their case against Paul to the governor.
Acts 24:2  When Paul was called, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, “Through you we enjoy much peace, and reforms are being made for this nation through your foresight.
Acts 24:3  In every way and everywhere we acknowledge this, most excellent Felix, with all gratitude.
Acts 24:4  But so that I may not detain you further, I ask you in your kindness to hear us briefly.
Acts 24:5  For we have found this man to be a plague, stirring up disturbances among all the Jews throughout the inhabited world, and a ringleader of the party of the Nazarenes.
Acts 24:6  He even tried to profane the temple, and we seized him.
Acts 24:8  By examining him yourself, you will be able to learn about all these things of which we accuse him.”
Acts 24:9  The Jews also joined in the attack, asserting that these things were so.
Acts 24:10  When the governor motioned for him to speak, Paul answered, “Knowing that you have been a judge of this nation for many years, I cheerfully make my defense concerning myself.
Acts 24:11  You can confirm that it is no more than twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem to worship.
Acts 24:12  They did not find me disputing with anyone or gathering a crowd, whether in the temple, in the synagogues, or in the city.
Acts 24:13  Nor can they present proof to you of the things they now accuse me of.
Acts 24:14  But I confess this to you: according to the Way, which they call a sect, I worship the God of our fathers, believing everything in accordance with the law and everything written in the prophets,
Acts 24:15  having hope in God—which these people themselves also await—that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the unrighteous.
Acts 24:16  For this reason I myself strive always to have a blameless conscience toward God and human beings.
Acts 24:17  After several years I came to bring alms to my nation and offerings.
Acts 24:18  While I was engaged in these, they found me purified in the temple, with neither a crowd nor an uproar.
Acts 24:19  But there were some Jews from Asia who ought to be present before you and bring charges, if they had anything against me.
Acts 24:20  Or let these men themselves say what wrongdoing they found when I stood before the council,
Acts 24:21  except for this one declaration I cried out while standing among them: ‘It is concerning the resurrection of the dead that I am being judged before you today.’”
Acts 24:22  Felix, who had more accurate knowledge of the Way, adjourned their case, saying, “When Lysias the tribune comes down, I will decide your case.”
Acts 24:23  He ordered the centurion to keep Paul in custody but grant him some freedom, and not prevent any of his own people from attending to him.
Acts 24:24  After some days Felix came with his own wife Drusilla, who was Jewish. He summoned Paul and heard him concerning faith in Christ Jesus.
Acts 24:25  As Paul reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment, Felix became afraid and answered, “Go away for now. When I find an opportunity, I will summon you.”
Acts 24:26  At the same time he hoped that Paul would give him money. Therefore he summoned him more frequently and conversed with him.
Acts 24:27  When two years were completed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus. Wishing to gain favor with the Jews, Felix left Paul bound.

Acts 25
Acts 25:1  Three days after arriving in the province, Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
Acts 25:2  The chief priests and the leading men of the Jews presented their case against Paul to him and urged him,
Acts 25:3  asking as a favor against Paul that he summon him to Jerusalem, while planning an ambush to kill him along the road.
Acts 25:4  Festus answered that Paul was being kept at Caesarea, and that he himself would soon be going there.
Acts 25:5  He said, “Let the influential men among you go down with me, and if there is anything wrong in the man, let them accuse him.”
Acts 25:6  After staying among them no more than eight or ten days, he went down to Caesarea. The next day he sat on the tribunal and ordered Paul to be brought in.
Acts 25:7  When he arrived, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many serious accusations that they could not prove.
Acts 25:8  Paul made his defense: “I have committed no offense against the law of the Jews, against the temple, or against Caesar.”
Acts 25:9  But Festus, wishing to gain favor with the Jews, answered Paul, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and be judged there before me concerning these things?”
Acts 25:10  Paul said, “I am standing before Caesar’s tribunal, where I ought to be judged. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you yourself know very well.
Acts 25:11  If, then, I am doing wrong and have done anything deserving death, I do not refuse to die. But if there is nothing to their accusations against me, no one can hand me over to them as a favor. I appeal to Caesar.”
Acts 25:12  Then Festus conferred with his council and answered, “You have appealed to Caesar; to Caesar you will go.”
Acts 25:13  After some days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived in Caesarea to greet Festus.
Acts 25:14  While they stayed there for several days, Festus laid Paul’s case before the king, saying, “There is a man left as a prisoner by Felix.
Acts 25:15  When I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and elders of the Jews presented their case against him, asking for his condemnation.
Acts 25:16  I answered them that it is not Roman custom to hand anyone over as a favor before the accused has met his accusers face to face and received an opportunity to defend himself concerning the charge.
Acts 25:17  So when they gathered here, I made no delay, but on the next day sat on the tribunal and ordered the man brought in.
Acts 25:18  When his accusers stood up, they brought no charge of the evil things I had expected.
Acts 25:19  Instead, they had certain disputes with him concerning their own religion and a certain Jesus who had died, whom Paul asserted to be alive.
Acts 25:20  Uncertain how to investigate these matters, I asked whether he wished to go to Jerusalem and be judged there concerning them.
Acts 25:21  But when Paul appealed to be kept for Augustus’s decision, I ordered him held until I could send him to Caesar.”
Acts 25:22  Agrippa said to Festus, “I would like to hear the man myself.” He said, “Tomorrow you will hear him.”
Acts 25:23  The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the audience hall with the tribunes and the city’s prominent men. At Festus’s order, Paul was brought in.
Acts 25:24  Festus said, “King Agrippa and all you men present with us, you see this man concerning whom the whole multitude of the Jews petitioned me, both in Jerusalem and here, shouting that he ought not to live any longer.
Acts 25:25  I found that he had done nothing deserving death, but since he himself appealed to Augustus, I decided to send him.
Acts 25:26  I have nothing certain to write to the sovereign about him. Therefore I have brought him before you all, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after the examination I may have something to write.
Acts 25:27  For it seems unreasonable to me to send a prisoner without also indicating the charges against him.”

Acts 26
Acts 26:1  Agrippa said to Paul, “You are permitted to speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand and made his defense:
Acts 26:2  “Concerning everything of which I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate to make my defense before you today,
Acts 26:3  especially since you are familiar with all the Jewish customs and disputes. Therefore I ask you to hear me patiently.
Acts 26:4  All the Jews know my manner of life from my youth, lived from the beginning among my nation and in Jerusalem.
Acts 26:5  They have known me from the first, if they are willing to testify, that I lived as a Pharisee according to the strictest party of our religion.
Acts 26:6  Now I stand on trial because of hope in the promise made by God to our fathers,
Acts 26:7  which our twelve tribes, earnestly worshiping night and day, hope to attain. It is concerning this hope that I am accused by Jews, O king.
Acts 26:8  Why do you consider it unbelievable that God raises the dead?
Acts 26:9  I myself thought that I must do many things against the name of Jesus the Nazarene.
Acts 26:10  This I did in Jerusalem: I shut up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests, and when they were being killed, I cast my vote against them.
Acts 26:11  I punished them often in all the synagogues and tried to compel them to blaspheme. In my intense rage against them, I pursued them even to foreign cities.
Acts 26:12  In this pursuit I was traveling to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
Acts 26:13  when at midday, O king, I saw along the road a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those traveling with me.
Acts 26:14  When we had all fallen to the ground, I heard a voice speaking to me in the Hebrew language: ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me? It is hard for you to kick against goads.’
Acts 26:15  I said, ‘Who art Thou, Lord?’ The Lord said, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
Acts 26:16  But rise and stand on your feet, for I have appeared to you for this purpose: to appoint you a servant and witness of the things in which you have seen Me and those in which I will appear to you,
Acts 26:17  rescuing you from the people and from the Gentiles, to whom I am sending you,
Acts 26:18  to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from Satan’s authority to God, so that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an allotted share among those sanctified by faith in Me.’
Acts 26:19  Therefore, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,
Acts 26:20  but proclaimed first to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, throughout all the country of Judea, and to the Gentiles that they should repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.
Acts 26:21  For these reasons the Jews seized me in the temple and tried to kill me.
Acts 26:22  Having therefore received help from God, I stand to this day, testifying to small and great, saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen:
Acts 26:23  that the Christ would suffer and, as the first to rise from the dead, would proclaim light both to the people and to the Gentiles.”
Acts 26:24  As he was making this defense, Festus said with a loud voice, “You are mad, Paul! Your great learning is turning you to madness.”
Acts 26:25  Paul said, “I am not mad, most excellent Festus, but I speak words of truth and sound judgment.
Acts 26:26  For the king knows about these things, and I speak freely to him. I am persuaded that none of these things has escaped his notice, for this has not been done in a corner.
Acts 26:27  King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe.”
Acts 26:28  Agrippa said to Paul, “With so little, you are trying to persuade me to become a Christian.”
Acts 26:29  Paul said, “Whether with little or with much, I would pray to God that not only you but also all who hear me today might become as I am, except for these bonds.”
Acts 26:30  The king rose, along with the governor, Bernice, and those seated with them.
Acts 26:31  After withdrawing, they spoke to one another, saying, “This man is doing nothing deserving death or imprisonment.”
Acts 26:32  Agrippa said to Festus, “This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.”

Acts 27
Acts 27:1  When it was decided that we should sail to Italy, they handed Paul and some other prisoners over to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan cohort.
Acts 27:2  We boarded a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail to the ports along Asia, and set sail. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.
Acts 27:3  The next day we put in at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly and allowed him to go to his friends and receive care.
Acts 27:4  From there we set sail and sailed under the shelter of Cyprus because the winds were contrary.
Acts 27:5  We crossed the open sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia and came to Myra in Lycia.
Acts 27:6  There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing to Italy and put us aboard it.
Acts 27:7  We sailed slowly for many days and with difficulty came off Cnidus. Since the wind would not permit us to proceed, we sailed under the shelter of Crete off Salmone.
Acts 27:8  Coasting along it with difficulty, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near which was the city of Lasea.
Acts 27:9  Much time had passed, and sailing was already dangerous because even the Fast had now gone by. Paul advised them,
Acts 27:10  saying, “Men, I perceive that the voyage will bring damage and great loss, not only of the cargo and the ship but also of our lives.”
Acts 27:11  But the centurion was more persuaded by the pilot and the shipowner than by what Paul said.
Acts 27:12  Since the harbor was unsuitable for wintering, the majority decided to sail from there, hoping somehow to reach Phoenix, a harbor of Crete facing southwest and northwest, and winter there.
Acts 27:13  When a south wind blew gently, they supposed they had gained their purpose, weighed anchor, and sailed close along Crete.
Acts 27:14  But not long afterward a hurricane wind called Euraquilo rushed down from the island.
Acts 27:15  The ship was seized and could not face the wind, so we gave way and were driven along.
Acts 27:16  Running under the shelter of a small island called Cauda, we were barely able to secure the boat.
Acts 27:17  After hoisting it aboard, they used supports to hold the ship together from beneath. Fearing they would run aground on the Syrtis, they lowered the gear and were driven along in this way.
Acts 27:18  As we were violently battered by the storm, the next day they began throwing cargo overboard.
Acts 27:19  On the third day they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.
Acts 27:20  When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and a fierce storm kept battering us, all remaining hope of our being saved was taken away.
Acts 27:21  After a long time without food, Paul stood among them and said, “Men, you ought to have listened to me and not sailed from Crete, and so avoided this damage and loss.
Acts 27:22  Now I urge you to take courage, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.
Acts 27:23  For this night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I worship stood beside me,
Acts 27:24  saying, ‘Do not fear, Paul. You must stand before Caesar, and look, God has granted you all who sail with you.’
Acts 27:25  Therefore take courage, men, for I believe God that it will be just as I have been told.
Acts 27:26  But we must run aground on some island.”
Acts 27:27  When the fourteenth night came, as we were being driven across the Adria, about midnight the sailors suspected that some land was approaching them.
Acts 27:28  They took a sounding and found twenty fathoms. After going a little farther, they sounded again and found fifteen fathoms.
Acts 27:29  Fearing we might run aground somewhere on rocky places, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for day to come.
Acts 27:30  The sailors sought to flee from the ship and lowered the boat into the sea, pretending that they were about to lay out anchors from the bow.
Acts 27:31  Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these men remain in the ship, you cannot be saved.”
Acts 27:32  Then the soldiers cut the boat’s ropes and let it fall away.
Acts 27:33  As day was about to come, Paul urged everyone to take food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day you have continued waiting without food, taking nothing.
Acts 27:34  Therefore I urge you to take food, for this is for your safety. Not a hair from the head of any of you will be lost.”
Acts 27:35  After saying these things, he took bread, gave thanks to God before everyone, broke it, and began to eat.
Acts 27:36  They all took courage and themselves took food.
Acts 27:37  There were two hundred and seventy-six persons in all aboard the ship.
Acts 27:38  When they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.
Acts 27:39  When day came, they did not recognize the land, but noticed a bay with a beach and planned, if they could, to drive the ship onto it.
Acts 27:40  They cast off the anchors and left them in the sea, while also loosening the lashings of the steering oars. They raised the foresail to the wind and headed for the beach.
Acts 27:41  But they struck a place between two seas and ran the ship aground. The bow stuck fast and remained immovable, while the stern was breaking apart under the force of the waves.
Acts 27:42  The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners so that none might swim away and escape.
Acts 27:43  But the centurion, wishing to save Paul, prevented them from carrying out their plan. He ordered those able to swim to jump overboard first and make for land,
Acts 27:44  and the rest to follow, some on planks and some on pieces from the ship. In this way everyone reached land safely.

Acts 28
Acts 28:1  After reaching safety, we learned that the island was called Melite.
Acts 28:2  The people who did not speak Greek showed us extraordinary kindness. They kindled a fire and welcomed us all because of the rain that had begun and because of the cold.
Acts 28:3  Paul gathered a bundle of brushwood and put it on the fire. A viper came out because of the heat and fastened onto his hand.
Acts 28:4  When the people who did not speak Greek saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “This man is certainly a murderer. Although he escaped from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live.”
Acts 28:5  But he shook the creature into the fire and suffered no harm.
Acts 28:6  They expected him to swell up or suddenly fall down dead. After waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said that he was a god.
Acts 28:7  Near that place were lands belonging to the island’s chief man, named Publius. He welcomed us and hospitably gave us lodging for three days.
Acts 28:8  Publius’s father lay sick with fevers and dysentery. Paul went in to him, prayed, laid his hands upon him, and healed him.
Acts 28:9  After this happened, the other sick people on the island also came and were healed.
Acts 28:10  They honored us with many honors, and when we sailed, they supplied what we needed.
Acts 28:11  After three months we sailed in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered at the island, with the Dioscuri as its emblem.
Acts 28:12  We put in at Syracuse and stayed three days.
Acts 28:13  From there we cast off and reached Rhegium. After one day a south wind arose, and on the second day we came to Puteoli.
Acts 28:14  There we found brothers and were invited to stay with them seven days. And so we came to Rome.
Acts 28:15  From there the brothers, having heard about us, came to meet us as far as the Forum of Appius and Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.
Acts 28:16  When we entered Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself with the soldier guarding him.
Acts 28:17  After three days he called together the leading Jews. When they gathered, he said to them, “Men, brothers, although I had done nothing against the people or the ancestral customs, I was handed over as a prisoner from Jerusalem into Roman hands.
Acts 28:18  After examining me, they wished to release me, because there was no cause for death in my case.
Acts 28:19  But when the Jews objected, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, though I had no accusation to bring against my nation.
Acts 28:20  For this reason I asked to see you and speak with you, for it is because of Israel’s hope that I wear this chain.”
Acts 28:21  They said to him, “We have received no letters from Judea about you, nor has any of the brothers who arrived reported or spoken anything evil about you.
Acts 28:22  But we consider it right to hear from you what you think, for concerning this sect we know that it is opposed everywhere.”
Acts 28:23  They appointed a day with him and came to his lodging in greater numbers. From morning until evening he explained to them, bearing solemn witness to the kingdom of God and seeking to persuade them concerning Jesus from both the law of Moses and the prophets.
Acts 28:24  Some were persuaded by what was said, while others did not believe.
Acts 28:25  Disagreeing with one another, they began to leave after Paul made one statement: “The Holy Spirit spoke well through Isaiah the prophet to your fathers,
Acts 28:26  saying, ‘Go to this people and say: “You will hear and hear, yet never understand; you will look and look, yet never see.
Acts 28:27  For this people’s heart has grown dull, their ears have become hard of hearing, and they have closed their eyes, lest they see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn back, and I would heal them.”’
Acts 28:28  Therefore let it be known to you that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles; they will listen.”
Acts 28:30  He remained two whole years in his own rented lodging and welcomed all who came to him,
Acts 28:31  proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, unhindered.

ROMANS

Romans 1
Romans 1:1  Paul, a slave of Christ Jesus, called as an apostle, set apart for the gospel of God,
Romans 1:2  which He promised beforehand through His prophets in holy Scriptures,
Romans 1:3  concerning His Son, who came from David’s seed according to the flesh,
Romans 1:4  who was designated Son of God in power according to the Spirit of holiness by resurrection from the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord,
Romans 1:5  through whom we received grace and apostleship for the obedience of faith among all the nations for His name,
Romans 1:6  among whom you also are, called by Jesus Christ:
Romans 1:7  to all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called as saints: grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Romans 1:8  First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is proclaimed in the whole world.
Romans 1:9  For God, whom I serve in my spirit in the gospel of His Son, is my witness that I remember you without ceasing,
Romans 1:10  always in my prayers asking whether somehow now at last I may be granted a way, by the will of God, to come to you.
Romans 1:11  For I long to see you, to share with you some spiritual gift so that you may be strengthened,
Romans 1:12  that is, to be encouraged together among you through one another’s faith, both yours and mine.
Romans 1:13  And I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that I often planned to come to you—and was hindered until now—so that I might have some fruit among you also, just as among the other nations.
Romans 1:14  I am a debtor both to Greeks and to those who do not speak Greek, both to the wise and to the senseless.
Romans 1:15  Thus, for my part, I am eager to proclaim the gospel also to you who are in Rome.
Romans 1:16  For I am not ashamed of the gospel, for it is God’s power for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.
Romans 1:17  For in it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith, as it is written, “But the righteous one will live by faith.”
Romans 1:18  For God’s wrath is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of people who suppress the truth in unrighteousness,
Romans 1:19  because what is known of God is plain among them, for God made it plain to them.
Romans 1:20  For His invisible qualities, both His eternal power and divinity, have been clearly seen since the creation of the world, understood through the things made, so that they are without excuse,
Romans 1:21  because, although they knew God, they did not glorify Him as God or give thanks, but became futile in their thoughts, and their senseless heart was darkened.
Romans 1:22  Claiming to be wise, they became foolish,
Romans 1:23  and exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of corruptible humanity, and of birds and four-footed animals and creeping things.
Romans 1:24  Therefore God handed them over, in the desires of their hearts, to impurity, so that their bodies would be dishonored among them,
Romans 1:25  who exchanged the truth of God for the lie, and revered and worshiped the creation instead of the Creator, who is blessed throughout the ages. Amen.
Romans 1:26  For this reason God handed them over to dishonorable passions; for their females exchanged natural relations for those contrary to nature,
Romans 1:27  and likewise the males, leaving natural relations with the female, burned in their desire for one another, males with males committing what is shameful and receiving in themselves the due penalty for their error.
Romans 1:28  And just as they did not see fit to retain God in their knowledge, God handed them over to an unfit mind, to do what is not fitting:
Romans 1:29  filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, greed, evil; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, malice; whisperers,
Romans 1:30  slanderers, haters of God, insolent, proud, boastful, inventors of evils, disobedient to parents,
Romans 1:31  without understanding, faithless, without natural affection, merciless;
Romans 1:32  who, knowing God’s righteous decree, that those who practice such things are worthy of death, not only do them, but also approve those who practice them.

Romans 2
Romans 2:1  Therefore you are without excuse, O man—whoever you are who judges. For when you judge another, you condemn yourself, because you who judge practice the same things.
Romans 2:2  And we know that God’s judgment against those who practice such things is according to truth.
Romans 2:3  But do you think, O man—you who judge those who practice such things and do them yourself—that you will escape God’s judgment?
Romans 2:4  Or do you despise the wealth of His kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that God’s kindness leads you to repentance?
Romans 2:5  But by your hardness and unrepentant heart, you store up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and revelation of God’s righteous judgment,
Romans 2:6  who will repay each according to his works:
Romans 2:7  to those who, through perseverance in good work, seek glory and honor and incorruptibility, eternal life;
Romans 2:8  but to those acting from selfish ambition, who disobey the truth but obey unrighteousness, wrath and fury,
Romans 2:9  affliction and distress upon every human soul that does evil—the Jew first and also the Greek;
Romans 2:10  but glory and honor and peace to everyone who does good, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.
Romans 2:11  For there is no partiality with God.
Romans 2:12  For all who sinned without law will also perish without law; and all who sinned under law will be judged through law.
Romans 2:13  For it is not the hearers of law who are righteous before God, but the doers of law will be justified.
Romans 2:14  For whenever Gentiles who do not have law do by nature the things of the law, these, though not having law, are a law to themselves,
Romans 2:15  who show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience bearing witness with it, and their reasonings among themselves accusing or even defending,
Romans 2:16  on the day when God judges people’s secrets according to my gospel through Christ Jesus.
Romans 2:17  But if you bear the name Jew, and rest upon law and boast in God,
Romans 2:18  and know His will and approve the things that matter, being instructed from the law,
Romans 2:19  and are confident that you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light to those in darkness,
Romans 2:20  an instructor of the senseless, a teacher of infants, having in the law the embodiment of knowledge and truth—
Romans 2:21  you then who teach another, do you not teach yourself? You who proclaim that one must not steal, do you steal?
Romans 2:22  You who say that one must not commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?
Romans 2:23  You who boast in law, do you dishonor God through transgression of the law?
Romans 2:24  For “the name of God is blasphemed among the nations because of you,” just as it is written.
Romans 2:25  For circumcision benefits you if you practice law; but if you are a transgressor of law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
Romans 2:26  So if the uncircumcised person keeps the law’s righteous requirements, will not his uncircumcision be reckoned as circumcision?
Romans 2:27  And the one uncircumcised by nature who fulfills the law will judge you who, with the written letter and circumcision, are a transgressor of law.
Romans 2:28  For the Jew is not the one outwardly so, nor is circumcision what is outward in flesh;
Romans 2:29  but the Jew is the one inwardly so, and circumcision is of the heart, in Spirit, not in letter, whose praise is not from people but from God.

Romans 3
Romans 3:1  What, then, is the Jew’s advantage, or what is the benefit of circumcision?
Romans 3:2  Much in every way. First, indeed, because they were entrusted with the oracles of God.
Romans 3:3  For what if some were unfaithful? Will their unfaithfulness nullify God’s faithfulness?
Romans 3:4  May it never be! But let God be true, and every human being a liar, just as it is written, “So that Thou mayest be justified in Thy words, and wilt prevail when Thou art judged.”
Romans 3:5  But if our unrighteousness demonstrates God’s righteousness, what shall we say? Is God unrighteous when He brings wrath? I speak in human terms.
Romans 3:6  May it never be! For then how will God judge the world?
Romans 3:7  But if God’s truth abounded through my falsehood to His glory, why am I still judged as a sinner?
Romans 3:8  And why not say—as we are slandered and as some claim we say—“Let us do evil things so that good things may come”? Their condemnation is just.
Romans 3:9  What, then? Are we better off? Not at all; for we have already charged both Jews and Greeks with all being under sin,
Romans 3:10  just as it is written: “There is no righteous one, not even one;
Romans 3:11  there is no one who understands; there is no one who seeks God.
Romans 3:12  All turned aside; together they became useless. There is no one who shows kindness; there is not even one.
Romans 3:13  Their throat is an opened tomb; with their tongues they practiced deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips;
Romans 3:14  their mouth is full of cursing and bitterness.
Romans 3:15  Their feet are swift to pour out blood;
Romans 3:16  ruin and misery are in their ways,
Romans 3:17  and the way of peace they did not know.
Romans 3:18  There is no fear of God before their eyes.”
Romans 3:19  And we know that whatever the law says, it speaks to those under the law, so that every mouth may be stopped and the whole world may become answerable to God;
Romans 3:20  because by works of law no flesh will be justified before Him, for through law comes knowledge of sin.
Romans 3:21  But now, apart from law, God’s righteousness has been revealed, witnessed by the law and the prophets:
Romans 3:22  God’s righteousness through faith in Jesus Christ, for all who believe. For there is no distinction,
Romans 3:23  for all sinned and fall short of God’s glory,
Romans 3:24  being justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus,
Romans 3:25  whom God set forth as a propitiation in His blood, through faith, to demonstrate His righteousness because of the passing over of sins committed beforehand,
Romans 3:26  in God’s forbearance, to demonstrate His righteousness at the present time, so that He may be righteous and justify the one who has faith in Jesus.
Romans 3:27  Where, then, is boasting? It was excluded. Through what kind of law? Of works? No, but through a law of faith.
Romans 3:28  For we reckon that a person is justified by faith apart from works of law.
Romans 3:29  Or is God the God of Jews only? Is He not also of Gentiles? Yes, also of Gentiles,
Romans 3:30  since God is one, who will justify the circumcised from faith and the uncircumcised through faith.
Romans 3:31  Do we then nullify law through faith? May it never be! Rather, we establish law.

Romans 4
Romans 4:1  What, then, shall we say Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, has found?
Romans 4:2  For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast of—but not before God.
Romans 4:3  For what does the Scripture say? “And Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.”
Romans 4:4  Now to the one who works, the wage is not reckoned according to grace, but according to what is owed.
Romans 4:5  But to the one who does not work, but believes in the One who justifies the ungodly, his faith is reckoned as righteousness,
Romans 4:6  just as David also speaks of the blessedness of the person to whom God reckons righteousness apart from works:
Romans 4:7  “Blessed are those whose lawless deeds were forgiven and whose sins were covered;
Romans 4:8  blessed is the man whose sin the Lord certainly will not reckon.”
Romans 4:9  Is this blessedness, then, upon the circumcised, or also upon the uncircumcised? For we say, “Faith was reckoned to Abraham as righteousness.”
Romans 4:10  How, then, was it reckoned? While he was circumcised, or uncircumcised? Not while circumcised, but while uncircumcised.
Romans 4:11  And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith he had while uncircumcised, so that he might be father of all who believe while uncircumcised, so that righteousness might be reckoned to them also,
Romans 4:12  and father of the circumcised, to those who are not only circumcised but also walk in the footsteps of the faith our father Abraham had while uncircumcised.
Romans 4:13  For the promise to Abraham or to his seed that he would be heir of the world was not through law, but through the righteousness of faith.
Romans 4:14  For if those from law are heirs, faith has been emptied and the promise has been nullified;
Romans 4:15  for the law brings wrath, but where there is no law, neither is there transgression.
Romans 4:16  For this reason it is from faith, so that it may be according to grace, so that the promise may be secure to all the seed—not only to the one from the law, but also to the one from Abraham’s faith. He is father of us all,
Romans 4:17  just as it is written, “I have made you father of many nations,” before the God whom he believed, who gives life to the dead and calls the things that are not as though they are.
Romans 4:18  Against hope, he believed in hope, so that he might become father of many nations, according to what had been said, “So shall your seed be.”
Romans 4:19  And without growing weak in faith, he considered his own body, already deadened as it was, being about a hundred years old, and the deadness of Sarah’s womb;
Romans 4:20  but with regard to God’s promise he did not waver in unbelief, but was strengthened in faith, giving glory to God,
Romans 4:21  and being fully assured that what He has promised He is also able to do.
Romans 4:22  Therefore it was also reckoned to him as righteousness.
Romans 4:23  But “it was reckoned to him” was not written for his sake alone,
Romans 4:24  but also for our sake, to whom it is to be reckoned, who believe in the One who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead,
Romans 4:25  who was handed over for our trespasses and was raised for our justification.

Romans 5
Romans 5:1  Therefore, having been justified from faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,
Romans 5:2  through whom we have also obtained access by faith into this grace in which we stand; and we boast in hope of God’s glory.
Romans 5:3  And not only this, but we also boast in afflictions, knowing that affliction produces perseverance,
Romans 5:4  and perseverance, proven character, and proven character, hope.
Romans 5:5  And hope does not put us to shame, because God’s love has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us.
Romans 5:6  For while we were still weak, even then Christ died at the appointed time for the ungodly.
Romans 5:7  For rarely will someone die for a righteous person; though perhaps for the good person someone even dares to die.
Romans 5:8  But God demonstrates His own love toward us in that, while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
Romans 5:9  Much more, then, having now been justified in His blood, we will be saved through Him from wrath.
Romans 5:10  For if, while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of His Son, much more, having been reconciled, we will be saved in His life.
Romans 5:11  And not only this, but we also boast in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.
Romans 5:12  For this reason, just as through one person sin entered the world, and through sin, death, and so death passed to all people, because all sinned—
Romans 5:13  for before the law came, sin was in the world, but sin is not charged to account when there is no law;
Romans 5:14  nevertheless death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who did not sin in the likeness of Adam’s transgression, who is a type of the One to come.
Romans 5:15  But the gift is not like the trespass. For if by the one man’s trespass the many died, much more did God’s grace and the gift in the grace of the one Man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many.
Romans 5:16  And the gift is not like what came through one who sinned; for the judgment from one trespass resulted in condemnation, but the gift from many trespasses resulted in justification.
Romans 5:17  For if, by the one man’s trespass, death reigned through the one, much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and the gift of righteousness reign in life through the One, Jesus Christ.
Romans 5:18  So then, as through one trespass there was condemnation for all people, so also through one righteous act there is justification of life for all people.
Romans 5:19  For just as through the disobedience of the one person the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the One the many will be made righteous.
Romans 5:20  But law came in alongside, so that the trespass might increase; but where sin increased, grace abounded beyond measure,
Romans 5:21  so that, just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness for eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

Romans 6
Romans 6:1  What, then, shall we say? Should we remain in sin so that grace may increase?
Romans 6:2  May it never be! We who died to sin, how will we still live in it?
Romans 6:3  Or do you not know that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death?
Romans 6:4  Therefore we were buried with Him through baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the Father’s glory, so we also might walk in newness of life.
Romans 6:5  For if we have become united with the likeness of His death, we will also be united with that of His resurrection,
Romans 6:6  knowing this, that our old self was crucified with Him, so that the body of sin might be rendered powerless, so that we would no longer be enslaved to sin;
Romans 6:7  for the one who died has been justified from sin.
Romans 6:8  And if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with Him,
Romans 6:9  knowing that Christ, having been raised from the dead, no longer dies; death no longer rules over Him.
Romans 6:10  For the death He died, He died to sin once for all; but the life He lives, He lives to God.
Romans 6:11  So also reckon yourselves to be dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.
Romans 6:12  Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body, so that you obey its desires;
Romans 6:13  Do not present the parts of your body to sin as weapons of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as those alive from the dead, and the parts of your body to God as weapons of righteousness.
Romans 6:14  For sin will not rule over you, for you are not under law, but under grace.
Romans 6:15  What, then? Should we sin because we are not under law, but under grace? May it never be!
Romans 6:16  Do you not know that when you present yourselves to someone as slaves to obey, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, either of sin leading to death, or of obedience leading to righteousness?
Romans 6:17  But thanks be to God that, though you were slaves of sin, you obeyed from the heart the pattern of teaching to which you were handed over;
Romans 6:18  and, having been set free from sin, you were enslaved to righteousness.
Romans 6:19  I speak in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. For just as you presented the parts of your body as slaves to impurity and to lawlessness leading to lawlessness, so now present the parts of your body as slaves to righteousness leading to sanctification.
Romans 6:20  For when you were slaves of sin, you were free from righteousness.
Romans 6:21  What fruit, then, did you have at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? For the end of those things is death.
Romans 6:22  But now, having been set free from sin and enslaved to God, you have your fruit leading to sanctification, and the end, eternal life.
Romans 6:23  For sin’s wages are death, but God’s gift is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

Romans 7
Romans 7:1  Or do you not know, brothers—for I speak to those who know law—that the law rules over a person for as long as he lives?
Romans 7:2  For the married woman is bound by law to her living husband; but if the husband dies, she has been released from the law of the husband.
Romans 7:3  So then, while the husband lives, she will be called an adulteress if she belongs to another man; but if the husband dies, she is free from the law, so that she is not an adulteress when she belongs to another man.
Romans 7:4  So, my brothers, you also were put to death to the law through the body of Christ, so that you might belong to Another, the One raised from the dead, so that we might bear fruit for God.
Romans 7:5  For when we were in the flesh, the sinful passions aroused through the law were at work in the parts of our body, to bear fruit for death.
Romans 7:6  But now we were released from the law, having died to that in which we were held, so that we serve in the newness of the Spirit and not in the oldness of the letter.
Romans 7:7  What, then, shall we say? Is the law sin? May it never be! Rather, I did not know sin except through law; for I would not have known desire if the law had not said, “You shall not desire.”
Romans 7:8  But sin, taking opportunity through the commandment, produced every desire in me; for apart from law sin is dead.
Romans 7:9  And I was once alive apart from law; but when the commandment came, sin came to life,
Romans 7:10  and I died; and the commandment that was for life proved to bring me death.
Romans 7:11  For sin, taking opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through it killed me.
Romans 7:12  So the law is holy, and the commandment holy and righteous and good.
Romans 7:13  Did the good, then, become death to me? May it never be! But sin did, so that it might appear as sin, producing death in me through the good, so that through the commandment sin might become sinful beyond measure.
Romans 7:14  For we know that the law is spiritual; but I am of flesh, sold under sin.
Romans 7:15  For I do not understand what I do; for I do not practice what I want, but what I hate, this I do.
Romans 7:16  But if I do what I do not want, I agree with the law that it is good.
Romans 7:17  But now it is no longer I who do it, but sin dwelling in me.
Romans 7:18  For I know that good does not dwell in me—that is, in my flesh. For the will is there, but doing what is good is not.
Romans 7:19  For I do not do the good that I want, but the evil that I do not want, this I practice.
Romans 7:20  But if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but sin dwelling in me.
Romans 7:21  So I find this law: when I want to do the good, evil is at hand for me.
Romans 7:22  For I delight in God’s law in my inner self,
Romans 7:23  but I see another law in the parts of my body, waging war against the law of my mind and taking me captive in the law of sin that is in the parts of my body.
Romans 7:24  Wretched person that I am! Who will rescue me from the body of this death?
Romans 7:25  Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then I myself, with the mind, serve God’s law, but with the flesh, sin’s law.

Romans 8
Romans 8:1  So then, there is now no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus.
Romans 8:2  For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus set you free from the law of sin and death.
Romans 8:3  For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God did: sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and concerning sin, He condemned sin in the flesh,
Romans 8:4  so that the law’s righteous requirement might be fulfilled in us who walk not according to flesh, but according to Spirit.
Romans 8:5  For those who are according to flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, but those according to Spirit, on the things of the Spirit.
Romans 8:6  For the mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace,
Romans 8:7  because the mind of the flesh is hostility toward God; for it does not submit to God’s law, nor indeed can it.
Romans 8:8  And those who are in flesh cannot please God.
Romans 8:9  But you are not in flesh, but in Spirit, if indeed God’s Spirit dwells in you. But if anyone does not have Christ’s Spirit, that person does not belong to Him.
Romans 8:10  But if Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the Spirit is life because of righteousness.
Romans 8:11  And if the Spirit of the One who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, the One who raised Christ from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit dwelling in you.
Romans 8:12  So then, brothers, we are debtors—not to the flesh, to live according to flesh;
Romans 8:13  for if you live according to flesh, you are going to die; but if by Spirit you put to death the body’s practices, you will live.
Romans 8:14  For all who are led by God’s Spirit are sons of God.
Romans 8:15  For you did not receive a spirit of slavery leading again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption as sons, in whom we cry, “Abba, Father.”
Romans 8:16  The Spirit Himself bears witness with our spirit that we are God’s children.
Romans 8:17  And if children, then also heirs: heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ, if indeed we suffer with Him so that we may also be glorified with Him.
Romans 8:18  For I reckon that the sufferings of the present time are not worth comparing with the glory that is to be revealed in us.
Romans 8:19  For creation eagerly awaits the revealing of God’s sons;
Romans 8:20  for creation was subjected to futility, not willingly, but because of the One who subjected it, in hope
Romans 8:21  that creation itself also will be set free from slavery to corruption into the freedom of the glory of God’s children.
Romans 8:22  For we know that the whole creation groans together and labors in birth pangs together until now;
Romans 8:23  and not only creation, but we ourselves also, having the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan within ourselves, awaiting adoption as sons, the redemption of our body.
Romans 8:24  For in hope we were saved. But hope that is seen is not hope; for who hopes for what he sees?
Romans 8:25  But if we hope for what we do not see, we await it with perseverance.
Romans 8:26  And likewise the Spirit also helps our weakness; for we do not know what to pray for as we ought, but the Spirit Himself intercedes with groanings beyond words.
Romans 8:27  And the One who searches hearts knows the mind of the Spirit, because He intercedes for saints according to God.
Romans 8:28  And we know that all things work together for good for those who love God, those who are called according to purpose.
Romans 8:29  Because those whom He foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, so that He might be firstborn among many brothers;
Romans 8:30  and those whom He predestined, these He also called; and those whom He called, these He also justified; and those whom He justified, these He also glorified.
Romans 8:31  What, then, shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who is against us?
Romans 8:32  He who did not spare His own Son, but handed Him over for us all, how will He not also graciously give us all things with Him?
Romans 8:33  Who will bring a charge against God’s chosen ones? God is the One who justifies.
Romans 8:34  Who is the one who condemns? Christ Jesus is the One who died—more than that, was raised—who is also at God’s right hand, who also intercedes for us.
Romans 8:35  Who will separate us from Christ’s love? Affliction, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or sword?
Romans 8:36  Just as it is written, “For Thy sake we are put to death all day long; we were reckoned as sheep for slaughter.”
Romans 8:37  But in all these things we more than conquer through the One who loved us.
Romans 8:38  For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor rulers, neither things present nor things to come nor powers,
Romans 8:39  neither height nor depth nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from God’s love in Christ Jesus our Lord.

Romans 9
Romans 9:1  I speak truth in Christ; I do not lie, my conscience bearing witness with me in the Holy Spirit,
Romans 9:2  that I have great sorrow and unceasing anguish in my heart.
Romans 9:3  For I could wish that I myself were accursed, away from Christ, for the sake of my brothers, my kinsmen according to the flesh,
Romans 9:4  who are Israelites. Theirs are the adoption as sons and the glory and the covenants and the giving of the law and the worship and the promises;
Romans 9:5  theirs are the fathers, and from them comes the Christ according to the flesh, who is over all, God blessed throughout the ages. Amen.
Romans 9:6  But it is not as though God’s word has failed. For not all who are from Israel are Israel;
Romans 9:7  neither, because they are Abraham’s seed, are they all children; but, “In Isaac your seed will be called.”
Romans 9:8  That is, the children of the flesh are not thereby God’s children, but the children of the promise are reckoned as seed.
Romans 9:9  For this is a word of promise: “At this time I will come, and Sarah will have a son.”
Romans 9:10  And not only this, but also Rebecca, having conceived by one man, Isaac our father—
Romans 9:11  for when they had not yet been born or done anything good or bad, so that God’s purpose according to election might remain,
Romans 9:12  not from works but from the One who calls, it was said to her, “The older will serve the younger,”
Romans 9:13  just as it is written, “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.”
Romans 9:14  What, then, shall we say? Is there unrighteousness with God? May it never be!
Romans 9:15  For He says to Moses, “I will have mercy on whomever I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whomever I have compassion.”
Romans 9:16  So then, it depends not on the one who wills, nor on the one who runs, but on God who has mercy.
Romans 9:17  For the Scripture says to Pharaoh, “For this very purpose I raised you up, so that I might demonstrate My power in you, and so that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth.”
Romans 9:18  So then, He has mercy on whom He wills, and whom He wills He hardens.
Romans 9:19  You will then say to me, “Why, then, does He still find fault? For who has resisted His purpose?”
Romans 9:20  But who are you, O man, to answer back to God? Will what is formed say to the One who formed it, “Why didst Thou make me this way?”
Romans 9:21  Or does the potter not have authority over the clay, from the same lump to make one vessel for honor and another for dishonor?
Romans 9:22  But what if God, willing to demonstrate wrath and to make His power known, endured with much patience vessels of wrath fitted for destruction,
Romans 9:23  and did so to make known the wealth of His glory upon vessels of mercy, which He prepared beforehand for glory,
Romans 9:24  even us whom He also called, not only from Jews but also from Gentiles?
Romans 9:25  As He also says in Hosea, “I will call those who are not My people ‘My people,’ and her who is not beloved ‘beloved’;
Romans 9:26  and it shall come to pass that in the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not My people,’ there they will be called sons of the living God.”
Romans 9:27  But Isaiah cries out concerning Israel, “Though the number of Israel’s sons be like the sand of the sea, the remnant will be saved;
Romans 9:28  for the Lord will carry out a word on the earth, completing it and cutting it short.”
Romans 9:29  And just as Isaiah has said beforehand, “Unless the Lord Sabaoth had left us seed, we would have become like Sodom and would have been made like Gomorrah.”
Romans 9:30  What, then, shall we say? That Gentiles who were not pursuing righteousness attained righteousness, namely the righteousness from faith;
Romans 9:31  but Israel, pursuing a law of righteousness, did not attain law.
Romans 9:32  Why? Because it was not from faith, but as though from works. They stumbled against the stone of stumbling,
Romans 9:33  just as it is written, “Behold, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, and the one who believes in Him will not be put to shame.”

Romans 10
Romans 10:1  Brothers, my heart’s desire and my prayer to God for them are that they may be saved.
Romans 10:2  For I bear them witness that they have zeal for God, but not according to knowledge;
Romans 10:3  for, not knowing God’s righteousness and seeking to establish their own righteousness, they did not submit to God’s righteousness.
Romans 10:4  For Christ is the end of law for righteousness to everyone who believes.
Romans 10:5  For Moses writes about the righteousness from the law: the person who does these things will live by them.
Romans 10:6  But the righteousness from faith speaks in this way: “Do not say in your heart, ‘Who will ascend into heaven?’”—that is, to bring Christ down;
Romans 10:7  or, “‘Who will descend into the abyss?’”—that is, to bring Christ up from the dead.
Romans 10:8  But what does it say? “The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart”—that is, the word of faith that we proclaim.
Romans 10:9  Because if you confess Jesus as Lord with your mouth, and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved;
Romans 10:10  for with the heart one believes for righteousness, and with the mouth one confesses for salvation.
Romans 10:11  For the Scripture says, “Whoever believes in Him shall not be put to shame.”
Romans 10:12  For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek, for the same Lord is Lord of all, being rich toward all who call upon Him;
Romans 10:13  for “everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.”
Romans 10:14  How, then, are they to call upon One in whom they have not believed? And how are they to believe in One whom they have not heard? And how are they to hear without someone proclaiming?
Romans 10:15  And how are they to proclaim unless they are sent? Just as it is written, “How beautiful are the feet of those announcing good things!”
Romans 10:16  But not all obeyed the gospel. For Isaiah says, “O Lord, who has believed our report?”
Romans 10:17  So faith is from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ.
Romans 10:18  But I say, did they not hear? Indeed they did: “Their sound went out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the inhabited world.”
Romans 10:19  But I say, did Israel not know? First Moses says, “I will make you jealous by what is not a nation; by a senseless nation I will provoke you to anger.”
Romans 10:20  And Isaiah speaks boldly and says, “I was found among those who did not seek Me; I became known to those who did not ask for Me.”
Romans 10:21  But concerning Israel He says, “All day long I stretched out My hands toward a disobedient and contrary people.”

Romans 11
Romans 11:1  I say, then, has God rejected His people? May it never be! For I too am an Israelite, from Abraham’s seed, of Benjamin’s tribe.
Romans 11:2  God has not rejected His people whom He foreknew. Or do you not know what the Scripture says in the passage about Elijah, how he pleads with God against Israel?
Romans 11:3  “Lord, they killed Thy prophets, they demolished Thy altars, and I alone was left, and they seek my life.”
Romans 11:4  But what does the divine response say to him? “I left for Myself seven thousand men who did not bend the knee to Baal.”
Romans 11:5  So then, at the present time also there has come to be a remnant according to an election of grace.
Romans 11:6  But if by grace, it is no longer from works; otherwise grace is no longer grace.
Romans 11:7  What, then? What Israel seeks, it did not obtain; but the chosen obtained it, and the rest were hardened,
Romans 11:8  just as it is written, “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes not to see and ears not to hear, until this very day.”
Romans 11:9  And David says, “Let their table become a snare and a trap and a stumbling block and a repayment to them;
Romans 11:10  let their eyes be darkened so as not to see, and bend their back continually.”
Romans 11:11  I say, then, did they stumble so that they might fall? May it never be! But by their trespass salvation has come to the Gentiles, to make them jealous.
Romans 11:12  But if their trespass is the world’s wealth and their loss the Gentiles’ wealth, how much more their fullness!
Romans 11:13  And I speak to you Gentiles. Insofar as I am an apostle of Gentiles, I glorify my ministry,
Romans 11:14  if somehow I may make my own flesh jealous and save some of them.
Romans 11:15  For if their rejection is the world’s reconciliation, what will their acceptance be except life from the dead?
Romans 11:16  And if the firstfruits are holy, so is the lump; and if the root is holy, so are the branches.
Romans 11:17  But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them and came to share in the olive tree’s rich root,
Romans 11:18  do not boast over the branches. But if you boast, it is not you who bear the root, but the root bears you.
Romans 11:19  You will then say, “Branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in.”
Romans 11:20  Well: they were broken off because of unbelief, but you stand by faith. Do not be haughty, but fear;
Romans 11:21  for if God did not spare the natural branches, neither will He spare you.
Romans 11:22  See, then, God’s kindness and severity: severity upon those who fell, but God’s kindness upon you, if you remain in the kindness; otherwise you too will be cut off.
Romans 11:23  And they also, if they do not remain in unbelief, will be grafted in; for God is able to graft them in again.
Romans 11:24  For if you were cut from what is by nature a wild olive, and contrary to nature were grafted into a cultivated olive, how much more will these natural branches be grafted into their own olive tree!
Romans 11:25  For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of this mystery, so that you may not be wise in your own eyes: that a partial hardening has come upon Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles enters,
Romans 11:26  and in this way all Israel will be saved, just as it is written: “The Deliverer will come from Zion; He will turn away ungodliness from Jacob.
Romans 11:27  And this is My covenant with them, when I take away their sins.”
Romans 11:28  With regard to the gospel, they are enemies for your sake; but with regard to election, beloved for the fathers’ sake.
Romans 11:29  For God’s gifts and calling are irrevocable.
Romans 11:30  For just as you once disobeyed God, but now received mercy through their disobedience,
Romans 11:31  so they also now disobeyed, so that through the mercy shown to you they also may now receive mercy.
Romans 11:32  For God confined all in disobedience so that He might have mercy on all.
Romans 11:33  O depth of God’s wealth and wisdom and knowledge! How unsearchable His judgments and untraceable His ways!
Romans 11:34  “For who knew the Lord’s mind? Or who became His counselor?
Romans 11:35  Or who gave to Him first, and it will be repaid to him?”
Romans 11:36  Because from Him and through Him and to Him are all things. To Him be the glory throughout the ages. Amen.

Romans 12
Romans 12:1  Therefore I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God—your rational worship.
Romans 12:2  And do not be conformed to this age, but be transformed by the renewal of the mind, so that you may discern what God’s will is: the good and pleasing and perfect.
Romans 12:3  For through the grace given me I say to everyone among you not to think more highly than one ought to think, but to think with sound judgment, as God apportioned to each a measure of faith.
Romans 12:4  For as we have many parts in one body, and the parts do not all have the same function,
Romans 12:5  so we, the many, are one body in Christ, and each one is a member of the others.
Romans 12:6  And since we have gifts differing according to the grace given to us: if prophecy, let it be according to the proportion of faith;
Romans 12:7  if service, in serving; if one teaches, in teaching;
Romans 12:8  if one exhorts, in exhortation; the one who shares, with generosity; the one who leads, with diligence; the one who shows mercy, with cheerfulness.
Romans 12:9  Let love be without hypocrisy. Abhor what is evil; cling to what is good.
Romans 12:10  In brotherly love be tenderly devoted to one another; take the lead in honoring one another;
Romans 12:11  do not be slack in zeal; be fervent in spirit; serve the Lord;
Romans 12:12  rejoice in hope; persevere in affliction; persist in prayer;
Romans 12:13  share in the needs of the saints; pursue hospitality.
Romans 12:14  Bless those who persecute you; bless, and do not curse.
Romans 12:15  Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.
Romans 12:16  Have the same mind toward one another. Do not set your minds on lofty things, but associate with the lowly. Do not become wise in your own eyes.
Romans 12:17  Repay no one evil for evil. Take thought for what is honorable before all people.
Romans 12:18  If possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with all people.
Romans 12:19  Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but make room for wrath; for it is written, “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”
Romans 12:20  But if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink; for by doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head.
Romans 12:21  Do not be conquered by evil, but conquer evil with good.

Romans 13
Romans 13:1  Let every soul submit to the higher authorities, for there is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been appointed by God.
Romans 13:2  Therefore the one who sets himself against authority has resisted God’s ordering, and those who resist will receive judgment upon themselves.
Romans 13:3  For rulers are not a terror to good work, but to evil. Do you want to be free from fear of the authority? Do the good, and you will have praise from it;
Romans 13:4  for it is God’s servant to you for good. But if you do evil, be afraid; for it does not bear the sword without purpose. For it is God’s servant, an avenger who brings wrath on the one who practices evil.
Romans 13:5  Therefore it is necessary to submit, not only because of wrath, but also because of conscience.
Romans 13:6  For this reason you also pay taxes, for they are God’s ministers, devoted to this very task.
Romans 13:7  Pay everyone what is owed: tax to whom tax is due, duty to whom duty is due, fear to whom fear is due, honor to whom honor is due.
Romans 13:8  Owe no one anything except to love one another; for the one who loves the other has fulfilled law.
Romans 13:9  For “You shall not commit adultery,” “You shall not murder,” “You shall not steal,” “You shall not desire,” and if there is any other commandment, it is summed up in this word: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”
Romans 13:10  Love does no evil to the neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of law.
Romans 13:11  And do this knowing the time, that it is already the hour for you to rise from sleep; for now salvation is nearer to us than when we believed.
Romans 13:12  The night has advanced, and the day has drawn near. Therefore let us put away the works of darkness and put on the weapons of light.
Romans 13:13  Let us walk honorably as in daytime, not in revelries and drunkenness, not in sexual promiscuity and licentiousness, not in strife and jealousy;
Romans 13:14  but put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and do not make provision for the flesh to satisfy its desires.

Romans 14
Romans 14:1  Welcome the one who is weak in faith, but not to dispute over opinions.
Romans 14:2  One believes he may eat all things, but the weak person eats vegetables.
Romans 14:3  Do not let the one who eats despise the one who does not eat; and do not let the one who does not eat judge the one who eats, for God welcomed him.
Romans 14:4  Who are you to judge another’s household slave? To his own master he stands or falls; and he will be made to stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.
Romans 14:5  For one judges one day above another, but another judges every day alike. Let each be fully assured in his own mind.
Romans 14:6  The one who regards the day regards it for the Lord. And the one who eats eats for the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and the one who does not eat refrains for the Lord and gives thanks to God.
Romans 14:7  For none of us lives for himself, and none dies for himself;
Romans 14:8  for if we live, we live for the Lord, and if we die, we die for the Lord. So whether we live or die, we are the Lord’s.
Romans 14:9  For to this end Christ died and lived, so that He might be Lord of both the dead and the living.
Romans 14:10  But why do you judge your brother? Or you also, why do you despise your brother? For we will all stand before God’s judgment seat,
Romans 14:11  for it is written, “As I live, says the Lord, every knee will bend to Me, and every tongue will confess to God.”
Romans 14:12  So then, each of us will give an account of himself to God.
Romans 14:13  Therefore let us no longer judge one another; but judge this instead: not to place a stumbling block or a snare for a brother.
Romans 14:14  I know and am convinced in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself; except that to the one who reckons something unclean, to that person it is unclean.
Romans 14:15  For if your brother is grieved because of food, you no longer walk according to love. Do not destroy with your food the one for whom Christ died.
Romans 14:16  Therefore do not let your good be spoken of as evil.
Romans 14:17  For God’s kingdom is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit;
Romans 14:18  for the one who serves Christ in this is pleasing to God and approved by people.
Romans 14:19  So then, let us pursue what makes for peace and what builds up one another.
Romans 14:20  Do not tear down God’s work for the sake of food. All things indeed are clean, but it is evil for a person to eat in a way that causes stumbling.
Romans 14:21  It is good not to eat meat or drink wine or do anything by which your brother stumbles.
Romans 14:22  The faith you have, keep to yourself before God. Blessed is the one who does not judge himself in what he approves.
Romans 14:23  But the one who doubts, if he eats, has been condemned, because it is not from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.

Romans 15
Romans 15:1  And we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of those without strength, and not to please ourselves.
Romans 15:2  Let each of us please our neighbor for his good, to build him up.
Romans 15:3  For even Christ did not please Himself; but just as it is written, “The reproaches of those who reproach Thee fell upon Me.”
Romans 15:4  For whatever was written beforehand was written for our instruction, so that through perseverance and through the encouragement of the Scriptures we might have hope.
Romans 15:5  And may the God of perseverance and encouragement grant you to have the same mind among one another according to Christ Jesus,
Romans 15:6  so that with one accord and one mouth you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Romans 15:7  Therefore welcome one another, just as Christ also welcomed you, to God’s glory.
Romans 15:8  For I say that Christ has become a servant of the circumcision for God’s truth, to confirm the promises of the fathers,
Romans 15:9  and for the Gentiles to glorify God for mercy, just as it is written, “For this reason I will give thanks to Thee among the Gentiles, and sing praise to Thy name.”
Romans 15:10  And again it says, “Rejoice, Gentiles, with His people.”
Romans 15:11  And again, “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and let all the peoples praise Him.”
Romans 15:12  And again Isaiah says, “There will be the root of Jesse, and the One who rises to rule Gentiles; upon Him Gentiles will hope.”
Romans 15:13  And may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that you may abound in hope in the power of the Holy Spirit.
Romans 15:14  And I myself am convinced about you, my brothers, that you yourselves also are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish one another.
Romans 15:15  But I wrote more boldly to you on some points, to remind you again, because of the grace given me by God
Romans 15:16  to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles, performing priestly service with God’s gospel, so that the offering of the Gentiles may become acceptable, sanctified in the Holy Spirit.
Romans 15:17  Therefore I have reason to boast in Christ Jesus concerning the things of God;
Romans 15:18  for I will not dare to speak of anything that Christ did not work through me for the Gentiles’ obedience, in word and deed,
Romans 15:19  in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of the Spirit of God, so that from Jerusalem and around as far as Illyricum I have fulfilled the proclamation of Christ’s gospel,
Romans 15:20  and so making it my ambition to proclaim the gospel where Christ has not been named, so that I would not build on another’s foundation,
Romans 15:21  but just as it is written, “Those to whom nothing about Him was announced will see, and those who have not heard will understand.”
Romans 15:22  For this reason I was also often hindered from coming to you;
Romans 15:23  but now, no longer having a place in these regions, and having a longing for many years to come to you,
Romans 15:24  whenever I travel to Spain—for I hope to see you as I pass through, and to be sent onward there by you, if I may first be filled in some measure by your company—
Romans 15:25  but now I am traveling to Jerusalem, serving the saints.
Romans 15:26  For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.
Romans 15:27  For they were pleased, and they are their debtors; for if the Gentiles shared in their spiritual things, they also owe them service in material things.
Romans 15:28  Therefore, having completed this and sealed this fruit for them, I will depart by way of you for Spain.
Romans 15:29  And I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of Christ’s blessing.
Romans 15:30  And I urge you, brothers, through our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit, to struggle together with me in prayers to God for me,
Romans 15:31  so that I may be rescued from those who disobey in Judea, and my service for Jerusalem may become acceptable to the saints,
Romans 15:32  so that, coming to you in joy through God’s will, I may find rest together with you.
Romans 15:33  And may the God of peace be with you all. Amen.

Romans 16
Romans 16:1  And I commend to you Phoebe our sister, who is also a deacon of the Church in Cenchreae,
Romans 16:2  so that you may welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and stand by her in whatever matter she may need from you; for she herself has been a patron of many, and of me personally.
Romans 16:3  Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,
Romans 16:4  who risked their own neck for my life, to whom not only I give thanks, but also all the Churches of the Gentiles;
Romans 16:5  and greet the Church in their house. Greet Epaenetus my beloved, who is the firstfruits of Asia for Christ.
Romans 16:6  Greet Mary, who labored much for you.
Romans 16:7  Greet Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen and fellow prisoners, who are distinguished among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me.
Romans 16:8  Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.
Romans 16:9  Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and Stachys my beloved.
Romans 16:10  Greet Apelles, approved in Christ. Greet those of Aristobulus’s household.
Romans 16:11  Greet Herodion my kinsman. Greet those of Narcissus’s household who are in the Lord.
Romans 16:12  Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who labor in the Lord. Greet Persis the beloved, who labored much in the Lord.
Romans 16:13  Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.
Romans 16:14  Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.
Romans 16:15  Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas and all the saints with them.
Romans 16:16  Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the Churches of Christ greet you.
Romans 16:17  And I urge you, brothers, to watch those who cause divisions and snares contrary to the teaching you learned, and turn away from them;
Romans 16:18  for such people do not serve our Lord Christ, but their own belly, and through smooth speech and flattery they deceive the hearts of the unsuspecting.
Romans 16:19  For your obedience has reached everyone; therefore I rejoice over you, but I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil.
Romans 16:20  And the God of peace will crush Satan under your feet soon. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with you.
Romans 16:21  Timothy my fellow worker greets you, and Lucius and Jason and Sosipater, my kinsmen.
Romans 16:22  I, Tertius, who wrote the letter, greet you in the Lord.
Romans 16:23  Gaius, my host and host of the whole Church, greets you. Erastus the city steward greets you, and Quartus the brother.
Romans 16:24  [[The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.]]
[EDITORIAL NOTE: Supplemental doxology · Romans 16:25–27]
Romans 16:25  [Now to the One able to strengthen you according to my gospel and the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of a mystery kept silent through long ages,
