2 Corinthians 9:8  And God is able to make every grace abound toward you, so that, always having all sufficiency in everything, you may abound in every good work.
2 Corinthians 9:9  As it is written, “He scattered abroad; he gave to the poor; his righteousness remains for the age.”
2 Corinthians 9:10  Now the One who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed and increase the fruits of your righteousness.
2 Corinthians 9:11  You are being enriched in everything for all generosity, which produces thanksgiving to God through us,
2 Corinthians 9:12  because the ministry of this service not only supplies what the saints lack but also overflows through many thanksgivings to God.
2 Corinthians 9:13  Because of the proof this ministry provides, they glorify God for your submission to the good news of Christ that you confess, and for your generous sharing with them and with all,
2 Corinthians 9:14  while they too, in prayer on your behalf, long for you because of the surpassing grace of God upon you.
2 Corinthians 9:15  Thanks be to God for His indescribable gift!

2 Corinthians 10
2 Corinthians 10:1  Now I myself, Paul, appeal to you through the meekness and gentleness of Christ—I who am lowly among you face to face, but bold toward you when absent.
2 Corinthians 10:2  And I beg that, when I am present, I may not have to show the bold confidence with which I intend to confront some who think we walk according to the flesh.
2 Corinthians 10:3  For though we walk in flesh, we do not wage war according to flesh,
2 Corinthians 10:4  for the weapons of our warfare are not fleshly, but powerful through God for the pulling down of strongholds. We pull down arguments
2 Corinthians 10:5  and every lofty thing raised against the knowledge of God, and take captive every thought into obedience to Christ,
2 Corinthians 10:6  and stand ready to punish every disobedience when your obedience is complete.
2 Corinthians 10:7  Look at what is right before you. If anyone is confident in himself that he belongs to Christ, let him consider this again for himself: just as he belongs to Christ, so also do we.
2 Corinthians 10:8  For even if I boast somewhat more abundantly concerning our authority, which the Lord gave for building you up and not for pulling you down, I will not be put to shame.
2 Corinthians 10:9  I do not want to seem as though I would terrify you through the letters.
2 Corinthians 10:10  For someone says, “The letters are weighty and strong, but his bodily presence is weak and his speech is despised.”
2 Corinthians 10:11  Let such a person consider this: what we are in word through letters when absent, such we are also in deed when present.
2 Corinthians 10:12  For we do not dare to class or compare ourselves with some of those who commend themselves. But they, measuring themselves by themselves and comparing themselves with themselves, do not understand.
2 Corinthians 10:13  But we will not boast beyond measure, but according to the measure of the sphere that God apportioned to us, a measure reaching even as far as you.
2 Corinthians 10:14  For we are not overextending ourselves as though we did not reach you, for we came even as far as you in the good news of Christ.
2 Corinthians 10:15  We do not boast beyond measure in others’ labors, but have hope that, as your faith grows, we may be greatly enlarged among you according to our sphere,
2 Corinthians 10:16  so as to proclaim the good news in the regions beyond you, not to boast in another’s sphere over things already prepared.
2 Corinthians 10:17  But let the one who boasts boast in the Lord.
2 Corinthians 10:18  For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.

2 Corinthians 11
2 Corinthians 11:1  I wish you would bear with me in a little foolishness. Indeed, do bear with me.
2 Corinthians 11:2  For I am jealous for you with God’s jealousy, for I betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ.
2 Corinthians 11:3  But I fear lest somehow, as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, your minds might be corrupted and drawn away from the simplicity and purity toward Christ.
2 Corinthians 11:4  For if the one who comes proclaims another Jesus whom we did not proclaim, or you receive a different spirit that you did not receive, or a different good news that you did not accept, you bear with it well!
2 Corinthians 11:5  For I reckon that I have fallen short in nothing of the exceedingly great apostles.
2 Corinthians 11:6  Even if I am untrained in speech, I am not in knowledge; but in every way we have made it clear to you in all things.
2 Corinthians 11:7  Or did I commit a sin by humbling myself so that you might be exalted, because I proclaimed God’s good news to you free of charge?
2 Corinthians 11:8  I plundered other Churches, taking wages for the ministry to you.
2 Corinthians 11:9  And when I was present with you and in need, I burdened no one, for the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied what I lacked. And in everything I kept myself from being a burden to you, and will keep myself so.
2 Corinthians 11:10  The truth of Christ is in me: this boasting will not be silenced in me in the regions of Achaia.
2 Corinthians 11:11  Why? Because I do not love you? God knows.
2 Corinthians 11:12  But what I do I will also continue to do, so that I may cut off the opportunity of those who desire an opportunity, so that in what they boast they may be found just as we are.
2 Corinthians 11:13  For such people are false apostles, deceitful workers, disguising themselves as apostles of Christ.
2 Corinthians 11:14  And no wonder, for Satan himself disguises himself as an angel of light.
2 Corinthians 11:15  Therefore it is no surprise if his ministers also disguise themselves as ministers of righteousness; their end will be according to their works.
2 Corinthians 11:16  Again I say, let no one think me foolish. But if you do, receive me even as a fool, so that I too may boast a little.
2 Corinthians 11:17  What I speak, I speak not according to the Lord, but as in foolishness, in this confident boasting.
2 Corinthians 11:18  Since many boast according to the flesh, I too will boast.
2 Corinthians 11:19  For you gladly bear with fools, being wise yourselves!
2 Corinthians 11:20  For you bear with it if someone enslaves you, if someone devours you, if someone takes from you, if someone exalts himself, if someone strikes you in the face.
2 Corinthians 11:21  I say this to my shame: as though we had been weak! But in whatever anyone dares—I speak in foolishness—I also dare.
2 Corinthians 11:22  Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they Abraham’s offspring? So am I.
2 Corinthians 11:23  Are they ministers of Christ? I speak as one out of his mind: I am more so—in more labors, in more imprisonments, in beatings beyond measure, often facing death.
2 Corinthians 11:24  From Jews five times I received forty lashes less one.
2 Corinthians 11:25  Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked; I have spent a night and a day in the deep.
2 Corinthians 11:26  On frequent journeys, in dangers of rivers, dangers of robbers, dangers from my own people, dangers from Gentiles, dangers in a city, dangers in a wilderness, dangers at sea, dangers among false brothers;
2 Corinthians 11:27  in labor and toil, in sleepless nights often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.
2 Corinthians 11:28  Apart from outward things, there is the pressure on me day by day, my concern for all the Churches.
2 Corinthians 11:29  Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is made to stumble, and I do not burn?
2 Corinthians 11:30  If I must boast, I will boast of the things of my weakness.
2 Corinthians 11:31  The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is blessed for the ages, knows that I am not lying.
2 Corinthians 11:32  In Damascus the ethnarch under King Aretas was guarding the city of the Damascenes to seize me,
2 Corinthians 11:33  and through a window I was lowered in a basket through the wall, and escaped his hands.

2 Corinthians 12
2 Corinthians 12:1  I must boast. It is not beneficial, but I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.
2 Corinthians 12:2  I know a man in Christ. Fourteen years ago—whether in the body I do not know, or outside the body I do not know; God knows—such a one was caught up as far as the third heaven.
2 Corinthians 12:3  And I know such a man—whether in the body or apart from the body I do not know; God knows—
2 Corinthians 12:4  that he was caught up into Paradise and heard inexpressible words, which a human being is not permitted to speak.
2 Corinthians 12:5  On behalf of such a one I will boast, but on my own behalf I will not boast except in weaknesses.
2 Corinthians 12:6  For if I should desire to boast, I will not be a fool, for I will speak truth. But I refrain, lest anyone think more of me than what he sees me to be or anything he hears from me warrants.
2 Corinthians 12:7  And because of the surpassing revelations, therefore, so that I might not be exalted, a thorn was given me in the flesh, a messenger of Satan, to strike me, so that I might not be exalted.
2 Corinthians 12:8  Concerning this I appealed to the Lord three times, that it might depart from me.
2 Corinthians 12:9  And He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made complete in weakness.” Therefore I will most gladly boast rather in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may pitch its tent over me.
2 Corinthians 12:10  Therefore I am content in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions and distresses, for Christ’s sake; for whenever I am weak, then I am strong.
2 Corinthians 12:11  I have become a fool; you compelled me. For I ought to have been commended by you, for I fell short in nothing of the exceedingly great apostles, even if I am nothing.
2 Corinthians 12:12  Indeed, the signs of the apostle were worked among you in all endurance, with signs and wonders and acts of power.
2 Corinthians 12:13  For in what were you treated as inferior to the other Churches, except that I myself did not burden you? Forgive me this wrong.
2 Corinthians 12:14  Look, for the third time I am ready to come to you, and I will not be a burden. For I seek not what is yours but you; for the children ought not to store up for the parents, but the parents for the children.
2 Corinthians 12:15  And I will most gladly spend and be spent for your souls. If I love you more abundantly, am I loved less?
2 Corinthians 12:16  But let it be so: I did not burden you. Yet, being crafty, I caught you by deceit!
2 Corinthians 12:17  Did I take advantage of you through anyone whom I sent to you?
2 Corinthians 12:18  I urged Titus, and sent the brother with him. Did Titus take advantage of you? Did we not walk in the same spirit? In the same footsteps?
2 Corinthians 12:19  Have you been thinking all this time that we are defending ourselves to you? We speak before God in Christ. And all things, beloved, are for your building up.
2 Corinthians 12:20  For I fear lest somehow, when I come, I may find you not as I wish, and I may be found by you not as you wish; lest there be strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, selfish ambitions, slanders, whisperings, inflations of pride, disorders;
2 Corinthians 12:21  lest, when I come again, my God may humble me before you, and I may mourn many of those who sinned before and did not repent of the impurity and sexual immorality and licentiousness they practiced.

2 Corinthians 13
2 Corinthians 13:1  This is the third time I am coming to you. “By the mouth of two witnesses and three every matter will be established.”
2 Corinthians 13:2  I have warned those who sinned before and all the rest, and I warn them now while absent, as I did when present the second time: if I come again, I will not spare,
2 Corinthians 13:3  since you seek proof of Christ speaking in me. He is not weak toward you, but is powerful among you.
2 Corinthians 13:4  For indeed He was crucified in weakness, but lives by the power of God. For we too are weak in Him, but will live with Him by the power of God toward you.
2 Corinthians 13:5  Test yourselves to see whether you are in the faith; examine yourselves. Or do you not recognize this about yourselves—that Jesus Christ is in you? Unless indeed you fail the test.
2 Corinthians 13:6  But I hope you will know that we do not fail the test.
2 Corinthians 13:7  And we pray to God that you may do nothing evil, not that we may appear to pass the test, but that you may do what is honorable, even if we seem to fail it.
2 Corinthians 13:8  For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth.
2 Corinthians 13:9  For we rejoice whenever we are weak but you are strong; this we also pray for: your restoration.
2 Corinthians 13:10  For this reason I write these things while absent, so that when present I may not act sharply according to the authority the Lord gave me, for building up and not for pulling down.
2 Corinthians 13:11  Finally, brothers, rejoice, be restored, be encouraged, be of the same mind, be at peace; and the God of love and peace will be with you.
2 Corinthians 13:12  Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the saints greet you.
2 Corinthians 13:13  The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.

GALATIANS

Galatians 1
Galatians 1:1  Paul, an apostle, not from human beings nor through a human being, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Him from the dead,
Galatians 1:2  and all the brothers with me, to the Churches of Galatia:
Galatians 1:3  grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ,
Galatians 1:4  who gave Himself for our sins, to rescue us from the present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father,
Galatians 1:5  to whom be the glory for the ages of ages. Amen.
Galatians 1:6  I am astonished that you are so quickly deserting the One who called you in the grace of Christ for a different gospel,
Galatians 1:7  which is not another gospel, except that there are some who trouble you and want to distort the gospel of Christ.
Galatians 1:8  But even if we or an angel from heaven should proclaim to you a gospel contrary to what we proclaimed to you, let him be accursed.
Galatians 1:9  As we have said before, so now I say again: if anyone proclaims to you a gospel contrary to what you received, let him be accursed.
Galatians 1:10  For am I now seeking the approval of human beings, or of God? Or am I seeking to please human beings? If I were still pleasing human beings, I would not be Christ’s slave.
Galatians 1:11  For I make known to you, brothers, that the gospel proclaimed by me is not of human origin.
Galatians 1:12  For I neither received it from a human being nor was taught it, but received it through a revelation of Jesus Christ.
Galatians 1:13  For you have heard of my former conduct in Judaism, how I persecuted the Church of God beyond measure and ravaged it,
Galatians 1:14  and I advanced in Judaism beyond many of my own age among my people, being far more zealous for the traditions of my ancestors.
Galatians 1:15  But when God, who set me apart from my mother’s womb and called me through His grace, was pleased
Galatians 1:16  to reveal His Son in me, so that I might proclaim Him among the nations, I did not immediately consult flesh and blood,
Galatians 1:17  nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me, but I went away to Arabia and returned again to Damascus.
Galatians 1:18  Then, after three years, I went up to Jerusalem to become acquainted with Cephas, and I stayed with him fifteen days.
Galatians 1:19  But I saw none of the other apostles except James, the Lord’s brother.
Galatians 1:20  Now in what I am writing to you, behold, before God, I am not lying.
Galatians 1:21  Then I went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
Galatians 1:22  But I was unknown by sight to the Churches of Judea that are in Christ.
Galatians 1:23  They only kept hearing, “The one who once persecuted us now proclaims the faith he once ravaged.”
Galatians 1:24  And they glorified God because of me.

Galatians 2
Galatians 2:1  Then, after fourteen years, I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus along as well.
Galatians 2:2  I went up in accordance with a revelation, and I set before them the gospel I proclaim among the nations, privately before those held in esteem, lest somehow I was running, or had run, in vain.
Galatians 2:3  But not even Titus, who was with me, was compelled to be circumcised, though he was a Greek.
Galatians 2:4  Yet because of the false brothers secretly brought in, who slipped in to spy out our freedom which we have in Christ Jesus, so that they might enslave us—
Galatians 2:5  we did not yield to them in submission even for an hour, so that the truth of the gospel might remain with you.
Galatians 2:6  But as for those held to be something—whatever they once were makes no difference to me; God does not favor a person’s outward standing—those held in esteem added nothing to me.
Galatians 2:7  On the contrary, seeing that I had been entrusted with the gospel for the uncircumcised, just as Peter with that for the circumcised,
Galatians 2:8  for the One who worked through Peter for an apostleship to the circumcised worked also through me for the nations,
Galatians 2:9  and recognizing the grace given to me, James and Cephas and John, who were regarded as pillars, gave me and Barnabas their right hands in fellowship, so that we should go to the nations and they to the circumcised.
Galatians 2:10  Only we were to remember the poor, the very thing I was also eager to do.
Galatians 2:11  But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face, because he stood condemned.
Galatians 2:12  For before certain people came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles. But when they came, he began drawing back and separating himself, fearing those of the circumcision.
Galatians 2:13  And the other Jews also joined him in hypocrisy, so that even Barnabas was carried away by their hypocrisy.
Galatians 2:14  But when I saw that they were not walking straight in line with the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas before them all, “If you, though a Jew, live like the Gentiles and not like the Jews, how can you compel the Gentiles to live as Jews?
Galatians 2:15  “We are Jews by birth and not sinners from the Gentiles,
Galatians 2:16  yet knowing that a human being is not justified by works of law but through faith in Jesus Christ, we too believed in Christ Jesus, so that we might be justified by faith in Christ and not by works of law, because by works of law no flesh will be justified.
Galatians 2:17  But if, in seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves were also found to be sinners, is Christ then a servant of sin? May it never be!
Galatians 2:18  For if I rebuild the things I tore down, I show myself to be a transgressor.
Galatians 2:19  For through law I died to law, so that I might live to God. I have been crucified with Christ.
Galatians 2:20  And I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself for me.
Galatians 2:21  I do not set aside the grace of God. For if righteousness comes through law, then Christ died for nothing.”

Galatians 3
Galatians 3:1  O foolish Galatians, who bewitched you, before whose eyes Jesus Christ was publicly portrayed as crucified?
Galatians 3:2  This alone I want to learn from you: did you receive the Spirit by works of law or by hearing with faith?
Galatians 3:3  Are you so foolish? Having begun by the Spirit, are you now being brought to completion by the flesh?
Galatians 3:4  Did you suffer so much in vain—if indeed it was in vain?
Galatians 3:5  So then, does the One who supplies you with the Spirit and performs acts of power among you do so by works of law or by hearing with faith?
Galatians 3:6  Just as Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.
Galatians 3:7  Know, then, that those who are of faith are the sons of Abraham.
Galatians 3:8  And Scripture, foreseeing that God justifies the nations by faith, proclaimed the gospel beforehand to Abraham: “In you all the nations will be blessed.”
Galatians 3:9  So then, those who are of faith are blessed with believing Abraham.
Galatians 3:10  For all who are of works of law are under a curse, for it is written, “Accursed is everyone who does not abide by all the things written in the book of the law, to do them.”
Galatians 3:11  Now it is clear that no one is justified before God by law, because “The righteous one will live by faith.”
Galatians 3:12  But the law is not of faith; rather, “The one who does these things will live by them.”
Galatians 3:13  Christ bought us free from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us, because it is written, “Accursed is everyone who hangs upon a tree,”
Galatians 3:14  so that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the nations, so that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.
Galatians 3:15  Brothers, I speak in human terms: even when a human covenant has been ratified, no one sets it aside or adds provisions to it.
Galatians 3:16  Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. It does not say, “And to seeds,” as concerning many, but as concerning one, “And to your seed,” who is Christ.
Galatians 3:17  What I mean is this: the law, which came four hundred and thirty years later, does not invalidate a covenant previously ratified by God, so as to nullify the promise.
Galatians 3:18  For if the inheritance is from law, it is no longer from promise. But God has graciously given it to Abraham through promise.
Galatians 3:19  Why, then, the law? It was added because of transgressions, until the seed should come to whom the promise had been made, and it was ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator.
Galatians 3:20  Now a mediator is not for one alone, but God is one.
Galatians 3:21  Is the law, then, against the promises of God? May it never be! For if a law had been given that could give life, righteousness really would have come from law.
Galatians 3:22  But Scripture confined everything under sin, so that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.
Galatians 3:23  Now before faith came, we were guarded under law, confined until the faith that was to be revealed.
Galatians 3:24  So the law became our guardian until Christ, so that we might be justified by faith.
Galatians 3:25  But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian.
Galatians 3:26  For you are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
Galatians 3:27  For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
Galatians 3:28  There is neither Jew nor Greek; there is neither slave nor free; there is no male and female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
Galatians 3:29  And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham’s seed, heirs according to promise.

Galatians 4
Galatians 4:1  Now I say that as long as the heir is a child, he differs in no way from a slave, though he is master of everything.
Galatians 4:2  Rather, he is under guardians and stewards until the date appointed by his father.
Galatians 4:3  So also we, when we were children, were enslaved under the elements of the world.
Galatians 4:4  But when the fullness of time came, God sent forth His Son, born of a woman, born under law,
Galatians 4:5  to redeem those under law, that we might receive adoption as sons.
Galatians 4:6  And because you are sons, God sent forth the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying, “Abba, Father!”
Galatians 4:7  So you are no longer a slave but a son; and if a son, then also an heir through God.
Galatians 4:8  But at that time, not knowing God, you were enslaved to those that by nature are not gods.
Galatians 4:9  Now, however, having come to know God—or rather, having been known by God—how do you turn back again to the weak and impoverished elements, to which you want to be enslaved all over again?
Galatians 4:10  You carefully observe days and months and seasons and years.
Galatians 4:11  I fear for you, lest somehow I have labored over you in vain.
Galatians 4:12  Become as I am, because I too became as you are, brothers; I beg you. You did me no wrong.
Galatians 4:13  And you know that it was because of a weakness of the flesh that I first proclaimed the gospel to you.
Galatians 4:14  And though my flesh was a trial for you, you did not despise or reject me, but you welcomed me as an angel of God, as Christ Jesus.
Galatians 4:15  Where, then, is your sense of blessedness? For I testify to you that, if possible, you would have dug out your eyes and given them to me.
Galatians 4:16  So have I become your enemy by telling you the truth?
Galatians 4:17  They are zealous for you, but not for good; they want to shut you out, so that you may be zealous for them.
Galatians 4:18  But it is good to be sought zealously for a good purpose at all times, and not only when I am present with you,
Galatians 4:19  my children, for whom I am again in labor until Christ is formed in you.
Galatians 4:20  I wish I could be present with you now and change my tone, because I am perplexed about you.
Galatians 4:21  Tell me, you who want to be under law, do you not listen to the law?
Galatians 4:22  For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the slave woman and one by the free woman.
Galatians 4:23  But the one by the slave woman was born according to the flesh, and the one by the free woman through promise.
Galatians 4:24  These things are being interpreted allegorically, for these women are two covenants: one from Mount Sinai, bearing children into slavery, which is Hagar.
Galatians 4:25  Now Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia, and corresponds to the present Jerusalem, for she is enslaved with her children.
Galatians 4:26  But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother.
Galatians 4:27  For it is written, “Rejoice, barren woman who does not bear; break out and cry aloud, you who are not in labor, because the children of the deserted woman are more numerous than those of the woman who has a husband.”
Galatians 4:28  Now you, brothers, are children of promise, like Isaac.
Galatians 4:29  But just as then the one born according to the flesh persecuted the one born according to the Spirit, so it is also now.
Galatians 4:30  But what does Scripture say? “Cast out the slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave woman shall certainly not inherit with the son of the free woman.”
Galatians 4:31  Therefore, brothers, we are not children of a slave woman but of the free woman.

Galatians 5
Galatians 5:1  For freedom Christ set us free. Stand firm, therefore, and do not be held again under a yoke of slavery.
Galatians 5:2  Look, I, Paul, tell you that if you receive circumcision, Christ will be of no benefit to you.
Galatians 5:3  And I testify again to every man who receives circumcision that he is obligated to do the whole law.
Galatians 5:4  You who seek to be justified by law have been severed from Christ; you have fallen from grace.
Galatians 5:5  For we, by the Spirit, through faith, eagerly await the hope of righteousness.
Galatians 5:6  For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any strength, but faith working through love.
Galatians 5:7  You were running well. Who hindered you from obeying the truth?
Galatians 5:8  This persuasion is not from the One who calls you.
Galatians 5:9  A little leaven leavens the whole batch of dough.
Galatians 5:10  I am confident about you in the Lord that you will think nothing else. But the one troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be.
Galatians 5:11  But I, brothers, if I still proclaim circumcision, why am I still persecuted? Then the stumbling block of the cross has been abolished.
Galatians 5:12  I wish those who unsettle you would even castrate themselves!
Galatians 5:13  For you were called to freedom, brothers. Only do not make freedom a base of operations for the flesh, but through love serve one another as slaves.
Galatians 5:14  For the whole law is fulfilled in one saying: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”
Galatians 5:15  But if you bite and devour one another, watch out that you are not consumed by one another.
Galatians 5:16  But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will certainly not fulfill the desire of the flesh.
Galatians 5:17  For the flesh desires what is against the Spirit, and the Spirit what is against the flesh; for these oppose one another, so that you do not do the things you want.
Galatians 5:18  But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under law.
Galatians 5:19  Now the works of the flesh are evident: sexual immorality, impurity, licentiousness,
Galatians 5:20  idolatry, sorcery, hostilities, strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, selfish ambitions, divisions, factions,
Galatians 5:21  envies, drunkenness, revelries, and things like these. I tell you beforehand, just as I told you before, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
Galatians 5:22  But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
Galatians 5:23  gentleness, self-control. Against such things there is no law.
Galatians 5:24  And those who belong to Christ Jesus crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.
Galatians 5:25  If we live by the Spirit, let us also keep in step with the Spirit.
Galatians 5:26  Let us not become conceited, provoking one another, envying one another.

Galatians 6
Galatians 6:1  Brothers, even if a person is overtaken in some transgression, you who are spiritual are to restore such a person in a spirit of gentleness, watching yourself, lest you too be tempted.
Galatians 6:2  Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
Galatians 6:3  For if anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.
Galatians 6:4  But let each test his own work, and then he will have his reason for boasting in relation to himself alone, and not in relation to someone else.
Galatians 6:5  For each will carry his own load.
Galatians 6:6  Let the one instructed in the word share all good things with the one who instructs.
Galatians 6:7  Do not be deceived; God is not mocked. For whatever a person sows, that he will also reap.
Galatians 6:8  For the one who sows into his own flesh will reap corruption from the flesh, but the one who sows into the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
Galatians 6:9  And let us not grow weary in doing good, for in the proper season we will reap, if we do not give up.
Galatians 6:10  So then, as we have opportunity, let us do good to everyone, especially to those of the household of faith.
Galatians 6:11  See with what large letters I have written to you in my own hand.
Galatians 6:12  All who want to make a good outward show in the flesh compel you to receive circumcision, only so that they may not be persecuted for the cross of Christ.
Galatians 6:13  For even those who receive circumcision do not themselves keep the law, but they want you to receive circumcision so that they may boast in your flesh.
Galatians 6:14  But may I never boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
Galatians 6:15  For neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything, but a new creation does.
Galatians 6:16  And as many as will keep in step with this rule, peace and mercy be upon them, and upon the Israel of God.
Galatians 6:17  From now on, let no one cause me trouble, for I carry the marks of Jesus in my body.
Galatians 6:18  The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.

EPHESIANS

Ephesians 1
Ephesians 1:1  Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, to the saints who are [in Ephesus] and faithful in Christ Jesus:
Ephesians 1:2  grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Ephesians 1:3  Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ,
Ephesians 1:4  just as He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world, so that we should be holy and without blemish before Him in love,
Ephesians 1:5  having predestined us for adoption as sons through Jesus Christ to Himself, according to the good pleasure of His will,
Ephesians 1:6  to the praise of the glory of His grace, with which He favored us in the Beloved.
Ephesians 1:7  In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of transgressions, according to the riches of His grace,
Ephesians 1:8  which He lavished on us in all wisdom and understanding,
Ephesians 1:9  having made known to us the mystery of His will, according to His good pleasure which He purposed in Him,
Ephesians 1:10  for an administration of the fullness of the times, to sum up all things in Christ, the things in the heavens and the things on the earth, in Him.
Ephesians 1:11  In Him we were also allotted an inheritance, having been predestined according to the purpose of the One who works all things according to the counsel of His will,
Ephesians 1:12  so that we who had hoped beforehand in Christ should be to the praise of His glory.
Ephesians 1:13  In Him you also, having heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, and having believed in Him, were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit,
Ephesians 1:14  who is the pledge of our inheritance, toward the redemption of the possession, to the praise of His glory.
Ephesians 1:15  For this reason I too, having heard of your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love toward all the saints,
Ephesians 1:16  do not cease giving thanks for you, remembering you in my prayers,
Ephesians 1:17  so that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give you a spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of Him,
Ephesians 1:18  with the eyes of your heart enlightened, so that you may know what is the hope of His calling, what are the riches of the glory of His inheritance among the saints,
Ephesians 1:19  and what is the surpassing greatness of His power toward us who believe, according to the working of the might of His strength,
Ephesians 1:20  which He exercised in Christ when He raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand in the heavenly places,
Ephesians 1:21  far above every rule and authority and power and dominion and every name that is named, not only in this age but also in the one to come.
Ephesians 1:22  And He subjected all things under His feet and gave Him as head over all things to the Church,
Ephesians 1:23  which is His body, the fullness of the One who fills all things in all.

Ephesians 2
Ephesians 2:1  And you were dead in your transgressions and sins,
Ephesians 2:2  in which you once walked according to the age of this world, according to the ruler of the authority of the air, of the spirit now working in the sons of disobedience—
Ephesians 2:3  among whom we too all once lived in the desires of our flesh, carrying out the wishes of the flesh and of our thoughts, and we were by nature children of wrath, like the rest.
Ephesians 2:4  But God, being rich in mercy, because of His great love with which He loved us,
Ephesians 2:5  even when we were dead in transgressions, made us alive together with Christ—by grace you have been saved—
Ephesians 2:6  and raised us together and seated us together in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus,
Ephesians 2:7  so that in the ages to come He might show the surpassing riches of His grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus.
Ephesians 2:8  For by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not from yourselves; it is the gift of God,
Ephesians 2:9  not from works, so that no one may boast.
Ephesians 2:10  For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand, so that we should walk in them.
Ephesians 2:11  Therefore remember that once you, the Gentiles in the flesh, called “uncircumcision” by what is called “circumcision,” made by hands in the flesh—
Ephesians 2:12  that at that time you were without Christ, alienated from the commonwealth of Israel and strangers to the covenants of the promise, having no hope and without God in the world.
Ephesians 2:13  But now in Christ Jesus, you who once were far away have become near by the blood of Christ.
Ephesians 2:14  For He Himself is our peace, who made both one and broke down the dividing wall of the barrier, the hostility, in His flesh,
Ephesians 2:15  having abolished the law of commandments in decrees, so that He might create in Him one new human being out of the two, making peace,
Ephesians 2:16  and might reconcile both in one body to God through the cross, having killed the hostility by it.
Ephesians 2:17  And He came and proclaimed peace to you who were far away, and peace to those who were near,
Ephesians 2:18  because through Him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father.
Ephesians 2:19  So then you are no longer strangers and resident foreigners, but you are fellow citizens with the saints and members of God’s household,
Ephesians 2:20  having been built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus Himself being the cornerstone,
Ephesians 2:21  in whom the whole building, fitted together, grows into a holy sanctuary in the Lord,
Ephesians 2:22  in whom you also are being built together into a dwelling place of God in the Spirit.

Ephesians 3
Ephesians 3:1  For this reason I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus for you Gentiles—
Ephesians 3:2  if indeed you have heard of the stewardship of God’s grace that was given to me for you,
Ephesians 3:3  that the mystery was made known to me by revelation, as I wrote briefly before.
Ephesians 3:4  By reading this you can perceive my understanding of the mystery of Christ,
Ephesians 3:5  which in other generations was not made known to the sons of human beings as it has now been revealed to His holy apostles and prophets in the Spirit:
Ephesians 3:6  that the Gentiles are fellow heirs and fellow members of the body and fellow sharers of the promise in Christ Jesus through the gospel,
Ephesians 3:7  of which I became a servant according to the gift of God’s grace given to me according to the working of His power.
Ephesians 3:8  To me, the very least of all saints, this grace was given: to proclaim to the nations the untraceable riches of Christ,
Ephesians 3:9  and to enlighten everyone about the administration of the mystery hidden from the ages in God, who created all things,
Ephesians 3:10  so that now, through the Church, the richly varied wisdom of God might be made known to the rulers and authorities in the heavenly places,
Ephesians 3:11  according to the purpose of the ages which He accomplished in Christ Jesus our Lord,
Ephesians 3:12  in whom we have boldness and access with confidence through faith in Him.
Ephesians 3:13  Therefore I ask you not to lose heart at my afflictions for you, which are your glory.
Ephesians 3:14  For this reason I bend my knees before the Father,
Ephesians 3:15  from whom every family in the heavens and on earth is named,
Ephesians 3:16  so that according to the riches of His glory He may grant you to be strengthened with power through His Spirit in the inner person,
Ephesians 3:17  so that Christ may dwell through faith in your hearts, being rooted and founded in love,
Ephesians 3:18  so that with all the saints you may have strength to grasp what is the breadth and length and height and depth,
Ephesians 3:19  and to know the love of Christ which surpasses knowledge, so that you may be filled to all the fullness of God.
Ephesians 3:20  Now to the One who is able to do far more abundantly than all we ask or think, according to the power working in us,
Ephesians 3:21  to Him be glory in the Church and in Christ Jesus for all generations of the age of ages. Amen.

Ephesians 4
Ephesians 4:1  Therefore I, the prisoner in the Lord, urge you to walk worthily of the calling with which you were called,
Ephesians 4:2  with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love,
Ephesians 4:3  making every effort to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace:
Ephesians 4:4  one body and one Spirit, just as you were also called in one hope of your calling;
Ephesians 4:5  one Lord, one faith, one baptism;
Ephesians 4:6  one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all.
Ephesians 4:7  But grace was given to each one of us according to the measure of Christ’s gift.
Ephesians 4:8  Therefore it says, “Having ascended on high, He took captivity captive; He gave gifts to human beings.”
Ephesians 4:9  Now what does “He ascended” mean, except that He also descended into the lower parts of the earth?
Ephesians 4:10  The One who descended is also the One who ascended far above all the heavens, so that He might fill all things.
Ephesians 4:11  And He Himself gave some as apostles, some as prophets, some as evangelists, and some as shepherds and teachers,
Ephesians 4:12  for the equipping of the saints for the work of service, for building up the body of Christ,
Ephesians 4:13  until we all attain to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a mature man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ,
Ephesians 4:14  so that we may no longer be children, tossed by waves and carried about by every wind of teaching, by human trickery, by cunning in deceitful schemes,
Ephesians 4:15  but, being truthful in love, we may grow in all things into Him who is the head, Christ,
Ephesians 4:16  from whom the whole body, fitted and held together through every supporting joint, as each individual part works in its proper measure, produces the growth of the body for building itself up in love.
Ephesians 4:17  So I say this and testify in the Lord: you must no longer walk as the Gentiles also walk, in the futility of their mind,
Ephesians 4:18  being darkened in understanding, alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance in them, because of the hardness of their heart.
Ephesians 4:19  Having become unfeeling, they handed themselves over to licentiousness for the practice of every impurity in greed.
Ephesians 4:20  But you did not learn Christ in this way,
Ephesians 4:21  if indeed you heard Him and were taught in Him, as truth is in Jesus:
Ephesians 4:22  that, concerning your former conduct, you put off the old human being, which is being corrupted according to deceitful desires,
Ephesians 4:23  and be renewed in the spirit of your mind,
Ephesians 4:24  and put on the new human being, created according to God in righteousness and holiness of truth.
Ephesians 4:25  Therefore, putting away falsehood, let each speak truth with his neighbor, because we are members of one another.
Ephesians 4:26  Be angry and do not sin. Do not let the sun go down upon your anger,
Ephesians 4:27  nor give a place to the devil.
Ephesians 4:28  Let the one who steals steal no longer, but rather let him labor, doing what is good with his own hands, so that he may have something to share with the one in need.
Ephesians 4:29  Let no rotten word come out of your mouth, but only what is good for building up as needed, so that it may give grace to those who hear.
Ephesians 4:30  And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
Ephesians 4:31  Let all bitterness and rage and anger and shouting and slander be taken away from you, with all malice.
Ephesians 4:32  But be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, just as God in Christ forgave you.

Ephesians 5
Ephesians 5:1  Therefore become imitators of God, as beloved children,
Ephesians 5:2  and walk in love, just as Christ also loved us and gave Himself for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God for a fragrant aroma.
Ephesians 5:3  But sexual immorality and every impurity or greed must not even be named among you, as is fitting for saints,
Ephesians 5:4  nor shamefulness and foolish talk or coarse joking, which are unfitting, but rather thanksgiving.
Ephesians 5:5  For know this with certainty: no sexually immoral or impure or greedy person, that is, an idolater, has an inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God.
Ephesians 5:6  Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of these things the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience.
Ephesians 5:7  Therefore do not become their fellow sharers.
Ephesians 5:8  For you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Walk as children of light,
Ephesians 5:9  for the fruit of the light is in all goodness and righteousness and truth,
Ephesians 5:10  testing what is pleasing to the Lord.
Ephesians 5:11  And do not share in the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather expose them,
Ephesians 5:12  for it is shameful even to speak of the things done by them in secret.
Ephesians 5:13  But all things, when exposed by the light, become visible,
Ephesians 5:14  for everything that becomes visible is light. Therefore it says, “Awake, you who sleep, and arise from the dead, and Christ will shine upon you.”
Ephesians 5:15  So watch carefully how you walk, not as unwise but as wise,
Ephesians 5:16  buying up the opportunity, because the days are evil.
Ephesians 5:17  For this reason do not become foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is.
Ephesians 5:18  And do not become drunk with wine, in which there is reckless excess, but be filled in the Spirit,
Ephesians 5:19  speaking to one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord,
Ephesians 5:20  always giving thanks for all things in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ to God the Father,
Ephesians 5:21  submitting to one another in the fear of Christ:
Ephesians 5:22  wives, to your own husbands as to the Lord,
Ephesians 5:23  because a husband is head of the wife as Christ also is head of the Church, He Himself being Savior of the body.
Ephesians 5:24  But as the Church submits to Christ, so also wives to their husbands in everything.
Ephesians 5:25  Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the Church and gave Himself for her,
Ephesians 5:26  so that He might sanctify her, having cleansed her by the washing of water with a word,
Ephesians 5:27  so that He Himself might present the Church to Himself glorious, having no spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but so that she should be holy and without blemish.
Ephesians 5:28  In this way husbands also ought to love their own wives as their own bodies. The one who loves his own wife loves himself.
Ephesians 5:29  For no one ever hated his own flesh, but nourishes and cherishes it, just as Christ also does the Church,
Ephesians 5:30  because we are members of His body.
Ephesians 5:31  “For this reason a man will leave father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh.”
Ephesians 5:32  This mystery is great, but I am speaking with reference to Christ and the Church.
Ephesians 5:33  Nevertheless, let each one of you also love his own wife as himself, and let the wife respect her husband.

Ephesians 6
Ephesians 6:1  Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right.
Ephesians 6:2  “Honor your father and mother”—which is the first commandment with a promise—
Ephesians 6:3  “so that it may be well with you and you may live long upon the earth.”
Ephesians 6:4  And fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, but nourish them in the discipline and admonition of the Lord.
Ephesians 6:5  Slaves, obey your masters according to the flesh with fear and trembling, in the sincerity of your heart, as you would Christ,
Ephesians 6:6  not serving only when their eyes are on you, as people-pleasers, but as slaves of Christ, doing the will of God from the soul,
Ephesians 6:7  serving with goodwill, as to the Lord and not to human beings,
Ephesians 6:8  knowing that whatever good each one does, this he will receive back from the Lord, whether slave or free.
Ephesians 6:9  And masters, act in the same way toward them, giving up threats, knowing that both their Master and yours is in the heavens, and there is no partiality with Him.
Ephesians 6:10  Finally, be strengthened in the Lord and in the might of His strength.
Ephesians 6:11  Put on the full armor of God, so that you may be able to stand against the schemes of the devil.
Ephesians 6:12  For our wrestling is not against blood and flesh, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the world-rulers of this darkness, against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places.
Ephesians 6:13  For this reason take up the full armor of God, so that you may be able to withstand in the evil day and, having accomplished everything, to stand.
Ephesians 6:14  Stand, therefore, having fastened truth around your waist and put on the breastplate of righteousness,
Ephesians 6:15  and having shod your feet with the readiness of the gospel of peace,
Ephesians 6:16  in all circumstances taking up the shield of faith, with which you will be able to extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one.
Ephesians 6:17  And receive the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God,
Ephesians 6:18  with every prayer and petition, praying at every time in the Spirit, and to this end keeping watch with all perseverance and petition for all the saints,
Ephesians 6:19  and for me, so that a word may be given to me when I open my mouth, to make known with boldness the mystery of the gospel,
Ephesians 6:20  for which I serve as an ambassador bound by a chain, so that in it I may speak boldly, as I ought to speak.
Ephesians 6:21  Now so that you also may know my circumstances, what I am doing, Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord, will make everything known to you.
Ephesians 6:22  I sent him to you for this very purpose, so that you may know about us and he may encourage your hearts.
Ephesians 6:23  Peace to the brothers, and love with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Ephesians 6:24  Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruptibility.

PHILIPPIANS

Philippians 1
Philippians 1:1  Paul and Timothy, slaves of Christ Jesus, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, together with overseers and deacons:
Philippians 1:2  grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Philippians 1:3  I thank my God every time I remember you,
Philippians 1:4  always in every petition of mine for all of you, making my petition with joy,
Philippians 1:5  because of your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now,
Philippians 1:6  being confident of this very thing, that the One who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus.
Philippians 1:7  It is right for me to think this about all of you, because I hold you in my heart, since both in my chains and in the defense and confirmation of the gospel you all share grace with me.
Philippians 1:8  For God is my witness how I long for all of you with the tender affection of Christ Jesus.
Philippians 1:9  And this I pray: that your love may abound still more and more in knowledge and every kind of discernment,
Philippians 1:10  so that you may approve the things that matter, so that you may be pure and without offense for the day of Christ,
Philippians 1:11  filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
Philippians 1:12  Now I want you to know, brothers, that my circumstances have instead served to advance the gospel,
Philippians 1:13  so that my chains have become known as being in Christ throughout the whole praetorium and to all the rest,
Philippians 1:14  and most of the brothers, having gained confidence in the Lord because of my chains, dare much more to speak the word without fear.
Philippians 1:15  Some indeed proclaim Christ because of envy and strife, but some also because of goodwill.
Philippians 1:16  The latter do so from love, knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the gospel;
Philippians 1:17  but the former announce Christ from selfish ambition, not purely, supposing that they will stir up affliction in my chains.
Philippians 1:18  What then? Only that in every way, whether in pretense or in truth, Christ is announced, and in this I rejoice. Yes, and I will rejoice,
Philippians 1:19  for I know that this will turn out for my salvation through your petition and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,
Philippians 1:20  according to my eager expectation and hope that I will not be put to shame in anything, but with all boldness, as always, so also now, Christ will be magnified in my body, whether through life or through death.
Philippians 1:21  For to me, to live is Christ and to die is gain.
Philippians 1:22  But if I am to live on in the flesh, this means fruitful work for me—and what I shall choose I do not know.
Philippians 1:23  But I am pressed between the two, having the desire to depart and be with Christ, for that is far better,
Philippians 1:24  yet to remain in the flesh is more necessary for your sake.
Philippians 1:25  And being confident of this, I know that I will remain and continue with all of you for your progress and joy in the faith,
Philippians 1:26  so that your boasting in Christ Jesus may abound because of me through my presence with you again.
Philippians 1:27  Only conduct your common life worthily of the gospel of Christ, so that whether I come and see you or remain absent, I may hear about you that you stand firm in one spirit, with one soul striving together for the faith of the gospel,
Philippians 1:28  and are not frightened in anything by your opponents. This is for them an indication of destruction, but of your salvation, and this is from God,
Philippians 1:29  because it has been graciously granted to you on behalf of Christ not only to believe in Him but also to suffer for Him,
Philippians 1:30  having the same struggle which you saw in me and now hear that I have.

Philippians 2
Philippians 2:1  So if there is any encouragement in Christ, if any consolation of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any tender affection and compassion,
Philippians 2:2  complete my joy by thinking the same thing, having the same love, united in soul, thinking the one thing,
Philippians 2:3  doing nothing from selfish ambition or conceit, but in humility considering one another above yourselves,
Philippians 2:4  each of you looking not to your own interests, but each also to the interests of others.
Philippians 2:5  Have this mind among yourselves which was also in Christ Jesus,
Philippians 2:6  who, existing in the form of God, did not regard being equal with God as something to exploit,
Philippians 2:7  but emptied Himself, taking the form of a slave, coming to be in the likeness of human beings; and being found in appearance as a human being,
Philippians 2:8  He humbled Himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross.
Philippians 2:9  Therefore God also highly exalted Him and graciously gave Him the name above every name,
Philippians 2:10  so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend, of those in heaven and on earth and under the earth,
Philippians 2:11  and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
Philippians 2:12  So then, my beloved, as you have always obeyed—not only in my presence, but now much more in my absence—work out your own salvation with fear and trembling,
Philippians 2:13  for God is the One working in you both to will and to work for His good pleasure.
Philippians 2:14  Do all things without grumbling and disputing,
Philippians 2:15  so that you may become blameless and innocent, children of God without blemish in the midst of a crooked and perverted generation, among whom you shine as lights in the world,
Philippians 2:16  holding fast the word of life, so that I may boast in the day of Christ that I did not run in vain or labor in vain.
Philippians 2:17  But even if I am being poured out upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice and rejoice together with all of you.
Philippians 2:18  And in the same way you too rejoice and rejoice together with me.
Philippians 2:19  Now I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I too may be encouraged when I know about your circumstances.
Philippians 2:20  For I have no one of like mind who will sincerely care about your circumstances,
Philippians 2:21  for all seek their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ.
Philippians 2:22  But you know his proven character, that as a child with a father he served with me for the gospel.
Philippians 2:23  So I hope to send him immediately, as soon as I see how things stand with me.
Philippians 2:24  And I am confident in the Lord that I myself also will come soon.
Philippians 2:25  But I considered it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother and fellow worker and fellow soldier, and your messenger and minister to my need,
Philippians 2:26  since he was longing for you all and was distressed because you had heard that he was sick.
Philippians 2:27  Indeed, he was sick, near death; but God had mercy on him, and not on him alone but also on me, so that I might not have sorrow upon sorrow.
Philippians 2:28  Therefore I sent him all the more eagerly, so that seeing him again you might rejoice and I might be less sorrowful.
Philippians 2:29  So welcome him in the Lord with all joy, and hold such people in honor,
Philippians 2:30  because he came near to death for the work of Christ, risking his life to make up what was lacking in your service to me.

Philippians 3
Philippians 3:1  Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you is no trouble to me, and is a safeguard for you.
Philippians 3:2  Watch out for the dogs; watch out for the evil workers; watch out for the mutilation.
Philippians 3:3  For we are the circumcision, who worship by the Spirit of God and boast in Christ Jesus and put no confidence in the flesh,
Philippians 3:4  though I myself have grounds for confidence even in the flesh. If anyone else thinks he can be confident in the flesh, I have more:
Philippians 3:5  circumcised on the eighth day, of the people of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew from Hebrews; with respect to law, a Pharisee;
Philippians 3:6  with respect to zeal, persecuting the Church; with respect to righteousness in law, having become blameless.
Philippians 3:7  But whatever things were gains to me, these I have considered loss because of Christ.
Philippians 3:8  Indeed, I even consider all things to be loss because of the surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord, for whose sake I suffered the loss of all things, and consider them refuse, so that I may gain Christ
Philippians 3:9  and be found in Him, not having my own righteousness from law but that through faith in Christ, the righteousness from God on the basis of faith,
Philippians 3:10  to know Him and the power of His resurrection and fellowship in His sufferings, being conformed to His death,
Philippians 3:11  if somehow I may attain to the resurrection from the dead.
Philippians 3:12  Not that I have already obtained it or have already been perfected, but I press on to see if I may take hold, because I too was taken hold of by Christ Jesus.
Philippians 3:13  Brothers, I do not consider myself to have taken hold. But one thing: forgetting the things behind and stretching forward to the things ahead,
Philippians 3:14  I press on toward the goal for the prize of the upward calling of God in Christ Jesus.
Philippians 3:15  So let all of us who are mature think this way; and if you think differently about anything, God will reveal this also to you.
Philippians 3:16  Only, as far as we have attained, let us keep in step with the same course.
Philippians 3:17  Join together in imitating me, brothers, and observe those who walk in this way, just as you have us as a pattern.
Philippians 3:18  For many walk as enemies of the cross of Christ; I have often told you about them, and now tell you even with tears.
Philippians 3:19  Their end is destruction, their god is the belly, and their glory is in their shame; they set their minds on earthly things.
Philippians 3:20  For our citizenship is in the heavens, from which we also eagerly await a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ,
Philippians 3:21  who will transform the body of our humiliation to be conformed to the body of His glory, according to the working by which He is able even to subject all things to Himself.

Philippians 4
Philippians 4:1  So then, my beloved and longed-for brothers, my joy and crown, stand firm in the Lord in this way, beloved.
Philippians 4:2  I urge Euodia and I urge Syntyche to think the same thing in the Lord.
Philippians 4:3  Yes, I ask you also, true yoke-fellow, help these women, who strove with me in the gospel together with Clement and the rest of my fellow workers, whose names are in the book of life.
Philippians 4:4  Rejoice in the Lord always. Again I will say: rejoice.
Philippians 4:5  Let your gentleness be known to all people. The Lord is near.
Philippians 4:6  Be anxious about nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.
Philippians 4:7  And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.
Philippians 4:8  Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever are honorable, whatever are just, whatever are pure, whatever are lovely, whatever are well spoken of, if there is any excellence and if there is any praise, consider these things.
Philippians 4:9  Practice the things you learned and received and heard and saw in me; and the God of peace will be with you.
Philippians 4:10  Now I rejoiced greatly in the Lord that at last your concern for me blossomed again. You were indeed concerned, but lacked opportunity.
Philippians 4:11  Not that I speak because of need, for I have learned to be content whatever my circumstances.
Philippians 4:12  I know how to be brought low, and I know how to abound. In everything and in all things I have learned the secret, both to be filled and to hunger, both to abound and to be in need.
Philippians 4:13  I have strength for all things in the One who empowers me.
Philippians 4:14  Nevertheless, you did well to share in my affliction.
Philippians 4:15  And you Philippians also know that at the beginning of the gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no Church shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving except you alone,
Philippians 4:16  because even in Thessalonica you sent once and twice for my need.
Philippians 4:17  Not that I seek the gift, but I seek the fruit that increases to your account.
Philippians 4:18  But I have received everything and have an abundance; I have been filled, having received from Epaphroditus the things from you, a fragrant aroma, an acceptable sacrifice, well pleasing to God.
Philippians 4:19  And my God will fill every need of yours according to His riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
Philippians 4:20  Now to our God and Father be glory for the ages of ages. Amen.
Philippians 4:21  Greet every saint in Christ Jesus. The brothers with me greet you.
Philippians 4:22  All the saints greet you, especially those of Caesar’s household.
Philippians 4:23  The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.

COLOSSIANS

Colossians 1
Colossians 1:1  Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Timothy our brother,
Colossians 1:2  to the saints and faithful brothers in Christ who are in Colossae: grace to you and peace from God our Father.
Colossians 1:3  We thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, always praying for you,
Colossians 1:4  having heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and the love you have toward all the saints,
Colossians 1:5  because of the hope laid up for you in the heavens, of which you heard beforehand in the word of truth, the gospel
Colossians 1:6  that has come to you, just as also in all the world it is bearing fruit and growing, as it does also among you from the day you heard and came to know the grace of God in truth,
Colossians 1:7  just as you learned from Epaphras, our beloved fellow slave, who is a faithful servant of Christ on your behalf,
Colossians 1:8  who also made known to us your love in the Spirit.
Colossians 1:9  For this reason we too, since the day we heard, have not ceased praying for you and asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of His will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding,
Colossians 1:10  to walk worthily of the Lord, pleasing Him in every way, bearing fruit in every good work and growing in the knowledge of God,
Colossians 1:11  being empowered with every power according to the might of His glory for all endurance and patience with joy,
Colossians 1:12  giving thanks to the Father who made you fit for a share of the inheritance of the saints in the light,
Colossians 1:13  who rescued us from the authority of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of the Son of His love,
Colossians 1:14  in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins.
Colossians 1:15  He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation,
Colossians 1:16  because in Him all things were created, in the heavens and upon the earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities. All things have been created through Him and for Him.
Colossians 1:17  And He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together.
Colossians 1:18  And He is the head of the body, the Church; He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that He Himself might have first place in all things,
Colossians 1:19  because God was pleased that all the fullness should dwell in Him,
Colossians 1:20  and through Him to reconcile all things to Himself, having made peace through the blood of His cross, [through Him], whether the things upon the earth or the things in the heavens.
Colossians 1:21  And you, who were once alienated and enemies in mind in your evil works—
Colossians 1:22  yet now He has reconciled you in the body of His flesh through death, to present you holy and without blemish and beyond accusation before Him,
Colossians 1:23  if indeed you continue in the faith, founded and steadfast and not shifting from the hope of the gospel which you heard, which was proclaimed in all creation under heaven, of which I, Paul, became a servant.
Colossians 1:24  Now I rejoice in my sufferings for you, and I fill up in my flesh what is lacking in the afflictions of Christ for His body, which is the Church,
Colossians 1:25  of which I became a servant according to the stewardship from God given to me for you, to fulfill the word of God,
Colossians 1:26  the mystery hidden from the ages and from the generations, but now revealed to His saints,
Colossians 1:27  to whom God willed to make known what are the riches of the glory of this mystery among the nations, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.
Colossians 1:28  Him we announce, admonishing every person and teaching every person in all wisdom, so that we may present every person mature in Christ.
Colossians 1:29  For this I also labor, struggling according to His working, which works in me with power.

Colossians 2
Colossians 2:1  For I want you to know how great a struggle I have for you and those in Laodicea and all who have not seen my face in the flesh,
Colossians 2:2  so that their hearts may be encouraged as they are knit together in love, and that they may come to all the riches of full assurance in understanding, to the knowledge of the mystery of God—Christ,
Colossians 2:3  in whom all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden.
Colossians 2:4  I say this so that no one may deceive you with persuasive argument.
Colossians 2:5  For even if I am absent in the flesh, yet in spirit I am with you, rejoicing and seeing your order and the firmness of your faith in Christ.
Colossians 2:6  Therefore, as you received Christ Jesus the Lord, walk in Him,
Colossians 2:7  rooted and being built up in Him and being established in the faith just as you were taught, abounding in thanksgiving.
Colossians 2:8  Watch out that no one carries you off as spoil through philosophy and empty deceit, according to human tradition, according to the elements of the world, and not according to Christ,
Colossians 2:9  for in Him all the fullness of deity dwells bodily,
Colossians 2:10  and you have been filled in Him, who is the head of every ruler and authority,
Colossians 2:11  in whom you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made by hands, in the stripping off of the body of the flesh, in the circumcision of Christ,
Colossians 2:12  having been buried together with Him in baptism, in which you were also raised together through faith in the working of God, who raised Him from the dead.
Colossians 2:13  And you, who were dead in transgressions and the uncircumcision of your flesh, He made you alive together with Him, having forgiven us all the transgressions,
Colossians 2:14  having wiped out the handwritten record with its decrees that was against us, which was opposed to us, and He has taken it out of the way, having nailed it to the cross.
Colossians 2:15  Having stripped the rulers and authorities, He displayed them openly, leading them in triumph in it.
Colossians 2:16  Therefore let no one judge you in eating and drinking, or in the matter of a festival or new moon or Sabbaths,
Colossians 2:17  which are a shadow of the things to come, but the body belongs to Christ.
Colossians 2:18  Let no one disqualify you, delighting in humility and worship of angels, dwelling on what he has seen, puffed up without cause by the mind of his flesh,
Colossians 2:19  and not holding fast to the head, from whom the whole body, supplied and knit together through joints and ligaments, grows with the growth of God.
Colossians 2:20  If you died with Christ to the elements of the world, why, as though living in the world, do you submit to decrees:
Colossians 2:21  “Do not handle, do not taste, do not touch,”
Colossians 2:22  which all concern things that perish with use, according to human commandments and teachings?
Colossians 2:23  These indeed have a reputation of wisdom in self-chosen worship and humility and severe treatment of the body, but are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh.

Colossians 3
Colossians 3:1  If, then, you were raised together with Christ, seek the things above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God.
Colossians 3:2  Set your minds on the things above, not on the things upon the earth,
Colossians 3:3  for you died, and your life has been hidden with Christ in God.
Colossians 3:4  When Christ, your life, is revealed, then you also will be revealed with Him in glory.
Colossians 3:5  Therefore put to death the members that are upon the earth: sexual immorality, impurity, passion, evil desire, and greed, which is idolatry.
Colossians 3:6  Because of these things the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience,
Colossians 3:7  in which you also once walked when you lived in these things.
Colossians 3:8  But now you too put away all these: anger, rage, malice, slander, foul speech from your mouth.
Colossians 3:9  Do not lie to one another, having stripped off the old human being with his practices
Colossians 3:10  and put on the new, who is being renewed in knowledge according to the image of the One who created him,
Colossians 3:11  where there is no Greek and Jew, circumcision and uncircumcision, barbarian, Scythian, slave, free, but Christ is all and in all.
Colossians 3:12  Therefore put on, as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved, tender compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, patience,
Colossians 3:13  bearing with one another and forgiving one another if anyone has a complaint against someone. Just as the Lord forgave you, so you also must forgive.
Colossians 3:14  And above all these things put on love, which is the bond of completeness.
Colossians 3:15  And let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, to which you were also called in one body; and be thankful.
Colossians 3:16  Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly, teaching and admonishing one another in all wisdom with psalms, hymns, spiritual songs, singing with gratitude in your hearts to God.
Colossians 3:17  And whatever you do in word or in deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks through Him to God the Father.
Colossians 3:18  Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.
Colossians 3:19  Husbands, love your wives and do not be bitter toward them.
Colossians 3:20  Children, obey your parents in all things, for this is well pleasing in the Lord.
Colossians 3:21  Fathers, do not provoke your children, so that they may not lose heart.
Colossians 3:22  Slaves, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh, not serving only when their eyes are on you, as people-pleasers, but in sincerity of heart, fearing the Lord.
Colossians 3:23  Whatever you do, work from the soul, as for the Lord and not for human beings,
Colossians 3:24  knowing that from the Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance. You serve the Lord Christ.
Colossians 3:25  For the one who does wrong will receive back the wrong he did, and there is no partiality.

Colossians 4
Colossians 4:1  Masters, provide your slaves with what is just and equitable, knowing that you too have a Master in heaven.
Colossians 4:2  Persevere in prayer, keeping watch in it with thanksgiving,
Colossians 4:3  praying at the same time for us also, so that God may open for us a door for the word, to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I am also bound,
Colossians 4:4  so that I may make it clear as I ought to speak.
Colossians 4:5  Walk in wisdom toward those outside, buying up the opportunity.
Colossians 4:6  Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how you ought to answer each one.
Colossians 4:7  Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful servant and fellow slave in the Lord, will make known to you all my circumstances.
Colossians 4:8  I sent him to you for this very purpose, so that you may know about us and he may encourage your hearts,
Colossians 4:9  with Onesimus, the faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They will make known to you all the things here.
Colossians 4:10  Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, greets you, and Mark, the cousin of Barnabas, concerning whom you received instructions—if he comes to you, welcome him—
Colossians 4:11  and Jesus who is called Justus. From among those of the circumcision, these alone are fellow workers for the kingdom of God; they have become a comfort to me.
Colossians 4:12  Epaphras, who is one of you, a slave of Christ Jesus, greets you, always struggling for you in his prayers, so that you may stand mature and fully assured in all the will of God.
Colossians 4:13  For I testify about him that he takes great pains for you and those in Laodicea and those in Hierapolis.
Colossians 4:14  Luke, the beloved physician, greets you, and Demas.
Colossians 4:15  Greet the brothers in Laodicea, and Nympha and the Church in her house.
Colossians 4:16  And when the letter has been read among you, arrange for it also to be read in the Church of the Laodiceans, and for you also to read the one from Laodicea.
Colossians 4:17  And say to Archippus, “Attend to the service which you received in the Lord, so that you may fulfill it.”
Colossians 4:18  The greeting is in my own hand, Paul’s. Remember my chains. Grace be with you.

1 THESSALONIANS

1 Thessalonians 1
1 Thessalonians 1:1  Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the Church of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: grace to you and peace.
1 Thessalonians 1:2  We always give thanks to God for all of you, mentioning you in our prayers, unceasingly
1 Thessalonians 1:3  remembering your work of faith and labor of love and endurance of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ before our God and Father,
1 Thessalonians 1:4  knowing, brothers beloved by God, your election,
1 Thessalonians 1:5  because our gospel did not come to you in word alone, but also in power and in the Holy Spirit and in great assurance, just as you know what kind of people we became among you for your sake.
1 Thessalonians 1:6  And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, receiving the word in great affliction with joy from the Holy Spirit,
1 Thessalonians 1:7  so that you became an example to all who believe in Macedonia and in Achaia.
1 Thessalonians 1:8  For from you the word of the Lord has sounded out, not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but your faith toward God has gone out in every place, so that we have no need to say anything.
1 Thessalonians 1:9  For they themselves report about us what our coming to you was like, and how you turned to God from idols, to serve the living and true God
1 Thessalonians 1:10  and to await His Son from the heavens, whom He raised from the dead—Jesus, who rescues us from the coming wrath.

1 Thessalonians 2
1 Thessalonians 2:1  For you yourselves know, brothers, that our coming to you has not been in vain.
1 Thessalonians 2:2  But after we had already suffered and been shamefully treated in Philippi, as you know, we were bold in our God to speak to you the gospel of God amid much struggle.
1 Thessalonians 2:3  For our appeal does not come from error or impurity, nor is it made in deceit.
1 Thessalonians 2:4  But just as we have been approved by God to be entrusted with the gospel, so we speak, pleasing not people but God, who tests our hearts.
1 Thessalonians 2:5  For we never came with a word of flattery, as you know, nor with a pretext for greed—God is witness—
1 Thessalonians 2:6  nor seeking glory from people, either from you or from others,
1 Thessalonians 2:7  though we could have carried weight as apostles of Christ. But we became little children among you. As a nursing mother would cherish her own children,
1 Thessalonians 2:8  so, longing for you, we were pleased to share with you not only the gospel of God but also our own lives, because you had become beloved to us.
1 Thessalonians 2:9  For you remember, brothers, our labor and toil: working night and day so as not to burden any of you, we proclaimed to you the gospel of God.
1 Thessalonians 2:10  You are witnesses, and God also, how devoutly and justly and blamelessly we conducted ourselves toward you who believe,
1 Thessalonians 2:11  just as you know how we dealt with each one of you, as a father with his own children,
1 Thessalonians 2:12  encouraging you and comforting you and solemnly urging you to walk worthily of God, who calls you into His own kingdom and glory.
1 Thessalonians 2:13  And for this reason we also thank God unceasingly: when you received the word of God that you heard from us, you accepted it as no human word, but as it truly is, the word of God, which also works in you who believe.
1 Thessalonians 2:14  For you, brothers, became imitators of the Churches of God in Christ Jesus that are in Judea, because you also suffered the same things from your own countrymen as they did from the Jews
1 Thessalonians 2:15  who both killed the Lord Jesus and the prophets and drove us out, and do not please God and are opposed to all people,
