1 Thessalonians 2:16  hindering us from speaking to the nations so that they might be saved, thus always filling up their sins. But wrath has overtaken them to the end.
1 Thessalonians 2:17  But we, brothers, having been bereaved of you for a short time—in face, not in heart—were all the more eager, with great longing, to see your face.
1 Thessalonians 2:18  For we wanted to come to you—I, Paul, both once and twice—and Satan hindered us.
1 Thessalonians 2:19  For what is our hope or joy or crown of boasting before our Lord Jesus at His coming? Is it not also you?
1 Thessalonians 2:20  For you are our glory and joy.

1 Thessalonians 3
1 Thessalonians 3:1  Therefore, when we could bear it no longer, we were willing to be left alone in Athens,
1 Thessalonians 3:2  and sent Timothy, our brother and God’s fellow worker in the gospel of Christ, to strengthen you and encourage you concerning your faith,
1 Thessalonians 3:3  so that no one would be shaken by these afflictions. For you yourselves know that we are appointed to this.
1 Thessalonians 3:4  For even when we were with you, we told you beforehand that we were going to suffer affliction, just as it also happened, as you know.
1 Thessalonians 3:5  For this reason, when I too could bear it no longer, I sent to learn of your faith, for fear that the tempter had tempted you and our labor might be in vain.
1 Thessalonians 3:6  But now Timothy has come to us from you and brought us good news of your faith and love, and that you always remember us kindly, longing to see us just as we also long to see you.
1 Thessalonians 3:7  For this reason, brothers, in all our distress and affliction we have been comforted about you through your faith,
1 Thessalonians 3:8  because now we live, if you stand firm in the Lord.
1 Thessalonians 3:9  For what thanksgiving can we return to God for you, for all the joy with which we rejoice because of you before our God,
1 Thessalonians 3:10  as night and day we pray most earnestly to see your face and supply what is lacking in your faith?
1 Thessalonians 3:11  Now may our God and Father Himself, and our Lord Jesus, direct our way to you.
1 Thessalonians 3:12  And may the Lord make you increase and overflow in love for one another and for all, just as we also do for you,
1 Thessalonians 3:13  so as to establish your hearts blameless in holiness before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all His saints. Amen.

1 Thessalonians 4
1 Thessalonians 4:1  Finally then, brothers, we ask and urge you in the Lord Jesus that, as you received from us how you ought to walk and please God—just as you are indeed walking—you may abound still more.
1 Thessalonians 4:2  For you know what instructions we gave you through the Lord Jesus.
1 Thessalonians 4:3  For this is the will of God, your sanctification: that you abstain from sexual immorality,
1 Thessalonians 4:4  that each of you know how to acquire his own vessel in sanctification and honor,
1 Thessalonians 4:5  not in the passion of desire, as do the nations that do not know God;
1 Thessalonians 4:6  that no one overstep and take advantage of his brother in the matter, because the Lord is an avenger concerning all these things, just as we told you beforehand and solemnly warned you.
1 Thessalonians 4:7  For God did not call us for impurity, but in sanctification.
1 Thessalonians 4:8  Therefore, the one who rejects this rejects no human being, but God, who also gives His Holy Spirit to you.
1 Thessalonians 4:9  Now concerning brotherly love, you have no need for someone to write to you, for you yourselves are taught by God to love one another.
1 Thessalonians 4:10  For you indeed do this toward all the brothers throughout Macedonia. But we urge you, brothers, to abound still more,
1 Thessalonians 4:11  and to make it your ambition to be quiet, to attend to your own affairs, and to work with your own hands, just as we instructed you,
1 Thessalonians 4:12  so that you may walk properly toward those outside and have need of no one.
1 Thessalonians 4:13  But we do not want you to be unaware, brothers, concerning those who are sleeping, so that you may not grieve as the rest do, who have no hope.
1 Thessalonians 4:14  For if we believe that Jesus died and rose, so also God, through Jesus, will bring with Him those who have fallen asleep.
1 Thessalonians 4:15  For this we say to you by a word of the Lord: we who are alive, who remain until the Lord’s coming, will certainly not precede those who have fallen asleep.
1 Thessalonians 4:16  For the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a commanding cry, with an archangel’s voice and with God’s trumpet, and the dead in Christ will rise first.
1 Thessalonians 4:17  Then we who are alive, who remain, will be caught up together with them in clouds to meet the Lord in the air; and so we will always be with the Lord.
1 Thessalonians 4:18  Therefore encourage one another with these words.

1 Thessalonians 5
1 Thessalonians 5:1  Now concerning the times and the seasons, brothers, you have no need for anything to be written to you.
1 Thessalonians 5:2  For you yourselves know exactly that the day of the Lord comes in this way, like a thief in the night.
1 Thessalonians 5:3  When they say, “Peace and security,” then sudden destruction comes upon them, as labor pain upon a pregnant woman, and they will certainly not escape.
1 Thessalonians 5:4  But you, brothers, are not in darkness, so that the day should overtake you like a thief.
1 Thessalonians 5:5  For you are all sons of light and sons of day. We are not of night or darkness.
1 Thessalonians 5:6  So then, let us not sleep as the rest do, but let us keep watch and be sober.
1 Thessalonians 5:7  For those who sleep sleep at night, and those who get drunk are drunk at night.
1 Thessalonians 5:8  But since we are of the day, let us be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love, and as a helmet, the hope of salvation.
1 Thessalonians 5:9  For God did not appoint us for wrath, but for obtaining salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ,
1 Thessalonians 5:10  who died for us, so that whether we keep watch or sleep, we may live together with Him.
1 Thessalonians 5:11  Therefore encourage one another and build each other up, just as you are indeed doing.
1 Thessalonians 5:12  Now we ask you, brothers, to recognize those who labor among you and lead you in the Lord and admonish you,
1 Thessalonians 5:13  and to hold them in exceedingly high regard in love because of their work. Be at peace among yourselves.
1 Thessalonians 5:14  And we urge you, brothers: admonish the disorderly, comfort the fainthearted, hold fast to the weak, be patient toward all.
1 Thessalonians 5:15  See that no one repays anyone evil for evil, but always pursue what is good for one another and for all.
1 Thessalonians 5:16  Rejoice always.
1 Thessalonians 5:17  Pray unceasingly.
1 Thessalonians 5:18  Give thanks in everything, for this is God’s will for you in Christ Jesus.
1 Thessalonians 5:19  Do not quench the Spirit.
1 Thessalonians 5:20  Do not despise prophecies.
1 Thessalonians 5:21  But test all things; hold fast to what is good.
1 Thessalonians 5:22  Abstain from every form of evil.
1 Thessalonians 5:23  Now may the God of peace Himself sanctify you completely, and may your spirit and soul and body be kept whole, blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
1 Thessalonians 5:24  He who calls you is faithful; He will also do it.
1 Thessalonians 5:25  Brothers, pray also for us.
1 Thessalonians 5:26  Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.
1 Thessalonians 5:27  I put you under oath by the Lord to have this letter read to all the brothers.
1 Thessalonians 5:28  The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

2 THESSALONIANS

2 Thessalonians 1
2 Thessalonians 1:1  Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the Church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:
2 Thessalonians 1:2  grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
2 Thessalonians 1:3  We ought always to give thanks to God for you, brothers, as is fitting, because your faith is growing abundantly and the love of each and every one of you for one another is increasing,
2 Thessalonians 1:4  so that we ourselves boast of you among the Churches of God for your endurance and faith in all your persecutions and the afflictions that you bear.
2 Thessalonians 1:5  This is evidence of God’s righteous judgment, that you may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you also suffer,
2 Thessalonians 1:6  since it is indeed just with God to repay affliction to those who afflict you,
2 Thessalonians 1:7  and to you who are afflicted, relief with us, at the revelation of the Lord Jesus from heaven with the angels of His power,
2 Thessalonians 1:8  in a flame of fire, bringing vengeance on those who do not know God and on those who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus.
2 Thessalonians 1:9  They will pay the penalty of eternal destruction from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of His strength,
2 Thessalonians 1:10  when He comes to be glorified in His saints and marveled at among all who have believed—because our testimony to you was believed—on that day.
2 Thessalonians 1:11  To this end we also always pray for you, that our God may count you worthy of the calling and fulfill every good resolve and work of faith with power,
2 Thessalonians 1:12  so that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in Him, according to the grace of our God and Lord Jesus Christ.

2 Thessalonians 2
2 Thessalonians 2:1  Now we ask you, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering together to Him,
2 Thessalonians 2:2  not to be quickly shaken from your understanding or alarmed, either by a spirit or by a word or by a letter as though from us, as if the day of the Lord is already present.
2 Thessalonians 2:3  Let no one deceive you in any way. For that day will not come unless the rebellion comes first and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of destruction,
2 Thessalonians 2:4  who opposes and exalts himself above everything called god or an object of worship, so that he takes his seat in God’s sanctuary, displaying himself as being God.
2 Thessalonians 2:5  Do you not remember that when I was still with you I used to tell you these things?
2 Thessalonians 2:6  And now you know what restrains, so that he may be revealed in his own time.
2 Thessalonians 2:7  For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work. Only, the one who now restrains does so until he is out of the way.
2 Thessalonians 2:8  And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will kill with the breath of His mouth and bring to nothing by the manifestation of His coming.
2 Thessalonians 2:9  His coming is according to the working of Satan, with all power and signs and wonders of falsehood,
2 Thessalonians 2:10  and with every deception of unrighteousness for those who are perishing, because they did not receive the love of the truth so that they might be saved.
2 Thessalonians 2:11  And for this reason God sends them a working of delusion, so that they believe the falsehood,
2 Thessalonians 2:12  in order that all who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in unrighteousness may be judged.
2 Thessalonians 2:13  But we ought always to thank God for you, brothers beloved by the Lord, because God chose you as firstfruits for salvation in sanctification by the Spirit and faith in the truth.
2 Thessalonians 2:14  To this He also called you through our gospel, for obtaining the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
2 Thessalonians 2:15  So then, brothers, stand firm and hold fast to the traditions you were taught, whether by word or by a letter from us.
2 Thessalonians 2:16  Now may our Lord Jesus Christ Himself, and God our Father, who loved us and gave us eternal encouragement and good hope in grace,
2 Thessalonians 2:17  encourage your hearts and establish them in every good work and word.

2 Thessalonians 3
2 Thessalonians 3:1  Finally, brothers, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may run and be glorified, just as it also is among you,
2 Thessalonians 3:2  and that we may be rescued from perverse and evil people, for not all have faith.
2 Thessalonians 3:3  But the Lord is faithful; He will establish you and guard you from the evil one.
2 Thessalonians 3:4  And we are confident in the Lord about you, that you both do and will do what we command.
2 Thessalonians 3:5  And may the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God and into the endurance of Christ.
2 Thessalonians 3:6  Now we command you, brothers, in the name of [our] Lord Jesus Christ, to keep away from every brother who walks in a disorderly way and not according to the tradition which they received from us.
2 Thessalonians 3:7  For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us, because we did not behave in a disorderly way among you,
2 Thessalonians 3:8  nor did we eat anyone’s bread without payment, but with labor and toil we worked night and day so as not to burden any of you.
2 Thessalonians 3:9  This was not because we lack the right, but so that we might give ourselves to you as an example for you to imitate.
2 Thessalonians 3:10  For even when we were with you, we gave you this command: if anyone is not willing to work, let him not eat either.
2 Thessalonians 3:11  For we hear that some among you are walking in a disorderly way, not working at all but working at everyone else’s business.
2 Thessalonians 3:12  Now such people we command and urge in the Lord Jesus Christ to work quietly and eat their own bread.
2 Thessalonians 3:13  But you, brothers, do not lose heart in doing good.
2 Thessalonians 3:14  And if anyone does not obey our word through this letter, take note of that person, and do not associate with him, so that he may be ashamed.
2 Thessalonians 3:15  Yet do not regard him as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother.
2 Thessalonians 3:16  Now may the Lord of peace Himself give you peace always in every way. The Lord be with all of you.
2 Thessalonians 3:17  The greeting is in my own hand—Paul’s—which is a sign in every letter. This is how I write.
2 Thessalonians 3:18  The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you.

1 TIMOTHY

1 Timothy 1
1 Timothy 1:1  Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus according to the command of God our Savior and Christ Jesus our hope,
1 Timothy 1:2  to Timothy, a true child in faith: grace, mercy, peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
1 Timothy 1:3  Just as I urged you to remain in Ephesus when I was going to Macedonia, so that you might command certain people not to teach differently,
1 Timothy 1:4  nor to pay attention to myths and endless genealogies, which produce speculations rather than God’s stewardship in faith—
1 Timothy 1:5  But the goal of the charge is love from a pure heart and a good conscience and sincere faith.
1 Timothy 1:6  Some, having missed these things, turned aside to empty talk,
1 Timothy 1:7  wanting to be teachers of law, understanding neither what they say nor the things about which they speak confidently.
1 Timothy 1:8  Now we know that the law is good if someone uses it lawfully,
1 Timothy 1:9  knowing this, that law is not laid down for a righteous person but for the lawless and insubordinate, the ungodly and sinners, the unholy and profane, those who strike fathers and those who strike mothers, murderers,
1 Timothy 1:10  sexually immoral people, men who bed males, enslavers, liars, perjurers, and whatever else opposes sound teaching,
1 Timothy 1:11  according to the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, with which I was entrusted.
1 Timothy 1:12  I am thankful to Christ Jesus our Lord, who empowered me, because He considered me faithful, appointing me to service,
1 Timothy 1:13  though formerly I was a blasphemer and persecutor and violent abuser. But I was shown mercy because I acted in ignorance in unbelief,
1 Timothy 1:14  and the grace of our Lord overflowed exceedingly, with faith and love in Christ Jesus.
1 Timothy 1:15  The saying is trustworthy and deserves full acceptance: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am foremost.
1 Timothy 1:16  But for this reason I was shown mercy, so that in me, the foremost, Christ Jesus might display all His patience as a pattern for those who would believe in Him for eternal life.
1 Timothy 1:17  Now to the King of the ages, incorruptible, invisible, the only God, be honor and glory for the ages of ages. Amen.
1 Timothy 1:18  This command I entrust to you, Timothy, my child, according to the prophecies previously spoken concerning you, so that by them you may wage the good campaign,
1 Timothy 1:19  holding faith and a good conscience, which some have thrust aside and suffered shipwreck concerning the faith.
1 Timothy 1:20  Among these are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I handed over to Satan so that they might be disciplined not to blaspheme.

1 Timothy 2
1 Timothy 2:1  Therefore I urge first of all that petitions, prayers, intercessions and thanksgivings be made for all people,
1 Timothy 2:2  for kings and all who are in high positions, so that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and dignity.
1 Timothy 2:3  This is good and acceptable before God our Savior,
1 Timothy 2:4  who wills all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of truth.
1 Timothy 2:5  For there is one God, and one mediator between God and human beings, the human being Christ Jesus,
1 Timothy 2:6  who gave Himself as a ransom in exchange for all, the testimony at the proper times.
1 Timothy 2:7  For this I was appointed a herald and an apostle—I speak truth, I do not lie—a teacher of nations in faith and truth.
1 Timothy 2:8  Therefore I want the men to pray in every place, lifting holy hands without anger and disputing.
1 Timothy 2:9  Likewise also women are to adorn themselves in orderly dress, with modesty and self-restraint, not with braids and gold or pearls or costly clothing,
1 Timothy 2:10  but through good works, as is fitting for women who profess reverence for God.
1 Timothy 2:11  Let a woman learn in quietness, in all submission.
1 Timothy 2:12  But I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man, but to be in quietness.
1 Timothy 2:13  For Adam was formed first, then Eve,
1 Timothy 2:14  and Adam was not deceived, but the woman, being deceived, came to be in transgression.
1 Timothy 2:15  But she will be saved through childbearing, if they continue in faith and love and sanctification with self-restraint.

1 Timothy 3
1 Timothy 3:1  The saying is trustworthy. If anyone aspires to oversight, he desires a good work.
1 Timothy 3:2  Therefore the overseer must be above reproach, a husband of one wife, sober, self-controlled, orderly, hospitable, able to teach,
1 Timothy 3:3  not given to wine, not a striker, but gentle, peaceable, not a lover of money,
1 Timothy 3:4  leading his own household well, having children in submission with all dignity.
1 Timothy 3:5  But if someone does not know how to lead his own household, how will he care for the Church of God?
1 Timothy 3:6  He must not be newly planted, lest, becoming conceited, he fall into the judgment of the devil.
1 Timothy 3:7  And he must also have a good testimony from those outside, lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.
1 Timothy 3:8  Deacons likewise must be dignified, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not seeking shameful gain,
1 Timothy 3:9  holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.
1 Timothy 3:10  And let these also be tested first; then let them serve as deacons if they are beyond accusation.
1 Timothy 3:11  Women likewise must be dignified, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things.
1 Timothy 3:12  Let deacons be husbands of one wife, leading their children and their own households well.
1 Timothy 3:13  For those who have served well as deacons acquire for themselves a good standing and great boldness in faith in Christ Jesus.
1 Timothy 3:14  I write these things to you, hoping to come to you soon,
1 Timothy 3:15  but if I delay, so that you may know how one ought to conduct oneself in the household of God, which is the Church of the living God, a pillar and foundation of the truth.
1 Timothy 3:16  And, by common confession, the mystery of godliness is great: He who was revealed in flesh, was vindicated in spirit, was seen by angels, was proclaimed among nations, was believed in the world, was taken up in glory.

1 Timothy 4
1 Timothy 4:1  But the Spirit says clearly that in later times some will depart from the faith, paying attention to deceiving spirits and teachings of demons,
1 Timothy 4:2  through the hypocrisy of liars, seared in their own conscience,
1 Timothy 4:3  who forbid marriage and require abstinence from foods which God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.
1 Timothy 4:4  For everything created by God is good, and nothing is to be rejected when received with thanksgiving,
1 Timothy 4:5  for it is sanctified through the word of God and intercession.
1 Timothy 4:6  By laying these things before the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished in the words of the faith and of the good teaching which you have followed.
1 Timothy 4:7  But reject profane and old women’s myths, and train yourself for godliness.
1 Timothy 4:8  For bodily training is of some benefit, but godliness is beneficial for all things, having a promise of life both now and to come.
1 Timothy 4:9  The saying is trustworthy and deserves full acceptance.
1 Timothy 4:10  For to this end we labor and struggle, because we have set our hope on the living God, who is Savior of all people, especially of believers.
1 Timothy 4:11  Command and teach these things.
1 Timothy 4:12  Let no one despise your youth, but become a pattern for believers in word, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.
1 Timothy 4:13  Until I come, devote yourself to the reading, the exhortation and the teaching.
1 Timothy 4:14  Do not neglect the gift in you, which was given to you through prophecy with the laying on of the hands of the council of elders.
1 Timothy 4:15  Practice these things; be absorbed in them, so that your progress may be clear to all.
1 Timothy 4:16  Pay attention to yourself and to the teaching; continue in them, for by doing this you will save both yourself and those who hear you.

1 Timothy 5
1 Timothy 5:1  Do not rebuke an older man harshly, but appeal to him as a father, younger men as brothers,
1 Timothy 5:2  older women as mothers, younger women as sisters, in all purity.
1 Timothy 5:3  Honor widows who are truly widows.
1 Timothy 5:4  But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn to practice godliness toward their own household and to repay their forebears, for this is acceptable before God.
1 Timothy 5:5  Now the woman who is truly a widow and left alone has set her hope on God and continues in petitions and prayers night and day.
1 Timothy 5:6  But the woman who lives in indulgence is dead while living.
1 Timothy 5:7  And command these things, so that they may be above reproach.
1 Timothy 5:8  But if someone does not provide for his own, and especially his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
1 Timothy 5:9  Let a widow be enrolled who is not less than sixty years old, a wife of one husband,
1 Timothy 5:10  attested for good works: if she brought up children, if she received strangers, if she washed saints’ feet, if she assisted the afflicted, if she followed every good work.
1 Timothy 5:11  But refuse younger widows, for when their desires turn them against Christ, they want to marry,
1 Timothy 5:12  incurring judgment because they set aside their first faith.
1 Timothy 5:13  And at the same time they learn to be idle, going around the houses, and not only idle but also gossips and busybodies, saying things they ought not to say.
1 Timothy 5:14  Therefore I want younger women to marry, bear children, manage a household, and give the opponent no opportunity for abuse.
1 Timothy 5:15  For some have already turned aside after Satan.
1 Timothy 5:16  If any believing woman has widows, let her assist them, and let the Church not be burdened, so that it may assist those who are truly widows.
1 Timothy 5:17  Let the elders who lead well be considered worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in word and teaching.
1 Timothy 5:18  For Scripture says, “You shall not muzzle an ox that threshes,” and, “The worker is worthy of his wage.”
1 Timothy 5:19  Do not receive an accusation against an elder except on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
1 Timothy 5:20  Reprove those who sin before all, so that the rest also may have fear.
1 Timothy 5:21  I charge you before God and Christ Jesus and the chosen angels that you keep these things without prejudgment, doing nothing from partiality.
1 Timothy 5:22  Do not lay hands on anyone hastily, nor share in the sins of others. Keep yourself pure.
1 Timothy 5:23  No longer drink only water, but use a little wine because of your stomach and your frequent illnesses.
1 Timothy 5:24  The sins of some people are evident beforehand, going ahead to judgment, but those of others follow after.
1 Timothy 5:25  Likewise good works also are evident, and those that are otherwise cannot remain hidden.

1 Timothy 6
1 Timothy 6:1  Let all who are slaves under a yoke consider their own masters worthy of all honor, so that the name of God and the teaching may not be blasphemed.
1 Timothy 6:2  And those who have believing masters must not despise them because they are brothers, but rather serve them more, because those receiving the benefit are believers and beloved. Teach and urge these things.
1 Timothy 6:3  If anyone teaches differently and does not adhere to sound words, those of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the teaching according to godliness,
1 Timothy 6:4  he has become conceited, knowing nothing, but is sick with disputes and battles over words, from which come envy, strife, slanders, evil suspicions,
1 Timothy 6:5  constant friction among people corrupted in mind and deprived of the truth, supposing godliness to be a means of gain.
1 Timothy 6:6  But godliness with contentment is great gain.
1 Timothy 6:7  For we brought nothing into the world, because neither can we carry anything out.
1 Timothy 6:8  But having food and coverings, with these we will be content.
1 Timothy 6:9  But those who want to become rich fall into temptation and a snare and many foolish and harmful desires, which plunge people into ruin and destruction.
1 Timothy 6:10  For the love of money is a root of all evils, and some, reaching for it, wandered from the faith and pierced themselves with many pains.
1 Timothy 6:11  But you, O man of God, flee these things. Pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance, gentleness.
1 Timothy 6:12  Fight the good fight of the faith; take hold of eternal life, to which you were called. And you confessed the good confession before many witnesses.
1 Timothy 6:13  I command you before God, who preserves all things alive, and Christ Jesus, who testified the good confession before Pontius Pilate,
1 Timothy 6:14  that you keep the commandment spotless, above reproach, until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ,
1 Timothy 6:15  which the blessed and only Sovereign will display at the proper times, the King of those who reign and Lord of those who rule,
1 Timothy 6:16  who alone has immortality, dwelling in unapproachable light, whom no human being has seen or can see; to Him be honor and eternal might. Amen.
1 Timothy 6:17  Command those who are rich in the present age not to be arrogant nor to set their hope on the uncertainty of wealth, but on God, who richly provides us all things for enjoyment,
1 Timothy 6:18  to do good, to be rich in good works, to be generous, ready to share,
1 Timothy 6:19  storing up for themselves a good foundation for the future, so that they may take hold of the life that is truly life.
1 Timothy 6:20  O Timothy, guard what has been entrusted, turning away from profane empty talk and the opposing claims of falsely named knowledge.
1 Timothy 6:21  Some, professing it, have missed the mark concerning the faith. Grace be with you.

2 TIMOTHY

2 Timothy 1
2 Timothy 1:1  Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, according to the promise of life in Christ Jesus,
2 Timothy 1:2  to Timothy, a beloved child: grace, mercy, peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
2 Timothy 1:3  I thank God, whom I serve, as my forebears did, with a pure conscience, as I remember you unceasingly in my petitions night and day,
2 Timothy 1:4  longing to see you, remembering your tears, so that I may be filled with joy,
2 Timothy 1:5  having been reminded of the sincere faith in you, which dwelt first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am convinced that it dwells also in you.
2 Timothy 1:6  For this reason I remind you to rekindle God’s gift, which is in you through the laying on of my hands.
2 Timothy 1:7  For God did not give us a spirit of cowardice, but of power and love and self-discipline.
2 Timothy 1:8  Therefore do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord or of me, His prisoner, but share suffering for the gospel according to the power of God,
2 Timothy 1:9  who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works but according to His own purpose and grace, which was given to us in Christ Jesus before the times of the ages,
2 Timothy 1:10  but has now been revealed through the appearing of our Savior Christ Jesus, who abolished death and brought life and incorruptibility to light through the gospel.
2 Timothy 1:11  For this I was appointed a herald and an apostle and a teacher.
2 Timothy 1:12  For this reason I also suffer these things, but I am not ashamed, for I know whom I have believed, and I am persuaded that He is able to guard my deposit for that day.
2 Timothy 1:13  Keep the pattern of sound words that you heard from me, in faith and love in Christ Jesus.
2 Timothy 1:14  Guard the good deposit through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.
2 Timothy 1:15  You know this, that all those in Asia turned away from me, among whom are Phygelus and Hermogenes.
2 Timothy 1:16  May the Lord give mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chain,
2 Timothy 1:17  but when he came to Rome, he earnestly searched for me and found me.
2 Timothy 1:18  May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord on that day. And you know very well how much service he gave in Ephesus.

2 Timothy 2
2 Timothy 2:1  You, then, my child, be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus,
2 Timothy 2:2  and the things you heard from me through many witnesses, entrust these to faithful people who will be able to teach others also.
2 Timothy 2:3  Share suffering as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
2 Timothy 2:4  No one serving as a soldier entangles himself in the affairs of ordinary life, so that he may please the one who enlisted him.
2 Timothy 2:5  And if someone competes as an athlete, he is not crowned unless he competes according to the rules.
2 Timothy 2:6  The farmer who labors must be first to share in the fruits.
2 Timothy 2:7  Consider what I say, for the Lord will give you understanding in all things.
2 Timothy 2:8  Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, from David’s seed, according to my gospel,
2 Timothy 2:9  for which I suffer hardship even to chains as a criminal. But the word of God has not been chained.
2 Timothy 2:10  For this reason I endure all things for the chosen ones, so that they too may obtain the salvation in Christ Jesus with eternal glory.
2 Timothy 2:11  The saying is trustworthy: for if we died with Him, we will also live with Him;
2 Timothy 2:12  if we endure, we will also reign with Him; if we deny Him, He also will deny us;
2 Timothy 2:13  if we are unfaithful, He remains faithful, for He cannot deny Himself.
2 Timothy 2:14  Remind them of these things, charging them before God not to quarrel over words, which does no good and leads to the ruin of those who hear.
2 Timothy 2:15  Be diligent to present yourself approved to God, a worker with no cause for shame, cutting a straight course for the word of truth.
2 Timothy 2:16  But avoid profane empty talk, for they will advance into further ungodliness,
2 Timothy 2:17  and their word will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,
2 Timothy 2:18  who missed the mark concerning truth, saying that the resurrection has already happened, and overturn the faith of some.
2 Timothy 2:19  Nevertheless, the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal: “The Lord knew those who are His,” and, “Let everyone who names the name of the Lord depart from unrighteousness.”
2 Timothy 2:20  Now in a great house there are vessels not only of gold and silver but also of wood and clay, some for honor and some for dishonor.
2 Timothy 2:21  Therefore if someone cleanses himself from these things, he will be a vessel for honor, sanctified, useful to the Master, prepared for every good work.
2 Timothy 2:22  But flee youthful desires, and pursue righteousness, faith, love, peace with those who call upon the Lord from a pure heart.
2 Timothy 2:23  And reject foolish and ignorant disputes, knowing that they give birth to fights.
2 Timothy 2:24  But a slave of the Lord must not fight, but must be gentle toward all, able to teach, patient with wrong,
2 Timothy 2:25  instructing opponents with gentleness, in case God may give them repentance toward the knowledge of truth,
2 Timothy 2:26  and they may regain their sobriety and escape the devil’s snare, having been captured by him to do his will.

2 Timothy 3
2 Timothy 3:1  But know this: in the last days difficult times will come.
2 Timothy 3:2  For people will be lovers of themselves, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, blasphemous, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, unholy,
2 Timothy 3:3  without natural affection, irreconcilable, slanderers, without self-control, savage, not loving the good,
2 Timothy 3:4  traitors, reckless, conceited, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God,
2 Timothy 3:5  having a form of godliness but denying its power. Turn away from these also.
2 Timothy 3:6  For among these are those who slip into houses and take captive weak women, laden with sins, led by various desires,
2 Timothy 3:7  always learning and never able to come to the knowledge of truth.
2 Timothy 3:8  And just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these too oppose the truth, people corrupted in mind, disqualified concerning the faith.
2 Timothy 3:9  But they will make no further progress, for their folly will be clear to all, as the folly of those men also became.
2 Timothy 3:10  But you followed my teaching, conduct, purpose, faith, patience, love, endurance,
2 Timothy 3:11  persecutions, sufferings, such as happened to me in Antioch, in Iconium, in Lystra, what persecutions I endured; and out of all of them the Lord rescued me.
2 Timothy 3:12  And all who want to live godly lives in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.
2 Timothy 3:13  But evil people and impostors will go from bad to worse, deceiving and being deceived.
2 Timothy 3:14  But you, remain in the things you learned and became convinced of, knowing those from whom you learned,
2 Timothy 3:15  and that from infancy you have known the sacred writings, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
2 Timothy 3:16  All Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, for training in righteousness,
2 Timothy 3:17  so that the person of God may be capable, fully equipped for every good work.

2 Timothy 4
2 Timothy 4:1  I charge you before God and Christ Jesus, who is to judge the living and the dead, and by His appearing and His kingdom:
2 Timothy 4:2  proclaim the word; be ready in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort, with all patience and teaching.
2 Timothy 4:3  For a time will come when they will not endure sound teaching, but with itching ears they will heap up teachers for themselves according to their own desires,
2 Timothy 4:4  and they will turn their hearing away from the truth and turn aside to myths.
2 Timothy 4:5  But you, be sober in all things, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, fulfill your service.
2 Timothy 4:6  For I am already being poured out, and the time of my departure has arrived.
2 Timothy 4:7  I have fought the good fight; I have finished the course; I have kept the faith.
2 Timothy 4:8  From now on the crown of righteousness is laid up for me, which the Lord, the righteous Judge, will award me on that day, and not to me alone but also to all who have loved His appearing.
2 Timothy 4:9  Make every effort to come to me soon,
2 Timothy 4:10  for Demas deserted me, having loved the present age, and went to Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia; Titus to Dalmatia.
2 Timothy 4:11  Luke alone is with me. Take Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for service.
2 Timothy 4:12  But I sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
2 Timothy 4:13  When you come, bring the cloak which I left in Troas with Carpus, and the books, especially the parchments.
2 Timothy 4:14  Alexander the coppersmith did me much harm; the Lord will repay him according to his works.
2 Timothy 4:15  You too must guard yourself against him, for he strongly opposed our words.
2 Timothy 4:16  At my first defense no one came to my side, but all deserted me. May it not be counted against them.
2 Timothy 4:17  But the Lord stood beside me and strengthened me, so that through me the proclamation might be fulfilled and all the nations might hear, and I was rescued from a lion’s mouth.
2 Timothy 4:18  The Lord will rescue me from every evil work and save me into His heavenly kingdom. To Him be glory for the ages of ages. Amen.
2 Timothy 4:19  Greet Prisca and Aquila and the household of Onesiphorus.
2 Timothy 4:20  Erastus remained in Corinth, but I left Trophimus sick in Miletus.
2 Timothy 4:21  Make every effort to come before winter. Eubulus greets you, and Pudens and Linus and Claudia and all the brothers.
2 Timothy 4:22  The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you all.

TITUS

Titus 1
Titus 1:1  Paul, a slave of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, for the faith of God’s chosen ones and the knowledge of the truth that accords with godliness,
Titus 1:2  in hope of eternal life, which God, who does not lie, promised before the ages,
Titus 1:3  and in His own appointed times He revealed His word through proclamation, with which I was entrusted by the command of God our Savior,
Titus 1:4  to Titus, a genuine child in a shared faith: grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.
Titus 1:5  For this reason I left you in Crete, so that you might put in order what remained unfinished and appoint elders in every city, as I directed you—
Titus 1:6  if anyone is beyond reproach, the husband of one wife, having faithful children who are not accused of reckless living or insubordinate.
Titus 1:7  For the overseer must be beyond reproach as God’s steward, not self-willed, not quick-tempered, not given to wine, not violent, not greedy for shameful gain,
Titus 1:8  but hospitable, loving what is good, self-controlled, just, devout, disciplined,
Titus 1:9  holding firmly to the trustworthy word in accordance with the teaching, so that he may be able both to encourage through sound teaching and to refute those who contradict it.
Titus 1:10  For there are also many insubordinate people, empty talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision,
Titus 1:11  whose mouths must be stopped. They overturn whole households, teaching what they ought not to teach for the sake of shameful gain.
Titus 1:12  One of their own, a prophet of theirs, said, “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, idle bellies.”
Titus 1:13  This testimony is true. For that reason, rebuke them sharply, so that they may be sound in the faith,
Titus 1:14  not paying attention to Jewish myths and commands of people who turn away from the truth.
Titus 1:15  To the pure, everything is pure; but to those who are defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure. Instead, both their mind and their conscience are defiled.
Titus 1:16  They profess to know God, but by their deeds they deny Him, being detestable and disobedient and unfit for every good work.

Titus 2
Titus 2:1  But you, speak what is fitting for sound teaching.
Titus 2:2  Older men are to be sober, dignified, self-controlled, sound in faith, in love, and in endurance.
Titus 2:3  Older women likewise are to be reverent in their conduct, not slanderers or enslaved to much wine, teachers of what is good,
Titus 2:4  so that they may train the younger women to love their husbands, to love their children,
Titus 2:5  to be self-controlled, pure, working at home, good, subject to their own husbands, so that God’s word may not be reviled.
Titus 2:6  Likewise, encourage the younger men to be self-controlled
Titus 2:7  in everything. Present yourself as a model of good works, showing integrity in teaching, dignity,
Titus 2:8  and sound speech that cannot be condemned, so that the opponent may be put to shame, having nothing bad to say about us.
Titus 2:9  Slaves are to be subject to their own masters in everything, to be pleasing to them, not contradicting them,
Titus 2:10  not pilfering, but showing complete good faith, so that in everything they may adorn the teaching of God our Savior.
Titus 2:11  For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation for all people,
Titus 2:12  training us so that, denying ungodliness and worldly desires, we may live self-controlled, just, and godly lives in the present age,
Titus 2:13  awaiting the blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ,
Titus 2:14  who gave Himself for us, so that He might ransom us from all lawlessness and purify for Himself a people for His own possession, eager for good works.
Titus 2:15  Speak these things, encourage, and rebuke with all authority. Let no one disregard you.

Titus 3
Titus 3:1  Remind them to be subject to rulers and authorities, to obey, and to be ready for every good work,
Titus 3:2  to slander no one, to be peaceable, considerate, showing complete gentleness toward all people.
Titus 3:3  For we too were once foolish, disobedient, led astray, enslaved to various desires and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, hating one another.
Titus 3:4  But when the kindness of God our Savior and His love for humanity appeared,
Titus 3:5  He saved us, not on the basis of works done by us in righteousness, but according to His mercy, through the washing of regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit,
Titus 3:6  whom He poured out richly upon us through Jesus Christ our Savior,
Titus 3:7  so that, justified by His grace, we might become heirs in accordance with the hope of eternal life.
Titus 3:8  The saying is trustworthy, and I want you to insist on these things, so that those who have believed God may take care to devote themselves to good works. These things are good and beneficial to people.
Titus 3:9  But avoid foolish controversies, genealogies, disputes, and quarrels about the law, for they are unprofitable and futile.
Titus 3:10  After a first and a second warning, have nothing further to do with a divisive person,
Titus 3:11  knowing that such a person has become perverted and is sinning, being self-condemned.
Titus 3:12  When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, make every effort to come to me at Nicopolis, for I have decided to spend the winter there.
Titus 3:13  Make every effort to send Zenas the legal expert and Apollos on their way, so that they lack nothing.
Titus 3:14  Let our people also learn to devote themselves to good works to meet essential needs, so that they may not be unfruitful.
Titus 3:15  All those with me greet you. Greet those who love us in faith. Grace be with all of you.

PHILEMON

Philemon 1
Philemon 1:1  Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy the brother, to Philemon, our beloved fellow worker,
Philemon 1:2  and to Apphia the sister, and Archippus our fellow soldier, and the Church in your house:
Philemon 1:3  Grace to you all and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Philemon 1:4  I thank my God always, remembering you in my prayers,
Philemon 1:5  hearing of your love and the faith that you have toward the Lord Jesus and toward all the saints,
Philemon 1:6  that the fellowship of your faith may become effective through recognition of every good thing among us for Christ.
Philemon 1:7  For I had great joy and encouragement because of your love, because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you, brother.
Philemon 1:8  Therefore, although I have great boldness in Christ to command you to do what is fitting,
Philemon 1:9  I appeal instead because of love, being as I am, Paul, an old man and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus—
Philemon 1:10  I appeal to you for my child Onesimus, whose father I became while in chains,
Philemon 1:11  who was once useless to you, but is now useful both to you and to me.
Philemon 1:12  I have sent him back to you—him, that is, my very heart.
Philemon 1:13  I wanted to keep him with me, so that in your place he might serve me in my chains for the gospel.
Philemon 1:14  But without your consent I did not want to do anything, so that your good deed might be voluntary, rather than as though compelled.
Philemon 1:15  For perhaps he was separated from you for a little while for this reason: that you might have him back forever,
Philemon 1:16  no longer as a slave, but more than a slave, a beloved brother, especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
Philemon 1:17  So if you regard me as a partner, welcome him as you would me.
Philemon 1:18  And if he has wronged you in anything, or owes you anything, charge that to my account.
Philemon 1:19  I, Paul, write this with my own hand: I will repay it—not to mention that you owe me even your own self.
Philemon 1:20  Yes, brother, let me have this benefit from you in the Lord; refresh my heart in Christ.
Philemon 1:21  Confident of your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I say.
Philemon 1:22  At the same time, prepare lodging for me also, for I hope that through your prayers I will be graciously given to you.
Philemon 1:23  Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, greets you,
Philemon 1:24  as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers.
Philemon 1:25  The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.

HEBREWS

Hebrews 1
Hebrews 1:1  In many portions and in many ways, God spoke long ago to the fathers in the prophets,
Hebrews 1:2  but in these last days He spoke to us in a Son, whom He appointed heir of all things, through whom He also made the ages.
Hebrews 1:3  He is the radiance of His glory and the imprint of His being, upholding all things by the word of His power. Having made purification of sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high,
Hebrews 1:4  having become so much greater than the angels as the name He has inherited is more excellent than theirs.
Hebrews 1:5  For to which of the angels did He ever say, “Thou art My Son; today I have begotten Thee”? And again, “I will be a Father to Him, and He will be a Son to Me”?
Hebrews 1:6  And when He again brings the firstborn into the inhabited world, He says, “And let all God’s angels worship Him.”
Hebrews 1:7  And concerning the angels He says, “He makes His angels spirits, and His ministers a flame of fire.”
Hebrews 1:8  But concerning the Son, “Thy throne, O God, endures forever and ever, and the scepter of uprightness is the scepter of Thy kingdom.
Hebrews 1:9  Thou didst love righteousness and hate lawlessness; for this reason God, Thy God, anointed Thee with the oil of exultation beyond Thy companions.”
Hebrews 1:10  And, “Thou, Lord, didst lay the foundation of the earth in the beginning, and the heavens are the works of Thy hands.
Hebrews 1:11  They will perish, but Thou remainest; and all will grow old like a garment,
Hebrews 1:12  and like a cloak Thou wilt roll them up; like a garment they will also be changed. But Thou art the same, and Thy years will not fail.”
Hebrews 1:13  But to which of the angels has He ever said, “Sit at My right hand until I make Thine enemies a footstool for Thy feet”?
Hebrews 1:14  Are they not all ministering spirits, sent out for service for the sake of those who are to inherit salvation?

Hebrews 2
Hebrews 2:1  For this reason we must pay all the more attention to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away.
Hebrews 2:2  For if the word spoken through angels became firm, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompense,
Hebrews 2:3  how will we escape if we neglect so great a salvation? It was first spoken through the Lord and was confirmed to us by those who heard,
Hebrews 2:4  God bearing witness together with signs and wonders and various mighty deeds and distributions of the Holy Spirit according to His own will.
Hebrews 2:5  For He did not subject to angels the inhabited world to come, of which we speak.
Hebrews 2:6  But someone testified somewhere, saying, “What is a human being, that Thou rememberest him, or a son of man, that Thou carest for him?
Hebrews 2:7  Thou didst make him a little lower than angels; Thou didst crown him with glory and honor;
Hebrews 2:8  Thou didst subject all things beneath his feet.” For in subjecting all things to him, He left nothing unsubjected to him. But now we do not yet see all things subjected to him.
Hebrews 2:9  But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than angels, crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death, so that by the grace of God He might taste death on behalf of everyone.
Hebrews 2:10  For it was fitting for Him, for whom are all things and through whom are all things, in bringing many sons into glory, to perfect the pioneer of their salvation through sufferings.
Hebrews 2:11  For both the One who sanctifies and those being sanctified are all from one. For this reason He is not ashamed to call them brothers,
Hebrews 2:12  saying, “I will announce Thy name to My brothers; in the midst of the assembly I will sing praise to Thee.”
Hebrews 2:13  And again, “I will put My trust in Him.” And again, “Behold, I and the children whom God gave Me.”
Hebrews 2:14  Therefore, since the children have shared in blood and flesh, He Himself likewise partook of the same, so that through death He might render powerless the one who has the power of death, that is, the devil,
Hebrews 2:15  and release those who through fear of death were subject to slavery throughout their whole lives.
Hebrews 2:16  For surely it is not angels He takes hold of, but He takes hold of Abraham’s seed.
Hebrews 2:17  Therefore He had to be made like His brothers in all things, so that He might become a merciful and faithful high priest in matters concerning God, to make propitiation for the sins of the people.
Hebrews 2:18  For because He Himself suffered when tested, He is able to help those who are being tested.

Hebrews 3
Hebrews 3:1  Therefore, holy brothers, partakers of a heavenly calling, consider the apostle and high priest of our confession, Jesus,
Hebrews 3:2  who is faithful to the One who appointed Him, as Moses also was in all His house.
Hebrews 3:3  For He has been considered worthy of greater glory than Moses, just as the one who builds a house has greater honor than the house.
Hebrews 3:4  For every house is built by someone, but the One who built all things is God.
Hebrews 3:5  And Moses indeed was faithful in all His house as an attendant, for a testimony of the things to be spoken,
Hebrews 3:6  but Christ as a Son over His house. We are that house if indeed we hold fast our confidence and the boast of our hope.
Hebrews 3:7  Therefore, just as the Holy Spirit says, “Today, if you hear His voice,
Hebrews 3:8  do not harden your hearts as in the provocation, on the day of testing in the wilderness,
Hebrews 3:9  where your fathers put Me to the test and saw My works
Hebrews 3:10  for forty years. Therefore I was indignant with this generation and said, ‘They always wander in their heart, and they did not know My ways,’
Hebrews 3:11  as I swore in My wrath, ‘They shall certainly not enter My rest.’”
Hebrews 3:12  Watch out, brothers, so that none of you has an evil, unbelieving heart that turns away from the living God.
Hebrews 3:13  But encourage one another each day, as long as it is called “Today,” so that none of you may be hardened by the deceit of sin.
Hebrews 3:14  For we have become partakers of Christ if indeed we hold firm the beginning of our confidence until the end,
Hebrews 3:15  while it is said, “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts as in the provocation.”
Hebrews 3:16  For who, having heard, provoked Him? Was it not all who came out of Egypt through Moses?
Hebrews 3:17  And with whom was He indignant for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
Hebrews 3:18  And to whom did He swear that they would not enter His rest, except those who disobeyed?
Hebrews 3:19  And we see that they could not enter because of unbelief.

Hebrews 4
Hebrews 4:1  Therefore let us fear, lest, while a promise remains of entering His rest, any of you should seem to have fallen short.
Hebrews 4:2  For we too have received good news just as they did, but the word they heard did not benefit them, because they had not been united by faith with those who heard.
Hebrews 4:3  For we who believed enter the rest, just as He has said, “As I swore in My wrath, ‘They shall certainly not enter My rest,’” although the works came into being from the foundation of the world.
Hebrews 4:4  For He has said somewhere about the seventh day in this way, “And God rested on the seventh day from all His works.”
Hebrews 4:5  And in this passage again, “They shall certainly not enter My rest.”
Hebrews 4:6  Since, then, it remains for some to enter it, and those who formerly received the good news did not enter because of disobedience,
Hebrews 4:7  He again appoints a certain day, “Today,” saying in David after so long a time, just as has been said before, “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.”
Hebrews 4:8  For if Joshua had given them rest, He would not have spoken after these things about another day.
Hebrews 4:9  So then, a Sabbath rest remains for the people of God.
Hebrews 4:10  For the one who entered His rest also rested from his own works, just as God did from His own.
Hebrews 4:11  Therefore let us be diligent to enter that rest, so that no one may fall in the same pattern of disobedience.
Hebrews 4:12  For the word of God is living and active and sharper than any two-edged sword, penetrating as far as the division of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
Hebrews 4:13  And no created thing is hidden before Him, but all things are naked and laid open to His eyes, to whom we must give account.
Hebrews 4:14  Therefore, having a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast the confession.
Hebrews 4:15  For we do not have a high priest unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but One who has been tested in every way as we are, yet without sin.
Hebrews 4:16  Therefore let us approach the throne of grace with boldness, so that we may receive mercy and find grace for help at the right time.

Hebrews 5
Hebrews 5:1  For every high priest taken from among people is appointed on behalf of people in matters concerning God, to offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins.
Hebrews 5:2  He can deal gently with those who are ignorant and wandering, since he too is surrounded by weakness,
Hebrews 5:3  and because of it he is obliged to make offerings for sins on his own behalf, just as on behalf of the people.
Hebrews 5:4  And no one takes the honor for himself, but receives it when called by God, just as Aaron was.
Hebrews 5:5  So also Christ did not glorify Himself to become high priest, but the One who said to Him, “Thou art My Son; today I have begotten Thee,”
Hebrews 5:6  as He also says in another place, “Thou art a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
Hebrews 5:7  In the days of His flesh, He offered petitions and supplications, with loud crying and tears, to the One able to save Him out of death, and was heard because of His reverent fear.
Hebrews 5:8  Although He was a Son, He learned obedience from the things He suffered,
Hebrews 5:9  and, having been perfected, He became the source of eternal salvation for all who obey Him,
Hebrews 5:10  having been designated by God high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.
Hebrews 5:11  Concerning this we have much to say, and it is hard to explain, since you have become slow to hear.
Hebrews 5:12  For although by this time you ought to be teachers, you again need someone to teach you the first elements of God’s oracles; you have come to need milk and not solid food.
Hebrews 5:13  For everyone who partakes of milk is inexperienced in the word of righteousness, for he is an infant.
Hebrews 5:14  But solid food belongs to the mature, whose faculties have been trained by practice to distinguish both good and evil.

Hebrews 6
Hebrews 6:1  Therefore, leaving the elementary teaching about Christ, let us be carried on to maturity, without laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works and faith toward God,
Hebrews 6:2  of instruction about washings and the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.
Hebrews 6:3  And this we will do, if indeed God permits.
Hebrews 6:4  For it is impossible to renew again to repentance those who were once enlightened, tasted the heavenly gift, became partakers of the Holy Spirit,
Hebrews 6:5  and tasted God’s good word and the powers of the coming age,
Hebrews 6:6  and fell away, since they are crucifying the Son of God again for themselves and exposing Him to public disgrace.
Hebrews 6:7  For land that drinks the rain often coming upon it, and produces vegetation useful to those for whose sake it is cultivated, shares in blessing from God.
Hebrews 6:8  But if it bears thorns and thistles, it is rejected and near a curse; its end is burning.
Hebrews 6:9  But concerning you, beloved, we are convinced of better things—things accompanying salvation—even though we speak this way.
Hebrews 6:10  For God is not unjust so as to forget your work and the love you showed toward His name by serving the saints, as you still serve them.
Hebrews 6:11  And we desire each of you to show the same diligence toward the full assurance of hope until the end,
Hebrews 6:12  so that you may not become sluggish, but imitators of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
Hebrews 6:13  For when God made a promise to Abraham, since He had no one greater by whom to swear, He swore by Himself,
Hebrews 6:14  saying, “Surely, blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply you.”
Hebrews 6:15  And so, having waited patiently, he obtained the promise.
Hebrews 6:16  For people swear by one greater, and among them an oath for confirmation ends every dispute.
Hebrews 6:17  In this, God, wishing to show more fully to the heirs of the promise the unchanging nature of His purpose, intervened with an oath,
Hebrews 6:18  so that through two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled for refuge might have strong encouragement to hold fast the hope set before us.
Hebrews 6:19  We have this hope as an anchor of the soul, both secure and firm, entering the inner place behind the veil,
Hebrews 6:20  where Jesus entered as a forerunner on our behalf, having become high priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.

Hebrews 7
Hebrews 7:1  For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him.
Hebrews 7:2  Abraham also apportioned to him a tenth of everything. His name is interpreted first as king of righteousness, and then also king of Salem, which is king of peace.
Hebrews 7:3  Without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither a beginning of days nor an end of life, but made like the Son of God, he remains a priest continually.
Hebrews 7:4  Consider how great this man was, to whom even Abraham the patriarch gave a tenth from the choice spoils.
Hebrews 7:5  Those from the sons of Levi who receive the priestly office have a commandment, according to the law, to collect a tenth from the people—that is, from their brothers—although they too have come from Abraham’s loins.
Hebrews 7:6  But the one whose genealogy is not traced from them has received a tenth from Abraham and has blessed the one who had the promises.
Hebrews 7:7  And beyond all dispute, the lesser is blessed by the greater.
Hebrews 7:8  Here, people who die receive tenths; but there, one of whom it is testified that he lives.
Hebrews 7:9  And, so to speak, through Abraham even Levi, who receives tenths, has paid a tenth,
Hebrews 7:10  for he was still in his father’s loins when Melchizedek met him.
Hebrews 7:11  Now if perfection came through the Levitical priesthood—for on its basis the people received the law—what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not to be spoken of according to the order of Aaron?
Hebrews 7:12  For when the priesthood is changed, a change of law necessarily takes place as well.
Hebrews 7:13  For the One concerning whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has served at the altar.
Hebrews 7:14  For it is clear that our Lord has sprung from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.
Hebrews 7:15  And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
Hebrews 7:16  who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
Hebrews 7:17  For it is testified, “Thou art a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
Hebrews 7:18  For there is a setting aside of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness,
Hebrews 7:19  for the law perfected nothing; and there is the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
Hebrews 7:20  And insofar as this was not without an oath—for those became priests without an oath,
Hebrews 7:21  but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, “The Lord swore and will not change His mind: Thou art a priest forever”—
Hebrews 7:22  to that extent Jesus has also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
Hebrews 7:23  And there were many of those priests, because death prevented them from continuing,
Hebrews 7:24  but He, because He remains forever, has a permanent priesthood.
Hebrews 7:25  Therefore He is also able to save completely those who approach God through Him, since He always lives to intercede on their behalf.
Hebrews 7:26  For such a high priest was indeed fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens.
Hebrews 7:27  He has no daily need, as the high priests do, to offer sacrifices first for His own sins and then for those of the people; for He did this once for all when He offered Himself.
Hebrews 7:28  For the law appoints people subject to weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son, perfected forever.

Hebrews 8
Hebrews 8:1  Now the main point in what is being said is this: we have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,
Hebrews 8:2  a minister of the holy places and of the true tent, which the Lord pitched, not a human being.
Hebrews 8:3  For every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices; therefore this One too must have something to offer.
Hebrews 8:4  Now if He were on earth, He would not even be a priest, since there are those who offer the gifts according to law.
Hebrews 8:5  They serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things, just as Moses was instructed when he was about to complete the tent. For He says, “See that you make everything according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain.”
Hebrews 8:6  But now He has obtained a more excellent ministry, insofar as He is also mediator of a better covenant, which has been established as law upon better promises.
Hebrews 8:7  For if that first covenant had been faultless, no place would have been sought for a second.
Hebrews 8:8  For, finding fault with them, He says, “Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will conclude a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,
Hebrews 8:9  not according to the covenant I made with their fathers on the day I took hold of their hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not remain in My covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord.
Hebrews 8:10  For this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws into their mind, I will also inscribe them upon their hearts, and I will be their God, and they will be My people.
Hebrews 8:11  And they shall certainly not teach, each his fellow citizen and each his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ because all will know Me, from the least of them to the greatest.
Hebrews 8:12  For I will be merciful toward their wrongdoings, and I will certainly remember their sins no more.”
Hebrews 8:13  By saying “new,” He has made the first old. And what is growing old and aging is close to disappearing.

Hebrews 9
Hebrews 9:1  Now the first covenant also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
Hebrews 9:2  For a tent was prepared, the first, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the loaves; it is called the Holy Place.
Hebrews 9:3  And behind the second curtain was a tent called the Holy of Holies,
Hebrews 9:4  having a golden incense altar and the ark of the covenant, covered on every side with gold. In it were a golden jar containing the manna, Aaron’s rod that had sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant.
Hebrews 9:5  Above it were cherubim of glory overshadowing the atonement cover. We cannot now speak of these things in detail.
Hebrews 9:6  With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship.
Hebrews 9:7  But into the second only the high priest enters, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s sins of ignorance.
Hebrews 9:8  By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy places has not yet been disclosed while the first tent still has its standing.
Hebrews 9:9  This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
Hebrews 9:10  They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
Hebrews 9:11  But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
Hebrews 9:12  and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
Hebrews 9:13  For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify for the cleanness of the flesh,
Hebrews 9:14  how much more will the blood of Christ, who through an eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God!
Hebrews 9:15  And for this reason He is mediator of a new covenant, so that those who have been called might receive the promise of the eternal inheritance, since a death has occurred for redemption from the transgressions under the first covenant.
Hebrews 9:16  For where there is a testament, the death of the one who made it must be established.
Hebrews 9:17  For a testament takes effect at death, since it is never in force while the one who made it lives.
Hebrews 9:18  Therefore even the first covenant was not inaugurated without blood.
Hebrews 9:19  For when Moses had spoken every commandment according to the law to all the people, he took the blood of the calves and the goats, with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,
Hebrews 9:20  saying, “This is the blood of the covenant that God commanded for you.”
Hebrews 9:21  And he likewise sprinkled the tent and all the vessels of ministry with the blood.
Hebrews 9:22  And according to the law almost everything is cleansed with blood, and without the shedding of blood no forgiveness takes place.
Hebrews 9:23  Therefore it was necessary for the copies of the things in the heavens to be cleansed with these, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
Hebrews 9:24  For Christ did not enter holy places made by hands, counterparts of the true ones, but heaven itself, now to appear before the face of God on our behalf.
Hebrews 9:25  Nor did He enter to offer Himself many times, as the high priest enters the holy places year by year with another’s blood,
Hebrews 9:26  for then He would have had to suffer many times since the foundation of the world. But now, once at the end of the ages, He has appeared to set aside sin through His sacrifice.
Hebrews 9:27  And just as it is appointed for people to die once, and after this judgment,
Hebrews 9:28  so also Christ, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, apart from sin, to those eagerly awaiting Him, for salvation.

Hebrews 10
Hebrews 10:1  For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities, can never perfect those who approach by the same sacrifices offered continually year by year.
Hebrews 10:2  Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
Hebrews 10:3  But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
Hebrews 10:4  for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Hebrews 10:5  Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
Hebrews 10:6  In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Hebrews 10:7  Then I said, ‘Behold, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written concerning Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
Hebrews 10:8  After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
Hebrews 10:9  He then said, “Behold, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
Hebrews 10:10  By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
Hebrews 10:11  And every priest stands daily, ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.
Hebrews 10:12  But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
Hebrews 10:13  from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
Hebrews 10:14  For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
Hebrews 10:15  And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,
Hebrews 10:16  “This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws upon their hearts, I will also inscribe them upon their mind,”
Hebrews 10:17  He adds, “And their sins and their lawless deeds I will certainly remember no more.”
Hebrews 10:18  Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.
Hebrews 10:19  Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence for entry into the holy places in the blood of Jesus,
Hebrews 10:20  by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
Hebrews 10:21  and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
Hebrews 10:22  let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.
Hebrews 10:23  Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering, for the One who promised is faithful.
Hebrews 10:24  And let us consider one another, to stir up love and good works,
Hebrews 10:25  not abandoning our own gathering together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the day drawing near.
Hebrews 10:26  For if we sin deliberately after receiving the knowledge of the truth, no sacrifice for sins remains,
Hebrews 10:27  but a fearful expectation of judgment and a fury of fire about to consume the adversaries.
Hebrews 10:28  Anyone who has set aside the law of Moses dies without compassion on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
Hebrews 10:29  How much worse punishment do you think will be deserved by the one who has trampled the Son of God underfoot, regarded as common the blood of the covenant by which he was sanctified, and insulted the Spirit of grace?
Hebrews 10:30  For we know the One who said, “Vengeance belongs to Me; I will repay.” And again, “The Lord will judge His people.”
Hebrews 10:31  It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
Hebrews 10:32  But remember the earlier days, in which, after being enlightened, you endured a great contest of sufferings,
Hebrews 10:33  at one time publicly exposed to reproaches and afflictions, at another becoming companions of those treated in this way.
Hebrews 10:34  For you sympathized with the prisoners, and you accepted the seizure of your possessions with joy, knowing that you yourselves have a better possession, and a lasting one.
Hebrews 10:35  Therefore do not throw away your confidence, which has a great reward.
Hebrews 10:36  For you need endurance, so that, having done the will of God, you may receive the promise.
Hebrews 10:37  “For yet a very little while, the coming One will come and will not delay.
Hebrews 10:38  But My righteous one will live by faith; and if he draws back, My soul takes no pleasure in him.”
Hebrews 10:39  But we are not people who draw back to destruction, but people of faith for the preservation of the soul.

Hebrews 11
Hebrews 11:1  Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of realities not seen.
Hebrews 11:2  For by it the elders received testimony.
Hebrews 11:3  By faith we understand that the ages were formed by God’s word, so that what is seen did not come into being from visible things.
Hebrews 11:4  By faith Abel offered God a greater sacrifice than Cain, through which he received testimony that he was righteous, God testifying concerning his gifts; and through it, though he died, he still speaks.
Hebrews 11:5  By faith Enoch was taken away so as not to see death, and he was not found, because God took him away. For before his taking away he had received testimony that he had pleased God.
Hebrews 11:6  And without faith it is impossible to please Him, for the one approaching God must believe that He is and that He becomes a rewarder of those who seek Him.
Hebrews 11:7  By faith Noah, instructed concerning things not yet seen, acted with reverent fear and prepared an ark for the salvation of his household. Through this he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness according to faith.
Hebrews 11:8  By faith Abraham, when called, obeyed by going out to a place he was to receive as an inheritance; and he went out without knowing where he was going.
Hebrews 11:9  By faith he lived as a foreigner in the land of the promise as in a foreign land, dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, fellow heirs of the same promise.
Hebrews 11:10  For he was awaiting the city that has foundations, whose craftsman and maker is God.
Hebrews 11:11  By faith even Sarah herself, though barren, received power to conceive offspring even beyond the proper age, since she considered the One who promised faithful.
Hebrews 11:12  Therefore from one man, and that one as good as dead, there were born as many as the stars of heaven in multitude and as the innumerable sand along the seashore.
Hebrews 11:13  All these died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen and greeted them from afar and confessed that they were strangers and sojourners upon the earth.
Hebrews 11:14  For those who say such things make clear that they are seeking a homeland.
Hebrews 11:15  And if they had been thinking of that land from which they went out, they would have had opportunity to return.
Hebrews 11:16  But now they desire a better one, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed of them, to be called their God, for He has prepared a city for them.
Hebrews 11:17  By faith Abraham, when tested, offered Isaac; and the one who had welcomed the promises was offering his only son,
Hebrews 11:18  to whom it had been said, “In Isaac offspring will be named for you.”
Hebrews 11:19  He reasoned that God is able even to raise the dead; from there he also received him back, figuratively speaking.
Hebrews 11:20  By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau also concerning things to come.
Hebrews 11:21  By faith Jacob, when dying, blessed each of Joseph’s sons, and worshiped over the top of his staff.
Hebrews 11:22  By faith Joseph, when nearing his end, spoke of the exodus of the sons of Israel and gave instructions concerning his bones.
Hebrews 11:23  By faith Moses, when born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that the child was beautiful and did not fear the king’s decree.
Hebrews 11:24  By faith Moses, when grown, refused to be called a son of Pharaoh’s daughter,
Hebrews 11:25  choosing rather to be mistreated with the people of God than to have the temporary enjoyment of sin.
Hebrews 11:26  He considered the reproach of Christ greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking toward the reward.
Hebrews 11:27  By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the king’s anger, for he endured as though seeing the invisible One.
Hebrews 11:28  By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn might not touch them.
Hebrews 11:29  By faith they crossed the Red Sea as through dry land; when the Egyptians attempted it, they were swallowed up.
Hebrews 11:30  By faith the walls of Jericho fell after being encircled for seven days.
Hebrews 11:31  By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with those who disobeyed, having received the spies in peace.
Hebrews 11:32  And what more shall I say? For time will fail me as I recount Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David and Samuel and the prophets,
Hebrews 11:33  who through faith subdued kingdoms, worked righteousness, obtained promises, shut the mouths of lions,
Hebrews 11:34  extinguished the power of fire, escaped the edges of the sword, were strengthened from weakness, became mighty in battle, and turned back the armies of foreigners.
Hebrews 11:35  Women received their dead through resurrection. But others were tortured, not accepting release, so that they might obtain a better resurrection.
