Hebrews 11:36  And others experienced mockery and flogging, and also chains and imprisonment.
Hebrews 11:37  They were stoned, sawn apart, and died by slaughter with the sword. They went about in sheepskins, in goatskins, being destitute, afflicted, and mistreated—
Hebrews 11:38  of whom the world was not worthy—wandering in deserts and mountains and caves and the holes of the earth.
Hebrews 11:39  And all these, though they received testimony through faith, did not receive the promise,
Hebrews 11:40  since God had provided something better concerning us, so that they should not be perfected apart from us.

Hebrews 12
Hebrews 12:1  Therefore, since we too have so great a cloud of witnesses surrounding us, let us lay aside every weight and the sin that readily entangles us, and run with endurance the race set before us,
Hebrews 12:2  looking away to Jesus, the pioneer and perfecter of faith. For the joy set before Him He endured a cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
Hebrews 12:3  For consider the One who has endured such opposition from sinners against Himself, so that you may not grow weary, fainting in your souls.
Hebrews 12:4  You have not yet resisted to the point of blood in your struggle against sin,
Hebrews 12:5  and you have forgotten the encouragement that addresses you as sons: “My son, do not make light of the Lord’s discipline, nor faint when reproved by Him.
Hebrews 12:6  For the Lord disciplines the one He loves, and scourges every son He receives.”
Hebrews 12:7  Endure for discipline. God deals with you as sons; for what son is there whom a father does not discipline?
Hebrews 12:8  But if you are without discipline, in which all have become partakers, then you are illegitimate children and not sons.
Hebrews 12:9  Furthermore, we had our fathers in the flesh to discipline us, and we respected them. But shall we not much more submit to the Father of spirits and live?
Hebrews 12:10  For they disciplined us for a few days according to what seemed right to them, but He for our benefit, so that we may share in His holiness.
Hebrews 12:11  Now every discipline seems for the present to be a matter of sorrow, not joy, but afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those trained through it.
Hebrews 12:12  Therefore straighten the drooping hands and the weakened knees,
Hebrews 12:13  and make straight tracks for your feet, so that what is lame may not be dislocated, but rather healed.
Hebrews 12:14  Pursue peace with everyone, and sanctification, without which no one will see the Lord.
Hebrews 12:15  Watch lest anyone fall short of the grace of God, lest any root of bitterness grow up and cause trouble, and through it many be defiled,
Hebrews 12:16  lest anyone be sexually immoral or profane like Esau, who sold his own birthright for a single meal.
Hebrews 12:17  For you know that even afterward, when he desired to inherit the blessing, he was rejected, for he found no place for repentance, although he sought it with tears.
Hebrews 12:18  For you have not approached what can be touched, and a blazing fire, and gloom and darkness and storm,
Hebrews 12:19  and the sound of a trumpet and a voice speaking words, whose hearers begged that no further word be spoken to them.
Hebrews 12:20  For they could not bear the command: “Even if an animal touches the mountain, it shall be stoned.”
Hebrews 12:21  And so fearful was the sight that Moses said, “I am terrified and trembling.”
Hebrews 12:22  But you have approached Mount Zion and the city of the living God, heavenly Jerusalem, and myriads of angels in festive gathering,
Hebrews 12:23  and the assembly of firstborn ones enrolled in the heavens, and God the judge of all, and the spirits of righteous ones who have been perfected,
Hebrews 12:24  and Jesus the mediator of a new covenant, and sprinkled blood that speaks better than Abel.
Hebrews 12:25  See that you do not refuse the One who speaks. For if those who refused the One instructing them on earth did not escape, much less shall we, if we turn away from the One from the heavens.
Hebrews 12:26  His voice shook the earth then, but now He has promised, saying, “Yet once more I will shake not only the earth but also the heaven.”
Hebrews 12:27  Now “yet once more” indicates the removal of the things shaken, as things that have been made, so that the things not shaken may remain.
Hebrews 12:28  Therefore, since we are receiving an unshakable kingdom, let us be grateful, and through this gratitude serve God acceptably with reverence and awe,
Hebrews 12:29  for indeed our God is a consuming fire.

Hebrews 13
Hebrews 13:1  Let brotherly love remain.
Hebrews 13:2  Do not forget hospitality, for through it some unknowingly entertained angels.
Hebrews 13:3  Remember the prisoners as fellow prisoners, and those being mistreated, as you yourselves also are in a body.
Hebrews 13:4  Let marriage be honored among all, and the marriage bed undefiled, for God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers.
Hebrews 13:5  Let your way of life be free from the love of money, being content with what you have; for He Himself has said, “I will certainly not leave you, nor will I ever forsake you.”
Hebrews 13:6  So we may say with confidence, “The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear. What will a person do to me?”
Hebrews 13:7  Remember your leaders, who spoke the word of God to you. As you consider the outcome of their way of life, imitate their faith.
Hebrews 13:8  Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and for the ages.
Hebrews 13:9  Do not be carried away by varied and strange teachings, for it is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace, not by foods, which have not benefited those occupied with them.
Hebrews 13:10  We have an altar from which those serving the tent have no right to eat.
Hebrews 13:11  For the bodies of those animals whose blood the high priest brings into the holy places for sin are burned outside the camp.
Hebrews 13:12  Therefore Jesus also suffered outside the gate, so that He might sanctify the people through His own blood.
Hebrews 13:13  So let us go out to Him outside the camp, bearing His reproach.
Hebrews 13:14  For here we have no lasting city, but we seek the one to come.
Hebrews 13:15  Therefore through Him let us continually offer God a sacrifice of praise, that is, the fruit of lips confessing His name.
Hebrews 13:16  And do not forget to do good and to share, for God is pleased with such sacrifices.
Hebrews 13:17  Obey your leaders and yield to them, for they keep watch over your souls as those who will give an account, so that they may do this with joy and not groaning, for that would be unprofitable for you.
Hebrews 13:18  Pray for us, for we are convinced that we have a good conscience, wishing to conduct ourselves well in everything.
Hebrews 13:19  And I urge you all the more to do this, so that I may be restored to you sooner.
Hebrews 13:20  Now may the God of peace, who brought up from the dead the great shepherd of the sheep, our Lord Jesus, in the blood of an eternal covenant,
Hebrews 13:21  equip you with every good thing to do His will, working in us what is pleasing in His sight, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory for the ages of ages. Amen.
Hebrews 13:22  And I urge you, brothers, bear with the word of encouragement, for I have written to you briefly.
Hebrews 13:23  Know that our brother Timothy has been released; if he comes soon, I will see you with him.
Hebrews 13:24  Greet all your leaders and all the saints. Those from Italy greet you.
Hebrews 13:25  Grace be with you all.

JAMES

James 1
James 1:1  James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes in the dispersion: greetings.
James 1:2  Count it all joy, my brothers, whenever you encounter trials of various kinds,
James 1:3  knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance.
James 1:4  And let endurance have its complete work, so that you may be complete and whole, lacking in nothing.
James 1:5  But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives to all generously and without reproach, and it will be given to him.
James 1:6  But let him ask in faith, doubting nothing, for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind.
James 1:7  For that person must not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord,
James 1:8  a man of divided mind, unstable in all his ways.
James 1:9  Let the lowly brother boast in his exaltation,
James 1:10  and the rich person in his humiliation, because he will pass away like a flower of grass.
James 1:11  For the sun rose with its scorching heat and dried the grass, and its flower fell, and the beauty of its appearance perished. So also the rich person will wither in his pursuits.
James 1:12  Blessed is the man who endures a trial, because, having been approved, he will receive the crown of life that He promised to those who love Him.
James 1:13  Let no one who is tempted say, “I am being tempted by God.” For God cannot be tempted by evil, and He Himself tempts no one.
James 1:14  But each person is tempted when drawn away and enticed by his own desire.
James 1:15  Then desire, after conceiving, gives birth to sin; and sin, when fully grown, gives birth to death.
James 1:16  Do not be led astray, my beloved brothers.
James 1:17  Every good act of giving and every complete gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow from turning.
James 1:18  By His will He gave us birth through the word of truth, so that we might be a kind of firstfruits of His creatures.
James 1:19  Know this, my beloved brothers: let every person be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger,
James 1:20  for a man’s anger does not accomplish the righteousness of God.
James 1:21  Therefore, putting away every impurity and the abundance of evil, receive with gentleness the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
James 1:22  But become doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves.
James 1:23  For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man looking at his natural face in a mirror,
James 1:24  for he looked at himself and went away and immediately forgot what he was like.
James 1:25  But the one who looks closely into the complete law, the law of freedom, and continues in it—not a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work—will be blessed in what he does.
James 1:26  If anyone thinks he is religious while not bridling his tongue but deceiving his heart, that person’s religion is futile.
James 1:27  Religion that is pure and undefiled before God the Father is this: to care for orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.

James 2
James 2:1  My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with acts of favoritism.
James 2:2  For if a man with gold rings and splendid clothing enters your gathering, and a poor person in filthy clothing also enters,
James 2:3  and you pay attention to the one wearing splendid clothing and say, “You sit here in a good place,” but say to the poor person, “You stand, or sit there beneath my footstool,”
James 2:4  have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?
James 2:5  Listen, my beloved brothers: has not God chosen those poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom He promised to those who love Him?
James 2:6  But you have dishonored the poor person. Is it not the rich who oppress you and drag you into courts?
James 2:7  Do they not blaspheme the good name called over you?
James 2:8  If, however, you fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you do well.
James 2:9  But if you show favoritism, you commit sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors.
James 2:10  For whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles in one point has become accountable for all of it.
James 2:11  For He who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not murder.” Now if you do not commit adultery but do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law.
James 2:12  So speak and so act as those who are going to be judged through a law of freedom.
James 2:13  For judgment is without mercy to the one who has shown no mercy; mercy triumphs over judgment.
James 2:14  What good is it, my brothers, if someone says he has faith but does not have works? Can that faith save him?
James 2:15  If a brother or sister is without clothing and lacks daily food,
James 2:16  and one of you says to them, “Go in peace; be warmed and filled,” but you do not give them what the body needs, what good is it?
James 2:17  So also faith, if it does not have works, is dead by itself.
James 2:18  But someone will say, “You have faith, and I have works.” Show me your faith apart from works, and I will show you faith by my works.
James 2:19  You believe that God is one. You do well. Even the demons believe—and shudder.
James 2:20  But do you want to know, empty man, that faith apart from works is idle?
James 2:21  Was not Abraham our father justified by works when he offered Isaac his son upon the altar?
James 2:22  You see that faith was working together with his works, and by the works faith was brought to completion,
James 2:23  and the Scripture was fulfilled that says, “Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness,” and he was called a friend of God.
James 2:24  You see that a person is justified by works and not by faith alone.
James 2:25  And likewise was not Rahab the prostitute also justified by works, when she welcomed the messengers and sent them out by another way?
James 2:26  For just as the body without spirit is dead, so also faith without works is dead.

James 3
James 3:1  Not many of you should become teachers, my brothers, knowing that we will receive a greater judgment.
James 3:2  For we all stumble in many things. If anyone does not stumble in speech, that person is a complete man, able to bridle his whole body also.
James 3:3  Now if we put bits into horses’ mouths so that they obey us, we guide their whole body also.
James 3:4  Look also at ships: although so large and driven by harsh winds, they are guided by a very small rudder wherever the pilot intends.
James 3:5  So also the tongue is a small member and boasts great things. Look how small a fire sets so great a forest ablaze!
James 3:6  And the tongue is a fire. The tongue is established among our members as a world of unrighteousness, staining the whole body, setting the wheel of life ablaze, and itself set ablaze by Gehenna.
James 3:7  For every kind of wild animal and bird, of creeping creature and sea creature, is tamed and has been tamed by humankind;
James 3:8  but no human being can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.
James 3:9  With it we bless the Lord and Father, and with it we curse human beings who have been made in God’s likeness.
James 3:10  From the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to happen this way.
James 3:11  Does a spring pour out sweet and bitter water from the same opening?
James 3:12  My brothers, can a fig tree produce olives, or a vine figs? Neither can salt water produce sweet water.
James 3:13  Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show his works by good conduct in the gentleness of wisdom.
James 3:14  But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, do not boast against the truth and lie against it.
James 3:15  This is not the wisdom coming down from above; it is earthly, merely natural, demonic.
James 3:16  For where there are jealousy and selfish ambition, there are disorder and every foul practice.
James 3:17  But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, considerate, open to persuasion, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial, without hypocrisy.
James 3:18  And a fruit of righteousness is sown in peace for those who make peace.

James 4
James 4:1  Where do wars come from, and where do fights among you come from? Is it not from here—from your pleasures that wage war in your members?
James 4:2  You desire and do not have; you murder and envy and cannot obtain. You fight and wage war. You do not have because you do not ask.
James 4:3  You ask and do not receive, because you ask badly, so that you may spend it on your pleasures.
James 4:4  Adulteresses! Do you not know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Whoever therefore wishes to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God.
James 4:5  Or do you think Scripture says in vain, “He yearns jealously for the spirit that He made to dwell in us”?
James 4:6  But He gives greater grace. Therefore it says, “God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
James 4:7  Submit yourselves therefore to God; but resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
James 4:8  Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, sinners, and purify your hearts, you of divided mind.
James 4:9  Be wretched and mourn and weep. Let your laughter be turned into mourning and your joy into dejection.
James 4:10  Humble yourselves before the Lord, and He will exalt you.
James 4:11  Do not speak against one another, brothers. The one who speaks against a brother or judges his brother speaks against the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge.
James 4:12  There is one Lawgiver and Judge, the One able to save and destroy. But who are you to judge your neighbor?
James 4:13  Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to this city, spend a year there, trade, and make a profit”—
James 4:14  you who do not know what tomorrow brings. What is your life? For you are a vapor, appearing for a little while and then disappearing.
James 4:15  Instead, you ought to say, “If the Lord wills, we shall both live and do this or that.”
James 4:16  But now you boast in your pretensions. All such boasting is evil.
James 4:17  Therefore, if someone knows the good he ought to do and does not do it, it is sin for him.

James 5
James 5:1  Come now, you rich people: weep and howl over the miseries coming upon you.
James 5:2  Your riches have rotted, and your garments have become moth-eaten.
James 5:3  Your gold and silver have corroded, and their corrosion will be a testimony against you and will devour your flesh like fire. You have stored up treasure in the last days.
James 5:4  Look, the wages of the laborers who reaped your fields, withheld by you, cry out; and the cries of the harvesters have entered the ears of the Lord Sabaoth.
James 5:5  You lived luxuriously on the earth and indulged yourselves; you fattened your hearts on a day of slaughter.
James 5:6  You condemned; you murdered the righteous one. He does not oppose you.
James 5:7  Be patient, therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Look, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it until he receives the early and late rain.
James 5:8  You too be patient; strengthen your hearts, because the coming of the Lord has drawn near.
James 5:9  Do not groan against one another, brothers, so that you may not be judged. Look, the Judge stands before the doors.
James 5:10  Brothers, take as an example of suffering and patience the prophets who spoke in the Lord’s name.
James 5:11  Look, we call those who endured blessed. You heard of Job’s endurance and saw the outcome from the Lord, because the Lord is full of compassion and merciful.
James 5:12  But above all, my brothers, do not swear, either by heaven or by earth or by any other oath. Let your yes be yes, and your no be no, so that you may not fall under judgment.
James 5:13  Is anyone among you suffering? Let him pray. Is anyone cheerful? Let him sing praise.
James 5:14  Is anyone among you sick? Let him summon the elders of the Church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the Lord’s name.
James 5:15  And the prayer of faith will save the weary sick person, and the Lord will raise him up; and if he has committed sins, he will be forgiven.
James 5:16  Therefore confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, so that you may be healed. A righteous person’s petition has great strength when it is at work.
James 5:17  Elijah was a human being with experiences like ours, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain; and it did not rain upon the earth for three years and six months.
James 5:18  And he prayed again, and heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth its fruit.
James 5:19  My brothers, if anyone among you is led astray from the truth and someone turns him back,
James 5:20  let him know that the one who turns a sinner back from the error of his way will save his soul from death and cover a multitude of sins.

1 PETER

1 Peter 1
1 Peter 1:1  Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen resident aliens of the dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
1 Peter 1:2  according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, in sanctification by the Spirit, for obedience and sprinkling with the blood of Jesus Christ: May grace and peace be multiplied to you.
1 Peter 1:3  Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who, according to His great mercy, has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
1 Peter 1:4  into an inheritance imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, kept in heaven for you,
1 Peter 1:5  who are guarded by the power of God through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.
1 Peter 1:6  In this you rejoice, though now, for a little while, if necessary, you have been grieved by various trials,
1 Peter 1:7  so that the tested genuineness of your faith—more precious than gold that perishes, though tested by fire—may be found to result in praise and glory and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
1 Peter 1:8  Though you have not seen Him, you love Him; though you do not see Him now, yet believing in Him, you rejoice with joy inexpressible and full of glory,
1 Peter 1:9  receiving the outcome of your faith, the salvation of your souls.
1 Peter 1:10  Concerning this salvation, the prophets who prophesied about the grace for you searched and investigated,
1 Peter 1:11  investigating what time or what kind of time the Spirit of Christ within them was indicating, as He testified beforehand to the sufferings destined for Christ and the glories after them.
1 Peter 1:12  It was revealed to them that they were serving these things for you, and not for themselves—things now announced to you through those who proclaimed the good news to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, things into which angels long to look.
1 Peter 1:13  Therefore, gird up the loins of your mind; be sober, and set your hope fully on the grace being brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
1 Peter 1:14  As children of obedience, do not conform yourselves to the former desires of your ignorance,
1 Peter 1:15  but, in accordance with the Holy One who called you, become holy yourselves in all your conduct,
1 Peter 1:16  because it is written, “You shall be holy, because I am holy.”
1 Peter 1:17  And if you call upon as Father the One who judges impartially according to each person’s work, conduct yourselves in fear during the time of your sojourn,
1 Peter 1:18  knowing that you were ransomed from the futile conduct handed down from your ancestors, not with perishable things, silver or gold,
1 Peter 1:19  but with precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot—the blood of Christ,
1 Peter 1:20  who was foreknown before the foundation of the world but was manifested at the end of the times for your sake.
1 Peter 1:21  Through Him you are believers in God, who raised Him from the dead and gave Him glory, so that your faith and hope are in God.
1 Peter 1:22  Having purified your souls by obedience to the truth for sincere brotherly love, love one another earnestly from a pure heart,
1 Peter 1:23  having been born anew, not from perishable seed but from imperishable, through the living and enduring word of God.
1 Peter 1:24  For “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like a flower of grass. The grass has withered, and the flower has fallen,
1 Peter 1:25  but the word of the Lord remains forever.” And this is the word that was proclaimed to you as good news.

1 Peter 2
1 Peter 2:1  Therefore, putting away all malice and all deceit and hypocrisies and envies and all slanders,
1 Peter 2:2  like newborn infants, long for the pure spiritual milk, so that by it you may grow into salvation,
1 Peter 2:3  if you have tasted that the Lord is good.
1 Peter 2:4  Coming to Him, a living stone rejected by human beings but chosen and precious before God,
1 Peter 2:5  you yourselves, like living stones, are also being built into a spiritual house, for a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
1 Peter 2:6  For it stands in Scripture: “Behold, I am laying in Zion a stone, a chosen, precious cornerstone, and the one who believes in Him will certainly not be put to shame.”
1 Peter 2:7  Therefore, the honor is for you who believe; but for those who do not believe, “The stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner,”
1 Peter 2:8  and “a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense.” They stumble, disobeying the word; to this they were also appointed.
1 Peter 2:9  But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s possession, so that you may proclaim the excellences of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.
1 Peter 2:10  Once you were not a people, but now you are God’s people; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.
1 Peter 2:11  Beloved, I urge you, as aliens and sojourners, to abstain from fleshly desires that wage war against the soul,
1 Peter 2:12  keeping your conduct good among the Gentiles, so that, in the very matter for which they slander you as evildoers, they may observe your good works and glorify God on the day of visitation.
1 Peter 2:13  Submit yourselves to every human institution for the Lord’s sake, whether to a king as supreme,
1 Peter 2:14  or to governors as sent by him for the punishment of evildoers and the praise of those who do good.
1 Peter 2:15  For this is the will of God: that by doing good you should silence the ignorance of foolish people.
1 Peter 2:16  Live as free people, yet without using freedom as a covering for evil, but as slaves of God.
1 Peter 2:17  Honor everyone. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honor the king.
1 Peter 2:18  Household slaves, submit yourselves to your masters with all fear, not only to the good and considerate but also to the crooked.
1 Peter 2:19  For this is grace: if, out of awareness of God, someone bears sorrows while suffering unjustly.
1 Peter 2:20  For what credit is there if, when you sin and are beaten, you endure? But if, when you do good and suffer, you endure, this is grace before God.
1 Peter 2:21  For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, so that you might follow in His footsteps.
1 Peter 2:22  He committed no sin, nor was deceit found in His mouth.
1 Peter 2:23  When He was reviled, He did not revile in return; when He suffered, He did not threaten, but entrusted His cause to the One who judges justly.
1 Peter 2:24  He Himself bore our sins in His body upon the tree, so that, having died to sins, we might live for righteousness. By His bruise you were healed.
1 Peter 2:25  For you were wandering like sheep, but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.

1 Peter 3
1 Peter 3:1  Likewise, wives, submit yourselves to your own husbands, so that even if some disobey the word, they may be won without a word through the conduct of their wives,
1 Peter 3:2  when they observe your pure conduct in fear.
1 Peter 3:3  Let your adornment not be the outward kind—braiding hair, putting on gold ornaments, or dressing in garments—
1 Peter 3:4  but the hidden person of the heart, in the imperishable beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is very precious before God.
1 Peter 3:5  For this is how the holy women of former times, who hoped in God, also adorned themselves, submitting themselves to their own husbands,
1 Peter 3:6  as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord. You have become her children if you do good and do not fear any terror.
1 Peter 3:7  Likewise, husbands, live with your wives with understanding, honoring them as women—the weaker vessel—and also as fellow heirs of the grace of life, so that your prayers may not be hindered.
1 Peter 3:8  Finally, all of you, be of one mind, sympathetic, loving as brothers, tenderhearted, and humble-minded,
1 Peter 3:9  not repaying evil for evil or reviling for reviling, but, on the contrary, blessing, because you were called for this, so that you might inherit a blessing.
1 Peter 3:10  For “The one who wishes to love life and see good days must keep his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit.
1 Peter 3:11  He must turn away from evil and do good; he must seek peace and pursue it.
1 Peter 3:12  For the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and His ears attend to their petition, but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.”
1 Peter 3:13  And who will harm you if you become zealous for what is good?
1 Peter 3:14  But even if you should suffer for righteousness, you are blessed. Do not fear their fear, and do not be troubled,
1 Peter 3:15  but hallow Christ as Lord in your hearts, always ready to give a defense to everyone who asks you for an account of the hope within you,
1 Peter 3:16  yet with gentleness and fear, keeping a good conscience, so that, in the very matter for which you are slandered, those who abuse your good conduct in Christ may be put to shame.
1 Peter 3:17  For it is better, if the will of God should will it, to suffer while doing good than while doing evil.
1 Peter 3:18  For Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, so that He might bring you to God, being put to death in flesh but made alive in spirit,
1 Peter 3:19  in which He also went and proclaimed to the spirits in prison,
1 Peter 3:20  who were once disobedient, when the patience of God waited in the days of Noah while the ark was being prepared, in which a few—that is, eight souls—were brought safely through water.
1 Peter 3:21  Corresponding to this, baptism also now saves you—not a removal of dirt from the flesh, but an appeal to God for a good conscience—through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
1 Peter 3:22  who is at the right hand of God, having gone into heaven, with angels and authorities and powers subjected to Him.

1 Peter 4
1 Peter 4:1  Therefore, since Christ suffered in flesh, arm yourselves also with the same thought, because the one who has suffered in flesh has ceased from sin,
1 Peter 4:2  so as to live the remaining time in flesh no longer for human desires but for the will of God.
1 Peter 4:3  For you have spent enough time doing what the Gentiles want, walking in debaucheries, desires, bouts of drunkenness, revelries, drinking parties, and lawless acts of idolatry.
1 Peter 4:4  They are surprised that you do not run with them into the same flood of reckless living, and they slander you.
1 Peter 4:5  They will give an account to the One who is ready to judge the living and the dead.
1 Peter 4:6  For this is why the good news was proclaimed even to the dead: so that they might be judged according to human beings in flesh, but live according to God in spirit.
1 Peter 4:7  But the end of all things has drawn near. Therefore, be clear-minded and sober for your prayers.
1 Peter 4:8  Above all, maintain earnest love for one another, because love covers a multitude of sins.
1 Peter 4:9  Be hospitable to one another without grumbling.
1 Peter 4:10  As each has received a gift, use it in serving one another, as good stewards of God’s varied grace.
1 Peter 4:11  If anyone speaks, let it be as words from God; if anyone serves, let it be with the strength God supplies, so that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.
1 Peter 4:12  Beloved, do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal among you, which comes upon you for testing, as though something strange were happening to you.
1 Peter 4:13  But insofar as you share in the sufferings of Christ, rejoice, so that you may also rejoice with exultation at the revelation of His glory.
1 Peter 4:14  If you are reviled for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests upon you.
1 Peter 4:15  For let none of you suffer as a murderer, or a thief, or an evildoer, or as a meddler in others’ affairs.
1 Peter 4:16  But if anyone suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but let him glorify God in this matter.
1 Peter 4:17  For it is time for judgment to begin from the house of God; and if it begins first from us, what will be the outcome for those who disobey the good news of God?
1 Peter 4:18  And “If the righteous one is saved with difficulty, where will the ungodly person and sinner appear?”
1 Peter 4:19  Therefore, let those who suffer according to the will of God entrust their souls to a faithful Creator while doing good.

1 Peter 5
1 Peter 5:1  I exhort the elders among you, as a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and also a participant in the glory about to be revealed:
1 Peter 5:2  Shepherd the flock of God among you, exercising oversight, not under compulsion but willingly, according to God; not for shameful gain but eagerly;
1 Peter 5:3  not as lording it over those allotted to you, but becoming examples to the flock.
1 Peter 5:4  And when the Chief Shepherd is manifested, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.
1 Peter 5:5  Likewise, you who are younger, submit yourselves to the elders. And all of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, because “God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.”
1 Peter 5:6  Therefore, humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, so that He may exalt you in due time,
1 Peter 5:7  casting all your anxiety upon Him, because He cares for you.
1 Peter 5:8  Be sober; be watchful. Your adversary, the devil, walks about like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour.
1 Peter 5:9  Resist him, firm in the faith, knowing that the same kinds of sufferings are being experienced by your brotherhood in the world.
1 Peter 5:10  And the God of all grace, who called you to His eternal glory in Christ, after you have suffered a little while, will Himself restore, establish, strengthen, and firmly ground you.
1 Peter 5:11  To Him be the dominion forever. Amen.
1 Peter 5:12  Through Silvanus, whom I regard as a faithful brother, I have written to you briefly, exhorting and testifying that this is the true grace of God. Stand in it.
1 Peter 5:13  She who is in Babylon, chosen together with you, greets you, and so does Mark, my son.
1 Peter 5:14  Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace to all of you who are in Christ.

2 PETER

2 Peter 1
2 Peter 1:1  Simeon Peter, a slave and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have received a faith of equal honor with ours through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ:
2 Peter 1:2  May grace and peace be multiplied to you in the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.
2 Peter 1:3  Since His divine power has granted us everything pertaining to life and godliness through the knowledge of the One who called us by His own glory and excellence,
2 Peter 1:4  through these He has granted us the precious and very great promises, so that through them you may become participants in the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through desire.
2 Peter 1:5  And for this very reason, bringing every effort to bear, supply excellence in your faith, and knowledge in excellence,
2 Peter 1:6  and self-control in knowledge, and endurance in self-control, and godliness in endurance,
2 Peter 1:7  and brotherly love in godliness, and love in brotherly love.
2 Peter 1:8  For if these things are yours and abound, they make you neither idle nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
2 Peter 1:9  For the person who lacks these things is blind and shortsighted, having forgotten the cleansing of his former sins.
2 Peter 1:10  Therefore, brothers, be all the more diligent to make your calling and election firm, for if you do these things, you will certainly never stumble.
2 Peter 1:11  For in this way entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ will be richly supplied to you.
2 Peter 1:12  Therefore, I will always be ready to remind you of these things, even though you know them and are firmly established in the truth that is present with you.
2 Peter 1:13  And I consider it right, as long as I am in this tent, to stir you up by reminding you,
2 Peter 1:14  knowing that I will soon put off my tent, as our Lord Jesus Christ also made clear to me.
2 Peter 1:15  And I will also make every effort so that after my departure you may be able at any time to call these things to mind.
2 Peter 1:16  For we did not follow cleverly devised myths when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we became eyewitnesses of His majesty.
2 Peter 1:17  For He received honor and glory from God the Father when a voice such as this was borne to Him by the Majestic Glory: “This is My Son, My Beloved, in whom I have taken pleasure”—
2 Peter 1:18  and we ourselves heard this voice borne from heaven when we were with Him on the holy mountain.
2 Peter 1:19  And we have the prophetic word more firmly established, to which you do well to pay attention as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts,
2 Peter 1:20  knowing this first: that no prophecy of Scripture arises from one’s own interpretation.
2 Peter 1:21  For prophecy was never borne along by human will, but human beings spoke from God as they were borne along by the Holy Spirit.

2 Peter 2
2 Peter 2:1  But false prophets also arose among the people, just as there will also be false teachers among you. They will secretly bring in destructive factions, even denying the Master who bought them, bringing swift destruction upon themselves.
2 Peter 2:2  And many will follow their debaucheries, and because of them the way of truth will be slandered.
2 Peter 2:3  And in greed they will exploit you with fabricated words. Their judgment has not been idle since long ago, and their destruction does not sleep.
2 Peter 2:4  For if God did not spare angels when they sinned, but cast them into Tartarus and handed them over to chains of gloom, kept for judgment,
2 Peter 2:5  and did not spare the ancient world, but preserved Noah, a herald of righteousness, as one of eight, when He brought a flood upon a world of ungodly people,
2 Peter 2:6  and reduced the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to ashes, condemning them to overthrow, having made them an example for those who would live ungodly lives,
2 Peter 2:7  and rescued righteous Lot, who was distressed by the lawless people’s conduct in debauchery—
2 Peter 2:8  for by what he saw and heard, that righteous man, living among them, tormented his righteous soul day after day over their lawless deeds—
2 Peter 2:9  then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial, and to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment,
2 Peter 2:10  especially those who go after flesh in defiling desire and despise lordship. Reckless and self-willed, they do not tremble as they slander glorious beings,
2 Peter 2:11  whereas angels, though greater in strength and power, do not bring a slanderous judgment against them before the Lord.
2 Peter 2:12  But these people, like irrational animals born as creatures of instinct for capture and destruction, slandering things they do not understand, will also be destroyed in their destruction,
2 Peter 2:13  suffering harm as the wages of wrongdoing. They consider indulgence in the daytime a pleasure. They are spots and blemishes, reveling in their deceptions while feasting with you,
2 Peter 2:14  having eyes full of an adulteress and unable to stop sinning, enticing unstable souls, having a heart trained in greed—children of a curse!
2 Peter 2:15  Leaving the straight way, they wandered off, following the way of Balaam son of Bosor, who loved the wages of wrongdoing,
2 Peter 2:16  but received a rebuke for his own transgression: a speechless beast of burden spoke with a human voice and restrained the prophet’s madness.
2 Peter 2:17  These people are waterless springs and mists driven by a storm, for whom the gloom of darkness has been kept.
2 Peter 2:18  For, uttering inflated words of emptiness, they entice through fleshly desires and debaucheries those who are truly escaping from people who live in error,
2 Peter 2:19  promising them freedom while they themselves are slaves of corruption; for by whatever someone has been overcome, to this he has also been enslaved.
2 Peter 2:20  For if, after escaping the world’s defilements through the knowledge of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, they are again entangled in them and overcome, their last state has become worse than their first.
2 Peter 2:21  For it would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness than, after knowing it, to turn back from the holy commandment handed down to them.
2 Peter 2:22  What the true proverb says has happened to them: “A dog has returned to its own vomit,” and, “A sow, after washing, returns to wallowing in mud.”

2 Peter 3
2 Peter 3:1  Beloved, this is now the second letter I am writing to you. In these letters I stir up your sincere mind by reminding you,
2 Peter 3:2  so that you may remember the words spoken beforehand by the holy prophets and the commandment of the Lord and Savior through your apostles,
2 Peter 3:3  knowing this first: in the last days scoffers will come with scoffing, walking according to their own desires,
2 Peter 3:4  and saying, “Where is the promise of His coming? For ever since the fathers fell asleep, everything continues as it was from the beginning of creation.”
2 Peter 3:5  For they willingly overlook this: that heavens existed long ago, and earth was formed out of water and through water by the word of God,
2 Peter 3:6  through which the world that then existed was flooded with water and perished.
2 Peter 3:7  But the present heavens and earth have been stored up by the same word for fire, kept for the day of judgment and destruction of ungodly people.
2 Peter 3:8  But do not let this one thing escape you, beloved: with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day.
2 Peter 3:9  The Lord is not slow concerning the promise, as some consider slowness, but is patient toward you, not wishing anyone to perish but all to come to repentance.
2 Peter 3:10  But the day of the Lord will come like a thief. On that day the heavens will pass away with a rushing roar, and the elements will be dissolved by burning heat, and the earth and the works in it will not be found.
2 Peter 3:11  Since all these things are being dissolved in this way, what sort of people ought you to be in holy acts of conduct and godliness,
2 Peter 3:12  waiting for and hastening the coming of the day of God, because of which the heavens will be dissolved by fire and the elements melt in burning heat?
2 Peter 3:13  But according to His promise we await new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells.
2 Peter 3:14  Therefore, beloved, as you await these things, be diligent to be found by Him spotless and blameless, in peace,
2 Peter 3:15  and consider the patience of our Lord to be salvation, just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote to you according to the wisdom given to him,
2 Peter 3:16  as also in all his letters, speaking in them about these things. In them are some things hard to understand, which the unlearned and unstable will distort, just as they will distort the other Scriptures, to their own destruction.
2 Peter 3:17  Therefore, beloved, knowing this beforehand, guard yourselves so that you are not carried away by the error of lawless people and fall from your own firm position.
2 Peter 3:18  But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To Him be the glory both now and to the day of eternity.

1 JOHN

1 John 1
1 John 1:1  What was from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we looked upon and our hands touched, concerning the word of life—
1 John 1:2  and the life was manifested, and we have seen and bear witness and announce to you the eternal life that was with the Father and was manifested to us—
1 John 1:3  what we have seen and heard we announce also to you, so that you too may have fellowship with us. And our fellowship is with the Father and with His Son Jesus Christ.
1 John 1:4  And we write these things so that our joy may be made full.
1 John 1:5  And this is the message we have heard from Him and announce to you: God is light, and there is no darkness at all in Him.
1 John 1:6  If we say that we have fellowship with Him while walking in darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth.
1 John 1:7  But if we walk in the light, as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from every sin.
1 John 1:8  If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
1 John 1:9  If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
1 John 1:10  If we say that we have not sinned, we make Him a liar, and His word is not in us.

1 John 2
1 John 2:1  My little children, I write these things to you so that you may not sin. And if anyone sins, we have an Advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous,
1 John 2:2  and He Himself is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for the whole world.
1 John 2:3  And by this we know that we have come to know Him: if we keep His commandments.
1 John 2:4  The one who says, “I have come to know Him,” and does not keep His commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in that person.
1 John 2:5  But whoever keeps His word, in that person the love of God has truly been brought to completion. By this we know that we are in Him.
1 John 2:6  The one who says that he abides in Him ought himself also to walk just as He walked.
1 John 2:7  Beloved, I am not writing a new commandment to you, but an old commandment that you had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word you heard.
1 John 2:8  Again, I am writing a new commandment to you, which is true in Him and in you, because the darkness is passing away and the true light is already shining.
1 John 2:9  The one who says that he is in the light and hates his brother is still in the darkness.
1 John 2:10  The one who loves his brother abides in the light, and there is no cause of stumbling in him.
1 John 2:11  But the one who hates his brother is in the darkness and walks in the darkness, and he does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.
1 John 2:12  I write to you, little children, because your sins have been forgiven you for His name’s sake.
1 John 2:13  I write to you, fathers, because you have come to know Him who is from the beginning. I write to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one.
1 John 2:14  I have written to you, children, because you have come to know the Father. I have written to you, fathers, because you have come to know Him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God abides in you, and you have overcome the evil one.
1 John 2:15  Do not love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him.
1 John 2:16  For everything in the world—the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes, and the boastfulness of life—is not from the Father, but is from the world.
1 John 2:17  And the world is passing away, along with its desire; but the one who does the will of God abides forever.
1 John 2:18  Children, it is the last hour. And just as you heard that antichrist is coming, even now many antichrists have arisen; from this we know that it is the last hour.
1 John 2:19  They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would have remained with us. But this happened so that it might become clear that they are not all of us.
1 John 2:20  And you have an anointing from the Holy One, and all of you know.
1 John 2:21  I have not written to you because you do not know the truth, but because you know it, and because no lie is from the truth.
1 John 2:22  Who is the liar except the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the antichrist: the one who denies the Father and the Son.
1 John 2:23  Everyone who denies the Son does not have the Father either; the one who confesses the Son has the Father also.
1 John 2:24  As for you, let what you heard from the beginning abide in you. If what you heard from the beginning abides in you, you too will abide in the Son and in the Father.
1 John 2:25  And this is the promise He Himself promised us: eternal life.
1 John 2:26  I have written these things to you about those who are leading you astray.
1 John 2:27  And as for you, the anointing that you received from Him abides in you, and you have no need for anyone to teach you. But as His anointing teaches you about all things—and is true and is not a lie—so, just as it taught you, abide in Him.
1 John 2:28  And now, little children, abide in Him, so that when He is manifested we may have confidence and not shrink from Him in shame at His coming.
1 John 2:29  If you know that He is righteous, you know that everyone who practices righteousness has also been born of Him.

1 John 3
1 John 3:1  See what kind of love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God—and we are. For this reason the world does not know us, because it did not know Him.
1 John 3:2  Beloved, we are children of God now, and what we will be has not yet been manifested. We know that when He is manifested we will be like Him, because we will see Him as He is.
1 John 3:3  And everyone who has this hope in Him purifies himself, just as He is pure.
1 John 3:4  Everyone who practices sin also practices lawlessness, and sin is lawlessness.
1 John 3:5  And you know that He was manifested to take away sins, and there is no sin in Him.
1 John 3:6  Everyone who abides in Him does not sin; everyone who sins has neither seen Him nor come to know Him.
1 John 3:7  Children, let no one lead you astray. The one who practices righteousness is righteous, just as He is righteous.
1 John 3:8  The one who practices sin is from the devil, because the devil sins from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested: to undo the works of the devil.
1 John 3:9  Everyone who has been born of God does not practice sin, because His seed abides in him; and he cannot sin, because he has been born of God.
1 John 3:10  By this the children of God and the children of the devil are evident: everyone who does not practice righteousness is not from God, nor is the one who does not love his brother.
1 John 3:11  For this is the message you heard from the beginning: that we should love one another,
1 John 3:12  not as Cain, who was from the evil one and slaughtered his brother. And for what reason did he slaughter him? Because his own works were evil, but his brother’s were righteous.
1 John 3:13  And do not be surprised, brothers, if the world hates you.
1 John 3:14  We know that we have passed from death into life, because we love the brothers. The one who does not love abides in death.
1 John 3:15  Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him.
1 John 3:16  By this we have come to know love: He laid down His life for us; and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers.
1 John 3:17  But whoever has this world’s goods and sees his brother in need and closes his heart against him, how does the love of God abide in him?
1 John 3:18  Little children, let us not love in word or with the tongue, but in deed and truth.
1 John 3:19  And by this we will know that we are from the truth, and we will reassure our heart before Him,
1 John 3:20  whenever our heart condemns us, because God is greater than our heart and knows all things.
1 John 3:21  Beloved, if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence toward God,
1 John 3:22  and whatever we ask we receive from Him, because we keep His commandments and do what is pleasing before Him.
1 John 3:23  And this is His commandment: that we believe in the name of His Son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as He gave us a commandment.
1 John 3:24  And the one who keeps His commandments abides in Him, and He in that person. And by this we know that He abides in us: by the Spirit whom He gave us.

1 John 4
1 John 4:1  Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.
1 John 4:2  By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ as having come in the flesh is from God,
1 John 4:3  and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. And this is the spirit of the antichrist, which you heard was coming and is already in the world now.
1 John 4:4  You are from God, little children, and have overcome them, because He who is in you is greater than he who is in the world.
1 John 4:5  They are from the world; for this reason they speak from the world, and the world listens to them.
1 John 4:6  We are from God. The one who knows God listens to us; whoever is not from God does not listen to us. By this we know the spirit of truth and the spirit of error.
1 John 4:7  Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God, and everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.
1 John 4:8  The one who does not love has not come to know God, because God is love.
1 John 4:9  In this the love of God was manifested among us: God has sent His only Son into the world so that we might live through Him.
1 John 4:10  In this is love: not that we have loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son as propitiation for our sins.
1 John 4:11  Beloved, if God loved us in this way, we also ought to love one another.
1 John 4:12  No one has ever beheld God. If we love one another, God abides in us, and His love has been brought to completion in us.
1 John 4:13  By this we know that we abide in Him and He in us: He has given us of His Spirit.
1 John 4:14  And we have beheld and bear witness that the Father has sent the Son as Savior of the world.
1 John 4:15  Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God abides in that person, and that person in God.
1 John 4:16  And we have come to know and have believed the love that God has among us. God is love, and the one who abides in love abides in God, and God abides in that person.
1 John 4:17  In this love has been brought to completion with us, so that we may have confidence on the day of judgment: because just as He is, so are we in this world.
1 John 4:18  There is no fear in love, but complete love casts fear out, because fear involves punishment, and the one who fears has not been brought to completion in love.
1 John 4:19  We love because He first loved us.
1 John 4:20  If anyone says, “I love God,” and hates his brother, he is a liar. For the one who does not love his brother, whom he has seen, cannot love God, whom he has not seen.
1 John 4:21  And this commandment we have from Him: the one who loves God must love his brother also.

1 John 5
1 John 5:1  Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and everyone who loves the One who begot also loves the one begotten of Him.
1 John 5:2  By this we know that we love the children of God: when we love God and do His commandments.
1 John 5:3  For this is the love of God: that we keep His commandments; and His commandments are not burdensome,
1 John 5:4  because everything born of God overcomes the world. And this is the victory that has overcome the world: our faith.
1 John 5:5  And who is the one who overcomes the world except the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?
1 John 5:6  This is He who came through water and blood, Jesus Christ—not in water only, but in water and in blood. And the Spirit is the one who bears witness, because the Spirit is the truth.
1 John 5:7  For there are three who bear witness:
1 John 5:8  the Spirit and the water and the blood, and the three agree as one.
1 John 5:9  If we receive human testimony, the testimony of God is greater, because this is God’s testimony: He has borne witness concerning His Son.
1 John 5:10  The one who believes in the Son of God has the testimony within himself. The one who does not believe God has made Him a liar, because he has not believed in the testimony God has borne concerning His Son.
1 John 5:11  And this is the testimony: God gave us eternal life, and this life is in His Son.
1 John 5:12  The one who has the Son has life; the one who does not have the Son of God does not have life.
1 John 5:13  I have written these things to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, so that you may know that you have eternal life.
1 John 5:14  And this is the confidence we have toward Him: if we ask anything according to His will, He hears us.
1 John 5:15  And if we know that He hears us in whatever we ask, we know that we have the requests we have asked of Him.
1 John 5:16  If anyone sees his brother committing a sin not leading to death, he is to ask, and he will give him life—to those committing sin not leading to death. There is sin leading to death; I am not saying that he should make a request concerning that.
1 John 5:17  All unrighteousness is sin, and there is sin not leading to death.
1 John 5:18  We know that everyone who has been born of God does not sin, but the one born of God keeps himself, and the evil one does not touch him.
1 John 5:19  We know that we are from God, and the whole world lies in the evil one.
1 John 5:20  And we know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding so that we may know the True One. And we are in the True One, in His Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God and eternal life.
1 John 5:21  Little children, guard yourselves from idols.

2 JOHN

2 John 1
2 John 1:1  The elder, to the chosen lady and her children, whom I love in truth—and not I alone, but also all who have come to know the truth—
2 John 1:2  because of the truth that abides in us and will be with us forever:
2 John 1:3  Grace, mercy, and peace will be with us from God the Father and from Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.
2 John 1:4  I rejoiced greatly that I have found some of your children walking in truth, just as we received a commandment from the Father.
2 John 1:5  And now I ask you, lady—not as though writing you a new commandment, but the one we had from the beginning—that we love one another.
2 John 1:6  And this is love: that we walk according to His commandments. This is the commandment, just as you all heard from the beginning: that you walk in it.
2 John 1:7  For many deceivers have gone out into the world, those who do not confess Jesus Christ coming in the flesh. Such a person is the deceiver and the antichrist.
2 John 1:8  Watch yourselves, so that you do not lose what we have worked for, but receive a full reward.
2 John 1:9  Everyone who goes ahead and does not abide in the teaching of Christ does not have God. Whoever abides in the teaching has both the Father and the Son.
2 John 1:10  If anyone comes to you and does not bring this teaching, do not receive him into a house, and do not offer him a greeting,
2 John 1:11  for whoever offers him a greeting shares in his evil works.
2 John 1:12  Although I have many things to write to you all, I did not wish to do so with paper and ink. Instead, I hope to come to you and speak face to face, so that our joy may be made full.
2 John 1:13  The children of your chosen sister greet you.

3 JOHN

3 John 1
3 John 1:1  The elder, to the beloved Gaius, whom I love in truth.
3 John 1:2  Beloved, I pray that all may go well with you and that you may be in good health, just as all goes well with your soul.
3 John 1:3  For I rejoiced greatly when brothers came and bore witness to your truthfulness, just as you walk in truth.
3 John 1:4  I have no greater joy than this: to hear that my children are walking in the truth.
3 John 1:5  Beloved, you act faithfully in whatever you do for the brothers, even though they are strangers,
3 John 1:6  who have borne witness to your love before the Church. You will do well to send them onward in a manner worthy of God,
3 John 1:7  for they went out for the sake of the Name, receiving nothing from the Gentiles.
3 John 1:8  We therefore ought to support such people, so that we may become fellow workers with the truth.
3 John 1:9  I wrote something to the Church, but Diotrephes, who loves to be first among them, does not welcome us.
3 John 1:10  Therefore, if I come, I will call attention to the works he is doing: he is talking malicious nonsense about us. Not content with these things, he neither welcomes the brothers himself nor allows those who want to do so, and he puts them out of the Church.
3 John 1:11  Beloved, do not imitate what is evil, but what is good. The one who does good is from God; the one who does evil has not seen God.
3 John 1:12  Demetrius has received testimony from everyone and from the truth itself. We also bear witness, and you know that our testimony is true.
3 John 1:13  I had many things to write to you, but I do not wish to write to you with ink and a reed pen.
3 John 1:14  But I hope to see you soon, and we will speak face to face.
3 John 1:15  Peace to you. The friends greet you. Greet the friends by name.

JUDE

Jude 1
Jude 1:1  Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, to those who are called, beloved in God the Father and kept for Jesus Christ:
Jude 1:2  May mercy and peace and love be multiplied to you.
Jude 1:3  Beloved, while making every effort to write to you about the salvation we share, I found it necessary to write and urge you to contend for the faith delivered once for all to the saints.
Jude 1:4  For certain people have slipped in unnoticed, those written about long ago for this judgment: ungodly people who turn the grace of our God into shameless indulgence and deny our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ.
Jude 1:5  Now I wish to remind you, although you have come to know all this once for all, that Jesus, after saving a people from the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed those who did not believe.
Jude 1:6  And He has kept the angels who did not keep their own domain, but abandoned their proper dwelling, in everlasting chains under gloom for the judgment of the great day.
Jude 1:7  In the same way, Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them, which practiced sexual immorality and went after other flesh in a manner like these, are set before us as an example, undergoing the penalty of eternal fire.
Jude 1:8  Yet in the same way these people too, in their dreaming, defile flesh, reject dominion, and slander glorious ones.
Jude 1:9  But Michael the archangel, when he was contending with the devil and disputing about the body of Moses, did not dare to bring a slanderous judgment against him, but said, “May the Lord rebuke you.”
Jude 1:10  But these people slander whatever they do not know; and what they understand by instinct, like unreasoning animals, becomes the very thing by which they are corrupted.
Jude 1:11  Woe to them! For they have gone in the way of Cain, have poured themselves into Balaam’s error for pay, and have perished in Korah’s rebellion.
Jude 1:12  These are reefs at your love feasts, feasting together with you without fear, shepherding themselves; waterless clouds carried along by winds; late-autumn trees without fruit, twice dead, uprooted;
Jude 1:13  wild waves of the sea foaming up their own shames; wandering stars for whom the gloom of darkness has been kept forever.
Jude 1:14  Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied about these people, saying, “Look, the Lord came with His holy myriads,
Jude 1:15  to execute judgment against all and to convict every soul concerning all their ungodly works that they committed in ungodliness, and concerning all the harsh things that ungodly sinners spoke against Him.”
Jude 1:16  These are grumblers, faultfinders, walking according to their own desires; their mouth speaks boastful things, and they flatter people for the sake of advantage.
Jude 1:17  But you, beloved, remember the words spoken beforehand by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ,
Jude 1:18  for they used to tell you, “In the last time there will be mockers, walking according to their own ungodly desires.”
Jude 1:19  These are the ones who create divisions, unspiritual people who do not have the Spirit.
Jude 1:20  But you, beloved, building yourselves up upon your most holy faith and praying in the Holy Spirit,
Jude 1:21  keep yourselves in the love of God, awaiting the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ that leads to eternal life.
Jude 1:22  And have mercy on some who are doubting;
Jude 1:23  save others, snatching them out of the fire; and have mercy on others with fear, hating even the tunic stained by the flesh.
Jude 1:24  Now to Him who is able to guard you from stumbling and to make you stand blameless before His glory with exultation,
Jude 1:25  to the only God our Savior, through Jesus Christ our Lord, be glory, majesty, might, and authority before all time, and now, and into all the ages. Amen.

REVELATION

Revelation 1
Revelation 1:1  A revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His slaves what must take place soon. He made it known to His slave John by sending His angel,
Revelation 1:2  who testified to the word of God and the testimony of Jesus Christ, all that he saw.
Revelation 1:3  Blessed is the one who reads aloud, and blessed are those who hear the words of the prophecy and keep what is written in it, for the time is near.
Revelation 1:4  John, to the seven Churches in Asia: grace to you and peace from the One who is and who was and who is coming, and from the seven spirits before His throne,
Revelation 1:5  and from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, the firstborn of the dead and the ruler of the kings of the earth. To Him who loves us and freed us from our sins by His blood—
Revelation 1:6  and made us a kingdom, priests to His God and Father—to Him be the glory and dominion for the ages of the ages. Amen.
Revelation 1:7  Behold, He is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see Him, even those who pierced Him, and all the tribes of the earth will mourn over Him. Yea, amen.
Revelation 1:8  “I am the Alpha and the Omega,” says the Lord God, the One who is and who was and who is coming, the Almighty.
Revelation 1:9  I, John, your brother and fellow sharer in the affliction and kingdom and endurance in Jesus, was on the island called Patmos because of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus.
Revelation 1:10  I was in the Spirit on the Lord’s day and heard behind me a loud voice like a trumpet,
Revelation 1:11  saying, “Write what you see in a scroll and send it to the seven Churches: to Ephesus and to Smyrna and to Pergamum and to Thyatira and to Sardis and to Philadelphia and to Laodicea.”
Revelation 1:12  And I turned to see the voice that spoke with me. When I turned, I saw seven golden lampstands,
Revelation 1:13  and in the midst of the lampstands One like a son of man, clothed in a robe reaching to the feet and girded around the chest with a golden belt.
Revelation 1:14  And His head and hair were white like white wool, like snow, and His eyes like a flame of fire,
Revelation 1:15  and His feet like burnished bronze, as though made to glow in a furnace, and His voice like the sound of many waters.
Revelation 1:16  And He held seven stars in His right hand, and from His mouth a sharp two-edged sword was coming out, and His appearance was like the sun shining in its strength.
Revelation 1:17  And when I saw Him, I fell at His feet as dead. And He placed His right hand upon me, saying, “Fear not. I am the first and the last,
Revelation 1:18  and the Living One. I was dead, and behold, I am alive for the ages of the ages, and I have the keys of death and Hades.
Revelation 1:19  Therefore write what you saw, and what is, and what is to take place after these things.
Revelation 1:20  As for the mystery of the seven stars you saw upon My right hand, and the seven golden lampstands: the seven stars are angels of the seven Churches, and the seven lampstands are seven Churches.”

Revelation 2
Revelation 2:1  “To the angel of the Church in Ephesus write: Thus says the One who holds the seven stars in His right hand, who walks in the midst of the seven golden lampstands:
Revelation 2:2  ‘I know your works and your labor and endurance, and that you cannot bear evil people. You tested those who call themselves apostles and are not, and found them false.
Revelation 2:3  You have endurance, and you have borne up for My name’s sake and have not grown weary.
Revelation 2:4  But I have this against you: you abandoned your first love.
Revelation 2:5  Remember, therefore, from where you have fallen. Repent and do the works you did at first. Otherwise I am coming to you and will move your lampstand from its place, unless you repent.
Revelation 2:6  Yet this you have: you hate the works of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.
Revelation 2:7  Let the one who has an ear hear what the Spirit says to the Churches. To the one who conquers I will give to eat from the tree of life, which is in the Paradise of God.’
Revelation 2:8  And to the angel of the Church in Smyrna write: Thus says the First and the Last, who was dead and came to life:
Revelation 2:9  ‘I know your affliction and poverty—but you are rich—and the slander from those who say they are Jews and are not, but are a synagogue of Satan.
Revelation 2:10  Fear none of what you are about to suffer. Behold, the devil is about to throw some of you into prison so that you may be tested, and you will have affliction for ten days. Be faithful unto death, and I will give you the crown of life.
Revelation 2:11  Let the one who has an ear hear what the Spirit says to the Churches. The one who conquers will never be harmed by the second death.’
Revelation 2:12  And to the angel of the Church in Pergamum write: Thus says the One who has the sharp two-edged sword:
Revelation 2:13  ‘I know where you dwell, where Satan’s throne is. You hold fast My name and did not deny My faith, even in the days of Antipas, My witness, My faithful one, who was killed among you, where Satan dwells.
Revelation 2:14  But I have a few things against you: you have there those who hold the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to set a stumbling block before the sons of Israel, to eat things sacrificed to idols and to commit fornication.
Revelation 2:15  So you too have those who hold the teaching of the Nicolaitans in the same way.
Revelation 2:16  Repent, therefore. Otherwise I am coming to you quickly, and I will wage war against them with the sword of My mouth.
Revelation 2:17  Let the one who has an ear hear what the Spirit says to the Churches. To the one who conquers I will give some of the hidden manna, and I will give him a white stone, and on the stone a new name written, which no one knows except the one who receives it.’
Revelation 2:18  And to the angel of the Church in Thyatira write: Thus says the Son of God, whose eyes are like a flame of fire and whose feet are like burnished bronze:
Revelation 2:19  ‘I know your works and your love and faith and service and endurance, and that your latter works exceed the first.
Revelation 2:20  But I have this against you: you tolerate the woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess. She teaches and leads My slaves astray to commit fornication and to eat things sacrificed to idols.
Revelation 2:21  I gave her time to repent, and she does not wish to repent of her fornication.
Revelation 2:22  Behold, I am casting her onto a bed, and those who commit adultery with her into great affliction, unless they repent of her works.
Revelation 2:23  And I will kill her children with death, and all the Churches will know that I am the One who searches kidneys and hearts, and I will give to each of you according to your works.
Revelation 2:24  But to you, the rest in Thyatira, who do not hold this teaching and have not known the deep things of Satan, as they say, I say: I lay no other burden upon you.
Revelation 2:25  Only hold fast what you have until I come.
Revelation 2:26  To the one who conquers and keeps My works to the end, I will give authority over the nations,
Revelation 2:27  and he will shepherd them with an iron rod, as vessels of pottery are shattered,
Revelation 2:28  as I also have received from My Father; and I will give him the morning star.
Revelation 2:29  Let the one who has an ear hear what the Spirit says to the Churches.’

Revelation 3
Revelation 3:1  And to the angel of the Church in Sardis write: Thus says the One who has the seven spirits of God and the seven stars: ‘I know your works. You have a name for being alive, yet you are dead.
Revelation 3:2  Be watchful, and strengthen what remains and was about to die, for I have not found your works complete before My God.
Revelation 3:3  Remember, therefore, how you received and heard, and keep it and repent. If, then, you do not watch, I will come like a thief, and you will certainly not know at what hour I will come upon you.
Revelation 3:4  But you have a few names in Sardis who did not defile their garments, and they will walk with Me in white, for they are worthy.
Revelation 3:5  The one who conquers will thus be clothed in white garments, and I will never blot his name out of the book of life. I will confess his name before My Father and before His angels.
Revelation 3:6  Let the one who has an ear hear what the Spirit says to the Churches.’
Revelation 3:7  And to the angel of the Church in Philadelphia write: Thus says the Holy One, the True One, who has the key of David, who opens and no one will shut, and who shuts and no one opens:
Revelation 3:8  ‘I know your works. Behold, I have set before you an open door that no one can shut, because you have little strength and you kept My word and did not deny My name.
Revelation 3:9  Behold, I give some from the synagogue of Satan, from those who say they are Jews and are not, but lie. Behold, I will make them come and bow down before your feet and know that I have loved you.
Revelation 3:10  Because you kept the word of My endurance, I also will keep you from the hour of trial that is about to come upon the whole inhabited world, to try those who dwell upon the earth.
Revelation 3:11  I am coming quickly. Hold fast what you have, that no one may take your crown.
Revelation 3:12  The one who conquers, I will make him a pillar in the sanctuary of My God, and he will never go out again. I will write upon him the name of My God and the name of the city of My God, the new Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from My God, and My new name.
Revelation 3:13  Let the one who has an ear hear what the Spirit says to the Churches.’
Revelation 3:14  And to the angel of the Church in Laodicea write: Thus says the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of God’s creation:
Revelation 3:15  ‘I know your works, that you are neither cold nor hot. Would that you were cold or hot!
Revelation 3:16  So, because you are lukewarm, and neither hot nor cold, I am about to vomit you out of My mouth.
Revelation 3:17  Because you say, “I am rich, I have grown wealthy, and I need nothing,” and do not know that you are the one who is wretched and pitiable and poor and blind and naked,
Revelation 3:18  I counsel you to buy from Me gold refined by fire, that you may be rich, and white garments, that you may clothe yourself and the shame of your nakedness may not be seen, and salve to anoint your eyes, that you may see.
Revelation 3:19  Those whom I love, I reprove and discipline. Be zealous, therefore, and repent.
Revelation 3:20  Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in to him and dine with him, and he with Me.
Revelation 3:21  I will grant the one who conquers to sit with Me on My throne, as I also conquered and sat with My Father on His throne.
Revelation 3:22  Let the one who has an ear hear what the Spirit says to the Churches.’”

Revelation 4
Revelation 4:1  After these things I saw, and behold, a door stood open in heaven. The first voice I had heard, like a trumpet speaking with me, said, “Come up here, and I will show you what must take place after these things.”
Revelation 4:2  At once I was in the Spirit. And behold, a throne stood in heaven, and upon the throne sat One.
Revelation 4:3  And the One seated there was in appearance like jasper and sardius, and around the throne was a rainbow like an emerald in appearance.
Revelation 4:4  And around the throne were twenty-four thrones, and upon them sat twenty-four elders clothed in white garments, with golden crowns upon their heads.
Revelation 4:5  And from the throne come flashes of lightning and voices and peals of thunder, and before the throne burn seven fiery torches, which are the seven spirits of God.
Revelation 4:6  And before the throne was something like a sea of glass, like crystal. And in the midst of the throne and around the throne were four living creatures, full of eyes in front and behind.
Revelation 4:7  And the first living creature was like a lion, and the second living creature like a calf, and the third living creature had a face like a human being’s, and the fourth living creature was like an eagle flying.
Revelation 4:8  And the four living creatures each have six wings and are full of eyes all around and within. Day and night they have no rest, saying, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God Almighty, the One who was and who is and who is coming.”
Revelation 4:9  And whenever the living creatures give glory and honor and thanksgiving to the One seated upon the throne, who lives for the ages of the ages,
Revelation 4:10  the twenty-four elders will fall before the One seated upon the throne and will worship Him who lives for the ages of the ages. They will cast their crowns before the throne, saying,
Revelation 4:11  “Thou art worthy, our Lord and God, to receive the glory and the honor and the power, for Thou didst create all things, and because of Thy will they existed and were created.”

Revelation 5
Revelation 5:1  And I saw upon the right hand of the One seated upon the throne a scroll written within and on the back, sealed with seven seals.
Revelation 5:2  And I saw a mighty angel proclaiming with a loud voice, “Who is worthy to open the scroll and undo its seals?”
Revelation 5:3  And no one in heaven or upon the earth or beneath the earth was able to open the scroll or look at it.
Revelation 5:4  And I wept much, because no one was found worthy to open the scroll or look at it.
